title: cloister: register lsp_* route → notme-proxy UDS → LLO MCP
description:
Parent: rosary-ac0518. Depends on ley-line-open-ac5b3f (LLO HTTP MCP transport) + notme-ac2941 (UDS listen).

Register a new tool-name prefix in cloister's routeMethod / handleToolCall so that any lsp_* call (lsp_diagnostics, lsp_hover, lsp_defs, lsp_refs, lsp_symbols, lsp_get_node, lsp_find_callers, vec_search) is forwarded to the LLO daemon. Mirror the existing rosary HTTP-proxy pattern in src/index.ts.

Forwarding path:
- workerd cannot speak UDS directly. Forward HTTP-over-UDS via notme-proxy on a known UDS path (/run/notme/llo.sock), so the request body still flows through the attested mTLS bridge to LLO's HTTP MCP port.
- Service-binding-friendly: define LLO_MCP_URL in wrangler.toml + config.capnp env. In dev: http://127.0.0.1:8384/mcp. In prod (or when notme-proxy fronts it): the unix:-style URL the workerd HTTP proxy understands.
- All forwarded responses are pure JSON-RPC, no rewriting needed beyond stripping the lsp_ prefix if we want LLO's bare op names internally (or pass through if LLO accepts MCP-shaped tool names).

Test: spin up workerd + a stub LLO MCP server in the test harness; assert tools/list reports lsp_* tools and tools/call → lsp_diagnostics returns the stub's payload.

title: Claude Code plugin: route LSP through cloister + hook stale-didChange
description:
Parent: rosary-ac0518. Depends on cloister-ac8bcf (lsp_* route registered).

The actual fix for stale rust-analyzer diagnostics in CC sessions. Per Anthropic's plugin reference (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference), build a Claude Code plugin that:

1. Registers an MCP server entry pointing at cloister: { transport: 'http', url: 'http://localhost:8787/mcp' }. CC then sees lsp_diagnostics, lsp_hover, lsp_defs, etc. as mcp__cloister__lsp_* tools.

2. Hooks on Edit / Write tool completion: pushes a fresh-diagnostic notification into the agent loop for the edited file. Closes the gap that mcp__ide__getDiagnostics has today (IDE's rust-analyzer never gets didChange after CC edits → stale Problems panel).

3. Optionally augments / replaces the stock LSP tool's diagnostic source for languages LLO covers (rust, go, python, ts, ...).

Suggested layout: wrappers/claude-code/ in the cloister repo (or a sibling repo if scope grows). Plugin manifest + the small JS/TS that wires hook handlers.

Acceptance: edit a Rust file via CC → next agent turn, fresh diagnostics appear without manually invoking any tool. The 'I report stale rust-analyzer a lot' frustration goes away.

comments.text:
Shipping in PR opened from branch `feat/wrappers-claude-code-plugin-acbf27`.

## What lands

New plugin at `wrappers/claude-code/`:

```
wrappers/claude-code/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   ├── plugin.json              — leyline-stale-sync v0.1.0, AGPL-3.0
│   └── hooks/hooks.json         — PostToolUse matcher (Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit)
├── hooks/
│   └── post_tool_use_reparse.py — Python hook, ~180 LOC
├── .mcp.json                    — declares LLO as an MCP server CC can call
└── README.md
```

## Architectural notes (vs original framing)

The cloister LLM's "stale-didChange hook fires textDocument/didChange against LLO's rust-analyzer instance" was the wrong primitive — LLO doesn't expose an LSP wire today (the `leyline lsp` shim from ADR-0016 §8 is deferred). The right primitive is `reparse(files=[path])` over the existing MCP `tools/call` surface. The hook fires that against `POST http://localhost:8384/mcp` with the `x-leyline-token` header (ADR-0022). Daemon re-runs tree-sitter parse + LSP enrichment on the edited file. Next agent query returns fresh data.

This collapses L1+L2 into one cohesive plugin (~250 LOC including README). L3 (cloister-routed mode) is opt-in env var (`LEYLINE_MCP_URL`); no code work needed.

## Failure mode

Hook is best-effort. If daemon is down / token missing / network error / etc., logs to stderr and exits 0. CC's edit flow is never blocked. Verified via 4 smoke tests pre-commit (missing token, no file_path, malformed JSON, daemon-down — all exit 0 with clean debug logs).

## Cleanup

Cloister's `cloister/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (the stub `cloister-stale-sync`) is now superseded by this LLO plugin. Cloister-side cleanup is a separate cloister-repo PR — out of scope here.

description:
2026-08-06, ~21:15-21:22 UTC. GitHub had an active, critical, ongoing "Incident with Actions" (started 15:22 UTC, webhook delivery throttled to ~15%) that prevented PR #344's required check ("Check + Clippy + Test (task ci)") from ever registering — over an hour with zero checks queued.

main's branch protection has enforce_admins: true, which blocks the normal admin-merge-override path entirely. With explicit user confirmation, the required_status_checks sub-resource was removed via the GitHub API (DELETE .../branches/main/protection/required_status_checks), PR #344 was merged, and the exact original configuration was restored immediately after (PUT with the full snapshot, including the app_id: 15368 pin on the required check — verified byte-for-byte identical to the pre-bypass state via diff).

Justification, not just permission: the merged commit had already passed a full local `task ci` run with a real attestation receipt before any of this, and PR #342 (the underlying keyring fix this release ships) had already been independently verified by building the exact failing configuration inside a real Linux container on the repo's pinned toolchain — clean, both with and without the affected feature. This was not routing around an untested change; GHA's own incident was the only thing that hadn't yet confirmed what was already independently verified true.

No process change proposed here — this bead exists so the event has a durable record beyond the PR history and chat transcript, in case the pattern recurs.

title: mcp-descriptor: artifact-only producer mode — express an image publisher that serves no MCP, schema-valid
description:
Third leg of the MCP thread (with 60f0d3's spec pinning): notme-6e5330 showed the registry schema cannot describe a producer that publishes OCI images and serves no MCP — Package.required includes transport, and adding a placeholder stdio transport trades a validation failure for a runtime lie (cloister derives session behavior from that field). But the vendored schema (schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json) makes packages[] OPTIONAL (top-level required is only name/description/version), and _meta.'io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided' is the designed extension slot (additionalProperties: true, 'publisher-provided metadata for downstream registries').

Contract (ecosystem-agreed, cloister + notme beads reference this): an artifact-only descriptor emits NO packages[] and carries
_meta.'io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided'.artifacts = [{registryType: 'oci', identifier: '<registry/image>', version: '<vX.Y.Z>'}] — Package shape minus transport. leyline-mcp-descriptor gains this mode; render() validates the result against the vendored schema (it must pass, unlike today's refusal). Follow-up worth noting in the code: an upstream SEP asking the registry schema to model non-serving publishers directly.

title: (LLO-side) Grammar-derived property tests for LLO's gen'd surfaces (companion to mache-7qf0)
description:
## Why (companion to mache-7qf0)

mache filed an epic (`mache-7qf0`) capturing the PostHog SQL-parser insight: **property-based generation from the grammar + production-log shadow mode**. That epic targets mache's smell rules. The discipline applies equally to LLO's gen'd surfaces, but at a different layer.

LLO has two gen'd surfaces where grammar-derived testing would expose real bugs current hand-curated fixtures miss:

1. **capnp Rust↔Go codegen parity** — `clients/go/leyline-schema` is regenerated from `rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp`. The Rust codegen and Go codegen pipelines are independent. A divergence between them would show up as a deserialization mismatch — mache reads a capnp segment LLO wrote and gets wrong values. We have no test for this today.
2. **Per-language HDC canonical-map kind coverage** — each language LLO supports has a canonical map (`rs/ll-open/hdc/src/canonical/`). The map IS the kind alphabet HDC encodes against. Kinds the canonical map doesn't recognize fall into a generic bucket — which means a language's HDC quality depends on canonical-map completeness. We've never measured coverage.

## What this bead is

The parent / epic capturing the LLO-side of the discipline. Child beads carry per-deliverable work:

- **capnp parity property tests** — generate valid capnp messages, serialize Rust + deserialize Go (and vice versa), assert byte-equality on round trip. Coverage-guided: prefer message shapes that exercise unions / lists / nested groups not yet seen.
- **Per-language canonical-map coverage report** — for each language, walk tree-sitter grammars; generate AST shapes covering the grammar's kind set; check each kind against the canonical map; report (covered / mapped to generic / orphan) metrics. Surface gaps as a CI artifact.

Out of scope for THIS bead (file separately if scoped):
- Built-in smell-rule fixture generation in mache (covered by `mache-7qf0.1`)
- External smell-rule fuzzer CLI in mache (covered by `mache-7qf0.2`)

## Acceptance for the epic

Both children resolved; an ADR (probably ADR-0026 if released numbering holds, otherwise next available) documents the discipline + how the generated fixtures gate substrate identity going forward.

## Prior art

- PostHog SQL-parser rewrite (2026): https://posthog.com/blog/sql-parser
- Hypothesis (Python property-based testing): https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/
- Sibling epic: mache-7qf0

## Why patch this even matters

ADR-0024's substrate-identity rewrite (v0.5.0) introduced the discipline of pre-registered substrate-property tests. ADR-0025 carries it forward for HDC compositional value. This bead is the same discipline applied to the gen'd boundaries: any cross-language or cross-codegen divergence is a substrate-identity break that today's tests don't catch.

title: (LLO-side) capnp Rust↔Go codegen parity property tests
description:
## What

Property-based round-trip parity tests between LLO's two capnp codegen outputs (Rust + Go). Goal: catch any divergence where Rust serializes a message that Go deserializes incorrectly (or vice versa).

## Implementation sketch

1. **Generator**: walks `rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp` and emits valid messages per top-level type. Coverage-guided: prefer message shapes exercising unions, lists, nested groups, anyPointer fields not yet seen.
2. **Roundtrip test**: for each generated message, (a) serialize via Rust capnp, (b) deserialize via the Go `clients/go/leyline-schema` package, (c) re-serialize via Go, (d) deserialize via Rust, (e) assert deep equality with the original.
3. **Failure mode**: any divergence (field missing, value coerced wrong, union tag mismatch) is a fail with a minimal-reproducer message dump.
4. **CI integration**: cargo test target in `rs/ll-core/public-schema/tests/` + a `go test` in `clients/go/leyline-schema/`. Both must pass for substrate-identity to hold across runtime boundaries.

## Acceptance

- Test corpus covers every top-level message type in `daemon.capnp` (one entry per `struct` / `interface` at the top level).
- Coverage metric: % of fields in each message shape that have been exercised by at least one generated instance.
- Both Rust and Go test targets exist and run in `task ci`.
- A docs/research entry or appendix in ADR-0014 captures the discipline so future schema edits know to maintain parity.

## Dependencies

Depends on parent epic. No code dependency on sibling bead (canonical-map coverage).

## Out of scope

- Wire-protocol-level shadow mode (replay production traces) — phase 2 if we ever capture wire traces at scale
- Multi-version compatibility (capnp v0.25 vs v0.26 etc.) — separate concern handled by the exact-pin in `schema-capnp/Cargo.toml`

title: (LLO-side) Per-language HDC canonical-map kind coverage report
description:
## What

For each language LLO supports via tree-sitter (`leyline-ts`), produce a coverage report measuring how completely the corresponding HDC canonical map (`rs/ll-open/hdc/src/canonical/`) covers the language's AST kind set.

## Why it matters

The canonical map IS the kind alphabet HDC encodes against. Kinds present in the language's grammar but missing from the canonical map fall into a generic catch-all bucket — which silently degrades HDC encoding quality for that kind of node. We have no way today to know, per language, what fraction of the grammar's kinds the canonical map actually distinguishes.

This bead generates the measurement so we can prioritize canonical-map gap-fill (or accept the gaps explicitly).

## Implementation sketch

1. **Kind enumeration per language**: walk each language's tree-sitter grammar metadata to list every node kind the parser emits. Tree-sitter grammars expose this via `Language::node_kind_for_id` over the full kind range.
2. **Canonical-map probe**: for each kind, ask the canonical map "do you recognize this?" Result is a tri-state: (recognized + mapped to a non-generic canonical), (recognized but mapped to generic), (unrecognized).
3. **Generated-shape augmentation**: for kinds that ARE recognized, generate sample AST shapes containing that kind (grammar-driven), encode via HDC, verify the encoded HV distinguishes from other-kind shapes. Catches "mapped but encoder collapses" cases.
4. **Report**: per-language markdown table with kind / canonical-mapping / encoding-distinguishability columns. Surface as CI artifact + commit a snapshot under `docs/research/canonical-coverage/`.

## Acceptance

- One coverage report per supported language under `docs/research/canonical-coverage/<lang>.md`, regenerated by a task.
- Per-language coverage % is documented in each canonical map's source file header comment (`rs/ll-open/hdc/src/canonical/rust.rs` etc.).
- CI runs the report regeneration on every PR touching `rs/ll-open/hdc/src/canonical/` and fails if the snapshot drifts vs the regenerated output without an explicit doc update.

## Dependencies

Depends on parent epic. Sibling bead (capnp parity) is independent.

## Out of scope

- Cross-language transfer (Rust canonical map should NOT cover Go kinds; coverage is reported per-language)
- HDC encoder changes if coverage exposes gaps — that's its own bead per language
- HDC compositional surface (ADR-0025 Phase α-δ) — different axis entirely

title: Nothing enforces "every nodes.record writer invalidates the chunk manifest" — 4 sites were missed; make it structural
description:
Follow-up from the adversarial review of `feat/cdc-materialize-on-read` (2026-07-23). The four bugs it found are FIXED with falsifying regression tests; this bead is about the structural gap that let all four through at once.

## What happened

`chunked.rs` documents the invariant: `nodes.record` is authoritative, the chunk manifest is a derived index, and ANY writer of `record` must invalidate it or the chunked read path serves stale bytes. The invariant was enforced by hand at three call sites (`write_content`, `flush_node`, `batch_splice`'s AST branch) and silently missed at four others:

- `truncate` — silent no-op for chunk-backed nodes (verified: returned 5 bytes after truncate)
- `remove_node` — CROSS-GENERATION CONTENT LEAK. Node ids are PATHS and paths get reused, so an orphaned manifest attaches to whatever node is created at that path next. Verified: write "secret-old-bytes" -> remove_node -> create_node(same path) -> read returns "secret-old-bytes" on a brand-new, never-written file.
- `batch_splice` non-AST arm — both the update and delete sub-arms write `nodes` directly; the post-reproject invalidation loop walks `_ast`-derived ids so it structurally cannot see them
- `rename_node` — manifest keyed by old id with no FK, orphans onto the vacated path

All four now fixed + tested (`truncate_invalidates_the_chunk_manifest`, `recreating_a_removed_path_does_not_leak_the_old_content`, `removing_a_directory_invalidates_descendant_manifests`, `batch_splice_plain_node_arm_invalidates`, `rename_does_not_orphan_a_manifest_on_the_vacated_path`) — each verified to FAIL when its fix is removed.

## Why it is still fragile

Correctness depends on a human remembering to add a call at every future write site. The next writer added to `graph.rs` reintroduces the same class of bug, and the failure mode is silent wrong data (or content disclosure), not an error.

## Options to make it structural (pick one, they are alternatives)

1. **Single choke point.** Route every `nodes` mutation through one `write_record(conn, id, Option<&str>)` / `delete_nodes(conn, id)` helper in `graph.rs` that invalidates as part of the same call. Then "forgot to invalidate" becomes "bypassed the helper", which is greppable and lintable.
2. **Push it into SQL.** `content_manifest.node_id` currently has no FK. Add `FOREIGN KEY(node_id) REFERENCES nodes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE` and enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`. Kills the remove/rename leaks at the storage layer (does NOT cover the update-in-place cases — truncate/record-update still need explicit invalidation). Note: the arena is `sqlite3_deserialize`d and portability of the pragma across the arena lifecycle needs checking.
3. **Freshness token.** Store the `size`+`mtime` the manifest was built from and have `has_chunked_content` compare against the node row, so a stale manifest fails CLOSED (falls back to `record`) instead of serving bytes. Costs one small indexed read per read; covers every writer including ones outside this crate, which options 1 and 2 do not.

Option 3 is the only one that also defends against a writer in another crate (leyline-ts already writes `record` directly), which is why the current design needs `flush_node`/`batch_splice` invalidation at all.

## Coverage gap that hid it

`task mutants` scopes `cargo mutants` to `ll-open/cdc/src/lib.rs` + `ll-open/fs/src/chunked.rs`. `graph.rs` is deliberately out of scope (~1900 lines of pre-existing untested surface would swamp the gate — see the Taskfile comment). So mutants verified `invalidate_chunked_content`'s BODY while nothing verified that `graph.rs` CALLS it at each write site. Consider a narrowly-scoped mutation run over just the write-path functions in `graph.rs` (`cargo mutants --re` can filter by function name) rather than the whole file.

comments.text: Reconciled against merged main e35697e. Option 3 is implemented structurally: content_manifest_meta records source_len/source_mtime transactionally; has_chunked_content joins against live nodes and fails closed; an_unknown_writer_cannot_cause_stale_bytes_to_be_served and equal-length rewrite tests prove external/unaware writers fall back to nodes.record. The code explicitly documents that every graph invalidation call can be removed without correctness failure; mutation gates passed in PR #265 (fs: 65 caught, 4 unviable, 0 missed; CDC: 57 caught, 7 unviable, 9 timeouts, 0 missed). Explicit invalidation remains only for storage hygiene and has its own deletion/cascade pins. Acceptance is satisfied; closing as already shipped rather than duplicating a solved abstraction.

title: Add reachability GC and storage accounting for CDC chunks
description: Production CDC activation makes content_chunks long-lived. Current invalidation deletes manifest rows but deliberately retains every historical chunk forever; module docs say a reachability sweep is required before a long-lived writable mount. Add explicit transactional GC over chunks unreachable from content_manifest plus dry-run/storage accounting. Preserve chunks shared by any live manifest and keep GC off the write hot path. The production command should be safe to rerun and report reclaimed rows/bytes.

title: Re-key the review restriction on node_hash / stable container identity (deployment precondition) [was f38a86]
description:
ADR-0031 caveat #1 / deployment precondition. The restriction-addressed review-cache experiment (rs/ll-open/sheaf/tests/restriction_review_real.rs, on main via #240) keys review restrictions by container NAME (fn:score), not the daemon's positional node_id. A positional container id shifts on any line change above F → restriction degenerates to whole-file sensitivity (stays sound, loses true-skips). Fix: key on stable, reflow-invariant identity — ADR-0027 node_hash. Also graduate the restriction/review/oracle logic from the test into a reusable sheaf module so the git-replay + second-family beads build on it. Proof fixture: an edit inserting lines ABOVE F (F byte-identical) must NOT invalidate F's call-target restriction. Keep the 9 original fixtures green. Honest outcome allowed: if node_hash keying needs cmd_parse/daemon integration a sheaf test can't reach, report the exact interface. IN PROGRESS (agent bead-f38a86 running; recreated after beads.db reset lost id f38a86).

Verification: cargo test -p leyline-sheaf --test restriction_review_real (above-F fixture + 9 originals green); task ci.

comments.text:
Executed (was f38a86). Branch `worktree-agent-a7903e770a63df777`, commit `da5b41d`. NOT pushed, no PR. task ci green (fmt first), EXIT=0.

## Stable-identity approach used
Local stable node_hash-style STAND-IN, not the real cmd_parse fold (which is not reachable from a sheaf test — see integration gap below). The container identity is a bottom-up merkle fold in ADR-0027's exact shape (hash_leaf/hash_internal: domain ‖ tag ‖ uvarint(len(kind)) ‖ kind ‖ token/child-hashes, source order, spans OUT) computed over F's SIGNATURE subtree (function_item minus its `body` block).

Two things had to be true, and only signature-scoping gives both:
- reflow/position-invariant (node_hash property) → survives insert-above;
- BODY-invariant → the whole-function node_hash changes on ANY body edit, which would kill the headline body-only true-skips (local-rename, body-arith). Excluding the body block keeps those skips while still invalidating on a signature change. This is a real finding: the container key must be the node_hash of the function's DECLARATION/signature node, NOT the whole function_item.

## Above-F fixture: RED → GREEN (measured)
New test `stable_identity_survives_insert_above`: insert a new import + comment + whole new fn ABOVE `score`, `score` byte-identical.
- RED (temporarily forced Stable→positional id): FAILED at "stable node_hash keying must survive insert-above and skip soundly" — positional container id shifts function_item_0 → function_item_1, restriction hash changes, cache wastefully recomputes (ADR-0031 caveat-#1 whole-file degeneration).
- GREEN (real signature node_hash): PASS. Oracle confirms score's resolved call graph unchanged, so the skip is sound. Positional keying is asserted RED in the same test (`!restriction_unchanged(Positional)`).

## 9 original fixtures stay green under Stable keying
Verdict now runs under ContainerKeying::Stable (the deployment-sound identity), reproducing ADR-0031 exactly:
```
policy          false_skip_rate  true_skip_rate  recompute_saved
WholeObject                0/4             0/5                 0
AstShape                   4/4             4/5                 4  (ADR-0030 blind spot)
Restriction                0/4             5/5                 5
```
local-rename + body-arith: sound SKIP (restriction unchanged, review confirmed unchanged) while WholeObject recomputes. callee-swap / import-path / qualifier-swap / corpus-def-rename: correctly recompute. Cost test green (restriction 6 rows vs review 400→20k; cheaper wall-time at scale).

## Module surface exposed for f3a81e / f463aa
`leyline_sheaf::restriction_cache` (pub, parser-INDEPENDENT, ships in production — zero leyline-ts dep):
- rows: DefRow, RefRow, ImportRow
- FactSubstrate::from_rows(defs, refs, imports, container_by_fn) + container_for_fn(name)
- ContainerKeying { Name, Positional, Stable }
- restriction_for_call_target(sub, container, &mut rows_touched) -> [u8;32]
- review_call_targets(sub, container, &mut rows_touched) -> BTreeSet<ResolvedEdge>; ResolvedEdge
- whole_object_hash(corpus) -> [u8;32]
- Policy, FixtureResult, PolicyStats, stats
Parser-dependent extraction lives in tests/common/mod.rs (dev/bench shared): build_substrate(corpus, keying), ast_shape_hash, the node_hash fold. f3a81e (git-replay bench) and f463aa (second review family) reuse the src module + build_substrate without duplication.

## Integration gap (precise, for the follow-up)
The real ADR-0027 node_hash is computed by cmd_parse's `fold_children` (cli-lib), which depends on leyline-sheaf — so a sheaf test CANNOT call the production node_hash without a dependency inversion. The fold also produces node_hash per NAMED NODE; the container key needs the node_hash of the function's DECLARATION node specifically (whole function_item is body-sensitive). Two documented stand-in deviations in restriction_cache.rs / tests/common:
1. SHA-256 (sheaf's hash) not BLAKE3 — the container id is an opaque string; only reflow/body invariance matters for the experiment.
2. raw tree-sitter node.kind() not TsLanguage::canonical_kind (κ canonicalization is in leyline-ts).

What the daemon-side deploy needs (f38a86-follow-up interface): the fold already emits a node_hash for every named node onto _ast/node_content. To re-key the live restriction, expose the node_hash of the function's declaration/signature node (or add a signature-scoped node_hash to the fold) and store it as the node_refs container identity in place of the positional container_node_id. No new hashing primitive is required — hash_leaf/hash_internal already exist in cmd_parse; the change is (a) hash the declaration subtree not the whole function_item, and (b) thread that hash as the container key. Leaving bead OPEN.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
GO — git-replay superset-correctness stress complete. restriction false_skip == 0 over 1786 real region-edits.

## What was built
New bench `rs/ll-open/sheaf/benches/restriction_git_replay.rs` (harness=false), mirroring the ADR-0030 rung-2 replay pattern (`git_replay_invalidation.rs`) but over the reusable `restriction_cache` module (PR #242) + `tests/common` extraction of the REAL `extract_rust` facts. Registered in `sheaf/Cargo.toml`. Extraction support added to `tests/common/mod.rs`: public `review_targets()` + `stable_container_id()` (container_id's Stable arm refactored onto it, DRY) so a driver resolves a specific function region to the Stable container id its refs are grouped under — the name-keyed `container_by_fn` collides across a multi-file corpus.

## Method
Replay N commits touching rs/. Each commit's changed .rs files (that parse on BOTH parent and commit) form a MULTI-FILE corpus, so `review_call_targets` resolves call targets ACROSS files — exercising the cross-object dependency the fixture `corpus-def-rename` proved load-bearing. Build FactSubstrate before/after under ContainerKeying::Stable; for every function_item region present on both sides whose OWN bytes changed (a real region-edit), compute restriction-changed? (`restriction_for_call_target`) vs review-changed? (`review_call_targets`, the oracle). Same-signature targets (Stable-id collision, refs merge) excluded so each unit is exactly one function.

## Corpus + N (measured, RESTR_N_COMMITS=600)
- 577 commits touching rs/ scanned; 510 multi-file commit-corpora measured
- **1786 real region-edits** (>> the N>=400 bar)
- 1423 same-signature targets excluded (Stable body-invariant id collision — symmetric for restriction and review, so exclusion hides no gap)
- review CHANGED (oracle): 1034 | review UNCHANGED: 752

## Confusion matrix (restriction hash vs review oracle, Stable keying)
```
                        | review UNCHANGED  review CHANGED
  restriction UNCHANGED |            682             0     <- false_skip = 0
  restriction CHANGED   |             70          1034
```
- **restriction false_skip = 0** (false_skip_rate = 0/1034 = 0.0000)
- restriction true_skip = 682 (true_skip_rate = 682/752 = 90.7% of review-unchanged edits)
- wasted_inval (over-invalidation, sound) = 70
- true_inval = 1034
- **WholeObject true_skip = 0** by construction (the corpus always holds a changed file) — restriction recovers 682 sound skips WholeObject cannot, at 0 false-skips.

## Outcome
Zero false-skips over 1786 real region-edits => `restriction-unchanged ⇒ review-output-unchanged` SURVIVES replay. The ADR-0031 positive claim (rung-2 analog) holds on real edits, not just the 9 fixtures. No missed dependency found; nothing engineered away.

Scope note (honest): the unit is a region-edit (F's own bytes changed), over a per-commit multi-file corpus. The pure cross-file-def-rename class (F byte-identical, only a callee def in another file renamed) is out of this replay's region-edit population and remains fixture-covered (corpus-def-rename). Sweep the finding with RESTR_N_COMMITS higher if a broader corpus is wanted.

- sig-typedef-rename (Widget->Panel in math.rs ONLY; score's file byte-identical)  review_changed  Restriction RECOMPUTE  <- multi-object span across node_defs

title: TS extraction: establish whether 0day's 21:1 ref:def ratio is legitimate or an algebra gap — non-function const bindings emit no def
description:
Reported from 0day (their bead 0day-c904b5 holds the honesty rule: symbol edges come from node_defs/node_refs or not at all): on 0day's own TypeScript, mache sees node_defs=102 vs node_refs=2,165 (21:1). Go-heavy repos do not look like that. Either most refs point at external modules (exactly what cross-repo edges want) or TS def extraction is shallower than Go's — and symbol edges resting on the second case give plausible-looking partial coverage, worse than none.

Triage (2026-07-29, verified against queries/typescript/tags.scm): TS def coverage is NOT naively shallow — 10 def patterns incl. arrow/function-expression assignments, method_definition, interface/type-alias/enum/abstract-class. But variable_declarator with a NON-function value emits no def: const FOO = 42, const config = {...}, const schema = z.object({...}) — module-scoped constant bindings, a large share of a modern TS repo's referenced symbol surface (0day is TS+zod-heavy, so schema consts alone could account for much of the unmatched-ref mass). Same family as ley-line-open-651909 (Go package-level consts emit no defs; qualified selector args emit no refs).

Work, in order:
1. MEASURE before fixing: on a real TS fixture (or 0day's own tree), decompose the 2,165 refs — (a) tokens resolving to an _imports alias (external, legitimate), (b) tokens matching a const-bound name that WOULD be a def under the extended algebra (the gap), (c) neither (investigate). This decides how much of 21:1 each explanation owns; put the numbers on this bead.
2. If (b) is material: add non-function variable_declarator defs to typescript/javascript tags.scm — κ 'constant' for const, 'variable' for let/var, module-scope reasoning mirrors Go's (they join cleanly, unlike SQL's bare columns). Pin with refs.rs fixtures; EXTRACTION_EPOCH bump.
3. Tell 0day the decomposition either way — c904b5's rule stays: edges from node_defs/node_refs only, never a parser in tools/graph.

If Go sits far lower, the TS gap is real and material.

title: CI attestation hashes .beads/beads.jsonl, so filing a bead during task ci destroys the run — the receipt's scope is wrong, not its mechanism
description:
Filed 2026-07-29 after this cost three full `task ci` runs in one session —
twice after I had described the trap in detail and then walked into it anyway.
That is not a knowledge problem; it is a design that punishes a workflow the
repo itself requires.

## What happens

`ci_snapshot()` hashes the whole tree:

    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$temporary_index" git read-tree HEAD
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$temporary_index" git add -A -- .
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$temporary_index" git write-tree

`.beads/beads.jsonl` is TRACKED, so it is in that hash. rsry rewrites it on
every bead create/update/comment — by me, or by any other agent working the
shared checkout. So any bead written between `begin` and `finish` produces:

    repository or CI contract changed during task ci; refusing attestation

The run's tests all pass; only the attestation refuses. ~8 minutes discarded,
and the natural thing to do while waiting for a build is exactly the thing that
destroys it.

## The mechanism is right; the SCOPE is wrong

Worth separating, because the mechanism deserves defending:

- it writes to a `GIT_INDEX_FILE` temp index in a subshell with `set -eu` and a
  trap, so it never touches the real staging area
- `read-tree HEAD` + `add -A` = "HEAD plus working-tree changes", which is the
  correct thing to certify
- `add -A` is far safer here than it looks: this repo's `.gitignore` is
  deny-all (`*` + `!` allowlist), so untracked strays are ignored rather than
  swept in. Verified incidentally — `git check-ignore -v probe_tmp.rs` returns
  `.gitignore:3:*`.

The defect is that the receipt claims "task ci passed for this TREE" when what
it should claim is "for these INPUTS". A file CI never reads does not belong in
that hash.

## Verified: beads is not a CI input

    $ grep -rn "\.beads" Taskfile.yml tools/*.sh .github/workflows/*.yml \
        | grep -v ci_attestation
    (no matches)

And `task ci` runs only `*:check` / `*-check` / `*fixture-test` variants — never
`compat:gen` or `gen:server-json`. So **no CI task writes any tracked file**,
and `.beads/beads.jsonl` is the only tracked path that moves mid-run.
`compatibility.json` and `server.json` are tracked and regenerable, but CI only
ever compares them.

## Fix

One pathspec:

    git add -A -- . ':(exclude).beads/beads.jsonl'

Narrow on purpose — that one path, not `.beads/`, and emphatically not a
general "tolerate churn" mode. Anything else moving mid-run must still refuse;
that behaviour caught a genuinely concurrent edit earlier today and is the
reason the gate is worth having.

## The part that keeps it honest

The exclusion rests on a checkable claim — "no CI task reads this path" — so it
must carry a test asserting that claim, in `tools/test_ci_attestation.sh`:

1. a bead write during a run no longer invalidates the receipt;
2. a source edit during a run STILL does;
3. **no `task ci` subtask reads `.beads/`** — if a future gate starts consuming
   the bead ledger, the exclusion silently becomes a hole, and that must fail
   loudly instead.

Without (3) this is an exclusion justified by a fact nobody re-checks, which is
the same shape as every other defect found this week.

## Related

`ley-line-open-2607d2` (assert the mechanism fired), and the wider point that a
gate people route around has already failed — three discarded runs in one
session is the empirical form of that.

title: Σ Phase 2 (minimal): impl ContentAddressed for [u8] — unblocks Group A retrofit
description:
## Context

Phase 0+1 (bead `ley-line-open-e7b983`, PR #47) shipped characterization tests + audit for the 4 Group A inline `blake3::hash` sites. Phase 2 is the minimal-viable substrate impl that unblocks Phase 3 migration of those sites.

## Scope correction from the audit

The original ladder said "Phase 2: implement `MemBlobStore` + `WholeFileBlobStore`." Re-reading the substrate trait surface (`rs/ll-core/core/src/substrate.rs`):

- `BlobStore::put(&[u8]) -> Hash` requires **(IM)** axiom — "once `get(h)` returns `Some(_)`, it returns `Some(_)` forever." (substrate.rs:135-138)
- The arena is a **single-slot byte buffer** addressed by `current_root`. After `put(v2)`, `get(h1)` returns None because the buffer is now v2.
- **The arena does NOT satisfy `BlobStore`.** A `WholeFileBlobStore` impl as I'd originally sketched would violate the trait's documented axioms.

The arena is actually the "root pointer's underlying buffer" — closer to a `RootPointer` impl shape than a `BlobStore`. The true multi-blob `BlobStore` is `FsBlobStore` (bead `ley-line-open-bb0316`, separate, pending).

What Group A retrofit ACTUALLY needs from the substrate trait surface is just the σ function:

```rust
let new_root = bytes.hash();  // ContentAddressed::hash via [u8] impl
ctrl.set_arena_with_root(&arena_path, size, *new_root.as_bytes())?;
```

So Phase 2's minimal viable form: ship `impl ContentAddressed for [u8]`. Done.

## Deliverables (this bead)

1. `impl ContentAddressed for [u8]` in `rs/ll-core/core/src/substrate.rs` (or sibling module).
   - The existing trait docstring at line 122-123 already promises this impl ("The default impl for `[u8]` and `Vec<u8>` hashes the raw bytes via BLAKE3") — this fulfills existing design intent.
2. Conformance tests pinning:
   - `bytes.hash().as_bytes() == &blake3::hash(bytes).as_bytes()` byte-for-byte (so Phase 3 migration is bit-exact)
   - Determinism (DET) across instances
   - Empty input — `(&[]).hash()` returns canonical BLAKE3-of-empty (not `Hash::ZERO`)
   - Roundtrip with `Hash::from_bytes` / `as_bytes`

## NOT in scope (separate beads)

- `MemBlobStore` impl — useful for future multi-blob work but not needed for Group A. **Defer to a sibling bead** filed alongside the eventual `FsBlobStore` work (`ley-line-open-bb0316`).
- `WholeFileBlobStore` impl — wrong abstraction (see scope correction above). Don't file; document the finding.
- `RootSigner` impl (signet integration) — Phase 5 in the original ladder; separate bead.
- Migration of the 4 Group A sites — that's Phase 3 (next bead).

## Audit constraints respected

- **F2** (substrate.rs:28-50 BLAKE3 lock): `impl ContentAddressed for [u8]` uses `blake3::hash(self)`. Algorithm stays baked.
- **F3** (separate write from publish): Phase 2 only ships the σ (hash) function. Publish (controller-side `set_arena_with_root`) stays as a separate call at the migration sites. The trait's `BlobStore::put` is NOT what we use here — we use `ContentAddressed::hash` directly.
- **F4** (empty buffer accept): the impl handles `hash(&[])` correctly (BLAKE3-of-empty is `af1349b9...`, not zero); migration sites that compare against zero sentinel keep that branch.

## Tracks

- Parent: `ley-line-open-e7b983` (Phase 0+1, in PR #47)
- Unblocks: this bead's PR + Phase 3 migration bead (to be filed once this lands)
- Downstream: `ley-line-open-dffb77` (the "me" repo) — substrate trait surface becomes load-bearing once Group A migrates

title: Canonicalize leyline-net wire frames in LLO — ToolCall/ToolResult/Manifest capnp so cloister + rosary vendor from upstream
description:
The leyline-net frame format (length-prefixed Manifest + ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD envelope + ToolCall/ToolResult payloads, AD-bound manifest) is spec'd in cloister/wire/cloister.capnp (cloister ADR-0005) and VENDORED by rosary as schemas/cloister.capnp (rosary-6371e3, build.rs capnpc codegen for `rsry mcp --ipc-socket`). Verified 2026-07-15: LLO has no copy — schema-capnp holds ast/binding/cache/head/source/common, public-schema holds daemon/cache, schema-spec holds _traits + capability specs. A leyline-named substrate protocol currently has its canonical copy in a cloister subdirectory, and rosary re-vendors from there in lockstep by hand.

Per ADR-0035 ("leyline-* names belong in LLO") and the leyline-sign / leyline-schema-spec lift precedents:
- Split cloister/wire/cloister.capnp: the GENERIC wire frames (Manifest, ToolCall, ToolResult, frame layout + AEAD binding rules) move to LLO (rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/net.capnp or a new leyline-net spec dir under schema-spec with pinned test vectors, matching the VECTORS.sha256 discipline); cloister-deployment-specific structs stay in cloister/wire.
- Exact-pin capnp toolchain discipline applies (LLO ADR-0014 — canonical bytes must not move under consumers).
- Downstream (separate beads at PR time): cloister repoints wire/cloister.capnp to import/extend upstream; rosary re-vendors schemas/cloister.capnp from LLO instead of cloister (rosary follow-up bead depends on this landing).
- Ship cross-runtime test vectors so the Rust (rosary), TS (cloister), and companion sides prove byte-equality against the same pinned frames.

The load-bearing cross-runtime bytes are the canonical struct encodings.

Cross-runtime vector anchor exists: cloister/wire/cross-check-fixtures.capnp defines 12 consts; test/wire/fixtures/canonical.ts pins their `capnp eval -b` bytes, validated by cloister's hand-rolled TS codec + Go bindings. I regenerated all 12 via `capnp eval -I .. --no-standard-import wire/cross-check-fixtures.capnp <const> -b` — byte-identical to canonical.ts. These are the golden frames.

Encoding-form finding (empirically verified with capnp =0.25.0 against the CURRENT cloister schema): `capnp eval -b` reference bytes are NOT strict canonical form for 9/12 values — set_root_canonical truncates trailing zero data/pointer words (e.g. tool-call-empty 56B→48B, tool-result-empty 40B→32B). Cloister's own cross-check tests state value-equivalence, not byte-equivalence, across encoders. Consequence: LLO pins BOTH forms per value — reference/ (byte-equal to cloister's pinned fixtures; proves compatibility with what TS+Go validate today) and canonical/ (set_root_canonical form, LLO's T8.10 fixture discipline; baseline digests captured from the cloister schema pre-split so the split is provably byte-neutral in both encodings).

(c) Tests in schema-capnp: digest-pinned consistency (hardcoded BLAKE3/SHA-256, fail-loud on frame edits), encode-canonical byte-equality, decode-direction field equality against reference bytes, capnp-eval byte-equality via an LLO fixtures.capnp, and a skip-if-missing cross-repo gate against the live cloister schema (build_cache_vectors_consistency pattern).

title: cargo-mutants gates every PR on a fixed 3-file CDC allowlist, so its green light says nothing about the PR
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while asking why PR #288 spent the day waiting on mutants.

## The defect

`task mutants` is a hardcoded allowlist, not a diff scope:

    mutants:cdc     -> leyline-cdc
    mutants:fs      -> --file ll-open/fs/src/chunked.rs
    mutants:fs-gc   -> --file ll-open/fs/src/gc.rs

PR #288 changed `outputs/zod.rs`, `ll-core/mcp-descriptor/**`, and tests.
**None of those are in the allowlist.** mutants ran, passed, and its result
carried zero information about the PR — while being the slowest check on it.

That is the same shape as the rest of #288: a mechanism reporting success
without doing the work anyone reading it would assume. A reviewer seeing
"cargo mutants: pass" reasonably concludes the PR's new logic survived
mutation testing. It was never mutated.

It is also not a required check, so it never gated merge — a day was spent
waiting on a signal that was neither blocking nor relevant.

## Fix

Two scopes, two triggers:

1. **PR gate** — `cargo mutants --in-diff <merge-base diff>` (supported,
   verified on cargo-mutants 27.1.0: `-D, --in-diff <IN_DIFF>`). Mutates only
   changed lines, so cost scales with the diff and the result is about the PR.
2. **Standing invariants** — keep the CDC allowlist, move it to a push-to-main
   or nightly run. Those files encode invariants worth continuous coverage,
   but they are not what a given PR changed.

Keep the command in the Taskfile; `mutants.yml` already just calls
`task mutants` and must keep doing so.

## The trap — do not ship this without it

`--in-diff` on a PR that touches only tests, docs, or YAML generates **zero
mutants**, and cargo-mutants exits 0. "0 mutants, 0 missed" renders as a
green check indistinguishable from "every mutant was caught".

That would replace one vacuous signal with a subtler one. The task MUST
distinguish the two: log the generated-mutant count, and make zero-generated
report as SKIPPED rather than PASSED. Assert the mechanism fired — a mutation
gate that mutated nothing has not verified anything.

## Acceptance criteria

A PR touching only `outputs/zod.rs` generates and runs mutants for that file
and no CDC files; a PR touching only markdown reports skipped-no-mutants
rather than pass; the CDC allowlist still runs on main. Proven by checking
the mutant count in each case, not the exit code alone.

comments.text:
## Correcting this bead before implementing against it — the premise was wrong

I filed this claiming mutants "gates every PR on a fixed 3-file allowlist."
**It does not gate every PR.** `.github/workflows/mutants.yml` is paths-filtered:

    paths:
      - 'rs/ll-open/cdc/**'
      - 'rs/ll-open/fs/src/chunked.rs'
      - 'rs/ll-open/fs/src/gc.rs'
      - 'Taskfile.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/mutants.yml'

Measured across the last five PRs:

    PR     touched Taskfile.yml    mutants ran
    #296   no                      no
    #295   yes                     yes
    #294   no                      no
    #293   no                      no
    #288   yes                     yes

Perfect correlation. The filter behaves exactly as designed. I inferred
"every PR" from seeing mutants on #288 and #289 without checking why, which is
the same not-verifying-the-premise error I have been flagging in other people's
reasoning all session.

The `Taskfile.yml` trigger is also NOT a bug: editing the `mutants:*` task
definitions should re-verify the gate still runs. That is a legitimate reason
to fire.

## What the actual, much smaller defect is

On a PR that touches BOTH `Taskfile.yml` and unrelated source (#288 changed
`Taskfile.yml`, `outputs/zod.rs`, and `mcp-descriptor`), the check runs, passes,
and renders as:

    cargo mutants (task mutants)   pass

A reader reasonably concludes the PR's new logic survived mutation testing. It
was never mutated — the run covered `leyline-cdc`, `chunked.rs` and `gc.rs`,
none of which the PR touched.

So the defect is **the check's name does not say what it covers**, not that it
runs when it shouldn't or wastes time on every PR. Both of those were wrong.

## Rescoped fix

1. **Rename the check** so its result cannot be over-read — e.g.
   `cargo mutants (CDC + chunked path)`. Cheapest, and fixes the actual
   misreading.
2. **Optionally** add `--in-diff` scoping for runs triggered by SOURCE changes,
   so a PR touching `chunked.rs` mutates its own diff rather than the whole
   file. Genuinely useful, but a smaller win than I claimed and NOT a
   correctness fix.
3. If (2) lands, the zero-mutants case must report **skipped**, not passed —
   `--in-diff` on a Taskfile-only change generates nothing and exits 0, which
   would be a new vacuous green replacing the old one.

Note the tension (2) creates and (1) does not: when the Taskfile's mutants
commands themselves change, `--in-diff` would mutate nothing, losing exactly
the "does the gate still work" check that trigger exists for. So (2) needs two
modes, and may not be worth it.

Downgrading priority accordingly. The misleading NAME is real; the
"gates every PR" cost was not.

title: leyline daemon has no admission control; two can run on same arena + idle daemon spins CPU
description:
LLO's `leyline daemon` has no mutex on the arena it mounts. Two processes can concurrently run `leyline daemon --arena PATH` and both succeed, resulting in two daemons sharing the same arena file + mount + control socket.

*This bead was re-filed after the original (`ley-line-open-569beb`) was lost when the rsry MCP server reconnected mid-session 2026-07-07.*

## Observed in the wild

Process list during profile of v0.5.9 cold-parse showed both:

- PID 86814 (Sat 12PM, 255min total CPU, **16.7% CPU right now while idle**) mounted at `/Users/jamesgardner/.mache/default.arena`
- PID 19752 (today 12:23PM, 4min CPU, 1% CPU) mounted at the same arena

Also 2× `mache serve --control` processes downstream (one per daemon — mache correctly starts one control server per leyline it observes; not a mache bug).

**Auto-respawn observed**: killing PID 86814 caused a fresh daemon (PID 33327) to spawn within seconds — some mache-serve session detects the daemon down and respawns. Without admission control, there is no upper bound on daemons.

## Two bugs, one bead

### A. No admission control (primary)

`leyline daemon --arena X` startup should refuse or no-op if another daemon holds X. Three implementation options:

1. **Advisory lockfile**: `fcntl F_SETLK` / `flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` on `<arena>.lock`. Fail-fast if held. Simplest, correct.
2. **Control-socket-ping**: connect to `--control` socket; if a live daemon answers, refuse to start (idempotent "start" semantics). Friendlier to `task install` / rerun UX because subsequent invocations become no-ops.
3. **PID lockfile**: `<arena>.pid`; fail if PID alive. Vulnerable to PID reuse, weaker than (1).

Recommend **(1) + (2) together**: (1) as the correctness gate, (2) as the ergonomic layer that returns "already running, PID <n>" instead of a raw lock error.

### B. Idle-daemon CPU spin (secondary)

The Saturday PID 86814 has been running ~2 days and consumes 16.7% CPU right now while no queries are active. Design intent is idle daemon → near-zero CPU. Root-cause TBD; likely candidates:

- Mount health-check loop with too-tight sleep
- WAL checkpoint polling
- Indexer queue drain in a hot loop
- Subscribe/event-relay task busy-looping (v0.5.7 keepalive path?)

## Design intent (user-confirmed)

Single global daemon per arena IS the correct design. The current implementation just doesn't ENFORCE it — naive spawn without admission control.

## Provenance

Discovered 2026-07-07 during profiling of v0.5.9 cold-parse; multiple daemons caused I/O contention that contaminated the samply profile with false hot spots. See ir-producer-7ed023 session for the `ps aux` + `iostat` data that surfaced it.

## Close condition / acceptance

- `leyline daemon --arena X` refuses (or no-ops) when another daemon holds arena X — new integration test spawns two daemons and asserts the second exits cleanly with a clear error naming the holding PID
- Idle-daemon CPU < 1% over a 60s sample after startup (regression test)
- `task ci` green including new tests

Wired into `run_daemon` as step 0, before any arena/db work. Six unit tests cover acquire/release/PID-in-error/lockfile-cleanup semantics.

Sub-problem B (idle-daemon CPU spin) NOT addressed here — root cause TBD. Filing separately since it's distinct investigation work with a different fix surface.

Closing this bead (admission control complete). New bead follows for the idle CPU work.

title: WAL 15a adversarial: ENOSPC during snapshot + WAL bloat when checkpoint fails
description:
Filed 2026-07-08. Remaining adversarial coverage from bead `ley-line-open-fd07d8` § "WAL 15a" that PR #144 didn't ship. Split into its own bead so momentum on load-bearing work isn't blocked; these are legitimate follow-ups with infrastructure cost.

## Two tests needed

### 1. ENOSPC during snapshot

**Claim:** if the daemon runs out of disk space during `snapshot_to_arena`, it fails loud without corrupting the existing arena.

**Infrastructure needed:** a filesystem-mock helper that returns ENOSPC on a specific write. Options:

- Use `libc::setrlimit` to set `RLIMIT_FSIZE` = current file size, causing next write to fail
- Use a size-capped tmpfs mount (macOS: `hdiutil` to create a tiny disk image; Linux: `mount -t tmpfs -o size=1M`)
- Mock the filesystem layer entirely (invasive; probably wrong for one test)

Recommend `RLIMIT_FSIZE` — no external dep, per-process, standard POSIX.

**Assert:**

- `snapshot_to_arena` returns Err with a message mentioning `ENOSPC` / `No space` / `disk full` / `file size limit`
- Existing arena file is untouched (compare pre/post byte hash)
- Existing `.live.db` file is untouched (fsync-per-blob durability contract from F2 says already-committed data survives)

### 2. WAL bloat with checkpoint disabled

**Claim:** if the daemon's `wal_autocheckpoint=0` (deliberately disabled), the WAL can grow unbounded. Startup after a crash/kill must still recover cleanly regardless of WAL size.

**Test method:**

- Boot daemon with a modified config that sets `wal_autocheckpoint=0` (add a test-only escape hatch or use `PRAGMA` after startup)
- Perform enough writes to grow the WAL to N MB (candidate: 100 MB — enough to prove no size-based checkpoint kicks in)
- SIGKILL the daemon (simulate crash before any manual checkpoint)
- Restart, assert daemon boots + `journal_mode="wal"` + writes are recovered from the bloated WAL

**Note:** the substrate default remains `wal_autocheckpoint=1000` (per PR #143). This test verifies the degenerate case, not that we ship it.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change the production `wal_autocheckpoint=1000` default
- Do NOT implement a size-based emergency checkpoint (that's a separate design question)
- Do NOT add generic disk-full injection framework — solve just enough for these two tests

## Close condition

Both tests in `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/wal_live_db_test.rs` (extend the existing file). `task ci` green including both.

## Provenance

- Parent gate bead: `ley-line-open-fd07d8` (adversarial testing sweep)
- Parent work: `ley-line-open-98fb67` sub-bead 15a shipped in PR #143 + PR #144
- Split from fd07d8 because ENOSPC needs infrastructure and WAL bloat needs a test-only config hatch — both are legitimate follow-up scope

title: confinement/v1 cannot express outbound-to-localhost — the proxy channel the spec assumes
description:
Found while validating whether §6 and the nono connect-only fix (ley-line-open-e41717) are complementary. They are — and the pair still leaves a hole, in the SPEC rather than in any mechanism.

confinement/v1's five dimensions are fs, network.allowHosts, port.bind, credentialSource, unixSocket. §4 is the BIND direction. §3 is HOSTNAME egress, refused on this tier because nono filters by port not host. Nothing names 'connect to localhost:8443'.

That matters because the spec assumes the proxy pattern in its own refusal text — §3 says 'route host-scoped egress through the proxy', §5 says 'vend credentials through the proxy' — while providing no way to express the channel TO that proxy. An LLO-executed workload on LINUX needing a local proxy today has: §6 refused (Landlock ABI), §3 refused (hostname), §4 the wrong direction. Nothing.

BOTH MECHANISMS EXIST AND ARE MEASURED:
  - Linux: AccessNet::ConnectTcp, landlock-0.4.5/src/net.rs:49, available ABI V4+ (from_all V4..V7). nono targets ABI 5, so it is in range now.
  - macOS: (allow network-outbound (remote tcp "localhost:N")) — measured working with network-bind ABSENT, on macOS 26.6 via sandbox-exec. Four cases with a passing control; see ley-line-open-e41717.

So unlike §4 (Linux-only) and §6 (macOS-only at current ABI), an outbound-localhost dimension would have NO PLATFORM SPLIT. That is directly relevant to ADR-0036 O3, whose whole subject is a grant needing per-platform digests because the channel dimensions disagree: this one would not.

RELATIONSHIP TO §6, so this is not read as replacing it. Complementary, not alternative:
  - transport: §6 needs a workload that dials AF_UNIX; this needs nothing of the client. Cloister's stock harnesses are TCP-only and cannot use §6 (their measurement).
  - identity: a UDS path is filesystem-named and permissioned; a loopback port is whoever bound it first. §6 is the STRONGER primitive where the transport allows it, and should stay the recommended form.
  - platform: §6 macOS-now/Linux-at-ABI-9; this both-now.

NOT PROPOSING THE SPEC CHANGE HERE — that is a v1-vs-v2 question (a sixth dimension is a breaking change for every consumer by design, per §1's exhaustive Dimensions struct) and it needs the operator. Filing the gap with the evidence so the decision is made on measurements rather than on the assumption that a proxy channel is already expressible. It is not.
acceptance_criteria: A manifest can name 'connect to localhost:N and nothing else', and it compiles to Landlock ConnectTcp on Linux and scoped network-outbound on macOS

title: Evaluate hotpath for LLO profiling — lock contention and async are the fit; its SQL support is sqlx/Diesel and LLO is rusqlite
description:
Filed 2026-07-28. Suggested by jamestexas. **Needs investigation — this bead
records what was checked, not a decision.**

## What it is (from https://hotpath.rs/, read rather than inferred)

`hotpath` — "an easy-to-configure Rust performance profiling toolkit that shows
exactly where your code spends time, burns CPU, and allocates memory." Covers
"CPU, memory, async execution, SQL and HTTP calls, I/O streams, lock contention
and channels from a single tool," and explicitly helps "distinguish between
functions that are slow because they wait on I/O and those that are
CPU-intensive."

- **Instrumentation, not sampling.** Decorators: `#[hotpath::measure]` on
  functions, `#[hotpath::main]` on entry points, `hotpath::measure_block!("name",
  { … })` for inline segments.
- **Feature-gated**, "zero cost when disabled" — flags `hotpath`,
  `hotpath-cpu`, `hotpath-alloc`.
- Installed via `cargo install hotpath --version '^0.22'`.

## The caveat that decides how useful this is

**Its SQL profiling is for `sqlx` and Diesel.** LLO uses **`rusqlite`**
(`rusqlite = "0.39.0"`, workspace deps). So the headline feature for a
SQLite-heavy repo does NOT apply out of the box.

That is worth stating up front because "profiles SQL queries" is the reason
this looks attractive for LLO, and it is the one part that would need
`measure_block!` wrapping by hand around rusqlite call sites — at which point
the value is the timing harness, not the SQL integration.

## Where it WOULD apply, and to which open question

Two LLO perf claims are currently unvalidated, and both are in hotpath's
remaining coverage:

1. **Lock contention.** LLO holds ~50 `parking_lot::Mutex` and 11 `RwLock`.
   `ley-line-open-f0239d` / `98fb67` propose `Mutex<Connection>` → a connection
   pool, claiming **~600× p99 read improvement**. That number is asserted in a
   bead, not measured here. Lock-contention profiling is the direct way to
   check it before committing to the change — and to check it AFTER, since a
   pool that does not actually reduce contention would leave the claim standing
   on nothing.

2. **Async / channel stalls.** `daemon/events.rs` runs a bounded (4096) tokio
   mpsc dispatch, and its own comment names the failure it guards: unbounded
   heap growth "if the dispatch loop ever stalled (e.g. on a contended
   `subscribers.write().await`)". On overflow it does `try_send` + `log::warn`
   and DROPS the event. So a consumer cannot distinguish "nothing happened"
   from "the channel was full" — the same silence-is-evidence problem noted
   elsewhere today. Measuring whether that stall is real, and how close to 4096
   the queue actually gets, would say whether the drop path is theoretical or
   routine.

## What investigation means here

- Confirm the license (the site does not state it) before adding a dependency.
- Confirm "zero cost when disabled" is genuinely zero — that it compiles out
  rather than leaving a no-op call — since the whole point of a feature-gated
  profiler is that the shipped build is unaffected. Verify, do not take the
  claim: this repo has already shipped one feature (`ley-line-open-918a75`)
  that was compiled out of every build while appearing wired.
- Decide whether wrapping rusqlite call sites in `measure_block!` is worth it
  versus a narrower purpose-built timer.
- Prefer a real question over adoption for its own sake: **start with f0239d's
  600× claim.** If hotpath can confirm or refute that, it has earned a place;
  if it cannot, this stays a curiosity.

## Related

`ley-line-open-f0239d`, `ley-line-open-98fb67` (WAL / connection pool),
`daemon/events.rs` bounded-channel drop path. Also the perf-gate fragility
noted 2026-07-28 (wall-clock ceiling rather than per-row) which was never
filed — a profiler does not fix a badly-shaped gate, and the two should not be
conflated.

title: Unify sheaf invalidation topic: daemon.sheaf.invalidate → sheaf.invalidate (Path A)
description:
Decision made 2026-07-08: Path A. Unify to the single topic `sheaf.invalidate`. Ship now, not later.

## Rationale

Same semantic event, source (consumer vs daemon) is provenance metadata that belongs in the payload if it belongs anywhere. Different topics for the same event class forces subscribers to double-subscribe or miss half the traffic.

## The fix

1. **LLO watcher emit** — `cmd_daemon.rs::emit_watcher_sheaf_invalidate` changes topic from `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` → `sheaf.invalidate`
2. **LLO tests** — update assertions in:
   - `sheaf_gap3_invalidate_emit_test.rs`
   - `sheaf_loop_end_to_end_test.rs`
   - any other file that checks for the old topic string
3. **Mache PR #500 (open)** — subscribes to both today; after LLO unifies, the `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` subscription becomes dead code but doesn't hurt. Follow-up mache PR can drop it.

## Backward-compat

- Existing consumers of `sheaf.invalidate` (from `op_sheaf_invalidate`) continue to work
- Mache PR #500 continues to work (subscribed to both)
- LLO's watcher emits now go to the same topic that existing consumers already listen on

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change the payload shape (still coarse-v1 fields per PR #140 + fine-grained per PR #146)
- Do NOT change consumer-driven `op_sheaf_invalidate` behavior
- Do NOT add a `source` field to the payload in this PR (deferred; can add if needed)

## Close condition

- LLO PR ships the topic change + test updates
- `task ci` green

title: daemon MCP surface implements a superseded handshake — 'initialize' + protocolVersion 2024-11-05 vs the pinned 2026-07-28 revision
description:

title: wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test::concurrent_readers_beat_pre_15b_mutex_shape flakes under workspace-parallel task ci load
description:
## Symptom

`concurrent_readers_beat_pre_15b_mutex_shape` (pin test for bead `ley-line-open-f0239d` WAL 15b — pool + writer split) intermittently fails during `task ci` with scale below the 3× floor:

Observed this session (2026-07-13):
- run 1: `scale=2.95×` (mutex=42107, pool=124076)
- run 2: `scale=2.06×` (mutex=60851, pool=125519)

Passes in isolation (`cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib --test wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test concurrent_readers_beat_pre_15b_mutex_shape` — debug OR release, hit rate 100%).

## Root cause

The assertion is `pool_reads / mutex_reads >= 3.0`. The **pool** number is stable (~124–125k across both fail runs — the pool shape works). The **mutex baseline** swings 40k → 60k → 90k depending on co-tenant CPU load during workspace-parallel test runs. When the mutex phase happens to hit a quiet moment, its throughput doubles and the ratio collapses below 3× — a pass/fail flip on pure co-tenant noise, not on any real change in the pool shape.

The test measures the wrong invariant: what the pool actually buys is "reads parallelize instead of serializing." A ratio against a wobbly baseline is contaminated by whatever else `cargo test --workspace` is scheduling.

## Fix (proposed)

`#[serial]` decorate the test — it's a wall-clock throughput comparison, and serial_test is already a workspace dev-dep. Excluding it from parallel workspace-test scheduling is legitimate (it's a perf test that needs isolation), not a band-aid. The 3-second wall-clock cost is a one-time hit in `task ci`.

Belt-and-suspenders: additionally add an absolute pool-floor assertion (`pool_reads >= 50_000` in 1.5s — well below the stable ~124k, above the ~40k mutex-shape a real regression would drop to) so a hypothetical pool regression to serialized behavior still fails loud even without the ratio.

## Verifiable close gate

`cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib --test wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test concurrent_readers_beat_pre_15b_mutex_shape` — must pass 5× in a row under `task ci` (workspace-parallel) load, not just in isolation. Loop:

```
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do task ci || exit 1; done
```

## Files

- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test.rs` (add `#[serial]` decoration + absolute floor)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/Cargo.toml` (already has `serial_test` per bead `ley-line-open-*sheaf_ablation*`; confirm)

title: Ship apko + melange in-repo for ley-line-open OCI image
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from cloister's deployment-readiness audit.

## What needs to happen

cloister's deployment topology (`~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp`) doesn't currently declare a ley-line-open bundle as a sibling container — today llo is reached via `LLO_MCP_URL` (external HTTP service, not a bundle in the cluster). But the cluster substrate (ADR-0009 + cluster-be0607) could absorb llo as a sibling bundle the same way it absorbs mache + rosary — IF llo has an in-repo apko/melange that produces a runnable OCI image.

ley-line-open currently has NO apko/melange. This bead is the work to add one.

## Architectural context (from the cloister side)

- llo is a **userspace FS optional projection** + memory arena. No FUSE kernel deps required. The image should be a plain subprocess container.
- The cloister-side wire to llo today is HTTP at `LLO_MCP_URL`. Eventually that should migrate to capnp-over-UDS to match mache + rosary (per ADR-0005 amendment — "cloister ↔ sibling bundles is plain capnp IPC inside the trust boundary"). This bead is the IMAGE-build piece; the wire migration is separate work.

## Scope

1. **Add `apko.yaml` + `melange.yaml` at the repo root**. Reference patterns:
   - `~/remotes/art/notme/packages/{apko-notme.yaml,melange-*.yaml}` (worker-bundle style)
   - `~/remotes/art/rosary/{apko.yaml,melange.yaml}` (Rust subprocess style — closer match for llo)
   - `~/remotes/art/cloister/{apko.yaml,melange.yaml}` (workerd Worker bundle)

2. **Add `Taskfile.yml` `task image` target**: `melange build` → `apko build` → produces tagged OCI artifact. Pin a version (e.g. `ley-line-open:0.1.0`).

3. **Verify the image runs**: `docker run ley-line-open:0.1.0 daemon --mcp-port 8384` (or whatever the current invocation is) should boot llo's MCP server on the published port.

4. **Document the build invocation** in llo's README.

## Eventual sibling-bundle integration (NOT in this bead)

Once the image ships, a follow-up bead in cloister will add llo as a `cluster.capnp` bundle entry alongside mache + rosary. The wire would switch from HTTP (today) to capnp-over-UDS (the cluster-internal contract).

## Acceptance

- `task image` builds on clean checkout.
- `ley-line-open:0.1.0` (or chosen tag) is loadable via `docker load`.
- The image runs llo's existing MCP server entrypoint correctly.
- README has a "Building the image" section.

## Cross-repo context

- **cloister** at `~/remotes/art/cloister/` — the future consumer (cluster topology + ADR-0005 wire contract).
- **mache** (`~/remotes/art/mache`) — sibling Go/Rust subprocess pattern; reference its apko once mache-172a50 lands.

## Out of scope

- WASM/wasi packaging (could be a follow-up given llo doesn't need FUSE).
- Migrating the wire to capnp-over-UDS (cloister-side follow-up bead).
- Adding llo to cluster.capnp (cloister-side follow-up bead, blocked on this).
