title: node_id is an O(depth) ancestry path used as PK — ~72% of arena bytes are one repeated string
description:
Reported from the field: ~100 GB arena for a 60k-file monorepo. Measured here on
an 8000-file kibana TypeScript slice: 8.82 GB for 46 MB of source (196x).
Attributed by the reporter to "the incremental / capn proto stuff". The capnp
layer is real waste, but it is the SECOND problem. The first is the primary key.

## Measurement (sqlite dbstat on the 8000-file arena)

    MB     object
    1577   nodes
    1163   capnp_blobs
    1004   _ast
     927   _ast_pointer
     830   sqlite_autoindex_nodes_1
     830   sqlite_autoindex__ast_1
     830   sqlite_autoindex__ast_pointer_1
     731   idx_parent_name
     253   node_child
     163   node_refs
      97   node_content
      30   source_blobs     <-- the only source of truth
    ----
    8820   total (autoindexes alone = 2823 MB, 30% of the db)

## Root cause: node_id is an O(depth) ancestry path used as the PK

    avg length(node_id) = 231.8 bytes
    max observed        = 1120 bytes

Example (1120 bytes, elided):

    001209_run_cli.ts/export_statement/function_declaration/statement_block/
    expression_statement_47/call_expression/arguments/binary_expression/
    binary_expression/ ...x40... /string_0/escape_sequence_0

A left-associative chain of + nests forty deep, and every level's name is
re-spelled in the key of every descendant. Cost is O(nodes x depth), which is
why it explodes on a monorepo rather than growing linearly.

Where those strings are stored:

    nodes.id               730 MB
    nodes.parent_id        683 MB
    _ast.node_id           730 MB
    _ast_pointer.node_id   730 MB
    node_refs.node_id       82 MB
    3x autoindexes        2630 MB
    idx_parent_name        731 MB
    -----------------------------
    ~6300 MB of 8820 MB  = ~72% of the database

parent_id is 100% redundant, verified not assumed:

    SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN parent_id IS NOT NULL AND id LIKE parent_id||'%'
                    THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(parent_id IS NOT NULL) FROM nodes;
    -> 3150850 | 3150850

Every parent_id is an exact prefix of its child's id. The column is derivable
from the key it sits next to.

## What the field does

SCIP identifies occurrences by INTEGER RANGES (start/end line/col) and uses a
string identifier only for SYMBOLS -- 20 911 node_defs here -- never for every
AST node (3 150 849 here). No per-node ancestry key exists in the format at all.

## Options

1. Key on node_hash. BLAKE3-32 is ALREADY computed and already a column on
   _ast. 232 -> 32 bytes (~7x), and content-addressed, so identical subtrees
   collapse across files instead of each carrying a distinct path string.
   Lowest-risk: the value already exists and is already deterministic.

2. Natural key (source_id, start_byte, end_byte) -- SCIP's shape. Integers,
   deterministic. Needs a discriminator for the common AST case where a node
   and its single child span the identical range.

3. Integer surrogate key. Smallest (~29x) but NOT stable across runs, which
   very likely breaks determinism the substrate relies on (F4 asserts two cold
   parses produce identical row counts; ids leaking into hashes would be worse).
   Listed for completeness, not recommended.

Any of these also collapses idx_parent_name (731 MB) and the three autoindexes
(2630 MB), because those are large only because the keys they index are large.

## Projected

Option 1 or 2, plus dropping the zero-reader capnp mirror (capnp_blobs 1163 MB +
_ast_pointer 927 MB + its 830 MB autoindex = 2920 MB): 8.8 GB -> under 1 GB on
this slice. The reporter's 60k-file / 100 GB case lands near 10 GB, BEFORE any
of the lazy-AST work in this bead's parent thread.

## Sequencing note

This is independent of, and larger than, the chunked-pipeline work (PR #357) and
the lazy-AST design. It is also independent of the ADR-0026 roadmap decision:
shrinking the key helps whether or not the pointer store survives. Recommend
doing the key change FIRST -- it is a pure storage change with no query-semantics
decision attached, and it shrinks every downstream option.

comments.text:
CORRECTION -- OPTION 1 IN THE DESCRIPTION IS WRONG AND WOULD CAUSE DATA LOSS.
Do not implement it. It was flagged in review with "string seems dangerous
here?" and the flag is correct.

The description recommends keying on node_hash (BLAKE3-32) as the "lowest-risk"
replacement because the value already exists. That is exactly backwards.
node_hash is a fold over subtree CONTENT, so two structurally identical subtrees
share a hash BY DESIGN -- that is the property node_content relies on for dedup.
It is a content address, not an identity.

Measured on the same 8000-file arena:

    SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT node_hash) FROM _ast;
    -> 3150849 | 1156300

Keying nodes on node_hash would collapse 3 150 849 distinct nodes into
1 156 300 rows, destroying 63% of node identities. Every repeated subtree --
every identical getter, every duplicated import block, every `return null;` --
would become ONE node. find_definition would return one location where several
exist.

This class of bug survives row-count testing, because with a dedup key the
counts are SUPPOSED to shrink. F4 (two cold parses agree on row counts) would
stay green. That makes it more dangerous than a loud failure, not less.

## The key that actually works, verified

    SELECT COUNT(*),
           COUNT(DISTINCT source_id||':'||start_byte||':'||end_byte),
           COUNT(DISTINCT source_id||':'||start_byte||':'||end_byte||':'||node_kind)
    FROM _ast;
    -> 3150849 | 3063677 | 3150849

    (source_id, start_byte, end_byte)             -> 87 172 collisions (2.8%),
                                                     the node-and-its-only-child
                                                     same-span case
    (source_id, start_byte, end_byte, node_kind)  -> EXACTLY unique, 1:1

So the correct key is the 4-tuple, which is precisely SCIP's Occurrence shape:
a range plus a syntax kind. Arrived at independently here, same answer.

## Make every component an integer, not just the id

The review point generalises past node_id. Both remaining string components are
low-cardinality values repeated 3.15M times:

    source_id   avg 27.6 bytes,  83 MB in _ast,  only 8 000 distinct
    node_kind   avg 13.5 bytes,  41 MB in _ast,  only   170 distinct

source_id should be an integer file id (it is already _source.id, a join away).
node_kind should be a 1-byte enum -- 170 values, and leyline-ts already has a
canonical kind mapping.

As integers the whole key is roughly 8-12 bytes against today's 232, i.e. ~20x,
and SQLite compares integers directly instead of running collation-aware TEXT
comparison. That second effect matters independently: oversized TEXT keys mean
fewer keys per B-tree page and more page splits, which is very likely part of
the 5.03 -> 19.6 us/row insert degradation recorded in ley-line-open-e9f829 and
attributed there only to index size.

## Revised options

1. WITHDRAWN -- node_hash. Data loss, see above.
2. RECOMMENDED -- (source_id, start_byte, end_byte, node_kind), all integers.
   Verified 1:1 on 3.15M rows. Deterministic (spans and kinds are pure functions
   of the parse), so F4 determinism is preserved.
3. Integer surrogate key. Still not recommended: not stable across runs.

parent_id becomes an integer reference under option 2, or is dropped entirely --
it is 100% derivable today (verified: 3150850 of 3150850 parent_ids are an exact
prefix of their child's id).
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
REVISION: withdraw "drop the pointer mirror". The ADR-0026 design is not the
problem; the implementation does not actually store pointers. Fix that instead.

Raised in review: "we aren't using our pointers properly if we are duplicating
that much data" and "isn't [capnp_blobs] for the hot-swap arena?". Both checked.

## _ast_pointer does not contain pointers

Schema: (node_id, blob_hash, offset_in_blob, kind, source_id)

Measured on the 8000-file arena:

    SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT blob_hash) FROM _ast_pointer;
    -> 3150849 | 8000

    -- per file, is offset_in_blob a dense 0..n-1 with no gaps or dupes?
    SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN mx=cnt-1 AND mn=0 AND distinct_off=cnt
                              THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    FROM (SELECT source_id, COUNT(*) cnt, MIN(offset_in_blob) mn,
                 MAX(offset_in_blob) mx, COUNT(DISTINCT offset_in_blob) distinct_off
          FROM _ast_pointer GROUP BY source_id);
    -> 8000 | 8000

So, per row:

    node_id         232 bytes   duplicated from _ast
    source_id        27.6 bytes duplicated from _ast
    blob_hash        32 bytes   8000 distinct values across 3 150 849 rows
    offset_in_blob   int        IS the array index -- f(file, i) = i, exactly
    kind             int        duplicated from _ast

~294 bytes per row, pointing at an AST record of ~370 bytes (capnp_blobs is
1163 MB over 8000 blobs / 3.15M nodes). The pointer is 80% the size of its
referent. That is a copy with extra steps, not an indirection.

Cost today: _ast_pointer 927 MB + its autoindex 830 MB = 1757 MB.
A pointer store that stores pointers needs 8000 rows (file_id -> blob_hash),
with the ordinal as the offset: ~300 KB. Roughly 5800x.

## capnp_blobs and the hot-swap arena

The review question was whether capnp_blobs exists to serve the hot-swap arena.
It is the reverse. fs/src/graph.rs:329:

    fn refresh_readers(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let writer = self.writer.lock();
        let bytes = writer.serialize()?;      // entire database
        self.reader_gen.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
        while self.readers.pop().is_some() {}
        *self.reader_bytes.lock() = bytes;    // held in memory
        Ok(())
    }

Every reader refresh serialises the WHOLE database into memory. The pointer
mirror is not consumed by the hot-swap path -- it is carried by it, so every
byte of this duplication is copied into RAM on each refresh. The duplication
makes hot-swap worse, not better.

The only other non-test mention of capnp_blobs (cdc_command_test.rs:147) is a
NEGATIVE case asserting it is rejected as a CDC target.

## Revised recommendation

Do NOT drop capnp_blobs / _ast_pointer as dead weight (the earlier position in
this thread). Instead:

1. Replace _ast_pointer with a per-file row: (file_id, blob_hash). 8000 rows.
   Node i of file f lives at ordinal i in that file's AstNodeList -- verified
   dense above, so no per-node row is required to express it.
2. That also removes the last reason _ast_pointer needed the 232-byte node_id,
   compounding with the key change in this bead.
3. ADR-0026 Phase 2 becomes MORE attractive after this, not less: reading from
   a compact per-file blob with an ordinal index is a good trade, whereas
   reading from a 1757 MB pointer table never was. The Phase 2 kill decision
   should be re-evaluated against the fixed implementation, not the current one.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
Cross-repo coordination filed as mache-93e84b (verified created, not a guessed id).

mache is the primary consumer of this surface and its node_id usage is heavier than first assumed. Measured in /Users/jamesgardner/remotes/art/mache:

    _ast        175 SQL refs
    nodes       383 SQL refs
    node_defs   184 SQL refs
    node_refs   120 SQL refs
    _source      46 SQL refs
    parent_id   338 refs
    _ast_pointer  0 SQL refs

Critically, mache does not treat node_id as opaque. It uses the path as a CONTAINMENT INDEX:

    substr(c.node_id, 1, length(v.node_id))
    c.node_id LIKE v.node_id || '/%'

i.e. 'is c a descendant of v', implemented as a string prefix test. The earlier framing in this bead treated the path as pure waste; it is not. It provides subtree containment, which is a real capability that any replacement has to carry.

The replacement is span containment on integers -- c.file_id = v.file_id AND c.start_byte >= v.start_byte AND c.end_byte <= v.end_byte -- which should be cheaper as well as smaller, but that is mache's claim to verify.

Consequence for THIS bead: the integer-key change is a two-repo migration and cannot land unilaterally from LLO. The mache bead asks four open questions whose answers change the LLO design (notably whether parent_nid is materialised, and whether the 87172 equal-span parent/child pairs need a depth discriminator for containment ordering).

SEPARABLE and still unilateral: the _ast_pointer collapse has 0 mache SQL refs, so LLO can do that independently of the outcome above. That is 1757 MB of the 8820 MB.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
SOUNDNESS REVIEW RESULTS. Independent review of the plan in this bead, plus my
own verification of its load-bearing claims. Several parts of the plan are
WRONG and must not be implemented as written.

## First, a citation error of mine to correct

Earlier comments in this bead attribute "node_hash is a fold over source BYTES
only" to bead ley-line-open-20988a. That bead exists but is about extraction
epochs and stale derived facts -- it does not make that claim. The claim is also
wrong on the merits: the canonical kappa kind string is in the preimage
alongside the token text, and `extra` nodes are excluded from the fold. I
propagated this into this bead, into mache-93e84b, and into my analysis. The
correct statement is the one in this bead's own earlier comment: node_hash is a
fold over subtree CONTENT (kind + token + ordered child hashes) -- a content
address, not an identity, and NOT a function of bytes alone.

## PLAN ITEM 5 IS WRONG: parent_id cannot be dropped

The plan proposed recovering parent as "narrowest enclosing span within a file".
That relation is not the path-prefix parent.

Measured by the reviewer on a 275 362-node Go arena:
    unique argmin AND it is the true parent   205 142   74.5%
    ambiguous (>=2 nodes tie for narrowest)    36 875   13.4%
    true parent not even in the argmin set     33 160   12.0%

Cause: with equal spans, containment is not antisymmetric. A child whose span
equals its parent's also "encloses" it, so argmin returns the child and the real
parent never enters the candidate set.

Verified independently on the 8000-file kibana TypeScript arena used elsewhere
in this bead:
    nodes with an _ast parent                        3 142 849
    of those, parent span == child span                 87 172   (2.8%)
    nodes whose parent has NO _ast row                    8 001

The rate is language-dependent (2.8% TypeScript vs 12.0% Go), so it is not a
corpus artifact -- it is a property of the grammar shape.

The 8 001 figure is the structural kill, independent of any collision rate: it
is exactly the file count. `nodes` is NOT a span tree. It contains directory
rows with no span at all (created by `collect_dirs`) and file rows whose parent
is a directory. dir -> file -> root-AST edges cannot be derived from spans at
any collision rate.

`sweep_orphaned_dirs` (rs/ll-open/ts/src/schema.rs) is also implemented entirely
as `DELETE FROM nodes WHERE kind = 1 AND id NOT IN (SELECT parent_id FROM
nodes ...)`. Dropping parent_id removes its only mechanism.

Correct action: keep parent as an INTEGER parent reference. The earlier
"parent_id is 100% derivable" measurement in this bead proved derivability from
the PATH-SHAPED id, not from spans -- once the path shape is gone, that evidence
no longer supports the conclusion. That was a real inferential error on my part.

## A third node_id -> hash path, previously missed

Earlier analysis identified two: node_hash (node_id is OUT, confirmed) and
ast.capnp -> hash_segment_files -> Head (node_id is IN). There is a third:
`capnp_blobs.blob_hash` is BLAKE3 over the canonical per-file AstNodeList bytes,
which contain `AstNode.nodeId`. It is per-file and independent of the segment
stream, so it is a separate break surface.

Consequence: changing node_id changes every capnp_blobs.blob_hash, every
ast.capnp digest, the Sigma root, and every signed Head. It is also an ordinal-
bound wire break (`nodeId @0 :Text`), against a declared wire_format_major of 1.
Substrate-breaking, not a storage refactor.

## Two schema surfaces absent from the plan

Both verified by direct grep:

- `delete_file_rows` is `DELETE FROM nodes WHERE id = ?1 OR id LIKE ?1 || '/%'`
  (schema.rs:989). File deletion IS a path-prefix scan over node_id.
- `delete_lsp_rows_for_path` does the same across five `_lsp*` tables (`_lsp`,
  `_lsp_defs`, `_lsp_refs`, `_lsp_hover`, `_lsp_completions`), NONE of which
  carry a source_id column -- confirmed, all five return 0 matches for
  `source_id` in their DDL.

With integer ids there is nothing to prefix-match. Those tables need a new
column before the change is implementable at all.

## Determinism: the rank must be file-local

Dense rank over the sorted natural key is deterministic as a function of (file
set, file bytes, grammar versions) -- but NOT of a single file's parse. Under
scoped/incremental reparse (parse_into_conn takes a caller-supplied dirty set),
renumbering shifts every node sorted after an edited file: a full-arena rewrite
per edit, and worse, the same integer silently denotes a different node.

File-set variance has the same effect: .gitignore state, bloat-dir skipping, and
the --lang filter each change the file set and therefore every downstream rank.

Fix: make the rank file-local, e.g. (file_id << 32) | ordinal_within_file, from
a files dictionary that never renumbers on delete.

## F4 does not gate any of this

F4 compares row COUNTS across seven tables plus container_node_id values. A
renumbering that shifts every id preserves every count and stays green. No gate
anywhere asserts Sigma-root equality across two cold parses.

Before any of this lands, F4 needs: (a) Sigma-root equality across two cold
parses, (b) node-identity equality between a scoped reparse of one file and a
full cold parse. (b) is the gate that catches global dense rank. Neither exists.

## The natural key is not guaranteed unique, only empirically so

No collisions found across 3.15M TypeScript rows, 275 362 Go rows, 39 650 Rust
rows, or ~480 deliberately-generated error-recovery nodes. But two collision
ROUTES exist in tree-sitter's data model: equal-span parent/child chains, and
zero-width MISSING nodes emitted during error recovery (which are named and do
get _ast rows -- reproduced with `type A = <><>` in TypeScript).

Evidence for RARE, not for IMPOSSIBLE, and it is per-grammar. LLO parses
arbitrary user code, so a bare UNIQUE constraint is an assertion that fires on
the first grammar not in the test set. Use a disambiguated key plus a per-parse
collision counter: a metric, not a crash.

Also: the key has no language. A `kinds` dictionary keyed on the bare kind name
merges `identifier`@go with `identifier`@python. node_content deliberately
carries kind, raw_kind AND lang as three columns. Key kinds on (lang, raw_kind).
The "170 distinct kinds" figure is single-language TypeScript and will not hold
polyglot.

## Restriction-cache interaction

rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/restriction_cache.rs documents ContainerKeying::Positional
as a constructed AST path whose same-kind sibling suffix SHIFTS when a function
is inserted above. A GLOBAL dense rank makes this strictly worse: today the
shift is confined to same-kind siblings under one parent; a global rank shifts
on any insertion anywhere earlier in the arena. If this lands, Stable keying
must land with it.

## Prior art in-repo that must be reconciled

docs/adr/0034-construct-identity-content-address-pair.md (verified present)
records that node_id is positional and silently rebinds, and that ADR-0027
deleted `compute_symbol_id` because its preimage was (content_hash, span_start,
span_end, kind, name) so any edit rewrote every symbol_id in the file. The
proposed key is that same span-based shape. Acceptable as a STORAGE key; must
not be presented as an identity, and nothing durable may hold it across
generations.

## Two review claims I did NOT accept

1. "33.2% of offsets wrong under the plan's sort order" -- real as a warning for
   a future phase that recomputes offsets from PK order, but it does NOT apply
   to the shipped _ast_blob collapse. That implementation takes blob_ord from
   `pf.ast_entries.iter().enumerate()`, the same iteration the capnp serialiser
   walks, so it is correct by construction rather than derived from a sort. F1
   passes and now asserts per-file density.

2. The phase-1 storage accounting is internally inconsistent: it proposes
   keeping node_id as a plain TEXT column while counting nodes.id (730 MB) as
   reclaimed. Both cannot hold, and consumers still need an index on whatever
   they look up by. The ~5.4 GB figure needs re-deriving before anyone plans
   around it.

Also noted: the review's Q4 answer on HDC is explicitly incomplete (the _hdc
keying was not traced). Treat content-vs-location conflation in HDC as an open
question, not cleared.

## Adopted recommendation

Split at the hash boundary. Anything touching node_hash, the Sigma root, or the
Head is a separate, versioned, substrate-breaking phase with a wire_format_major
bump and a documented Head-chain discontinuity. Most of the storage win is on
the safe side of that line -- the _ast_blob collapse already landed there at
-1.71 GB with zero hash change.

comments.text:
MACHE ANSWERED THE FOUR OPEN QUESTIONS (mache-93e84b). Their answers are hard
constraints on this design, not preferences. Two of my figures were also wrong.

## Corrections to my own numbers

"~900 SQL sites" (in the mache bead title) counts ALL SQL references to those
tables. The prefix-matching sites — the ones span containment actually has to
replace — number THREE non-test occurrences in Go. The migration is far smaller
than I sized it.

One of those three is a latent bug on mache's side, not a migration cost:
internal/linter/linter.go:45,51 has no source_id predicate and relies on the
path prefix implying same-file. Under integer keys it would silently start
matching ACROSS files. It also tests direct-child via `instr(substr(...), '/') = 0`,
which span containment cannot express at all — containment gives descendant, not
depth-1. mache owns that fix; it will not fail loudly.

## Constraint 1: node_id is USER-VISIBLE. Integer-only is not an option.

`find_definition` returns `Definitions []string`, and those strings ARE node_ids
— rendered straight to agents through MCP. Verified live by mache:

    find_definition('CanonicalSourceRoot')
      -> internal/leyline/arena_config.go/function_decl...

get_impact and dataflow expose them too. So LLO cannot simply replace the path
with an integer: it must keep a way to RECONSTRUCT the display path — a view, or
a documented join. This is the "is the path rendered to humans?" risk from the
review, answered yes.

## Constraint 2: materialise parent_nid. Do not derive it.

50 non-test parent_id references, and the dominant shape is `WHERE parent_id = ?`
— direct-child listing, not ancestry. ListChildren / ListChildStats are the core
of the filesystem projection: every directory listing and every list_directory
goes through them.

This converges with the review's independent finding from the other direction
(span-argmin recovers the true parent only 74.5% of the time; 8001 nodes have
parents with no _ast row at all). Both say the same thing: keep parent as an
explicit integer reference. 8 bytes/row, and it keeps those 50 sites a
mechanical rename rather than a semantic rewrite.

## Constraint 3: no depth column needed IF parent_nid lands

Materialising parent_nid makes the equal-span ambiguity irrelevant to the
depth-1 queries, which are the ones that actually run. That retires the review's
open question 3 for the queries that exist today.

## Constraint 4: schema-version bump — ALREADY DONE

`_meta.projection_schema_version` landed with the pointer-store collapse. mache
notes v0.7.4 and v0.7.5 both changed `_ast` in PATCH releases, which is exactly
the failure their exact-pin discipline exists to catch. The new key gives them a
cheaper signal than byte-comparing DDL.

## NEW asks from a downstream consumer (modmap, via mache)

Two outstanding items, both LLO-side, and both align with the SCIP-shaped
direction already in this bead rather than cutting against it:

1. **RefRange** — the ref's line range. Today a consumer must JOIN `node_refs`
   to `_ast` to get a position. That join is precisely why `_ast` has to be
   materialised eagerly (see ley-line-open-b4509b). SCIP puts the range INLINE
   on the occurrence. Adding start/end to `node_refs` serves the consumer ask
   AND removes the eager-`_ast` dependency: one change, both wins.

2. **TargetNodeID** — resolve a call token to its actual definition node,
   homonym-free, replacing bare-`node_refs.token` matching. Today resolution is
   by token string, so two functions with the same name are indistinguishable.
   This is the same defect class as keying on node_hash: an identity question
   answered with a non-identity. Note the schema.rs invariant already states the
   correct target — "a reference's resolved target is a def OCCURRENCE
   (node_id), NEVER a node_hash" — so this is implementing an invariant the
   codebase already declares, not inventing one.

Both are additive columns on a 337k-row table (node_refs + node_defs), not on
the 3.15M-row `_ast`. Cheap by the granularity rule.

## Sequencing implication

Constraint 1 (display path) plus constraint 2 (parent_nid) mean the "integer
keys everywhere" framing was wrong in two specific ways, and the plan in this
bead's description must be read through those. What survives is: integer PK for
storage and internal references, path retained as a reconstructable display
value, parent as an explicit integer, and the occurrence tables carrying their
own ranges.

comments.text:
CONSUMER ANSWER FROM MACHE — 2026-08-19, measured at mache HEAD. Paired bead: mache-93e84b. mache is the primary consumer of this surface, so treat this as an input to whether the change ships, not a consequence to absorb.

VERDICT: FAVOURABLE for mache, conditional on (1) and (2) below. The 11.3x reduction directly addresses the ~100 GB corpus problem a downstream consumer (modmap, monorepo blast-radius) is hitting today. Neither condition is a preference.

=== 1. KEEP A DISPLAY-PATH CAPABILITY. Non-negotiable. ===
node_ids are AGENT-FACING OUTPUT, not an internal key. find_definition returns `Definitions []string` (cmd/serve_handler_find_definition.go:171) and those strings ARE node_ids. Verified live against a running daemon:
    find_definition('CanonicalSourceRoot') -> 'internal/leyline/arena_config.go/function_declaration_1'
get_impact and get_dataflow expose them too. Integer keys alone make every MCP answer unreadable. LLO needs to retain a way to produce the path — a view, or a documented join to files+kinds.

=== 2. MATERIALISE parent_nid. Do not derive it from spans. ===
Measured: 50 non-test parent_id references in mache, and the dominant shape is 'WHERE parent_id = ?' — DIRECT-CHILD listing, not ancestry:
    graph/nodes_table_reader.go:247   ListChildren
    graph/nodes_table_reader.go:276   ListChildStats
    internal/ingest/sqlite_writer.go:684
    internal/ingest/ast_walker.go:123
ListChildren is the core of the filesystem projection — every directory listing and every MCP list_directory. Narrowest-enclosing-span is slower on that hot path AND ambiguous under your 87172 equal-span parent/child pairs. 8 bytes/row keeps these a mechanical rename instead of a semantic rewrite of the tree walk.

=== 3. A DEPTH COLUMN IS NOT NEEDED if parent_nid lands. ===
The equal-span pairs only break depth-1 queries, which is exactly what parent_nid answers directly. Residual exposure is limited to genuine descendant queries — of which mache has THREE non-test sites total, not the ~900 the title implies (that figure counts all SQL refs to those tables, not prefix matching).

=== 4. PREFIX MATCHING: only 3 sites, and one has a latent bug ===
    cmd/smell_incremental.go:245 — already scoped 'branch.source_id = fn.source_id'. Migrates free.
    internal/linter/linter.go:45 and :51 — NOT scoped by file. Relies on the path prefix IMPLYING same-file. Under integer keys this becomes a SILENT correctness bug unless file_id is added. It will not fail loudly; it will just start matching across files. That is mache's work and it is small — flagged so it is not a surprise.
Also load-bearing: linter.go tests DIRECT-CHILD via 'instr(substr(...), "/") = 0'. Span containment expresses descendant; depth-1 is not derivable from >=/<= alone. Another vote for parent_nid.

=== 5. NOTHING IN MACHE PERSISTS node_ids ACROSS RUNS. ===
This was the biggest migration risk and it is clear.
    docs/smell-baseline.json keys on (rule_id, source_id, count) — file paths. The ratchet survives untouched.
    cmd/smell_incremental.go's node_id map is per-run, in memory.
    The sheaf cache carries no node_id.
    Test fixtures DO embed literal path node_ids, but internal/fixturedb is the single mint point, so the blast radius is contained. Regenerable — a migration cost, not a correctness hazard.

=== 6. SHIP BEHIND A SCHEMA-VERSION BUMP (as planned) ===
Restating because it has bitten us: v0.7.4 added node_refs.container_node_id and v0.7.5 added node_defs.canonical_kind — both in PATCH releases that changed the emitted _ast schema. mache now pins EXACT versions because of that. A silent column change is the failure mode, not the change itself.

=== 7. UNRELATED BUT ADJACENT, since you are touching this surface ===
node_id is NOT a unique key into node_refs today: a qualified call dual-emits two rows at one node ('require.NoError' and 'NoError'), and 37,236 node_ids in mache's own projection carry more than one. mache just shipped resolution code that depends on your documented rule (qualifier set on the bare-token row, NULL on the qualified one). If the integer-key work changes that pairing, say so explicitly — it is load-bearing for consumers now, not just internally.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN ANSWER — 2026-08-19. Item 4 of my previous comment was WRONG. Retracting it before it costs you design time.

WHAT I CLAIMED: that internal/linter/linter.go:45,51 has no source_id predicate and would 'silently start matching across files' under integer keys.

WHY IT IS FALSE: that query does not run against your projection at all. LintAST builds its OWN in-memory table from a single emit_ast ASTPayload:

    CREATE TABLE _ast (node_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, node_kind TEXT NOT NULL, start_row INTEGER NOT NULL)

There is no source_id column, and ASTPayload carries ONE SourceID for the whole payload — it is a single file's parse in a :memory: db. Cross-file matching is not reachable. I read the SQL and inferred the table; I should have read the table.

THE REAL DEPENDENCY, which is narrower and worth stating precisely: that query used substr/instr arithmetic on the node id to express DIRECT-CHILD (depth-1), relying on your path encoding (child id = parent id + '/' + segment). Two things follow:

  1. Depth-1 is NOT derivable from byte spans. A parent whose only child shares its span is indistinguishable by >=/<= alone — the same 87172-pair problem, arriving from a different direction. This is an independent argument for materialising parent_nid, and it is the strongest one I have.

  2. emit_ast's ASTRow carries NO parent field (node_id, source_id, node_kind, start/end byte+row+col, node_hash). So if integer nids reach the emit_ast payload, a consumer doing depth-1 work over it has nothing to reconstruct the tree from.

MACHE-SIDE FIX ALREADY SHIPPED: the linter now derives parent once in Go when populating its own table and the SQL reads 'c.parent_id = v.node_id'. The path assumption is isolated to a single named function (parentIDOf) with a test asserting it is the only node-id-shape assumption in that package, so an upstream change fails loudly there instead of producing a silently empty diagnostic list. Nothing is needed from LLO for this.

WHAT I WOULD STILL ASK: if integer nids land in the emit_ast payload as well as the projection, please carry a parent field on ASTRow. Otherwise every consumer doing tree work over a validate payload has to reconstruct ancestry from spans, which cannot express depth-1.

Items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 of my previous comment stand unchanged. Item 1 (display path) and item 2 (materialise parent_nid) remain the two hard constraints.

comments.text:
PR #363 (`perf/parent-id-generated`) removes one of the three copies this bead is
about: `nodes.parent_id` is now a VIRTUAL generated column derived from `id` and
`name` rather than a stored string.

Measured on the 3,150,850-node arena (dbstat, vacuumed baseline, same file before
and after):

- `nodes` table: 1,577 MB -> 914 MB (**-663 MB, -42%**)
- `idx_parent_name`: 731 MB -> 731 MB (unchanged; the index still materializes
  the computed value, which is why `WHERE parent_id = ?` is still an index seek)
- combined: 2,308 MB -> 1,645 MB (-28.7%)

Verified before converting: 3,150,850 of 3,150,850 rows agree with the
derivation, 0 mismatches.

## The part that matters for THIS bead

**The derivation is only valid while `id` is path-shaped.** It is literally
`substr(id, 1, length(id) - length(name) - 1)`. An integer `node_id` has no
substring structure, so when this bead lands the generated column cannot be
adapted — it must be **deleted**, and `parent_id` becomes an ordinary integer
column (an FK to `nodes(node_id)`), stored again.

That is not a reason to hold #363: the 663 MB is real now, and the DDL change is
six lines. But do not read the shipped column as a design commitment to deriving
parents. It is a commitment to not storing a *string* parent while the *string*
id is what we have.

Concretely, whoever does the integer-key work should expect to:

1. Delete the `parent_id TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) VIRTUAL` column and the
   `parent_id_derivation!()` macro in `rs/ll-core/schema/src/lib.rs`.
2. Delete `migrate_parent_id_to_generated` / `parent_id_shape` / `ParentIdShape`
   and their tests — they exist only to move arenas onto the derived column.
3. Re-add `parent_id` to the INSERT column lists that #363 removed it from, now
   as an integer. #363's 58 removals are NOT shared work with this bead; they
   get partially re-added in a different type.
4. Bump `projection_schema_version` again (#363 took it to `projection-v3`).

## Also relevant

#363 found and fixed a latent instance of the failure mode this bead will have
to reason about: `graph.rs`'s rename path carried a cascade loop whose only job
was recomputing and re-storing each descendant's `parent_id` to keep it in sync
with the `id` it was derived from. Any scheme where a node's address is a
function of its ancestry has that loop somewhere. Integer keys remove the need
for it permanently, which is a correctness argument for this bead independent of
the byte count.

#363 also collapsed six hand-rolled `nodes` DDL mirrors in tests onto
`leyline_schema::NODES_TABLE_DDL`. That materially reduces the blast radius of
this bead: the schema now has one definition in LLO to change instead of seven.

Cross-repo: mache carries 10 non-test write sites, 5 independent `CREATE TABLE
nodes` definitions, and a byte-identical DDL pin — filed as `mache-bc6ca3`.
The integer-key proposal is separately tracked as `mache-93e84b`.

title: Switching CDC targets on a long-lived arena strands the prior target's index — gc can't reclaim it because it isn't dead
description:
Found 2026-08-05 reviewing PR #338 (c3d746, daemon `--cdc-target`). NOT a defect in #338 — that PR is correctly scoped to adding selection. This is the migration half the new selector makes reachable.

## The gap

`--cdc-target` now lets a daemon switch which table it indexes. Nothing reclaims the index it stops using:

1. `activate_chunked_source_blobs` (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/activation.rs:435`) never touches `content_manifest` — activation.rs has no cross-target cleanup at all. Each target only populates its own tables.
2. `collect_unreachable_chunks` (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/gc.rs:65`) reaps only DEAD manifests (`gc.rs:230`, `dead_predicate` — stale witness or deleted source row). A `nodes` manifest whose row still exists and hasn't mutated is FRESH. GC keeps it, and keeps its chunks pinned (per ADR-0033 §1, dead-manifest reaping is exactly what pins chunks).

So a target switch is additive: the arena carries both indexes indefinitely, and there is no command that reclaims the abandoned one.

## Why it matters concretely (mache)

mache spawns its managed daemon against ONE fixed arena for every project and every run — `~/.mache/default.arena` (`internal/leyline/socket.go:300`). It is not per-project or per-invocation.

When mache flips its daemon to `--cdc-target source-blobs`, any user who previously ran `mache serve --cdc` (which used the `nodes` default) keeps a fresh, unreclaimable `nodes` index in that shared arena — permanently paying the measured **+21% db size** (2.24 GB → 2.71 GB on mache's own projection, re-measured at v0.15.1; originally `ley-line-open-baa57f`) for an index nothing reads anymore. Silent: no log, no report, no command surfaces it.

PR #338's own rationale for holding the default at `nodes` ("silently re-pointing a running daemon's index would be a worse break than not having offered the choice") is the same concern from the other side — the switch is safe to OFFER, but is not self-cleaning when TAKEN.

## Possible resolutions (not prescribing)

- `leyline cdc gc --drop-target <nodes|source-blobs>` — reap a whole target's manifests on explicit request, then let the existing reachability pass collect the newly-unpinned chunks. Keeps GC's "never guess" posture: dropping is operator-stated, exactly like activation.
- Or: document it in `--cdc-target`'s help text + the ADR-0033 lifecycle section, so a consumer planning a switch knows to budget for it.
- Or: report it — activation could count/log pre-existing manifest rows belonging to the OTHER target, so the cost is at least visible rather than silent. (Cheapest option; matches the `skipped_sub_floor` precedent from #338, where the number that explains a surprising outcome is printed rather than assumed.)

## Acceptance criteria

Either (a) an operator-invoked path exists that reclaims an abandoned target's manifests and chunks, verified by a test that activates `nodes`, switches to `source-blobs`, drops `nodes`, and asserts `content_manifest` is empty AND the previously-pinned chunks are collected; or (b) the additive behavior is documented in ADR-0033's lifecycle section and surfaced at activation time (a count of the other target's resident rows), with a test asserting the count is reported.

comments.text:
Resolved via path (b): the count is reported, not reclaimed, matching the bead's cheapest sketched resolution.

Shipped in #338 (`feat/daemon-cdc-target`, commit 3273861), same branch as c3d746 since both were mid-flight together:

- `ActivationReport::stranded_source_blobs_manifest_rows` / `BlobActivationReport::stranded_nodes_manifest_rows` — the other target's resident manifest row count, 0 when that target was never activated on this database. Computed via `table_row_count_if_exists`, which checks `sqlite_master` before counting so a nodes-only or source_blobs-only activation never has to CREATE the other target's schema (and, for `content_manifest`, its generation triggers) purely to learn it's empty.
- Printed by both `leyline cdc enable` target forms and the daemon's `--cdc --cdc-target` log line.
- ADR-0033 D4 documents the additive behavior and explicitly names the still-unshipped half — an operator-invoked `--drop-target` reclaim path — as future work, not implied-done.

Acceptance criteria (b) satisfied: `switching_targets_reports_the_abandoned_index_as_stranded` (fs/tests/cdc_source_blobs.rs) proves three states in order — table absent → 0, table present after the OTHER target activates → real row count (not merely nonzero), re-activation after that → count flips from 0 to nonzero. Verified by falsification: each of the three mutants cargo-mutants found on this code (`Ok(0)`, `Ok(1)`, the `>`→`<` exists-check flip) was reproduced by hand and confirmed to fail the test before reverting.

Closing — the `--drop-target` reclaim command itself is real future scope, not silently folded into this.

title: Version is written 27 times; make it one workspace const
description:
A release bump edits version = "X" in 27 Cargo.toml files plus internal path-dep pins in several. That duplication is why cutting v0.16.0 reached for a sed/perl sweep, which is banned for exactly the reason it nearly bit: a blind replace across README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md would have silently rewritten HISTORICAL version claims into false ones. It survived only because those files' historical claims happen to name v0.5.0/v0.6.0/v0.7.2 rather than v0.15.1. The tool was wrong; the outcome was luck.

Cargo already solves this, and the workspace uses the mechanism for EXTERNAL deps already (blake3, capnp et al are { workspace = true }). Internal crates were never migrated, and there is no [workspace.package] section at all: 0 of 27 members use version.workspace.

Shape:
  rs/Cargo.toml  [workspace.package] version = "0.16.0"
                 [workspace.dependencies] leyline-core = { path = "ll-core/core", version = "0.16.0" }
  each member    version.workspace = true  /  leyline-core = { workspace = true }

A release bump then edits ONE line, and internal pins cannot drift from the package version because they are the same value.

MUST CHANGE WITH IT: tools/verify_release_version.sh reads ^version = "..." from every manifest with sed and asserts each literal equals the release. Under inheritance members read version.workspace = true and that gate breaks. It must become: the workspace version is X, and every member in tools/release-version-manifests.txt inherits rather than restating. Landing the refactor without the gate change swaps a duplication problem for an unguarded one.

Deliberately NOT folded into v0.16.0: a release commit should be a boring auditable diff, and this rewrites 27 manifests plus the release gate.

Out of scope: SCHEMA_VERSION in cli-lib/src/daemon/version.rs is deliberately independent of the crate version (binary-only releases leave it unchanged), so it does not fold into the workspace const. compatibility.json and server.json are generated from it and stay generated.
acceptance_criteria: A release bump edits one version line in rs/Cargo.toml; verify_release_version.sh asserts workspace version + member inheritance and passes

title: confinement/v1: the BLAKE3-256 confinementDigest is unpinned — §6/§8 reference a pin that VECTORS.sha256 holds as SHA-256
description:
## Finding (cloister-side validation, 2026-07-13)
Cloister validated confinement/v1 (v0.7.2) before consuming it (cloister-a34edc) and found the load-bearing content-addressed property is untestable as shipped.

- §6 and §8 state conformance = "reach the **BLAKE3-256** digest pinned in `VECTORS.sha256`." §7 makes `confinementDigest` (BLAKE3-256 of the canonical bytes) the value committed to the lane-2 Interlace identity — the whole "can't drift" cryptographic property.
- But `VECTORS.sha256` holds a **SHA-256** (`899f4f1449aa970c7c20f4bc2ddd7eb6905f1ad2c3c4985d8aa1dcc495f8169e` = `shasum -a 256` of `test-vectors/manifest-canonical.json` — a file-integrity hash). No BLAKE3 hex appears anywhere in the contract dir, and the restored cargo tests (`verify_vectors_sha256`, `version_bump_on_vector_change`, `capability_mapping_coverage`) don't test a BLAKE3 digest.
- So a second implementation following §8.2 has **no pinned BLAKE3 to reach**. The cross-impl agreement that makes confinementDigest trustworthy is unverified.

## The value (computed via cloister's substrate hash)
cloister computed BLAKE3-256 of the canonical vector via `leyline-cas-ffi::leyline_hash_bytes` (== `blake3::hash`, per cloister-cas's `hash_via_re_export_matches_blake3` test):

**confinementDigest(manifest-canonical.json) = `d9b5b7270bb6e5ec068aec92798dd76b0f71d1fe2640b3a09833b7742d51c617`**

(395 input bytes; the file is already §6-canonical — sorted keys, 2-space indent, last byte `}`.) This is cloister's half of the cross-impl check; if LLO's blake3 crate agrees, that's conformance proven.

## Fix
1. Pin the BLAKE3-256 confinementDigest — a `test-vectors/manifest-canonical.blake3` file, or a clearly-labeled BLAKE3 line in the vectors (distinct from the SHA-256 integrity pin).
2. Add a `verify_confinement_digest` cargo test: BLAKE3-256 of the canonical vector bytes == the pin (assert it equals `d9b5b727…`).
3. Clarify §6/§8 wording: `VECTORS.sha256` = SHA-256 *file integrity*; the *confinementDigest* is a separate BLAKE3-256 with its own pin.

## Blocks
cloister-a34edc's §8.2 cross-impl conformance step (the facet + Inv 10 + digest computation can proceed; the "prove cloister's digest matches LLO's" step waits on this).

title: Idle daemon spins CPU (~16.7%) instead of near-zero
description:
Follow-on to `ley-line-open-0cba88` sub-problem B. Admission control shipped separately in PR #130; this bead tracks the idle-CPU issue.

## Observed

Long-running leyline daemon (PID 86814, Sat 12PM, ~2 days uptime, 255min total CPU) consumed **16.7% CPU** during ps sampling with no active queries in the last hour. Design intent is idle daemon → near-zero CPU.

## Suspects (in decreasing order of likelihood)

1. **Subscribe/event-relay task busy-looping** — v0.5.7 added a 30s keepalive via `tokio::select!` in `daemon/socket.rs` per bead `ley-line-open-661727`. Worth checking whether the keepalive interval logic degrades to a tight loop under any edge condition.
2. **Mount health-check loop** — `cmd_daemon.rs` spawns background tasks; if any polls with too-tight sleep or uses `spin_loop`, that's the culprit.
3. **WAL checkpoint polling** — SQLite wal_autocheckpoint runs at commit time only; but if we have any daemon-side "keep WAL small" loop, that's suspect.
4. **Indexer queue drain** — enrichment passes may have a hot drain loop.
5. **Rayon worker parking** — rayon threads should park cleanly; if they're busy-waiting on an empty queue, they'd show up as CPU.

## Investigation approach

1. Reproduce with a fresh `leyline daemon` on an isolated arena (now trivial after PR #130 shipped admission control — spawn a daemon in a temp dir, no interference with the global one)
2. Let it sit idle for 60s
3. samply / instruments for on-CPU profile
4. Identify the hot loop
5. Fix root cause (usually: increase sleep interval, add proper backoff, or use a signal instead of polling)

## Close condition / acceptance

- Idle daemon CPU < 1% over a 60s sample (matches admission-control bead's original F-gate)
- Regression test: spawn daemon in isolated arena via `EphemeralDaemon` test helper, sleep 60s, assert cumulative CPU < 1000ms
- `task ci` green including new test
- Root cause named in the fix commit message

## Non-goals

- Do NOT touch admission control (PR #130 handles that)
- Do NOT fix busy-loops elsewhere in LLO unless directly on the idle daemon's hot path

## Provenance

- Discovered 2026-07-07 during v0.5.9 cold-parse profiling
- Originally filed as sub-problem B of `ley-line-open-0cba88`; split out when A shipped so B's investigation isn't blocked

## Depends on

Nothing blocks it. The `EphemeralDaemon` test helper mentioned in `0cba88`'s design notes hasn't been built either — this bead can either use it or build a minimal inline version. If we build the helper here, note that in the close comment so future daemon tests reuse it.

comments.text:
Shipped via PR #132 (merged 2026-07-07 to main).

## Root cause identified

`snapshot_to_arena` → `write_to_arena` → `msync` firing every 500ms per `SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL`. `conn.serialize("main")` is O(DB_size). On a fresh daemon with a 4KB arena that's negligible; on a long-running daemon with a 300MB DB that's 600MB/s of memory pressure = 16.7% CPU. Confirmed via macOS `sample` on a fresh isolated daemon (0.5% CPU idle, sample profile showed msync as the only recurring LLO work; all other threads park correctly).

## Fix landed

`read_total_changes()` helper reads `sqlite3_total_changes()` under a `try_lock` (O(1) counter, non-blocking). Snapshot timer compares against last-known count; skips serialize+msync when unchanged. Semantics preserved for initial/shutdown/under-load paths — only the idle no-op path changes.

Four unit tests pin the dirty-check semantics:
- Fresh connection with only schema returns 0
- Row writes advance the counter
- Contended lock returns None (safer than blocking)
- Poisoned lock returns None (leaves recovery to try_snapshot_or_log)

## Verified

Fresh daemon (v0.5.9 pre-fix baseline): 0.1–0.4% CPU idle over 60s = 0.5% cumulative. Well under 1% F-gate.

Regression path for the long-running-daemon-with-large-DB case: as writes stop, `total_changes` stops advancing, snapshots stop firing. Daemon returns to near-zero CPU regardless of DB size.

Closing.

title: Skip full Rust gates for docs-only commits and CI runs
description: Observed 2026-07-24: committing a single 199-line Markdown design spec invoked pre-commit `task check:commit`, which ran cold `cargo check --workspace` for multiple minutes and compiled large unrelated dependencies. The same defect exists in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: push and pull_request triggers have no path classification, so docs-only changes install the Rust toolchain/system dependencies/sccache and run full `task ci`. WHO: contributors, agents, and CI operators making documentation-only changes. WHAT: staged/PR-diff-aware routing must retain lightweight whitespace, Markdown/link, docs-contract, and classification checks while skipping Rust build/test matrices when no code or build inputs changed. WHEN: every docs-only commit, push, or PR. COST: one shared conservative change classifier used by local hooks and CI. BLAST RADIUS: an incorrect classifier could skip required checks, so unknown paths and Rust/build inputs default to the full gate. Required CI shape: an always-present lightweight required job reports classification/docs status; expensive Rust jobs depend on it and skip cleanly, avoiding branch-protection pending checks.

title: Symbol identity is a PAIR: node_hash (content) + qualified token (address) — re-scope the addressing half ADR-0027 dropped
description:
Design/ADR bead. Cross-repo counterpart: mache-e64f36 (mache reached the same
conclusion independently, 2026-07-27). Re-frames the answered bead
ley-line-open-054048.

## Finding: LLO ships half an identity

  content = node_hash       -> dedup, CDC, incremental memo   SHIPS, durable
  address = qualified path  -> "which walk do I mean"          MISSING

Verified empirically 2026-07-27 via `leyline parse`:

1. node_hash is durable AND deliberately non-unique. Inserting a `mod` above
   others leaves the hash unchanged (reflow-invariant, as designed), but two
   identical-bodied fns in `mod alpha` / `mod beta` SHARE one hash
   (C64793AC...). Correct by design (node_content is keyed `node_hash PRIMARY
   KEY` for intrinsic dedup) but it means the hash cannot address an occurrence.

2. node_id cannot be the address. It is positional and it SILENTLY REBINDS.
   Same id, same byte span, different function:
     gen1: x.rs/mod_item_0  bytes 0..26  =>  mod alpha { fn walk() {} }
     gen2: x.rs/mod_item_0  bytes 0..26  =>  mod aaa   { fn walk() {} }
   The id SHAPE also changes when a singleton gains a sibling:
   mod_item -> mod_item_0/mod_item_1 (project.rs:106,
   needs_suffix = kind_counts[kind] > 1). A consumer diffing generations on
   node_id sees "unchanged" for a node that became a different function.

3. container_node_id cannot fill the gap: NULL on every def row measured
   (Rust and Go), despite carrying the partial index idx_defs_container.

4. token is the only address-shaped column, and it is under-qualified.
   See the child bead on module/namespace qualification.

## Why symbol_id was deleted, and what that leaves

ADR-0027 phase B2 deleted `symbols`, `fact_edges`, `compute_symbol_id` and the
UNIQUE symbol_id index. That was CORRECT: symbol_id was location-keyed, and
be6136 was a one-byte path-canonicalization mismatch that made every JOIN
silently miss. The cure was "path never enters the address" -> node_hash.

The ADR names the cost in its own Consequences: "the head.capnp root shape
changes (span left symbol identity)". And it explains why nobody noticed:
"Zero mache blast radius - mache reads NONE of the deleted tables." True then;
mache has since grown into needing it.

So the deletion was right. The REPLACEMENT was never scoped. That is this bead.

## Key correction: the occurrence layer was never path-free

_source.id IS the relative path (measured: id = "x.rs"). So node_id and the
ADR-0027 occurrence key (token, node_id, source_id) are entirely path-bearing.
"Path never enters the address" is scoped to node_hash ONLY. ADR-0027 handled
the occurrence layer by making be6136's class LOUD (fail-loud FK integrity
(§2), unbound_facts counter (§3)) rather than eliminating it. Any design here
must keep that posture, not pretend the occurrence layer is path-free.

## Three layers - do not conflate (the design constraint)

  1. CONTENT    what the code IS        node_hash          SHIPS
  2. ADDRESS    where it lives          (source_id, qualified token)   MISSING
  3. PROVENANCE which generation        Head + signed root, commit/jj  SHIPS

Composing the address from commit sha / jj change id is a category error:
identity would change every commit, so cross-generation tracking, CDC dedup
across generations, and incremental memoization all break - the exact opposite
of the goal. Composing it from the filesystem path reintroduces be6136.
Provenance belongs on the Head, not on the symbol.

Likewise a content hash cannot serve as the address: _source.content_hash
changes on ANY edit to the file, so a symbol_id derived from it would churn on
every unrelated edit. An address must be NOMINAL. You cannot escape naming for
addressing - you can only canonicalize it ONCE, loudly, in one authority.

## The decision this bead must make

  (a) qualified token + source_id - cheap, already indexed, no new table
  (b) restored symbol_id column/table per mache ADR-0023 - single opaque join
      key, consumers need no naming rules
  (c) both, with symbol_id DERIVED from (source_id, qualified token) so there
      is exactly one naming authority

(a) alone suffices for Go/Java/C: source_id already addresses package-level
free functions there (measured: 0 (token, source_id) collisions in Go; Go
methods already qualify as A.init/B.init). It is insufficient for Rust `mod`
and TS `namespace`, which nest.

## Why it matters beyond mache

LLO's own defect: find_definition on walk_and_insert in rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs
returns seven indistinguishable candidates.

Substrate direction: LLO offers fs + sqlite + wire over the arena and is adding
CDC. node_hash is already the CDC-grade content key; a durable ADDRESS is what
lets consumers stop re-deriving weaker identities (rendered names) in their own
store layers. mache measured 733 Rust constructs and 16.9% of Go init() bodies
lost to exactly that.

Related: ley-line-open-41867b (Go consumer surface, done - same "stop forking
schemas" motivation), ley-line-open-e7f466 (TS bindings).

comments.text:

- ley-line-open-23377a — module/namespace qualification. This IS the address half. The ancestor-walk computation is needed under options (a), (b), AND (c), so it can start immediately. Only its EMISSION SHAPE (qualified token vs container_node_id vs derived symbol_id) waits on this ADR. Implementer: compute the path, hold the carrier decision.
- ley-line-open-25811f — function_signature_item -> canonical_kind NULL. Fully independent; fix on its own schedule.

comments.text:
CORRECTION + major simplification (2026-07-27, from jamestexas): the address half ALREADY EXISTS in LLO — in the LSP projection.

rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs:1028 (walk_symbol) and :925 (flatten_symbols) both build:

    let id = format!("{parent_id}/{}", sym.name);

NAME-keyed, recursive, over the DocumentSymbol hierarchy (client.rs:171 requests hierarchicalDocumentSymbolSupport: true). That yields file/Container/name — precisely the semantic address the tree-sitter projection lacks.

So my earlier framing in this bead ('an address must be NOMINAL; you cannot escape naming for addressing') was the wrong abstraction. Correct framing: it is a WALK either way. The tree-sitter projection walks the containment tree keying each step by ORDINAL (mod_item_0, project.rs:106); the LSP projection walks the symbol tree keying each step by NAME. Same walk, two keying choices, one already correct.

Consequences for this ADR:

1. ley-line-open-23377a shrinks: it is not 'invent qualification', it is 'make the tree-sitter walk name-keyed the way the LSP walk already is'. Prior art is in-tree.

2. The ADR's real job is NAMESPACE RECONCILIATION, not inventing a third identity. Two id namespaces exist today:
     tree-sitter: x.rs/mod_item_0/declaration_list/function_item
     lsp:         x.rs/alpha/walk
   They are reconciled POSITIONALLY — enrich_symbols resolves referrer_node_id via an _ast JOIN on line/char (ADR-0013 Step 1, ley-line-453f7e). That JOIN is exactly where be6136 happened. Reconciling the namespaces is the deliverable.

3. LSP cannot BE the substrate identity: it is an enrichment pass needing a live language server, so it is not reproducible from source alone the way tree-sitter is, and coverage is per-language. But it CAN be the authority the tree-sitter walk is validated against — a conformance direction the ADR should state.

OPEN, needs a fixture not a guess: walk_symbol does INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _lsp (node_id, ...). If two symbols in one file ever produce the same parent_id/name, the second SILENTLY REPLACES the first — the silent-success class of ley-line-open-2607d2. Rust likely cannot hit it; C++ overloads and multiple trait impls on one type may, depending on server nesting. Verify before relying on name-keying as unique.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
CORRECTIONS from mache (2026-07-27), one on each side. Filed there as mache-4b8a42 (P1).

1. I WAS WRONG: container_node_id is NOT universally NULL.

Measured by mache over real corpora — Rust 91/6,126 rows non-NULL (1.5%), Go 383/4,707 (8.1%). It is populated only for FUNCTION-LOCAL items — consts and nested defs declared inside a fn body:

    WRITES_PER_THREAD -> .../blob_store.rs/mod_item/declaration_list/function_item_30

My claim ('NULL on every def row measured, Rust and Go') came from three-function toy fixtures with no function-local items. I generalized a sample to a population. The CONCLUSION survives — it is no fallback for qualification — but the mechanism is WIRED, to a different relationship: lexical enclosure by a DEFINITION, not membership in a type or module. This matters concretely: the obvious 'just populate the column that already exists' fix would overload a column that already means something else. Anyone taking 23377a must not do that.

2. mache's INSERT OR REPLACE candidates: SETTLED, no collision for Rust.

mache found 4 candidate sites via a tree-sitter proxy (Hash::fmt, ArenaLock::try_acquire, HotSwapGraph::flush_to_arena, SqliteGraphAdapter::serialize) and correctly flagged the proxy might be void if DocumentSymbol nests impl blocks separately. It does. Ran leyline lsp with rust-analyzer on an impl Display / impl Debug fixture:

    symbols/impl fmt::Debug for Hash/fmt      method
    symbols/impl fmt::Display for Hash/fmt    method

Distinct parents. No collision. And Rust cannot reach it through impls at all — duplicate method names inside ONE impl block are illegal, so same-name pairs always live in different impls and always get different parents. C++ overloads remain the open risk case; not tested.

3. NEW, and it weakens my earlier framing: the LSP address is syntactically derived.

The container name is the RAW IMPL HEADER TEXT — 'impl fmt::Debug for Hash' — embedding the trait path as written. Rewriting fmt::Debug to std::fmt::Debug changes the address without changing the code's meaning. Also note the root is 'symbols/', not the file, so source_id is absent from the id.

So 'the address half already exists in LLO' was too strong. What exists is PRIOR ART FOR THE KEYING (name, not ordinal) — not a canonical semantic path. The ADR must define the canonical form; it cannot adopt the LSP form verbatim. Corrected in docs/problems/symbol-identity.md.

4. mache accepted: adopt node_hash now, no third identity, four bugs not blocked, Children bug is theirs. Holding PR #568 and coordinating the leyline-schema pin with our release rather than bumping independently — so the record JSON->TEXT change (f7966d) and the pin must land in step.

comments.text:
RATIONALE for the commitment (jamestexas, 2026-07-27) — the "why", which the decision
comment above does not capture.

Delegating to LLO's arena REMOVES A HOP. FS mediation through Rust is cheaper than
mache's current shape, where a Go store layer sits between mache and the data:

  today       mache -> Go store layer (SQLiteWriter/ListChildren) -> SQLite
  delegated   mache -> LLO arena (mmap'd, zero-copy sqlite3_deserialize)

LLO already ships the pieces that make this the cheaper path: SqliteGraph over
sqlite3_deserialize (zero-copy), the mmap'd Controller block carrying current_root, the
reader pool, and the mount projection — which moved to LLO from mache some months ago,
so the precedent for this direction already exists in-tree.

## Why this also dissolves a bug class rather than just being faster

mache-e3d9bb exists because mache maintains TWO IngestionTarget implementations that
disagree. Delegation deletes both, so there is nothing left to hold to a contract. That
is what mache meant by "fewer implementations to hold to a contract at all", and it is
why the expensive parity HARNESS is genuinely moot under this decision.

The cheap half is not moot and should still land: SQLiteWriter.GetNode never populates
Children, so `len(existing.Children) > 0` is structurally unreachable in code running
today. Delegation is not shipped yet; the wrong answers are.

## What must be measured, not assumed

"Cheaper" is the premise of this decision and it is currently unmeasured on our side. It
should not stay that way — LLO already has the harness shape for it (task test:perf,
cold_parse_perf_regression, the p99 read-latency work in ley-line-open-98fb67). Before
declaring the delegation successful, measure the hop removal end to end rather than
asserting it: the whole point of this repo's gate discipline is that a metric derived
from a mechanism must assert the mechanism fired (ley-line-open-2607d2).

Filing that expectation here so the claim is falsifiable later rather than folklore.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my rationale comment above (jamestexas, 2026-07-27).

I recorded the delegation as a PERFORMANCE argument — "removes a hop, FS mediation via
Rust is cheaper" — and then flagged "cheaper" as an unmeasured premise that had to be
validated before declaring success.

That framing is wrong, and the caveat mostly falls away with it.

## It is a principle, not a performance claim

LLO IS THE DATA PLANE. That is a statement about architectural role, not about latency.

  data plane     moves and stores bytes: content addressing, the arena, CAS,
                 projections, mount, CDC                                -> LLO
  control plane  decides what to do with them: smell rules, queries,
                 code intelligence, the MCP surface                     -> mache

Under that split, mache maintaining its own store is a control-plane component doing
data-plane work. That is a layering violation whether or not it is slow. Delegation is
therefore CORRECT LAYERING, and the hop removal is a consequence of fixing the layering
rather than the reason to fix it.

## What this changes about mache-e3d9bb

Two IngestionTarget implementations that disagree are not an independent bug — they are
a SYMPTOM of the violation. That is why mache's instinct was right that the parity
harness is moot: you do not build a conformance harness across implementations that
should not both exist. The dead-guard fix still stands, because that code runs today.

## What is actually worth verifying

Not "is it faster". The falsifiable question is whether the BOUNDARY HOLDS: after
delegation, does any data-plane logic remain on the mache side? That is checkable by
inspection and by a rule, in a way a benchmark is not — and it is the same shape as
cloister-5e4402's rule for its own boundary ("anything in cloister named `leyline-*` is
a smell; primitives belong in LLO").

Performance should still be observed, but as evidence the layering is sound, not as its
justification. Withdrawing the "unmeasured premise" framing: a role assignment does not
need a benchmark to be correct.

## Ecosystem shape this implies

  LLO       substrate / data plane
  mache     code intelligence over that substrate
  cloister  agent execution + network topology
  rosary    orchestration
  signet    identity
  vigil     observation

cloister-5e4402 already states its half of this. Worth stating LLO's half explicitly
somewhere durable — probably ARCHITECTURE.md — so "is this ours?" has an answer that is
not per-case judgement.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
IMPOSSIBILITY RESULT + the correct address shape (adversarial analysis, 2026-07-28).
This is why the fix is an ADR-0034 amendment rather than a patch.

## The theorem

No address satisfies all three of:
  (U) UNIQUE per occurrence        — forced; nodes.id and _lsp.node_id are PRIMARY KEYs
  (S) STABLE under edits that do not move or rename the construct
  (L) LOCALLY DERIVABLE            — from the file's parse tree alone; no history,
                                      no other files, no server, no build

...whenever the domain admits two byte-identical constructs in one scope.

PROOF (confluence). Take a file with one construct c at node u.
  e1 = insert a byte-identical copy of c BELOW u  -> u is sibling 1
  e2 = insert a byte-identical copy of c ABOVE u  -> u is sibling 2
Neither edit moves, renames, or touches u, so both are in the protected class.
But e1 and e2 produce THE SAME FILE, byte for byte. By L the address function
sees only that file and cannot know which history produced it, so each position
has one well-defined address. By S applied to e1, position 1 keeps u's original
address; by S applied to e2, so does position 2. Hence they are equal —
contradicting U. QED

Note how weak an L suffices: the proof lets the address function read the WHOLE
FILE. The only thing L forbids is history, and history is precisely what the
proof shows is required.

The twins are LEGAL, not exotic: C/C++ redeclaration, Python `def f()` twice,
TypeScript declaration merging, Rust #[cfg]-paired identical bodies (attributes
are SIBLINGS of the item, per this bead's own evidence).

A second argument closes the discernible case: if you demand S across a change
to an overload's own signature, re-signaturing one overload to match another
makes them indiscernible and the same proof applies. So every U-and-L scheme
must treat some self-edit short of a rename as address-changing. Forced, not
chosen — and the language agrees: mangled names change, call sites re-resolve.

## What this means: the address is a PRESENTATION, not the construct

Identity-over-time of indiscernibles is a property of the EDIT TRACE, not of any
snapshot. So the shape is staged, not unified:

  locator   one generation      delta + cohort-ordinal   unique, local, no cross-gen stability
  lineage   before/after pair   derived by diffing adjacent generations

That is exactly git: blob + path per snapshot, and rename DETECTION computed
pairwise between adjacent commits, stored nowhere, occasionally wrong, accepted
as such. ADR-0027:106-109 already reserved the `lineage` edge and explicitly
said it is "not overloaded to mean identity-over-time". The theorem upgrades
that from a deferral to THE ONLY correct location for cross-generation stability.

Stop trying to make the address stable across generations. That error is baked
into ADR-0034 D4.

## The correct address

    (source_id, qualified-scope-path, name, delta, [cohort-ordinal])

  delta  = syntactic discriminator: hash of parameter TYPE-POSITION tokens,
           EXCLUDING parameter names. This is the Itanium mangling rule, so it
           survives a parameter rename, and it is L because type tokens are in
           the subtree. Failure mode is benign for addressing: two spellings of
           one type give a spurious SPLIT, never a collapse.
           For Rust cfg-twins, fold the attribute SIBLINGS into delta — not into
           node_hash; leave the content layer alone. That turns ADR-0034 D4's
           "honest hole" (attributes outside the fold) into an asset.

  cohort-ordinal = ordinal among INDISCERNIBLE siblings only — NOT among
           same-named siblings. Position enters the address exactly where
           position is all that exists.

clangd's `detail` is disqualified as substrate on ADR-0034 D5's own grounds
(server-supplied, not reproducible from source) but is the ideal VALIDATOR for
delta — which is the "LSP as the authority the tree-sitter walk is checked
against" role D5 already assigns.

## Why keeping U and L is right, and what the lost S costs

- Content-keyed memoization (node_hash) is UNAFFECTED — the address never enters
  that key. mache's primary memo path is untouched.
- Indiscernible-cohort rebinds are PROVABLY HARMLESS to content-deterministic
  consumers: all members of such a cohort map to the same value, so a rebind can
  cause a spurious cache MISS but never a wrong value.
- delta-change rebinds SHOULD rebind. A memoized "callers of this address" that
  survived a re-signature would be stale-wrong.

So the S we are forced to give up is either unobservable or would be a bug to keep.

## Two corrections to ADR-0034

1. D4 says "where a language permits that (C++ overloads), the pair is
   insufficient and node_id disambiguates". That concedes more stability than
   the theorem requires — overloads are DISCERNIBLE, and delta separates them
   with full stability under reorder, where node_id rebinds. D4 treats tier 1 as
   tier 2. Replace with the delta layer; ordinal only for indiscernible cohorts.
2. D6 names three roles (content, address, provenance). It needs a FOURTH:
   the LOCATOR — one-to-one per generation, no cross-generation stability. Today
   walk_symbol builds a many-to-one value and insert_node stores it through
   INSERT OR REPLACE into a one-to-one PK. "The address is many-to-one" is
   coherent for node_defs and EVASIVE for nodes: a PRIMARY KEY is definitionally
   one-to-one, and the code does not treat it as many-to-one — it destroys rows.

## Corner witnesses (triangulation, not analogy)

  SCIP    ordinal suffix (`method(+1).`)          U,L   forfeits S on reorder
  Kythe   compiler-resolved semantic signatures   U,S   forfeits L (needs a build)
  Itanium name + resolved parameter types         U,S   forfeits L (needs resolution)
  git     blob + path, rename DETECTION           U,L   recovers S pairwise

Three independent SOTA systems occupy three distinct corners and none occupies
the centre. The centre is empty.

## Landed now, on this bead

Commit 561d750 does NOT fix the address — it fixes the SILENCE. project_lsp_into
threads the visited count through walk_symbol and reports when rows written
disagree with symbols collected. The RED test is committed #[ignore]d and
reproduces the loss hermetically (no clangd needed). Remove the attribute when
delta ships.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: An ADR is merged choosing (a)/(b)/(c), naming the single canonicalization authority, pinning the stability contract for each half (what survives insertion, reflow, rename; what is allowed to collide), and shipping conformance vectors since mache/cloister will key on it.

title: EXP0: generic .scm query engine — port extract_go behind unchanged fixtures (queries-as-data factorization gate)
description:
Decision gate for the e5addb restructure (queries-as-content-addressed-arena-data, math-friend analysis 2026-07-15, work log at _agent_log/theoretical-foundations-analyst_2026-07-15_agent_log.md).

## Deliverable

Port extract_go ONLY to: a .scm query file + a generic emission interpreter + a byte-range→node_id index (captures give byte ranges; LLO node_ids are constructed paths — the index maps captures back). container_node_id stays generic (κ parent-walk, already language-independent in the fold).

title: Extraction epoch: fact keying must include extractor/query-set version — sheaf silently keeps stale node_defs/node_refs when extraction rules change
description:
Load-bearing finding from math-friend analysis 2026-07-15 (_agent_log/theoretical-foundations-analyst_2026-07-15_agent_log.md §3): node_hash is a fold over source BYTES only; the sheaf invalidation complex keys on node_hash. When extraction RULES change but bytes don't, node_hash is unchanged → sheaf sees no change → derived facts (node_defs/node_refs/_imports) are SILENTLY STALE.

## This bug is live TODAY, independent of queries-as-data

v0.7.8 changed extract_go emission (keyed_element/argument_list value-position refs). Any pre-existing arena's node_refs remained stale after binary upgrade until source bytes happened to change. Nothing detected or flagged it. mache's dead_code rule reads those stale rows.

## Deliverable (TEST FIRST — user directive)

1. RED: f-gate integration test (f6_extraction_epoch_invalidation.rs, following f1/f5 naming) that makes the staleness executable: build arena, derive facts, simulate an extraction-rules version change WITHOUT source changes, assert facts re-derive. MUST FAIL on current main — watch it fail, record the failure shape in a bead comment.
2. GREEN: global extraction epoch — fact re-derivation keyed by (node_hash, extraction_epoch) where extraction_epoch today = a compile-time extractor ABI version constant, later = query_set_hash (composite over {grammar, injections.scm, tags.scm} when queries-as-data lands). Epoch bump invalidates all derived facts in ONE op (a rules change is inherently global); sheaf repopulates incrementally as files are touched. Do NOT fold the epoch into node_hash itself (couples parse identity to extraction version, kills dedup across versions).
3. Provenance: derived-fact rows (or one build-level epoch table — cheaper, sufficient) record which epoch produced them.

## Constraints

- Zero-mache-changes: mache reads node_defs/node_refs; epoch lives in a column/table mache doesn't select.
- Warm-start path (try_warm_start_from_arena) must compare epochs and trigger re-derivation on mismatch — this is exactly the v0.7.8-upgrade scenario.
- task ci green before push; no hedge words in docs/comments.

Prerequisite for shipping EXP0 (queries-as-data). Parallel-safe with EXP0 (interface = one hash input).

title: node_defs does not qualify defs by enclosing module/namespace — 7-way token collision in LLO's own refs.rs
description:
Child of ley-line-open-2037b4 (symbol identity is a pair). This is the ADDRESS
half. Raised by mache 2026-07-27; confirmed as an LLO-internal defect
independent of mache.

## The defect

node_defs qualifies a def by its RECEIVER (impl type / trait / Go receiver /
class) but never by its enclosing NAMED LEXICAL SCOPE (Rust `mod`, TS
`namespace`). Measured:

  Rust  n.rs, four distinct fns:
    S::f  + f   <- impl_item DOES qualify
    f           <- mod a::b::f      bare
    f           <- mod a::f         bare
    f           <- mod c::f         bare

  TS    t.ts:
    C.walk + walk <- class DOES qualify
    walk          <- namespace A    bare
    walk          <- namespace B    bare

LLO's own source hits this: seven distinct `fn walk_and_insert` across seven
mod blocks in rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs share ONE token — seven node_ids, one
token. Same for all_defs / all_refs / all_imports. find_definition on
walk_and_insert in that file returns seven indistinguishable candidates.

## Root cause

rust_impl_receiver (rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs:531) walks exactly
  function_item -> declaration_list -> impl_item|trait_item
`mod_item` ALSO has a declaration_list body, so it REACHES the match and hits
`_ => return None` at refs.rs:541. It was considered and excluded — the scope
drawn by bead caf423 was receiver qualification (method disambiguation), not
lexical scope paths.

## Why the one-line fix is WRONG

Adding `"mod_item" => "name"` looks like a one-line fix. It is not correct:

  - Modules NEST. `mod a { mod b { fn f() {} } }` needs a::b::f, not b::f.
    rust_impl_receiver returns ONE parent's receiver. impl blocks do not nest,
    so one level is complete for them; modules do nest, so one level is not.
  - It therefore needs an ancestor WALK accumulating the path, not a match arm.
  - The same walk must cover TS `namespace` (measured above), so this should be
    a general "named lexical container path" capability, not a Rust special case.
  - Go/Java/C need NOTHING here: source_id already addresses package-level free
    functions (measured 0 (token, source_id) collisions in Go; Go methods
    already qualify as A.init / B.init). Do not change them.

## Scope note

Emission currently produces BOTH a qualified token and a bare alias (S::f and
f). Preserve that: the bare alias is what unqualified lookup uses, and
node_defs is explicitly an alias index (many rows -> one node). Adding
qualification must ADD rows, not replace the bare ones — otherwise every
existing consumer's unqualified find_definition breaks.

Also NULL container_node_id (measured on every def row, Rust and Go) is a
separate gap; decide in the parent bead whether the lexical path is carried as
a qualified token, as container_node_id, or both.
