comments.text:
RESCOPED 2026-07-27 after adversarial review (Fable) + independent reproduction.

## The acceptance criteria on this bead were HARMFUL — replace them

They said 'Go/Java/C emission byte-identical to before'. Java is measured-BROKEN, so that clause REQUIRED preserving the bug this bead exists to fix. Anyone implementing to spec would have fixed Rust/TS and pinned the Java defect in the same change. My error: I measured Go, then generalized to Java and C without checking.

## Measured collisions — leyline parse, node_defs grouped by (token, source_id)

    python   Helper x2   Helper.run x2   run x2     nested classes; EVERY decorator makes a nested def
    java     Builder x2  Builder.build x2  build x2 nested types ARE named in-file scopes
    cpp      helper x2                              in-namespace defs emit bare
    rust     f x3 across mod a::b / mod a / mod c   plus Handler::run across mods
    ts       walk x2 across namespace A / B
    go       (none)                                 the ONLY measured-clean language

Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Scala, C# have NO extractor — no dispatch arm in refs.rs, zero node_defs rows. 'Unaffected' there is vacuous, not safe; record them as out of scope explicitly rather than letting them read as passing.

## Root cause is uniform, so the fix must be generic

Every per-language extractor qualifies exactly ONE ancestor level:
  python_enclosing_class  refs.rs:685
  java_enclosing_type     refs.rs:964
  cpp_enclosing_class     refs.rs:1117
  rust_impl_receiver      refs.rs:531
One level is complete for RECEIVERS (impls/classes do not nest as receivers) and incomplete for LEXICAL SCOPES (which do). So this is a generic enclosing-named-scope accumulation with a per-language audit — not a Rust/TS patch.

## Additional work the original scoping missed

AST scope nodes are frequently NAMELESS: impl_item has no name field (rust-analyzer synthesizes 'impl Handler' server-side), C++ has anonymous namespaces, TS internal_module emits no def and has no kappa mapping. Name synthesis for nameless scopes is part of this bead.

## Sequencing constraint — read before emitting

This bead makes ADR decision #1 (ley-line-open-2037b4) DE FACTO. The path SYNTAX — separator, depth, how receiver and scope compose (alpha::Handler::run vs alpha/Handler/run) — IS the single canonicalization authority the ADR reserves. Once qualified tokens land in node_defs.token and a consumer keys on them, changing the scheme is a breaking re-emission. The CARRIER (column vs derived symbol_id) is genuinely deferrable; the canonicalization is not. Decide the syntax before emitting, even if the carrier waits. My earlier 'compute the path, hold the carrier decision' guidance was only half right.

## Replacement acceptance criteria

Per-language fixtures each yield DISTINCT qualified tokens for same-named defs in different enclosing named scopes, with bare aliases PRESERVED (node_defs is a many-to-one alias index; unqualified lookup depends on the bare rows):
  Rust   mod a{mod b{fn f}} mod a{fn f} mod c{fn f} -> a::b::f, a::f, c::f
  TS     namespace A / namespace B
  Java   Outer1.Builder.build vs Outer2.Builder.build
  Python nested classes AND nested defs (decorators)
  C++    in-namespace definitions
  Go     emission byte-identical (only measured-clean language)
  Ruby/PHP/Kotlin/Scala/C# recorded as out of scope, not silently passing
Plus: cargo test -p leyline-ts; task ci.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
DONE — commit c35415e on branch fix/ley-line-open-f7966d-record-affinity (PR #281).
task ci green (TASK_CI_EXIT=0), receipt recorded for tree 8f1b66b.

Implements ADR-0034 D1 (docs/adr/0034-construct-identity-content-address-pair.md).

## Against the revised acceptance criteria

  rust    mod / impl(type) / trait         alpha::beta::f, alpha::H::run       PASS
  java    class/interface/enum/record      Outer1.Builder.build                PASS
  cpp     namespace / class/struct/union   alpha::helper, geo::Shape::area     PASS
  python  class + function_definition      Outer1.Helper.run, deco1.wrapper    PASS
  js/ts   internal_module / class          A.walk, A.C.walk                    PASS
  go      emission byte-identical                                              PASS
  bare aliases preserved everywhere                                            PASS

Go byte-identical is verified, not assumed: method_tokens_are_qualified_go and the
other 16 tests in cli-lib/tests/def_ref_extraction_fidelity_test.rs pass unchanged.
That suite pins consumer-visible emission, so it was the real blast-radius check.

Ruby, PHP, Kotlin, Scala, C# are RECORDED OUT OF SCOPE rather than silently
passing: they have no dispatch arm in refs.rs and therefore emit zero node_defs
rows. Nothing to qualify. This is written into ADR-0034's Consequences and
docs/problems/symbol-identity.md, not just here.

## Implementation shape

`enclosing_scope_path` walks the FULL ancestor chain; the per-language
`*_SCOPES` table carries the policy. That factoring is deliberate — the two real
judgement calls are data, not control flow:

- Rust OMITS function_item, so a function-local item stays bare. Preserves the
  prior behaviour where a nested fn was not qualified by its enclosing method.
- Python INCLUDES function_definition, because every decorator makes a nested def
  and two of them otherwise collide on a bare `wrapper`.

Anonymous scopes contribute NO segment rather than a placeholder (ADR-0034 D1):
anonymous C++ namespaces and Java anonymous-class bodies emit bare.

C++ needed more than the shared walker. Its declarator guard admitted only
field_identifier, so in-namespace free functions were never qualified AT ALL, not
merely under-qualified. Relaxed to also admit identifier; out-of-line
qualified_identifier definitions stay excluded as before.

Removed five now-subsumed one-level helpers (rust_impl_receiver,
python_enclosing_class, java_enclosing_type, cpp_enclosing_class,
js_ts_enclosing_class), each replaced by a note naming what took over.

## Two things a reviewer should check rather than trust

1. ONE EXISTING TEST EXPECTATION CHANGED. cpp's
   extract_class_namespace_and_inclass_method_defs asserted `Shape::area` for a
   class inside `namespace geo`; it now asserts `geo::Shape::area`. That test
   encoded the defect — two namespaces each with a Shape::area were
   indistinguishable under the old form. Changing an assertion to match new
   output is normally the wrong move, so it is called out explicitly.

2. PYTHON WAS WIRED BEFORE ITS TEST EXISTED — tests-after, not TDD. Rather than
   claim otherwise, the suite was mutation-tested twice:
     - collapsing the walk to one level  -> 5 tests fail, incl. nested-class
     - dropping function_definition from PYTHON_SCOPES -> exactly the decorator
       test fails
   Each mutation is caught by the test that specifically guards it. The
   single-level tests (cpp/ts defs_qualify_by_enclosing_namespace) correctly
   survive the first mutation — they assert "qualifies at all", not "accumulates".

Tests: 176 pass in leyline-ts --all-features; 17 pass in the cli-lib fidelity
suite. No new clippy warnings (the 3 remaining are pre-existing, in pyproject.rs
and lib.rs, untouched here).

## Downstream

mache is holding PR #568 on this. The address half now exists; per ADR-0034 D4
the ordering constraint still stands — ley-line-open-25811f must land before any
consumer pins to node_hash, because the preimage hashes
canonical_kind(raw).unwrap_or(raw) and that fix rewrites every trait-signature
hash.

title: Scope the local pre-push full gate to main; run GH CI on all PRs instead of only PRs to main
description: The pre-push hook runs the full task ci gate on every push regardless of target — a WIP push to a feature branch costs the same minutes as a main push, and doubles the attestation-race window. Meanwhile ci.yml's pull_request trigger filters to branches: [main], so PRs targeting an integration branch (release-hardening flow, 2026-07-29) run no CI at all. Matched pair: (1) pre_push_ci.sh consults PRE_COMMIT_REMOTE_BRANCH and runs the full gate only for refs/heads/main, exiting 0 with a deferral message otherwise; unset variable fails closed to current behavior. (2) ci.yml drops the pull_request branch filter so every PR gets task ci on a runner. Net: branch pushes are seconds, every PR still gets the full gate async, and the only local full-gate trigger is pushing main itself. Related: ley-line-open-5dc535 (main unprotected) is what makes the GH gate enforceable rather than advisory.

description:

## Problem

LLO's ingest walker (`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_parse.rs::collect_files` @ line 2469 + the duplicate walker `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/topology_pass.rs::collect_files` @ line 835) uses a hand-rolled `read_dir` recursion with an `is_bloat_dir` skiplist. Neither reads `.gitignore`.

Symptoms in production consumers:
- Users with `.gitignore`d `data/`, `.venv/`, model-checkpoint dirs get them indexed (blows up DB size + adds noise to smell rules).
- Mache maintains a git-archive tracked-tree workaround to feed LLO only tracked files — that workaround only exists because LLO doesn't respect gitignore.
- Rosary will inherit the same problem the moment it points at a real repo.

## Root fix

Replace the two `collect_files` recursions with `ignore::WalkBuilder` (from the `ignore` crate — same primitive ripgrep + mache use). It composes .gitignore/.ignore/.git/info/exclude/global git excludes with the existing `is_bloat_dir` skiplist as an add-on.

Escape hatch: `--respect-gitignore=false` flag (default true).

## Close condition

`cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib collect_files_respects_gitignore` — new test in cmd_parse.rs asserts a gitignored path is NOT collected. Plus `cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib -- --test-threads 1` passes end-to-end.

## Downstream

Mache drops the git-archive tracked-tree pre-pass. Rosary substrate ingest unblocks.

## Priority

P2. Non-blocking for v0.7.1 arc (already shipped).

title: function_signature_item emits canonical_kind NULL — trait signatures fall out of the partial index and collide with the migration escape
description:
Found while answering a mache consumer question, 2026-07-27.

extract_rust (rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs:355) matches
`"function_item" | "function_signature_item"` and emits a def row for BOTH,
stamping canonical_kind: TsLanguage::Rust.canonical_kind(node.kind()).

But the Rust arm of canonical_kind (rs/ll-open/ts/src/languages.rs:342-356) has
NO case for function_signature_item — it falls to `_ => None`. Every bodyless
trait signature therefore lands in node_defs with canonical_kind = NULL.

Measured on a 5-line fixture:

  trait Greet {
      fn hello(&self);   // signature, no body
      fn bye(&self) {}   // default method, has body
  }

  token        | canonical_kind | node_id
  Greet::bye   | function       | .../function_item
  bye          | function       | .../function_item
  Greet::hello | <NULL>         | .../function_signature_item
  hello        | <NULL>         | .../function_signature_item

## Why NULL is the wrong value (not merely a missing kind)

1. idx_defs_canonical_kind is a PARTIAL index `WHERE canonical_kind IS NOT
   NULL`. Signatures are not mis-kinded, they are OUT OF THE INDEX.
2. The filter DEFS_TABLE_DDL's own doc block names as load-bearing —
   `WHERE canonical_kind IN ('function','method','type')`, the mache
   dead-code/god-file query — silently drops every trait signature.
3. NULL is ALSO the documented open-world escape for pre-migration DBs
   ("Nullable so pre-migration DBs read as NULL"). So a consumer cannot
   distinguish "old projection" from "trait signature". The two states collide.

## The decision (this is the real content, not the match arm)

Should a bodyless signature be canonical_kind='function' (same kappa as a
definition), or a distinct kind?

  - Folding into 'function' makes DECLARATIONS indistinguishable from
    PROJECTABLE CONSTRUCTS. mache explicitly asked for that separation.
  - A distinct value (e.g. 'signature') is a kappa vocabulary addition and must
    clear the architecture-vocabulary gate.

Either is defensible; NULL is not, because it collides with the migration escape.

Check the sibling languages for the same shape before fixing: any language whose
grammar has a bodyless declaration node reachable from an emitting extractor
(C function_declarator, Java abstract methods, TS method_signature / overload
declarations) may have the identical NULL hole. Fix the class, not the instance.

title: Standing rule: a metric derived from a mechanism must assert the mechanism fired, or it is inadmissible
description:
Two instances found 2026-07-27, in two repos, from opposite directions, in one day. That makes it a class rather than two incidents.

## The rule

A metric computed from a mechanism is only evidence if the mechanism actually ran. Otherwise the number is arithmetic wearing evidence's clothes, and — worse — it is usually the SAFE-LOOKING value: zero findings, zero dedup, all clean.

## Instance 1: the CDC dedup measurement (ley-line-open-b5faa9)

`records_over_min_chunk` is 0 on all three corpora. Largest `nodes.record` is 5,633 bytes against MIN_CHUNK 8,192, and `next_boundary` returns `data.len()` immediately for sub-minimum input. The GearHash NEVER FIRES. Every dedup figure measured on that target is the arithmetic of chunking things below the minimum chunk size — not a property of the content.

The harness reported real-looking ratios for weeks of design discussion before anyone asked whether the chunker had run. Now instrumented as gate F10c on ADR-0033 (bead b6653a): assert a nonzero fraction of inputs reach MIN_CHUNK.

## Instance 2: the smell-rule gate (this repo, TODAY, green right now)

`rs/tools/smell-projector/src/main.rs::run_rule`:

    // Check `Requires` — every named table must exist. Rules whose
    // tables don't exist are silently skipped (mirrors mache's
    // `--rule '*'` behavior).
    ...
    if exists.is_none() {
        return Ok(Vec::new());
    }

A rule whose required table is absent returns an EMPTY FINDING LIST — bit-identical to "the rule ran and found nothing." `task smells` then prints "25 finding(s), all covered by baseline" and exits 0.

This is worse than instance 1, because instance 1 produced a number a human had to interpret while this produces a GREEN CI GATE. Nobody can tell from the output whether 3 rules ran or 30.

## Why this class is hard to see

The failure is always silent and always looks like success. A rule that no-ops reports clean. A chunker that never reaches its floor reports zero dedup, which reads as "no duplicates existed." Both are the value you would get from a healthy system with nothing to report.

Related shape, same day, same repo: mutation gates generate zero mutants for SQL logic (c45244) — 41 mutants on chunked.rs, none touching its 49 SQL-bearing lines, gate green. And `lint:architecture-vocabulary` was green while three documented claims were false (ef5c5a). Four instances if you count loosely; the common factor is that the gate's own coverage is never asserted.

## What to do

1. Fix instance 2 — report skipped rules in the smell gate output and fail if the skip count changes unexpectedly. Small and immediate.
2. Adopt the rule for new gates: any count-reporting gate states its denominator. "25 findings across 30/30 rules" is admissible; "25 findings" is not.
3. Audit existing `task ci` gates against it — smells, mutants, doc-claims, blake3-lint, architecture-vocabulary.

## Close condition

cargo test -p smell-projector, plus the per-gate disablement check in acceptance_criteria.

title: fix: auto-size arena after parse — respect ADR-001 tiered strategy
description:
## Problem

The daemon's `--arena-size-mib` defaults to 64MB. For large projects (e.g., mache with 200+ Go files), the parsed .db exceeds the 32MB buffer capacity (64MB arena = 4KB header + two 32MB buffers). Users have to manually guess `--arena-size-mib`.

## Root cause

ADR-001 (memory arena design) describes a tiered sizing strategy: linear for <2MB, demand-paged for large. The current implementation uses a fixed default with no auto-sizing.

## Fix

After `cmd_parse` produces the .db, check its size. If it exceeds the arena's buffer capacity, grow the arena to fit:

```rust
let db_size = std::fs::metadata(&db_path)?.len();
let min_arena = ArenaHeader::HEADER_SIZE + db_size * 2 + (1024 * 1024); // header + 2 buffers + 1MB margin
let arena_bytes = arena_bytes.max(min_arena);
```

This respects the 64MB default for small projects but auto-grows for large ones. The arena file is sparse on APFS/ext4, so oversizing costs no physical storage until written.

## Why not change the default

The 64MB default is intentional per ADR-001 — it fits in a single huge page (2MB) boundary region and works for most single-file projections. Changing it would affect the network transport path (ley-line private) which sizes arenas to match sender expectations.

title: Sheaf value ablation study — quantify sheaf-driven vs naive invalidation precision (Phase 2-independent)
description:
The load-bearing claim v0.7.0 ships marketing on: **sheaf-based topology gives region-precise invalidation that beats naive "invalidate everything on file change".** Architecturally proven (loop closed, E2E test at PR #142); empirically unproven (no numbers on the precision delta).

This bead ships the empirical study **without waiting for ADR-0026 Phase 2** (consumer migration).

## The falsifiable claim

For a realistic file-change workload on a real corpus, sheaf-driven `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` (with the fine-grained region diff from PR #146) invalidates SIGNIFICANTLY FEWER regions than a naive "invalidate every known region" baseline.

Quantified target: sheaf-driven invalidation touches ≤ 30% of regions per changed-file event on average (i.e., naive over-invalidates by ≥ 3.3×).

If sheaf-driven touches ≥ 80% of regions on average, the sheaf topology isn't distinguishing enough — the moat claim is falsified.

## Method

### 1. Instrument the invalidate path

Wrap the fine-grained diff computation in `daemon/cmd_daemon.rs::emit_watcher_sheaf_invalidate` to log side-by-side:

- `sheaf_regions`: what the fine-grained diff computes (current behavior)
- `naive_regions`: what "invalidate every currently-known region" would emit (coarse-v1 fallback shape)
- `changed_files`: the input

Log format (JSON lines to `LEYLINE_SHEAF_ABLATION_LOG=<path>`):
```json
{"ts": "...", "changed_files": [...], "sheaf_count": N, "naive_count": M, "sheaf_region_ids": [...], "naive_region_ids": [...]}
```

Under `#[cfg(feature = "sheaf-ablation")]` or an env var — off by default.

### 2. Real-corpus workload

Use mache-self or LLO-self as the corpus (~500 files). Drive file changes via:
- Random single-file edits (100 events)
- Multi-file edits from real git commits (replay N recent commits)
- Rename-heavy changes (30 renames from git log)
- Directory-scoped changes (edit 10 files in the same dir)

Total: ~300-500 invalidation events across the workload shapes.

### 3. Report

`docs/research/sheaf-ablation-study.md`:

- Per-workload table: sheaf_avg_region_count vs naive_avg_region_count vs "over-invalidation ratio" (naive/sheaf)
- Distribution: histogram of `sheaf_count / naive_count` per event
- Failure modes: any events where sheaf > naive (should be zero; if not, that's a real bug)
- Verdict: load-bearing / marginal / falsified per the target ratios

### 4. Composition with rigor

Adversarial: run the study twice on the same corpus. Numbers within 10% delta across runs = reliable. Otherwise flag the measurement.

## What this bead does NOT deliver

- **NO consumer migration** — that's ADR-0026 Phase 2. This study is Phase-2-independent.
- **NO wall-time measurement** — that's Phase 2's F2 gate. This study measures PRECISION (region count), not SPEED.
- **NO changes to production behavior** — the ablation log is opt-in via env var / feature flag.
- **NO retune of sheaf topology** — if the study falsifies, that's a real signal that becomes its own follow-up bead.

## Three possible outcomes

- **Load-bearing (sheaf ≤ 30% of naive on average)**: moat quantified. Update marketing doc + release notes with the number. Ship confidence.
- **Marginal (sheaf 30-80% of naive)**: some precision win but not dramatic. Design review — is the topology tuning right? Is the workload representative?
- **Falsified (sheaf ≥ 80% of naive)**: topology isn't distinguishing. Follow-up: either (a) fix labeling / cell computation, (b) accept sheaf as architecturally clean but not a precision moat, (c) rip out the fine-grained diff and go back to coarse-v1.

All three are real information.

## Related

- Bead `5b58ff` — sheaf granularity dispatcher (Phase 2 study; this bead ships the Phase-2-independent precision study first)
- Bead `38e1cc` — HDC value hypothesis (parallel falsification study for HDC)
- Bead `e76959` — producer/consumer contract discipline (meta-lesson)
- PR #146 — fine-grained region diff (the machinery this ablation measures)
- PR #147 — unified topic (the code path this instruments)
- Bead `a3f764` (closed) — audit anchor; this bead adds the empirical layer

## Provenance

User directive 2026-07-10: "continue - we need to prove sheaf right?"

title: mache's record reader cannot distinguish "not my format" from "parsed fine" — silent wrong reads today, independent of the contract
description:
Split out of ley-line-open-edec5b on review feedback. edec5b is the CONTRACT work — deciding what `nodes.record` holds. This bead is the bug that exists TODAY regardless of how that contract lands.

## The defect

mache graph/sqlite.go:162-175 reads `nodes.record` as a JSON envelope:

    var rec struct {
        Data       string                     `json:"data"`
        Properties map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"properties"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(r.record.String), &rec); err == nil {
        if rec.Data != "" { node.Data = []byte(rec.Data) }
        if len(rec.Properties) > 0 { node.Properties = rec.Properties }
    }

The `err == nil` guard means a parse failure produces NO ERROR, NO LOG, and NO METRIC. The node simply comes back with empty Data and empty Properties.

Meanwhile mache internal/ingest/ast_walker_calls.go:341 reads the SAME column as a raw token — `SELECT n_leaf.record AS call_token` — and LLO writes raw content bytes through `String::from_utf8_lossy`. So the values reaching the JSON reader are frequently NOT JSON, and every one of those reads silently yields an empty node.

## Why this is separable from the contract

Whatever `record` turns out to hold, a reader that cannot distinguish "this is not my format" from "this parsed fine and was empty" is wrong. The contract decision changes WHICH values are valid; it does not make silent misinterpretation acceptable. Fixing the contract without fixing this leaves the same blindness pointed at a different set of values.

It is also the reason the mis-target went unnoticed for as long as it did: nothing anywhere reported that reads were coming back empty.

## Same class as the day's other findings

- Smell rules whose Requires table is absent returned an empty finding list, indistinguishable from clean (fixed, bddaf32)
- CDC dedup measured on inputs that never reach MIN_CHUNK, so the ratio is arithmetic (gate F10c, bead b6653a)
- Standing rule filed as ley-line-open-2607d2

In every case the failure is silent AND produces the safe-looking value. Here the safe-looking value is an empty node, which reads downstream as "this node has no properties" rather than "I could not read this node."

## Cross-repo

The fix lands in mache, not here — this bead exists so the LLO side of the contract work (edec5b) does not absorb it and quietly close it. Needs agreeing with mache rather than declaring at it.

Suggested shape: return a typed outcome from the envelope parse, count unrecognized records as a metric, and decide deliberately whether an unrecognized record is an error or an expected other-format value. The count is the minimum — it converts an invisible failure into an observable one without requiring the contract decision first.

## Close condition

Verified by the acceptance criteria's feed-a-raw-token check, plus a matching mache change.
acceptance_criteria: A reader encountering a `nodes.record` value it cannot interpret in its expected format produces a distinguishable outcome — an error, a counted metric, or a typed "unrecognized" result — rather than an empty success. Verified by feeding a raw AST token to the JSON-envelope path and confirming the result is not silently a node with zero Data and zero Properties. Cross-repo: needs a matching change in mache's graph/sqlite.go.

comments.text:
**Pivoting from apko/melange to krust.**

Re-attempted the apko/melange build per the existing Taskfile and hit two blockers that make this path unworkable for local dev on Apple Silicon:

1. **Workspace tmpdir leak.** `melange build` defaults `--source-dir` to `dirname(melange.yaml)` = repo root. It then recursively copies the entire repo (including `rs/target/`, `.git`, prior `./packages/`, and any prior `melange-workspace-*` that landed in CWD) into a new `/var/folders/.../T/melange-workspace-XXXX` tmpdir before any pipeline step runs. With `--rm` not passed, those workspaces persist across runs. We accumulated ~80 GB across 10 leaked dirs from interrupted sessions (largest: 30 GB). Each run also stalls during the copy on Docker Desktop's virtiofs (millions of small files = pathological).

2. **apko x86_64 step will fail.** `apko.yaml` declares `archs: [x86_64, aarch64]`, but the Taskfile only invokes `melange build --arch aarch64`. apko has no graceful-skip for missing arches; it errors out with `unable to select packages: ley-line-open (no such package)` for x86_64. Per chainguard-dev/apko#415.

Both are fixable in-place (add `--rm`, `--cache-dir`, `--workspace-dir`, explicit `--source-dir <small dir>` to melange; add `--arch aarch64` override to apko CLI). But for a Rust binary → distroless image, **krust is the better fit:**

- No docker daemon involved in the build → no virtiofs bottleneck, no workspace leaks
- Cargo cache survives across runs (`target/krust/`), so subsequent builds are seconds
- Native cross-compile from M-Mac for both amd64+arm64 via `cargo-zigbuild` (no qemu)
- Static musl binary + distroless `cgr.dev/chainguard/static:latest` base = ~few MB image
- Multi-arch manifest list "for free"

Tooling already on system (`zig`, `cargo-zigbuild`, `krust 0.0.1` all installed via brew/cargo).

What apko was giving us that needs alternate handling under krust:
- `leyline` user/uid/gid/`runAs`: chainguard/static ships nonroot uid 65532; or use `cgr.dev/chainguard/static:nonroot`
- `/data` writable mount, `HOME=/data`, `RUST_LOG=info` env, `cmd: daemon --mcp-port 8384`: runtime concerns, set in the deployment surface (cloister) or a thin entrypoint wrapper
- OCI annotations (title, description, license, source): krust supports via `[package.metadata.krust]` in Cargo.toml

**Updating bead scope: build + verify LLO OCI image via krust** (was: via apko/melange). Will keep the existing `apko.yaml`/`melange.yaml`/`Taskfile` `image` task on disk for now (not deleting yet) but treat them as broken/deferred until/unless we revisit for CI publishing.

**Closing — image build verified end-to-end via krust + docker.**

`task image:smoke` runs clean:
```
== tools/list ==
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"tools":[{"description":"Daemon lifecycle status: ...
```

- **`image.Dockerfile` added** — single COPY, sets `HOME=/tmp` and `RUST_LOG=info`, ENTRYPOINT `/usr/bin/leyline`, CMD `daemon --mcp-port 8384`.
- **Daemon code fix:** `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:272` hardcoded `127.0.0.1` bind, which made the MCP listener unreachable from the host even with `docker -p host:8384` (loopback-only). Added `--mcp-bind <IpAddr>` flag (default `127.0.0.1` for back-compat); container deployments pass `--mcp-bind 0.0.0.0`. Threaded through `cmd_daemon::run_daemon` → `daemon::mcp::spawn`. title: release.yml and release-dryrun.yml duplicate setup with nothing enforcing parity — the dry-run caught a bug and the fix went into the wrong file
description:
Filed 2026-07-29 after v0.12.1's image jobs failed for a reason that had
already been found, reported, and fixed — in the other file.

## What happened

`release-dryrun.yml` (added in #295, so the release path gets exercised on a
branch) failed its own first run with:

    capnp codegen failed (is `capnp` on PATH?)

`leyline-schema-capnp`'s build script shells out to the capnp compiler. I fixed
it in `release-dryrun.yml` and **never propagated it to `release.yml`'s image
job**, so v0.12.1's image failed on exactly the same error.

Note the shape: this is NOT a gate that lied. The dry-run did precisely its job
— surfaced a real missing dependency, on a branch, before a tag. The signal was
correct and I applied it to the wrong file. That is a different failure mode
from the rest of this week's findings and needs a different fix.

Consequence: the OCI image has now failed on two consecutive tags for two
DIFFERENT reasons — v0.12.0 on `cargo install krust` resolving to an unrelated
crates.io package, v0.12.1 on missing capnp. Both releases published their 29
binary/generator assets fine; only the image is absent.

## Why it will recur

`release.yml` and `release-dryrun.yml` deliberately share setup — same
toolchain pin, same system deps, same zig install, same Taskfile version —
because the dry-run's whole value is being a faithful rehearsal. But nothing
asserts they stay in step. Today I verified they match by COUNTING grep hits in
a terminal, which is a check that exists only in a conversation.

A dry-run that has drifted from the thing it rehearses is worse than none: it
reports green while exercising a different pipeline, which is the vacuous-pass
shape in a new place.

## Fix

The repo already does this exact thing for toolchains — `lint:toolchain-parity`
asserts every workflow's `toolchain:` equals `rust-toolchain.toml`'s `channel`,
and is wired into `task ci`. Extend that pattern rather than invent one:

Assert that for each setup concern the two workflows share, both declare it:
system deps (`capnproto libcapnp-dev pkg-config`), the zig toolchain install,
the `arduino/setup-task` version, and the Rust toolchain pin. Compare the
declared values, not merely presence — two files can both install capnp and
still disagree on the Taskfile version.

Better still where possible: move the shared setup somewhere single-sourced.
The system-deps block is three lines of apt; a composite action or a Taskfile
target invoked by both would make the duplication structural rather than
textual. Consider whether `task ci:system-deps` is the honest home, given this
repo's rule that workflows call `task` and never re-implement commands.

## Acceptance criteria

Deleting the capnp install from EITHER workflow fails `task ci`. Changing the
`setup-task` version in one and not the other fails `task ci`. Proven by making
each edit and observing the failure — not by reading the gate.

## Related

`ley-line-open-e44960` (image publishing, the thing that keeps failing),
`ley-line-open-2607d2` (assert the mechanism fired), `lint:toolchain-parity`
(the existing precedent to extend).

IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF (written 2026-07-29 by the coordinating session; design agreed with James). Everything an agent needs is in this comment — do not guess beyond it.

## Ground rules
- Base branch: `release-hardening` (NOT main). Branch from it, PR back into it. main is branch-protected and moves only by deliberate integration merges.
- Commit format: `[ley-line-open-2bea72] type(scope): description`.
- Run the FULL `task ci` locally before push (repo rule). Do not run `rsry` writes while `task ci` runs (beads.jsonl churn is tolerated since PR #300, but stay conservative).
- The repo rule this work enforces: workflows invoke `task` targets; they never re-implement commands.
- Related beads, same principle (derive from one source instead of hand-mirroring copies): ley-line-open-60f0d3 (generate MCP protocol facts from the pinned spec's schema.json), ley-line-open-ea1e42 (use tree-sitter-md's INLINE_LANGUAGE instead of re-implementing a backtick parser). Do not implement those here — this note exists so the gate's design stays consistent with them.

## The change, in one sentence
Move every inline package-install out of the workflows into single-source Taskfile `deps:*` targets, then add `lint:workflow-parity` (wired into `task ci`) asserting the structure that remains assertable, with a fixture test proving each acceptance mutation fails the gate.

## New files / targets

### 1. Taskfile.yml — add these targets (verbatim below, adjust indentation to file style). Place `deps:*` near `cache:sccache:install`; place `lint:workflow-parity` next to `lint:toolchain-parity`; wire BOTH `- task: lint:workflow-parity` (after lint:toolchain-parity) and `- task: ci:workflow-parity:fixture-test` (next to ci:attestation:fixture-test) into the `ci` task's cmds.

```yaml
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CI system dependencies (bead ley-line-open-2bea72)
  #
  # One copy of every install command, invoked by the workflows — the same rule
  # the rest of this repo already follows for build/test commands. v0.12.1
  # failed on a capnp install that existed in release-dryrun.yml but not
  # release.yml; two hand-mirrored copies of a command WILL drift, so there is
  # now one copy here. tools/lint_workflow_parity.sh (wired into `task ci`)
  # asserts the workflows actually call these and never inline an install.
  #
  # `sudo` is deliberate: these run on CI runners. Locally they work too, but
  # your package manager will ask for your password — that is the target doing
  # what it says, not a bug.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------

  deps:capnp:
    desc: |
      Install the capnp compiler + standard schema includes + pkg-config.
      `leyline-schema-capnp`'s build script shells out to the capnp compiler,
      and libcapnp-dev (brew: capnp) ships the standard includes that
      `import "/capnp/c++.capnp"` resolves against — the capnproto package
      alone is just the binaries. Single source for ci.yml, release.yml,
      release-dryrun.yml, and leyline-schema-go.yml.
    cmds:
      - |
        set -eu
        case "${RUNNER_OS:-$(uname -s)}" in
          Linux)
            sudo apt-get update
            sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends capnproto libcapnp-dev pkg-config
            ;;
          macOS|Darwin)
            brew install capnp pkg-config
            ;;
          *)
            echo "deps:capnp: unsupported OS '${RUNNER_OS:-$(uname -s)}'" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac
        capnp --version
        pkg-config --version

  deps:ci:
    desc: |
      Everything `task ci` compiles against on a Linux runner: the capnp
      toolchain plus libdbus-1-dev (keyring) and libfuse-dev (fuser).
      ci.yml calls this; the extras ride on deps:capnp's apt-get update.
    cmds:
      - task: deps:capnp
      - sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libdbus-1-dev libfuse-dev

  deps:fuse:
    desc: |
      FUSE headers for the leyline-fs staticlib build (`fuse` feature links
      libfuse3). release.yml's build job calls this only for matrix entries
      that carry lib_asset.
    cmds:
      - |
        set -eu
        case "${RUNNER_OS:-$(uname -s)}" in
          Linux)
            sudo apt-get update
            sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libfuse3-dev
            ;;
          macOS|Darwin)
            brew install --cask fuse-t
            ;;
          *)
            echo "deps:fuse: unsupported OS '${RUNNER_OS:-$(uname -s)}'" >&2
            exit 1
            ;;
        esac

  deps:zig:
    desc: |
      The zigbuild cross-toolchain the OCI image build compiles with, plus
      the musl rustup target. RUST_TARGET is required — the image jobs pass
      their matrix target; there is no safe default to guess.
    requires:
      vars: [RUST_TARGET]
    cmds:
      - cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked
      - python3 -m pip install --break-system-packages ziglang
      - rustup target add "{{.RUST_TARGET}}"

  deps:cargo-mutants:
    desc: |
      cargo-mutants from source with --locked — installed from source rather
      than a prebuilt-binary action because every action in this repo is
      SHA-pinned against a verified commit, and an unvetted third-party
      action isn't a trade this repo makes to save ~2 min.
    cmds:
      - cargo install cargo-mutants --locked

  lint:workflow-parity:
    desc: |
      Assert the workflows stay in step: no inline package installs (one copy
      lives in deps:* above), every release-pair job that installs Rust calls
      `task deps:capnp`, every image-building job calls `task deps:zig`, and
      all setup-task pins are exact and identical. The v0.12.1 image job
      failed on exactly the drift this closes — the dry-run caught the bug,
      the fix landed in the dry-run file only (ley-line-open-2bea72).
    cmds:
      - sh tools/lint_workflow_parity.sh

  ci:workflow-parity:fixture-test:
    desc: Prove the parity gate fails on each drift it exists to catch
    cmds:
      - sh tools/test_workflow_parity.sh
```

### 2. tools/lint_workflow_parity.sh (verbatim starting point — iterate if the awk needs fixing, but keep all four rules and the WORKFLOWS_DIR override)

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Workflow parity gate (bead ley-line-open-2bea72).
#
# release-dryrun.yml exists so the release path gets rehearsed on a PR — which
# only means something if the two workflows run the SAME setup. v0.12.1 proved
# what happens when they drift: the dry-run caught the missing capnp install on
# a branch, the fix went into the dry-run file only, and the tag failed on the
# bug the rehearsal had already found. The signal was right; nothing enforced
# that both copies heard it.
#
# The durable half of the fix is structural: install commands live in Taskfile
# `deps:*` targets, so there is one copy to edit (same rule as everything else
# in this repo — workflows invoke task, they never re-implement commands).
# This gate asserts the facts that remain assertable after that move:
#
#   1. No workflow inlines a package install (apt-get/brew/cargo/pip). One
#      copy in the Taskfile, or it will drift.
#   2. In the release pair, every job that installs Rust also runs
#      `task deps:capnp` — installing a compiler means compiling the
#      workspace, and the workspace's capnp build script needs system deps.
#   3. In the release pair, every job that runs a `task image*` build target
#      also runs `task deps:zig` — the image build cross-compiles with
#      zigbuild.
#   4. Every arduino/setup-task pin is exact and identical across ALL
#      workflows — a floating or divergent go-task version is the same class
#      of drift rust-toolchain.toml exists to close.
#
# WORKFLOWS_DIR is overridable so tools/test_workflow_parity.sh can prove each
# rule fails on the mutation it guards against, not just that this file exists.
set -eu

dir=${WORKFLOWS_DIR:-.github/workflows}
fail=0

# --- Rule 1: no inline installs anywhere -----------------------------------
# Comment lines are stripped first: the history of the krust failure is TOLD
# in comments that legitimately contain the words `cargo install`.
inline=$(
    for wf in "$dir"/*.yml; do
        sed 's/#.*$//' "$wf" |
            grep -nE '(apt-get|brew|pip[0-9.]*|pip3) install|cargo install' |
            sed "s|^|$wf:|" || true
    done
)
if [ -n "$inline" ]; then
    echo "workflow-parity: inline package installs found — move the command into a" >&2
    echo "Taskfile deps:* target and invoke it, so there is one copy to keep true:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$inline" >&2
    fail=1
fi

# --- Rules 2+3: per-job structure of the release pair ----------------------
# Job boundaries in this repo's workflows are 2-space-indented keys under
# `jobs:`. The awk tracks the current job and what it contains, then emits
# one line per violation.
for wf in "$dir"/release.yml "$dir"/release-dryrun.yml; do
    test -f "$wf" || { echo "workflow-parity: $wf is missing" >&2; fail=1; continue; }
    violations=$(awk '
        function flush() {
            if (job == "") return
            if (has_rust && !has_capnp)
                print job ": installs a Rust toolchain but never runs task deps:capnp"
            if (has_image && !has_zig)
                print job ": runs a task image build target but never runs task deps:zig"
        }
        /^jobs:/       { injobs = 1; next }
        injobs && /^[a-z]/ { injobs = 0 }   # left the jobs: block entirely
        injobs && /^  [A-Za-z0-9_-]+:[ ]*$/ {
            flush()
            job = $1; sub(":", "", job)
            has_rust = has_capnp = has_image = has_zig = 0
            next
        }
        injobs && /rust-toolchain@/   { has_rust = 1 }
        injobs && /task deps:capnp/   { has_capnp = 1 }
        injobs && /run:.*task image(:publish)? / { has_image = 1 }
        injobs && /task deps:zig/     { has_zig = 1 }
        END { flush() }
    ' "$wf")
    if [ -n "$violations" ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$violations" | sed "s|^|workflow-parity: $wf: job |" >&2
        fail=1
    fi
done

# --- Rule 4: setup-task pins exact and identical ----------------------------
pins=$(
    for wf in "$dir"/*.yml; do
        awk '
            /arduino\/setup-task@/ { want = 1 }
            want && /version:/ {
                v = $0; sub(/.*version:[ ]*/, "", v); sub(/[ ]*#.*$/, "", v)
                print FILENAME ":" v; want = 0
            }
        ' "$wf"
    done
)
if [ -n "$pins" ]; then
    versions=$(printf '%s\n' "$pins" | cut -d: -f2- | sort -u)
    count=$(printf '%s\n' "$versions" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
    if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then
        echo "workflow-parity: setup-task versions diverge across workflows:" >&2
        printf '%s\n' "$pins" >&2
        fail=1
    fi
    case "$versions" in
        *x*|latest|"")
            echo "workflow-parity: setup-task pin '$versions' is floating — pin an exact version" >&2
            fail=1
            ;;
    esac
fi

if [ "$fail" != 0 ]; then
    echo "--- fix: install commands belong in Taskfile deps:* targets; the release" >&2
    echo "pair must call them from every job that compiles; setup-task pins must" >&2
    echo "be exact and shared. See bead ley-line-open-2bea72." >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "workflow parity OK — no inline installs, release pair calls deps targets, setup-task pins agree"
```

### 3. tools/test_workflow_parity.sh (verbatim starting point)

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Proves the workflow-parity gate fails on each drift it exists to catch
# (bead ley-line-open-2bea72). The acceptance criteria are the mutations the
# v0.12.x releases actually suffered: a dep install deleted from one file of
# the release pair, and a setup pin changed in one file but not the other.
# "Prove by making each edit, not by reading the gate" — this makes each edit
# on a copy of the REAL workflows, every run.
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH='' cd -P -- "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd -P)
tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/leyline-workflow-parity.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' 0 1 2 15

lint="$repo_root/tools/lint_workflow_parity.sh"

reset_fixture() {
    rm -rf "$tmp_dir/workflows"
    cp -R "$repo_root/.github/workflows" "$tmp_dir/workflows"
}

expect_pass() {
    if ! WORKFLOWS_DIR="$tmp_dir/workflows" "$lint" > /dev/null; then
        echo "workflow-parity gate failed on the unmutated workflows: $1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

expect_fail() {
    if WORKFLOWS_DIR="$tmp_dir/workflows" "$lint" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "workflow-parity gate PASSED a mutation it exists to catch: $1" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
}

# The gate must pass the real, unmutated workflows — otherwise every assertion
# below proves nothing.
reset_fixture
expect_pass "baseline"

# Acceptance 1: deleting the capnp deps call from EITHER file fails.
reset_fixture
grep -v 'task deps:capnp' "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml" > "$tmp_dir/m" \
    && mv "$tmp_dir/m" "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml"
expect_fail "deps:capnp deleted from release.yml"

reset_fixture
grep -v 'task deps:capnp' "$tmp_dir/workflows/release-dryrun.yml" > "$tmp_dir/m" \
    && mv "$tmp_dir/m" "$tmp_dir/workflows/release-dryrun.yml"
expect_fail "deps:capnp deleted from release-dryrun.yml"

# Acceptance 2: changing the setup-task pin in one file and not the other fails.
reset_fixture
sed 's/version: 3\.[0-9.]*/version: 3.999.0/' "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml" > "$tmp_dir/m" \
    && mv "$tmp_dir/m" "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml"
expect_fail "setup-task pin diverged in release.yml only"

# A floating pin is drift waiting to happen even when both files carry it.
reset_fixture
for wf in "$tmp_dir/workflows"/*.yml; do
    sed 's/version: 3\.[0-9.]*/version: 3.x/' "$wf" > "$tmp_dir/m" && mv "$tmp_dir/m" "$wf"
done
expect_fail "setup-task pin floated to 3.x everywhere"

# The zig toolchain is the other install the image jobs cannot run without.
reset_fixture
grep -v 'task deps:zig' "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml" > "$tmp_dir/m" \
    && mv "$tmp_dir/m" "$tmp_dir/workflows/release.yml"
expect_fail "deps:zig deleted from release.yml image job"

# Reintroducing an inline install — the drift vector the deps:* move closed —
# must fail no matter which workflow it lands in.
reset_fixture
printf '      - name: sneak an inline install back in\n        run: sudo apt-get install -y capnproto\n' \
    >> "$tmp_dir/workflows/ci.yml"
expect_fail "inline apt-get install reintroduced in ci.yml"

reset_fixture
printf '      - name: sneak a cargo install back in\n        run: cargo install cargo-zigbuild --locked\n' \
    >> "$tmp_dir/workflows/release-dryrun.yml"
expect_fail "inline cargo install reintroduced in release-dryrun.yml"

echo "workflow-parity fixture proved the gate fails on every drift it guards against"
```

## Workflow edits (the call-site migration)

Constraint that applies everywhere: the `arduino/setup-task` step MUST come before any `task deps:*` step in the same job. Where it currently comes after the install step, move the setup-task step up — it is independent of everything before it.

1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the "Install system deps" step (installs capnproto libcapnp-dev libdbus-1-dev libfuse-dev pkg-config) becomes `run: task deps:ci`. setup-task currently comes AFTER it — move setup-task above.
2. `.github/workflows/release.yml`:
   - build job: "Install system deps" (case Linux/macOS) → `run: task deps:capnp`. setup-task is currently AFTER this step (~line 129) — move it above.
   - build job: "Install FUSE deps (staticlib only)" → `run: task deps:fuse` (keep the `if: matrix.lib_asset` condition).
   - image job: "Install system deps" → `run: task deps:capnp`.
   - image job: "Install zig toolchain" → `run: task deps:zig RUST_TARGET="${{ matrix.rust_target }}"` (delete the step's env: RUST_TARGET block; pass as task var).
3. `.github/workflows/release-dryrun.yml`:
   - stage job: capnp install step → `run: task deps:capnp`.
   - image job: capnp install step → `run: task deps:capnp`.
   - image job: zig install step → `run: task deps:zig RUST_TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`.
4. `.github/workflows/mutants.yml`: "Install cargo-mutants" (`cargo install cargo-mutants --locked`) → `run: task deps:cargo-mutants`. setup-task currently comes AFTER — move it above.
5. `.github/workflows/leyline-schema-go.yml`: has NO setup-task step today. Add the SHA-pinned setup-task step (copy the exact `uses:` SHA + version + repo-token from ci.yml) before the capnp install, then replace the install block with `run: task deps:capnp`. (Note: this workflow's inline copy had already drifted — it was missing pkg-config. That drift is the point of this bead.)
- Keep the surrounding comments in the workflows where they explain WHY (e.g. the krust history in release.yml's image job); delete only the comment lines that narrate the now-removed inline commands.

## Traps, known
- release.yml's `image-manifest` job runs `task image:manifest` but must NOT require deps:zig (it assembles manifests, compiles nothing). The lint's rule-3 regex `task image(:publish)? ` is written to exclude it — do not "simplify" that regex.
- Leave release-dryrun.yml's `paths:` filter alone; the parity gate runs in `task ci` on every PR, not in the dryrun workflow.
- After the edits, `grep -rn "apt-get install\|brew install\|cargo install\|pip install" .github/workflows/*.yml` must return ONLY comment lines (the lint strips comments before matching — verify it passes).

## Acceptance (all four, prove by running, not by reading)
1. `sh tools/test_workflow_parity.sh` green — it mutates copies of the REAL workflows, proving: deleting the capnp deps call from EITHER release workflow fails the gate; changing setup-task's version in one file fails; floating the pin fails; deleting deps:zig fails; reintroducing an inline install fails.
2. `task lint:workflow-parity` green against the real tree.
3. Full `task ci` green (includes both the lint and the fixture test once wired).
4. The five workflow files contain zero non-comment inline installs.

## Close condition
PR into release-hardening with all acceptance green. Comment on this bead with the PR number and paste the fixture test's final output line. Do NOT close the bead until the PR is merged.

title: post-push bead-sync hook is a silent no-op on SQLite stores — beads.jsonl drifts unbacked
description:
The tracked ledger .beads/beads.jsonl is the committed source of truth; .beads/beads.db is gitignored. The installed .git/hooks/post-push rsry-managed block only syncs a Dolt store at .beads/dolt/$REPO, which does not exist in this repo (migrated to SQLite per ADR-0021 / bead ley-line-open-8d47b2). The guard is 'if [ -d "$BEADS_DIR" ]', so the hook exits silently and NOTHING keeps beads.jsonl in sync.

Observed 2026-07-27 on main @ 353dd07: the DB held 388 beads, the committed JSONL held 362. 26 beads existed ONLY in the gitignored DB — including ley-line-open-ef5c1d (p0, open) and the whole CDC review/follow-up thread (ef5c84, e6fb3e, bd8d33, 11a9b0). Two further beads (8d47b2, dc6fbf) were done in the DB and open in the JSONL. Prior sync had been done by hand in ad-hoc chore(beads) commits (2cad404, 38f439d, 41541f6), which is why drift between them is unbounded.

Secondary finding: the bulk restore in 41541f6 flattened created_at/updated_at for 82 beads to the restore timestamp (2026-07-22T20:34:12.49xxxx). The SQLite store retained true per-bead timestamps, so re-exporting repairs that provenance.

title: Expose leyline-cli-lib features through leyline-cli + add `all` meta-feature + install:full task
description:
`leyline-cli` currently exposes only `lsp`/`mount`/`vec`. Consumers can't reach `validate`, `hdc`, or `text-search` features via the CLI binary because `leyline-cli` has `default-features = false` on the cli-lib dep and doesn't pass those through.

## What ships

### 1. `rs/ll-open/cli/Cargo.toml` — expose all cli-lib features

- Add pass-through features: `validate`, `hdc`, `text-search`
- Bump `default = ["lsp"]` → `default = ["lsp", "validate", "hdc"]` to match cli-lib's baseline (pure-Rust, no system deps)
- Add `all` meta-feature: `["lsp", "mount", "vec", "validate", "hdc", "text-search"]`

### 2. `Taskfile.yml` — add `install:full` target

- `task install` stays lean (default)
- `task install:full` builds `--features all` for users who want the whole daemon-op surface

## Why not make `all` the default

- `mount` requires libfuse-t (macOS) / libfuse (Linux) — system deps break portability
- `vec` pulls fastembed + downloads ONNX model at first use — big + network
- Keeping default lean matches library-consumer expectations

## Why bump default to include validate + hdc

- Both are pure Rust; no system deps
- cli-lib already treats them as baseline (`default = ["lsp", "validate", "hdc"]`)
- Currently cli's minimal default silently omits daemon ops consumers may expect

## Non-goals

- No feature-set changes to `leyline-cli-lib` itself — only cli-side pass-throughs
- No new daemon ops
- No wire-format changes

## Rules

- Commit prefix `[ley-line-open-<this-bead-id>]`
- `task ci` green
- Verify: `cargo build --release -p leyline-cli --features all` compiles clean

## Provenance

User question 2026-07-09: "what should i run with task install to get all features? and should taht be default?"
acceptance_criteria: leyline-cli exposes lsp/mount/vec/validate/hdc/text-search + all meta-feature; default = lsp+validate+hdc; task install:full uses --features all; task ci green

title: Σ Phase 3: migrate 4 Group A blake3::hash sites onto ContentAddressed::hash
description:
## Context

Phases 0+1 (PR #47, characterization tests + audit) and Phase 2 (PR #48, `impl ContentAddressed for [u8]`) are merged. Phase 3 is the mechanical migration — replace inline `blake3::hash(bytes).into()` with `bytes.hash()` at the 4 Group A sites identified in the audit doc.

## Sites (per `docs/audits/2026-05-blake3-retrofit-audit.md`)

| File | Line | Function | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rs/ll-open/fs/src/lib.rs` | 82 | `verify_arena_root` (read-side) | `let actual: [u8; 32] = blake3::hash(data).into();` |
| `rs/ll-open/fs/src/graph.rs` | 954 | `flush_to_arena` | `let new_root: [u8; 32] = blake3::hash(&bytes).into();` |
| `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_load.rs` | 63 | `load_into_arena` | `let current_root: [u8; 32] = blake3::hash(db_bytes).into();` |
| `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs` | 734 | `snapshot_to_arena` | `let current_root: [u8; 32] = blake3::hash(&db_bytes).into();` |

## Retrofit pattern

```rust
// before
let new_root: [u8; 32] = blake3::hash(&bytes).into();
ctrl.set_arena_with_root(&arena_path, arena_size, new_root)?;

// after
use leyline_core::ContentAddressed;
let new_root = bytes.hash();
ctrl.set_arena_with_root(&arena_path, arena_size, *new_root.as_bytes())?;
```

The `set_arena_with_root` signature still takes `[u8; 32]` (per `Controller::set_arena_with_root` on `rs/ll-core/core/src/control.rs:311`); `Hash::as_bytes()` returns `&[u8; 32]`, dereferenced with `*` for the by-value param.

## NOT in scope

- `rs/ll-open/fs/src/graph.rs:1449` — inside `#[test] fn hotswap_zero_root_serves_empty_then_swaps_on_publish`. Test code legitimately computes BLAKE3 as oracle; stays inline (per audit Group B/C/test classification).
- Group B sites (hdc/sheaf.rs) — sheaf merkle, different semantic; stay inline per audit F5.
- Group C site (hdc/util.rs blake3_seed) — returns u64 not Hash; stays inline.
- `RootSigner` wiring (Phase 5 in original ladder; separate bead).
- Phase 4 lint gate forbidding new inline sites (separate follow-up).

## Verification gates

Existing tests are the zero-change contract:
- `fs/tests/characterization_blake3_sites.rs` — sites 3 + 4 exact-hash pins.
- `cli-lib/tests/characterization_blake3_sites.rs` — site 1 exact-hash + idempotence.
- `cli-lib/tests/integration.rs::snapshot_populates_current_root_with_blake3_of_db_bytes` — site 2 exact-hash.
- `rs/ll-core/core/src/substrate.rs::content_addressed_matches_inline_blake3_byte_for_byte` — proves `bytes.hash() == blake3::hash(bytes).into()`.

`task ci` MUST pass on the migrated branch with zero test changes. Any test that breaks during the migration is a behavior change, not a refactor — investigate.

## Depends on

- `ley-line-open-e7b983` (Phase 0+1, merged PR #47)
- `ley-line-open-082202` (Phase 2, merged PR #48)

title: epic: LLO as composable base layer — LL enriches, mache consumes
description:
## Problem

ley-line-open (LLO) and ley-line (LL) have no defined composition model. LLO produces base .db files (nodes + _ast + _source). LL has additional capabilities (LSP enrichment, embeddings, sheaf cache) that should layer on top. Mache should be ignorant of which produced the .db — it just checks for table presence.

## Design Principle

The .db file IS the interface contract. Tables are the API:
- **Base (LLO):** nodes, _ast, _source — always present
- **LSP enrichment (LL or LLO lsp crate):** _lsp, _lsp_hover, _lsp_defs, _lsp_refs — optional
- **Cross-refs (LL or mache build):** node_refs, node_defs — optional
- **Embeddings (LL only):** vector index sidecar — optional
- **Sheaf (LL only):** cache/invalidation metadata — optional

Mache never imports LL or LLO. It queries sqlite_master for table presence and activates features accordingly. This is already how useNodesTable works — extend the pattern.

## Decomposition

1. [DONE] `ll-open parse` — base .db producer (bead ley-line-open-6dc367)
2. `ll-open enrich-lsp` — LSP enrichment subcommand using the lsp/ crate
3. Cross-ref extraction — populate node_refs/node_defs from _ast queries
4. Composition interface — define how LL layers its private enrichments on an LLO base .db without LLO needing to know about LL
5. Pipeline orchestration — who calls what in what order (ll-open parse → ll-open enrich-lsp → leyline enrich-embed → mache mount)

title: ll-open enrich-lsp subcommand — LSP enrichment into existing .db
description:
Add `ll-open enrich-lsp` subcommand that takes an existing .db (produced by `ll-open parse`) and enriches it with _lsp, _lsp_hover, _lsp_defs, _lsp_refs tables by spawning language servers via the lsp/ crate.

The lsp/ crate (client.rs, protocol.rs) already supports: document_symbols, definition, references, hover, completion, diagnostics. This subcommand wires those into the .db enrichment pipeline.

**Why:** mache's serve_lsp.go and serve_handlers.go fall back to _lsp_defs/_lsp_refs tables when present. Pre-baking these avoids live LSP at mount time.

comments.text: The enrichment framework is in place (557e8a4): EnrichmentPass trait, op_enrich UDS op, dependency resolution. What remains: implement the actual LspEnrichmentPass that spawns language servers and populates _lsp* tables. This is a ley-line private pass registered via DaemonExt::enrichment_passes().

title: cross-ref extraction — populate node_refs/node_defs from _ast
description:
Add a pass (either in `ll-open parse` or as a separate `ll-open enrich-refs` subcommand) that queries the _ast table for call_expression, selector_expression, import_spec etc. and populates node_refs (token, node_id) and node_defs (token, dir_id) tables.

These tables power mache's callers/callees graph (GetCallers/GetCallees in sqlite_graph.go). Currently only populated by mache's SitterWalker (CGO path) or `mache build`. Having ll-open produce them means mache can skip CGO entirely for the refs path too.

**Why:** mache's fast path already checks for node_refs in the main DB (sqlite_graph.go:149). If present, it skips the sidecar .refs.db entirely.

title: witchcraft: len() overcounts on replace-by-node_id (was_present deadcoded)
description:
## Bug

In `rs/ll-open/text-search/src/witchcraft.rs::upsert`, the `was_present` computation is structurally `false`:

```rust
let was_present = inner.count > 0 && {
    // Heuristic: ...
    false
};
```

`expr && { false }` evaluates to `false` regardless of `expr`, so `was_present` is always `false`. The subsequent `if !was_present { inner.count += 1; }` increments `count` on every upsert — including `INSERT OR REPLACE` paths where `witchcraft::DB::add_doc` overwrites an existing row by uuid.

## Impact

After re-upserting the same N `node_id`s with refreshed content (a normal corpus-reindex pattern), `len()` reports ~2N for N actual rows. Trait docstring in `lib.rs::len()` promises "Number of distinct `node_id`s currently in the index" — strict contract violated.

## Fix options

1. **Probe before increment**: `let existed = inner.db.contains(&uuid); ...; if !existed { inner.count += 1; }` — one extra SELECT per upsert, exact contract.
2. **Loosen trait doc**: rename to `len_approx` or `upsert_event_count` and update the doc to "monotonic, may overcount under replace" — cheaper but callers can't rely on it for index size.

(1) is preferred — substrate is small enough that the extra read is fine, and downstream callers (rosary's witchcraft consumer, see rosary-e1760d) expect exact counts.

## Surfaced

PR #31 review, 2026-05-18.

comments.text: Stale — bug fixed. Verified 2026-06-25 at `rs/ll-open/text-search/src/witchcraft.rs:169,192`. `was_present` is now `let was_present = document_contains(&inner.db, &uuid)?;` — a real SQL existence check, not the dead `expr && { false }` pattern. The `if !was_present { inner.count += 1; }` paths at lines 174-176 now correctly increment only on genuine inserts. Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: composition interface — LL enrichment hook on LLO base .db
description:
Define how ley-line (private) layers enrichments onto an LLO-produced .db without LLO needing to know about LL. The .db file is the contract — LL opens it, adds tables (embeddings, sheaf cache), closes it. LLO never imports LL. LL imports LLO as a dependency.

The answer is probably: no code needed in LLO. The .db schema IS the interface. Document the table contracts and let LL do whatever it wants. This bead is about writing that documentation and validating the approach with a round-trip test (LLO parse → LL enrich → mache mount).

**Why:** Without this, LL vs LLO boundary stays undefined and features drift apart.

comments.text: The composition interface is now mechanically solved: DaemonExt::enrichment_passes() lets LL register passes with disjoint write sets. EnrichmentPass trait enforces reads()/writes() declaration. The framework is committed (557e8a4). What remains: write the TABLE_CONTRACT.md documenting which tables each layer owns.

title: release.yml: macos-13 runner perma-queued — cross-compile darwin-amd64 from macos-latest instead
description:
## Problem

`.github/workflows/release.yml`'s `build leyline-darwin-amd64` job uses `os: macos-13` (Intel hosted runner). For both v0.4.0 (tagged 2026-05-16) and v0.4.1 (tagged 2026-05-17), this job sits in `status=queued` indefinitely and never executes — verified via `gh api repos/agentic-research/ley-line-open/actions/runs/<id>/jobs`.

Result: both releases ship 3-of-4 binaries (`leyline-darwin-arm64`, `leyline-linux-amd64`, `leyline-linux-arm64`) — Intel Mac users have no binary download path. The top-level workflow status is permanently "queued" because GitHub waits forever on the stalled job.

The macos-13 hosted runner pool is heavily oversubscribed on the free tier and has been deprecated for newer projects.

## Fix

Switch `os: macos-13` to `os: macos-latest` (arm64) and rely on rust cross-compile via `target: x86_64-apple-darwin`. The existing `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` step already passes `targets: ${{ matrix.target }}`, so it'll install the x86_64-apple-darwin cross target. Apple's clang on macos-arm64 handles both archs natively (no extra linker config).

5-line diff in `.github/workflows/release.yml`:

```yaml
# Before
- os: macos-13
  target: x86_64-apple-darwin
  asset: leyline-darwin-amd64
# After
- os: macos-latest
  target: x86_64-apple-darwin
  asset: leyline-darwin-amd64
```

## Falsifiability

- Open a PR with the matrix change
- After merge, cut a release tag (could be v0.4.2-rc1 to validate, or fold into the next real release v0.4.2)
- Assert: `gh release view <tag> --json assets --jq '.assets | length'` returns 4, not 3
- Assert: the `build leyline-darwin-amd64` job completes within 30 minutes (vs queued >21h today)
- If the build succeeds but the resulting binary doesn't actually run on Intel Macs, the test is `file leyline-darwin-amd64` should show `Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64` — currently we can't even produce the binary to test

## Scope

Single-file change in `.github/workflows/release.yml`. No code changes. No tests affected.

Implementation done. The falsifiability gate (4-binary release vs 3) will be exercised at the next release tag — assert `gh release view <tag> --json assets --jq '.assets | length' == 4`. If still 3, reopen + file follow-up.

Closing as work is committed; validation deferred to next release event.

title: schema-bridge tooldefs: close the field-name + nested/free-form-object + numeric-bounds gaps blocking rosary's MCP registry
description:
Follow-up from rosary-08a278 (ADR-0006 revival). The `tooldefs` emitter (PR #232, ley-line-open-beb8bb) reproduces flat single-word-field tools, but 5 gaps block reproducing the rest of rosary's 41-tool MCP surface through the REAL `capnp compile → capnpc-schema-bridge-tooldefs` pipeline:

1. **snake_case field names (load-bearing).** `capnp compile` errors on underscores in field names ("declaration names ... must not contain underscores"), and the tooldefs emitter uses the capnp field name verbatim as the JSON property name — no camelCase→snake_case conversion, and it does not honor `$Json.name` (parse_field_annotations rejects it as UnmappedConstruct). So every rosary tool with a `repo_path`/`issue_type`/`test_files`/`comment_id`/`bead_id`/… field (nearly all of them, incl. `rsry_bead_create`) cannot be authored in a real .capnp. NOTE: the existing `bead_create_tooldefs_matches_live_tools_rs` fixture passes only because it pokes raw field-name bytes into a hand-built CodeGeneratorRequest, bypassing the capnp frontend — it does NOT prove bead_create round-trips through the plugin. Fix options: honor capnp `$Json.name("repo_path")` in the tooldefs/jsonschema emitters, OR add a `$name`/`$wireName` trait to _traits.capnp, OR apply a deterministic camelCase→snake_case conversion. Whichever lands must be proven by a fixture that goes through actual `capnp compile` (compile a real .capnp fixture, not poked bytes).
2. **Inline nested objects** (rosary `session_ref: {type:object, properties:{provider,id}, required:[…]}`). Struct-typed fields emit `"$ref":"#/$defs/…"`, and tooldefs has no `$defs` bag → dangling ref. Need inline object expansion for tool inputSchemas.
3. **Free-form objects** (`payload: {type:object, additionalProperties:true}`). capnp has no any-object type; needs a trait (e.g. `$JsonObject`) the emitter lowers to an open object.
4. **Array-of-object** (`rsry_bead_import.beads`: List of inline object).
5. **Numeric bounds** (`rsry_bead_search.limit: minimum:1, maximum:50`). No `$min`/`$max` trait; emitter only emits `minimum:0` for UInt.

Acceptance: `cargo test -p leyline-schema-bridge` gains fixtures — compiled through real `capnp compile` — that reproduce rsry_bead_create (snake_case fields), rsry_dispatch_record (nested session_ref), rsry_agent_run_event_record (payload free-form object), rsry_bead_import (array-of-object), and rsry_bead_search (numeric bounds) structurally against their live tools.rs entries.

title: feat: open daemon with UDS protocol + DaemonExt trait
description:
Add a `daemon` subcommand to leyline-cli-lib that runs the full coordination daemon: arena + mount + UDS socket + event router. Base ops (status, flush, load, query, reparse, subscribe) use only open crates. ley-line (private) extends via a `DaemonExt` trait to add sheaf, embed, network ops.

title: 5f7100-7a: lazy LSP enrichment runs on UDS thread (60f75d follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to ley-line-open-60f75d. Per-file timeout landed at cbca333 (#1 of 3 acceptance criteria). This bead tracks #2: move the enrichment off the UDS connection thread.

**Current behavior**: `op_lsp_hover` calls `with_lazy_enrich_retry` which (post-606e64 fix) drops the live_db lock then calls `try_enrich_file` synchronously on the same thread that's handling the UDS request. With LSP enrichment taking 1-5 seconds (per-file timeout), one slow `lsp_hover` head-of-line-blocks every other UDS op.

**Desired behavior**: `try_enrich_file` queues the work to a background tokio task and returns immediately with `enriched=false`. The hover op returns the current (empty) data; the background task populates `_lsp` for the next request. Optionally: the hover can wait via `Notify` for a bounded time (~100ms) to let the enrichment complete in the common-case fast path.

**Files**: rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs, rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mod.rs (DaemonContext gains a background-enrichment-tx channel or JoinSet), rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs (spawn the consumer task)

**Acceptance**:
- op_lsp_hover returns within UDS round-trip latency (~ms) regardless of LSP enrichment state
- background enrichment populates _lsp asynchronously
- pin test: 50 concurrent hovers on different files, p99 < 100ms (timeout-bounded by the wait, not by the enrichment)

**Related**: 5f7100-7b (LSP server pool) is the natural sibling — both reduce per-call cost.

comments.text:
[2026-05-08] Shipped at commit f6890a6.

**Change**: `try_enrich_file` now queues via `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and returns within microseconds. Pre-fix held `live_db.lock()` for 1-5s synchronously on the UDS thread.

**Behavior**:
- `op_lsp_hover` returns immediately with current (empty) data + `enriched: true` (retry hint).

title: Dual-codec daemon UDS wire: binary capnp + JSON via magic-byte dispatch
description:
Filed 2026-05-12 after b0ea2e (capnp-json wire codec) lands. P2 feature. Natural step 4 in the daemon-typed-wire decade.

## Why this is the right shape

After b0ea2e, `daemon.capnp` is the typed contract and `wire.rs` is gone — every handler builds a `capnp::message::Builder` and calls `capnp_json::to_json(reader)` to emit. The encoding is now a one-line swap per handler:

```rust
// JSON (post-b0ea2e):  capnp_json::to_json(reader)
// Binary:              capnp::serialize::write_message_to_words(reader)
```

The hard part (typed Builders, schema-as-SSOT, fixture gate) is done. Dual-codec is a pure carrier-layer change.

## What we'd gain with binary on the wire

- True ZC on receive — mache could borrow segment bytes directly, same way it consumes substrate segment files today
- No Int64-as-string awkwardness
- No "generation/last_reparse_at_ms emit `"0"` forever because UInt64 default is 0" issue
- No `enrichment` double-encoding (open-ended JSON inside Text)
- Faster — skip the parse step
- Homogeneous encoding — substrate and wire use the same canonical capnp bytes

## What we'd lose (preserved via dual-codec)

- Shell debuggability (`nc -U default.sock <<< '{"op":"status"}'`) — kept via the JSON path
- MCP HTTP transport stays JSON (external MCP spec) — naturally routes to JSON codec
- mache JSON path keeps working — opt-in to binary incrementally

## Implementation sketch

**Magic-byte dispatch** in `socket.rs`:
- capnp segment format starts with a 32-bit segment count (typically `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00` or `0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00`) — never `{`
- JSON line-delimited starts with `{` (or whitespace+`{` for pretty input)
- Server peeks first byte, routes to JSON or capnp handler
- ~50 lines in `socket.rs`

**Handler finalizer switch**: each handler today calls `capnp_json::to_json(reader)`. Refactor to return the typed `Reader` instead of a serialized String; the dispatcher picks the finalizer:

```rust
match codec {
    Codec::Json => capnp_json::to_json(reader)?,
    Codec::Binary => {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        capnp::serialize::write_message(&mut out, &builder)?;
        // length-prefix or stream-framed
        out
    }
}
```

~3 lines per handler; the Builder construction is shared.

**Framing nuance**: JSON is line-delimited (`\n` terminator). Binary capnp needs explicit length prefix OR capnp's stream-framed format (segment-table prefix). Pick one and document.

**Fixture gate extension**:
- Keep `daemon-protocol.json` with JSON `response` examples per op
- Add `tests/fixtures/daemon-protocol/<op>.bin` files (T8.10 substrate pattern, already known)
- Both Rust + Go gates decode both formats; assertion is "produces same typed struct"

## Acceptance

- `task ci` green with both codecs exercised
- `echo '{"op":"status"}' | nc -U <ctrl.uds>` still produces parseable JSON (back-compat)
- A new `--codec=binary` daemon flag (or per-connection negotiation) routes binary capnp on UDS
- mache client demonstrates binary path with measurable round-trip-time improvement
- README + ADR-0014 status section updated to reflect both codecs supported; binary is preferred for typed consumers, JSON for shell/debug/MCP-HTTP

## Forcing functions to watch

- mache files a bead asking for typed end-to-end (Int64 string-parsing friction, decode latency on hot loops)
- Profiling shows UDS encode/decode is non-trivial fraction of a daemon round trip (currently it isn't — UDS is control-plane, not hot path)
- A new typed consumer arrives (cloister `udsForward` triggers this naturally per cloister ADR-0005 §"Internal wire = leyline-net")
- Anyone reports the "generation: '0' forever" or Int64-as-string as actually painful

## Out of scope (deliberately)

- Changing the MCP HTTP transport (it's JSON-RPC by external spec — can't change)
- Dropping JSON support (preserves shell debugging)
- Schema changes — `daemon.capnp` is the unchanged SSOT; only the carrier changes

## Files

- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/socket.rs` (magic-byte dispatch)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs` (handler finalizer split)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/fixtures/daemon-protocol/` (binary fixture files)
- `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon/daemon_protocol_test.go` (binary decode path)
- `docs/adr/0014-capnp-as-protocol.md` (status section update)
- `README.md` (daemon protocol section: document both codecs)

## Related

- Bead: `ley-line-open-b0ea2e` (the post-3-step migration this builds on)
- Bead: `ley-line-open-b07a79` (the `op_query` structural skip — dual-codec doesn't fix it; that's separate)
- Decade: `daemon-typed-wire` (step 4)
- Thread: `daemon-json-type-lockdown` (this bead is the natural sequel — call it the wire-carrier-evolution thread once filed)

title: Spike parity-preserving SIMD and affine GearHash CDC scanner
description: Apply GigaToken-style techniques to LLO CDC without adding GigaToken as a dependency or changing chunk semantics. Build an internal scanner backend registry selected once per process (scalar oracle; aarch64 NEON; x86 backend only if it beats existing gearhash). Exploit GearHash's affine recurrence h[i+k] = 2^k*h[i] + sum(2^(k-j)*G[b[i+j]]) mod 2^64 to break the serial dependency into independent SIMD/register lanes while still testing every candidate boundary and returning the earliest exact match. Preserve MIN_CHUNK, MAX_CHUNK, BOUNDARY_MASK, offsets, hashes, and manifest bytes exactly. Keep boundary-policy/FastCDC normalization experiments separate because those intentionally change manifest identity. TDD order: failing backend differential and forced-dispatch tests first, then implementation, then end-to-end performance gate. Baseline observed on Apple M3 Max merged main: scan 1870-1875 MiB/s and full chunk+BLAKE3 1560-1572 MiB/s over five 256 MiB runs.
