title: Publish clients/go/leyline-schema as v0.2.1 — Go bindings for all public capnp schemas
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Establishes LLO's Go consumer surface so downstream repos (starting with mache) stop forking capnp schemas. Pattern: multi-module monorepo, kubernetes/api / stripe-go style.

## Background

mache today carries three forked copies of LLO capnp schemas:
- `mache/internal/leyline/schema/daemon.capnp` ← forks LLO `rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp`
- `mache/schemas/common.capnp` ← forks LLO `rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/common.capnp`
- `mache/schemas/binding.capnp` ← forks LLO `rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/binding.capnp`

The forks are byte-identical to upstream modulo `$Go.package` / `$Go.import` annotations. LLO ADR-0014 §F8.6.6 explicitly identifies this drift surface; per-language-binding forks are exactly what the toolchain-pin discipline is meant to prevent. Future TS / Swift clients (cloister-companion, control-room) would compound the problem.

## Decision

LLO publishes a Go module at `clients/go/leyline-schema/` containing generated bindings for ALL public capnp schemas. Consumers `go get` it like any other Go dependency. Local development uses the existing `~/remotes/art/go.work` workspace so changes flow without publish ceremony.

## Scope (one PR, one v0.2.1 release)

### 1. Module directory layout

```
ley-line-open/
└── clients/
    └── go/
        └── leyline-schema/
            ├── go.mod              # module github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema
            ├── go.sum
            ├── doc.go              # package leylineschema overview
            ├── README.md           # how to consume; never hand-edit *.capnp.go
            ├── daemon/             # one package per .capnp (Go convention)
            │   ├── daemon.capnp.go
            │   └── ...
            ├── common/
            │   └── common.capnp.go
            ├── binding/
            │   └── binding.capnp.go
            ├── ast/
            │   └── ast.capnp.go
            ├── head/
            │   └── head.capnp.go
            └── source/
                └── source.capnp.go
```

### 2. Bindings generation

- Use `capnp.org/go/capnp/v3/capnpc-go` (Go capnp runtime maintainer's generator). Pin the EXACT version per LLO ADR-0014 §3 toolchain triplet rule.
- Generate from `rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp` and `rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/schemas/*.capnp` (the latter implicitly promoted to "public" by virtue of being exposed in the Go module — document this in `doc.go`).
- Add `$Go.package` and `$Go.import` annotations as a per-language-overlay rather than baking them into the authoritative `.capnp` files. Two clean options:
  - **(a)** Author small annotation wrappers in `clients/go/leyline-schema/<name>/_annotations.capnp` that `import` the authoritative source and apply annotations. capnpc-go reads both.
  - **(b)** Strip `$Go.*` from the schemas entirely and tell capnpc-go where to write via flags / build scripts.
  - Either is fine; pick whichever fits the toolchain ergonomics. The non-negotiable is that the authoritative `.capnp` files in `rs/ll-core/...` stay annotation-free.
- Generated `*.capnp.go` files MUST be committed (so consumers don't need capnpc-go installed). LLO ADR-0014 §3 already commits to "Generated bindings are committed to source control."

### 3. CI gates (mandatory; non-negotiable)

- **F8.6.3-equivalent for Go**: a Go-side capnp fileId allowlist verified at build time.
- **Regen-and-diff gate**: CI re-runs capnpc-go against the authoritative `.capnp` sources and `git diff --exit-code` against the committed bindings. Drift fails the build.
- **F8.6.4 cross-runtime fixtures**: round-trip a canonical-encoded message Rust → Go and Go → Rust; assert byte-equality. This is the test LLO ADR-0014 calls out as "biggest single CI investment" and the strongest invariant of T8.

### 4. Versioning + release

- Tag as `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.2.1` — Go's multi-module monorepo convention requires the sub-module path as the tag prefix. (See golang.org/ref/mod#vcs-version § "Module paths in subdirectories.")
- LLO itself stays on its current versioning track; this is the Go-bindings sub-module's first published tag.
- Document the release procedure in `clients/go/leyline-schema/README.md`: bump version → regen if schemas changed → commit → push tag → consumers update `go.mod`.

### 5. Local dev workflow

- `~/remotes/art/go.work` (currently untracked at the workspace root) gets a `use ./ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema` line. Confirm with the user before committing go.work — that file's status is "user's call."
- During local dev, mache's `go.mod` resolves the leyline-schema import to the local checkout via go.work; production builds resolve to the pinned tag.

### 6. Workspace hygiene

- LLO's Cargo workspace must continue to ignore `clients/go/` (Rust shouldn't try to compile Go code).
- `clients/go/leyline-schema/.gitignore` for Go build artifacts.
- Top-level LLO README gets a short pointer: "Go consumers: see clients/go/leyline-schema/."

## Acceptance

- `cd ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema && go test ./...` passes.
- `go install github.com/agentic-research/ley-line-open/clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon` (or equivalent import path verification) works from a fresh checkout.
- The cross-runtime fixture suite passes both directions.
- Tag `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.2.1` exists and is consumable via `go get` against the public repo URL.
- LLO release notes / CHANGELOG note the new module under v0.2.1.

## Cross-repo context

- Consumer bead: `mache-3bf414` (replace daemon.capnp fork with import-from-LLO). Depends on this work landing.
- LLO ADR-0014: capnp as protocol, toolchain-pin discipline, F8.6.x falsifiable claims.
- mache ADR-0014: mache as consumer/projector in the constellation; the schemas-as-Go-module pattern aligns with the "mache reads the canonical event-log set" framing.
- cloister ADR-0005: future cloister-companion (Rust) consumes the same schemas via Rust crate; TS bindings for workerd will be a similar `clients/ts/` sub-module later.

## Out of scope

- TypeScript / Swift client bindings (file separately when needed).
- Changes to schema content (LLO ADR-0014 append-only-additive rule applies; any schema bump is a separate change).
- The mache-side consume work (`mache-3bf414`).
- The cloister-companion's Rust consumer story (it'll consume Rust crates from `rs/ll-core/`, not this Go module).

title: Apache-2.0/AGPL carveout is prose-only — no crate declares a license, nothing enforces the dependency direction
description:
Filed 2026-07-27. Found while designing where a publishable credential-isolation
contract should live (ley-line-open-e7f466).

## The gap

README.md:113 states the carveout:

> The schema and wire-contract crates are Apache-2.0. The implementation crates
> are AGPL-3.0-or-later.

That is the only place it exists. Grepping `^license` across every `Cargo.toml`
in the repo returns nothing — not one crate declares a `license` field. So:

1. **No crate is machine-identifiable** as Apache-2.0 or AGPL. Tooling
   (cargo-deny, license scanners, downstream SBOM generation) sees an
   unlicensed workspace and cannot verify the README's claim.
2. **Nothing enforces the dependency direction.** Apache-2.0 code must not
   depend on AGPL code — doing so makes the combined work AGPL and breaks the
   promise the Apache license makes to every downstream consumer. AGPL code
   depending on Apache-2.0 is fine; the asymmetry is the entire carveout. Today
   an "Apache" schema crate could take an AGPL dependency and nothing would say
   a word.

The claim is load-bearing for real consumers: cloister is AGPL-3.0-or-later and
rig is private, and both consume from this repo specifically because the
contract surface is permissive. If the carveout silently inverts, they are
mis-licensed and would not find out from the build.

## Why it matters more now

ley-line-open-e7f466 publishes `clients/ts` to npmjs under Apache-2.0. A
published package makes the claim externally visible and externally relied
upon, which is a materially different risk than an in-repo assertion.

## Scope

1. Declare `license` in every `Cargo.toml`, matching README.md:113. The npm
   package declares `"license": "Apache-2.0"` in `package.json` from the start.
2. Add a rail asserting the dependency direction: no Apache-2.0-declared crate
   may (transitively) depend on an AGPL-declared crate. `cargo-deny` has native
   support for this; a bespoke check over `cargo metadata` also works.
3. Companion test so the rail cannot pass vacuously — it must fail on a
   deliberately-inverted fixture.

## Related

The same unenforced-declaration shape appears in cloister (cloister-e83a33: 13
files cite a schema-spec path that resolves nowhere). Both are declarations
asserting an authority nothing checks.
acceptance_criteria: Every `Cargo.toml` declares a `license` field consistent with README.md:113, and a CI-gated check fails when an Apache-2.0-declared crate gains a transitive dependency on an AGPL-declared crate. The check is proven non-vacuous by failing against a deliberately-inverted fixture and passing against the shipped tree.

title: mcp-descriptor can't express multi-package or non-MCP producers — notme can't adopt it
description:
`leyline-mcp-descriptor` describes itself as "Shared by every ART producer so
the coverage invariants are not reimplemented per repo." That is currently
aspirational: adoption across the ecosystem is **zero**.

Checked 2026-07-28 — no references to `leyline-mcp-descriptor` /
`leyline_mcp_descriptor` in rosary, mache, canonical-hours, cloister,
ley-line, signet, crumb, or notme. Neither it nor `server-json-gen` is
published to crates.io (both 404 on the sparse index). rosary's and mache's
`server.json` are hand-maintained. Cloister *consumes* `server.json`
(`github://…/server.json@<sha>` in cluster.toml) but does not generate it.

## What blocked the first real adoption attempt

notme (notme-83706a) just added a `server.json` declaring two published OCI
images. It hand-wrote the file, because the descriptor cannot represent it:

1. **Single OCI package only.** `MetaIn` / `ServerMeta` carry singular
   `oci_image` + `oci_version` (`String`, not a collection). notme publishes
   **two** images from one repo — `ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme` and
   `.../notme-proxy` — which cloister declares as two separate
   hypervisor-tier bundles derived independently per ADR-0038. There is no way
   to express a second `packages[]` entry.

2. **MCP transport is mandatory.** `transport_type` and `transport_url` are
   required `String` fields, and `render()` validates tool/group coverage.
   notme is an identity authority with no MCP tools at all — it deliberately
   omits `remotes` and `packages[].transport` so cloister falls through
   cleanly instead of generating backends for tools that do not exist. A
   producer with zero tools cannot describe itself here.

`server-json-gen` is correctly out of scope for this — it is LLO-specific by
construction (its own Cargo.toml: "a printer over leyline-cli-lib's mcp
module", local `path =` deps on the daemon's tool registry). The reusable
surface is the descriptor crate.

## Why this is worth doing rather than dropping

The invariant has already been independently reimplemented, which is the exact
outcome the crate's description says it exists to prevent.

notme's `scripts/check-image-versions.ts` enforces the same two ADR-0041 §2
rules `render()` does — reject a tagged/digest-pinned identifier, reject an
absent version — and cites the same incident this crate's own error message
cites:

> Rejecting a tagged identifier without requiring the version that replaces it
> enforces half of cloister ADR-0041 … `ley-line-open-04300f` shipped that in
> v0.11.2.

Two implementations, same reasoning, arrived at independently. They will drift.

Each currently has something the other lacks:

| | descriptor | notme's check |
|---|---|---|
| tagged identifier + absent version | yes | yes |
| multiple OCI packages, per-entry | no | yes |
| asserts against the *pushed* tag | no | yes |
| melange recipe tracking, incl. apk `-`→`_` spelling | no | yes |
| MCP tool/group coverage | yes | n/a |

Two of those are worth pulling upstream regardless of the notme case:

- **Assert against the pushed tag, not a static value.** ADR-0041 §2 (corrected
  2026-07-28) is explicit that `version` must equal the tag the publish job
  actually pushes. A renderer that takes `oci_version` as input can't check
  that on its own; a `--expect-version` flag the publish job passes would.
- **apk version spelling.** apk reserves `-r<N>` for the release suffix, so a
  `0.1.0-rc1` OCI tag must be written `0.1.0_rc1` in a melange recipe —
  melange rejects the former outright. Any producer using melange + a
  prerelease tag hits this.

## Ask

Extend the descriptor so a producer can declare N OCI packages and zero MCP
surface:

- `packages: Vec<{ identifier, version }>` instead of singular `oci_image` /
  `oci_version`, validating each entry independently
- make `transport_*`, `tools`, and `groups` optional, emitting no `remotes` and
  no `_meta.art.cloister/v1.groups` when absent — the correct shape for a
  non-MCP package, and what notme hand-wrote
- optional `--expect-version <tag>` so a publish job can assert the manifest
  against the tag it is about to push

Then notme can drop its hand-written manifest and its bespoke check, and this
crate's description becomes true rather than aspirational.

Not urgent — notme is unblocked and shipping (v0.1.0-rc3 published and
verified). Filed so the duplication is tracked rather than silently drifting.

## Deliverable

```sql
CREATE TABLE _cfg (
  node_hash BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES node_content(node_hash),
  source_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  block_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  block_kind TEXT NOT NULL,
  entry_offset INTEGER NOT NULL,

  from_node_hash BLOB NOT NULL,
  from_block_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  to_node_hash BLOB NOT NULL,
  to_block_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
```

title: merge_symbol binds LSP symbols across FILES — the _ast JOIN has no source_id predicate
description:
Found by adversarial review (Fable) of docs/problems/symbol-identity.md, 2026-07-27;
confirmed independently by reading both call sites.

merge_symbol resolves an LSP symbol to an AST node positionally
(rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs:1089-1099):

    SELECT node_id FROM _ast
     WHERE start_row = ?1 AND start_col <= ?2 AND end_row >= ?3
     ORDER BY (end_byte - start_byte) ASC
     LIMIT 1

There is NO file predicate. In the daemon path this runs on ONE connection across ALL
files (merge_lsp_into_ast, project.rs:288, driven from daemon/lsp_pass.rs), so a symbol
in file B can resolve to the smallest node IN ANY FILE at those coordinates — and every
file has nodes at overlapping coordinates, because coordinates are line/column and every
file starts at line 0. The subsequent INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _lsp then writes the
attributes of one file's symbol onto another file's node.

The contrast is decisive. lookup_referrer_node_id, in the same file at :755-772, does it
correctly:

    SELECT node_id FROM _ast
     WHERE source_id = ?1
       AND start_row <= ?2 AND end_row >= ?2
       AND (start_row < ?2 OR start_col <= ?3)
       AND (end_row > ?2 OR end_col >= ?3)
     ORDER BY (end_byte - start_byte) ASC
     LIMIT 1

Same table, same purpose, same file — one filters by source_id and one does not.

## Why this is the be6136 class, and why no counter catches it

be6136 was a one-byte path-canonicalization mismatch that made _lsp_refs x _ast JOINs
silently miss. ADR-0027 responded by making that class LOUD: fail-loud FK integrity (§2)
and an unbound_facts counter (§3).

Neither fires here. A wrong-FILE match is not an unbound fact — the JOIN RESOLVES, just
to the wrong node. It produces a plausible, referentially-intact, incorrect row. That is
strictly worse than the miss ADR-0027 hardened against, and it is invisible to the
instrumentation built for it.

## Scope note

The standalone single-file path (project_lsp_into, :198 -> walk_symbol) is unaffected:
one file, one connection, no ambiguity. This is specifically a multi-file/daemon defect,
which is why single-file tests would not surface it.

Acceptance: a two-file fixture where both files contain a symbol at identical
(start_row, start_col, end_row) must produce _lsp rows bound to their OWN file's node —
RED before the fix; add the source_id predicate to the merge_symbol query; task ci.

title: Wire sccache as RUSTC_WRAPPER in Taskfile (caches release/incremental builds)
description:
Filed 2026-05-11. P3 chore, mechanical.

## Problem

`task release` / `task install` recompile the workspace from scratch ~50s each invocation on M-series. Most of that is rustc work on dependencies that are byte-identical between runs — sccache handles exactly this case.

Observed today: user installed `sccache 0.15.0` via brew but it's not yet wired in. Without `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` set, the cache is dormant.

## Work

In `Taskfile.yml`:

```yaml
env:
  PKG_CONFIG_PATH: '{{.FUSE_PKG_CONFIG_PATH}}'
  RUSTC_WRAPPER:
    sh: command -v sccache 2>/dev/null || true
```

The `sh:` block keeps it conditional — if sccache isn't installed, the env stays empty and cargo proceeds normally. No build-pipeline regression for contributors who don't have sccache.

Add a one-line note to `README.md` "Build" section: `brew install sccache` (macOS) recommended for caching across rebuilds.

## Acceptance

- `task release` on a warm sccache cache builds in <15s (vs current ~50s)
- `task ci` similarly benefits
- `sccache --show-stats` shows hits
- CI (GHA) gets a follow-up to install + configure sccache with the GitHub Actions cache backend, separate work

## Why P3

Cosmetic perf win, doesn't block anything. But low-effort and high-frequency-benefit for local dev.

title: Arena control block needs an odd/even seqlock — write-then-bump makes torn reads unfixable from any consumer
description:
Raised by mache 2026-08-17 after confirming arena/control mode is a PRODUCTION path, not research. Consumer-side bead: `mache-0df550`.

## The problem

The arena control block is shared memory that LLO writes and consumers (mache) read concurrently. The publish protocol today is:

1. writer mutates the 32-byte `current_root` (and `arena_path`, `arena_size`)
2. writer calls `bump_sync_counter_release()` (`rs/ll-core/core/src/control.rs:327`)

A reader does an Acquire-load of the sync counter (`sync_counter_acquire`, line 213) and then copies the root bytes. That fences the read against publishes whose Release-store the load already observed — but a writer that BEGINS after the reader's load can mutate the bytes underneath the copy. The reader gets a blend of two generations.

## Why the consumer cannot fix this

mache tried. A reader-side retry (load seq → copy → re-load seq → compare) narrows the window but cannot close it, because the writer never signals "write in progress". With a bump only AFTER the write, there is an interval in which the counter is stable while the payload changes. mache's falsification test observed a torn read at roughly 1-in-500 under concurrent publish.

The sync counter is a **shared cross-language atom** — its meaning is defined by the writer. mache cannot unilaterally adopt an odd/even discipline. Any fix is a writer-side protocol change.

mache's shipped code therefore documents the hole instead of claiming a guarantee it cannot deliver (`internal/control/control.go:113-133`), directing callers to re-open a fresh Controller for coherent identity. Honest, but not adequate for production.

## The ask

Standard seqlock on the control block:

- writer increments the counter to an **ODD** value BEFORE mutating any payload byte (Release)
- writer increments to the next **EVEN** value AFTER the mutation completes (Release)
- readers: load seq (Acquire); retry if odd; copy payload; re-load seq; retry if changed

Minimal change that makes a correct read possible for any consumer in any language. mache already has the reader-side retry scaffolding and can adopt it the moment the writer marks in-progress.

## Alternative worth considering

Rather than every consumer re-deriving the control block's byte layout — mache hardcodes `offSync` / `offCurrentRoot` / `offArenaPath` / `offArenaSize` and reads the mmap directly — LLO could expose arena reads as a primitive (FFI or IPC) and own synchronization internally. That fixes tearing AND removes duplicated layout knowledge, which today has no guard beyond a coarse version field: any offset change silently breaks mache.

Either resolution works for mache. The seqlock is smaller; the primitive is more durable.

## Impact if unfixed

Arena/control mode is how mache serves live hot-swapped projections. A torn `current_root` is a content address for a snapshot that was never published — every downstream identity check keyed on that digest then compares against a value with no referent.
acceptance_criteria: The arena writer marks the control block in-progress before mutating payload bytes and complete after (odd/even sync counter, Release ordering on both). A concurrent-publish stress test asserts a reader doing load-seq/copy/re-load-seq observes ZERO never-published roots over at least 10^5 iterations — the same falsification mache's reader-side test fails today at ~1-in-500. The layout/protocol version is bumped so a consumer built against the old discipline detects the change rather than silently mis-reading.

title: task image:smoke hangs forever — its readiness probe sends no ADR-0022 token, gets 401, and the until-loop has no timeout
description:
Found 2026-07-28 while verifying the krust → cargo-zigbuild port
(`ley-line-open-e44960`). **Pre-existing and unrelated to that change** — it
would do this against any image.

## What happens

`task image:smoke` starts the container, then polls:

    until curl -sf -m 1 -X POST http://localhost:$HOST_PORT/mcp \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || ! docker ps -q --filter name=llo-smoke | grep -q .; do
      sleep 0.3
    done

The probe sends **no auth token**. The daemon's ADR-0022 token gate answers
**401**, `curl -sf` treats 4xx as failure, and the container stays up — so
neither loop condition can ever become true. Confirmed directly:

    $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST localhost:18384/mcp -d '{}'
    HTTP 401
    $ curl -s -X POST localhost:18384/mcp -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
    {"error":"unauthorized"}

Meanwhile the daemon is perfectly healthy:

    MCP HTTP server listening on http://0.0.0.0:8384/mcp
    MCP HTTP token at /tmp/.local/share/leyline/daemon.token
    daemon ready

Observed: container up 10 minutes, loop still spinning, task never returns.

## Why this is worse than a failing test

**The loop has no timeout.** It does not fail — it waits forever. A test that
cannot fail also cannot pass, and a hanging gate reports nothing at all: in CI
it burns the job's whole time budget and the surfaced error is a timeout, which
points at the wrong thing.

That is the same silence-is-evidence class as the rest of this week's findings,
in the one task whose entire job is to prove the image works. It has presumably
been broken since the token gate landed, and nothing noticed because nobody
waits out a hang.

## Fix

Two independent parts; both are needed.

1. **Bound the wait.** A deadline (say 60s) after which the task FAILS with the
   container's logs, so the failure mode is a red gate rather than a hang.
   Also exit non-zero if the container died — today that path exits the loop
   and then proceeds to probe a dead container.
2. **Authenticate the probe.** Read the token the daemon writes
   (`/tmp/.local/share/leyline/daemon.token` inside the container) and send it,
   or start the daemon with auth disabled *for the smoke run only* and say so
   explicitly. Prefer the token: probing with auth is the shape a real consumer
   uses, and cloister's attested path depends on that gate working.

## Acceptance criteria

With a deliberately broken image (e.g. CMD replaced by `sleep 3600`),
`task image:smoke` exits non-zero within the deadline and prints the container
logs. With a good image it passes and asserts `tools/list` returned a non-empty
tool array — not merely that the endpoint answered. Prove both by running them,
not by reading the task.

Related: `ley-line-open-2607d2` (a check must assert the mechanism fired),
ADR-0022 (the token gate the probe ignores).

title: Adopt cloister's cert_chain.rs verifier for Interlace ephemeral certs
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 from cloister-bd8c41 audit. cloister forked `leyline-sign` into `rs/crates/sign/` and added a cert-chain verifier that's not present upstream in ll-open 0.2.0.

## What's there in cloister

`rs/crates/sign/src/cert_chain.rs` (~440 lines, AGPL-3-or-later):
- `verify_cert_chain(cert_der, master_pubkey) -> Result<CertClaims, ChainError>` — verifies an ephemeral Signet cert is signed by a pinned master, extracts validity window + ephemeral SPKI + Interlace claims
- Interlace OID extension parsing at `1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1.{4=epoch, 5=peer_fp, 6=scope}`
- Rejects critical unknown X.509 extensions per RFC 5280 §4.2 (cloister-c71977)
- `claims_to_json()` — compact JSON encoder for the FFI surface (no serde_json dep)
- `pub mod tests_helpers` — `mint_test_cert`, `mint_test_cert_with_extra_ext`; used by `examples/gen-fixture.rs` to produce deterministic test fixtures

24 native Rust tests, all passing under cloister's CI. Files-touched in cloister:
- `rs/crates/sign/src/cert_chain.rs` (new)
- `rs/crates/sign/src/lib.rs` (pub mod cert_chain)
- `rs/crates/sign/src/ffi.rs` (+ `leyline_verify_cert_chain` export)
- `rs/crates/sign/examples/gen-fixture.rs` (deterministic test fixture minter)
- `Cargo.toml` — depends only on what ll-open's leyline-sign already depends on (x509-cert, ed25519-dalek, der, const-oid, thiserror) + adds base64 as dev-dep for fixture binary

## Why this belongs upstream

cloister's copy is forked from llo's `rs/ll-open/sign/`. Both copies are AGPL-3; cloister kept its NOTICE pointing at llo as the public upstream. The cert-chain verifier is generic-purpose — it's not cloister-specific. Any Signet-aware client (notme, signet's Go side, future Rust consumers) benefits.

Adopting upstream means:
- One canonical implementation, one audit surface
- cloister can re-depend on ll-open's crate via path/git dep instead of carrying a local fork
- Future bug fixes / hardening flow through a single place

## Acceptance

- `rs/ll-open/sign/src/cert_chain.rs` lands with the same 24 tests
- `rs/ll-open/sign/src/ffi.rs` gains the `leyline_verify_cert_chain` export
- `rs/ll-open/sign/examples/gen-fixture.rs` lands (deterministic seed; outputs stable bytes)
- cloister's NOTICE updated to remove "cert_chain.rs as cloister-only delta"

## Refs
- cloister-bd8c41 — audit + NOTICE update (cloister-side acceptance met)
- cloister-9d49eb — original implementation bead in cloister
- cloister-c71977 — RFC 5280 critical-extension rejection (sub-feature)

title: Adopt cloister's wasm32 FFI exports (lsign_alloc / lsign_free)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 from cloister-bd8c41 audit. cloister's `rs/crates/sign/src/ffi.rs` adds wasm32 linear-memory exports that llo's `rs/ll-open/sign/src/ffi.rs` doesn't have.

## What's there in cloister

```rust
#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub extern "C" fn lsign_alloc(size: usize) -> *mut u8 { ... }

#[unsafe(no_mangle)]
pub unsafe extern "C" fn lsign_free(ptr: *mut u8, size: usize) { ... }
```

Required for any wasm32 consumer (workerd, browsers, WASI hosts) to pass byte buffers across the FFI boundary. Without these, wasm32 linear memory is opaque to JS — callers can't allocate input buffers, can't free them, can't read output bytes.

## Why this belongs upstream

`leyline-sign` already advertises itself as targeting wasm32 (Cargo.toml has wasm32-unknown-unknown bindings). The native cdylib FFI works without these (the host runtime owns memory); only wasm32 needs them. ll-open's omission is an oversight rather than a design choice — any wasm32 consumer hits the same need.

## Acceptance

- `lsign_alloc` + `lsign_free` exported from `rs/ll-open/sign/src/ffi.rs`
- Match cloister's safety doc-comments (paired alloc/free, double-free is UB)
- No new dependencies (uses `Vec::with_capacity` + `mem::forget` / `Vec::from_raw_parts` — std-only)
- cloister can drop the local fork once this lands

## Refs
- cloister-bd5241 — wasm32 ABI design
- cloister-bd8c41 — audit identifying the upstream gap
- ll-open-4a9e5a — sibling adoption bead for cert_chain

title: Research: Turso (MVCC SQLite-in-Rust) as the arena storage layer — solve the page/concurrency problem while keeping LLO's pieces
description:
User idea 2026-07-17: Turso's MVCC (multi-version concurrency control) likely solves "our page problem" — integrate it as the arena/storage substrate while retaining LLO's own layers (merkle CAS, _ast/_source/_lsp projection, sheaf, extraction epochs).

## The thesis to validate
Turso (turso.tech — the Rust rewrite of SQLite, successor lineage to libSQL) implements MVCC: concurrent readers + writers without SQLite's single-writer file lock, versioned pages instead of in-place mutation. LLO's arena today is a SQLite db (zero-copy via sqlite3_deserialize on the arena payload; mache reads it read-only mode=ro). The hypothesized "page problem" MVCC solves — CLARIFY with the user which of these it is:
- daemon write/read contention on the shared arena (the reference_leyline_daemon_pollution jitter class)?
- page-level lock contention during incremental re-extraction (extraction epochs re-derive facts — MVCC could make that concurrent-safe)?
- the frozen-_ast-until-re-parse gap the mache serve/mount + testfixtures leyline path documents (mache-37ae8b) — MVCC snapshots could give consistent reads during a live re-parse?
- something else.

## The constraint: "keep our pieces"
Turso would be the STORAGE/concurrency engine only. LLO must retain: the merkle node_hash CAS (content dedup), the projection schema (_ast/node_defs/node_refs/node_content/node_child/_source/_lsp*/_cfg), the sheaf substrate, extraction epochs, the validate/emit_ast daemon ops, the capnp wire (wire_format_major=1). Turso must be a drop-in for the SQLite page/txn layer WITHOUT changing the projected table contract mache consumes (mache reads via modernc.org/sqlite pure-Go driver + tableHasColumn probes — that contract is load-bearing across the ecosystem).

## Open questions
- Does Turso support sqlite3_deserialize / in-memory arena zero-copy, or does its storage model differ? (This is the crux — the arena zero-copy is central to LLO's design.)
- Wire/on-disk format compatibility: can mache's modernc.org/sqlite driver still open a Turso-produced db, or does Turso diverge from the SQLite file format? If it diverges, the whole consumer contract breaks.
- MVCC's cost vs benefit for LLO's mostly-read, batch-write workload.
- Turso maturity/production-readiness as of 2026-07.

## Deliverable
A design spike: benchmark the concurrency scenario ("page problem") on current SQLite-arena vs a Turso prototype; assess file-format compat with mache's pure-Go reader; recommend integrate / partial / no. Relates to the analysis-substrate storage layer + reference_leyline_daemon_pollution.

comments.text:
2026-07-24 direction update after reviewing Turso's CONTRIBUTING.md and SQLite's deserialize contract: do not treat the copy-based C-API MVP as the intended upstream path. The LLO-relevant PoC should go directly through a borrowed/buffer-backed `DatabaseStorage` and prove READONLY zero-copy attach against a real content-addressed arena image; fixed-capacity mutable + FREEONCLOSE are compatibility work, while RESIZEABLE may be explicitly deferred.

Important correction to the current write-up/code comments: LLO's `SqliteGraph::deserialize` calls rusqlite `deserialize_read_exact`, which allocates with `sqlite3_malloc` and copies via `Read::read_exact`; the current LLO path is therefore not actually zero-copy despite saying it is. A genuine E2E gate should map the arena, verify `current_root`, attach the verified active slice without an image-sized allocation/copy, query representative `_ast`/`nodes`/`node_defs` joins through Turso, keep the mmap alive for the connection lifetime, close cleanly, and demonstrate pointer/backing identity or allocation evidence. Keep the upstream issue and PoC parallel: issue coordinates storage/lifetime constraints; the fork proves them empirically.

2026-08-03 update on the READONLY zero-copy PoC directed in #317:

Implemented and verified on jamestexas/turso@feat/sqlite3-deserialize-mvp (commit 22496141a, rebased clean onto current upstream/main): a BorrowedImage/BorrowedImageFile wrapping the caller's raw pointer, attached via OpenOptions::storage through the existing DatabaseFile adapter — no image copy. Also found and fixed, on a separate branch (bug/checkpoint-pwritev-error-hang, built fresh off current upstream — the fork was ~13 days / ~19k commits stale, now current): a real hang in Turso's own checkpoint machinery. A persistent write failure during checkpoint backfill spun the process at 100% CPU forever instead of erroring (File::pwritev's default impl silently dropped Err from a child write), and once that's fixed, a second bug left the pager stuck (is_checkpointing() true forever, commit_info wedged) rather than cleanly erroring — caught by an adversarial Opus review pass before filing. Relevant to this research thread because it's exactly the kind of dependency-reliability finding that bears on "is Turso safe as our storage layer": no existing DatabaseStorage backend (real file, MemoryIO) can fail a write persistently, so nothing in Turso's own test suite had ever exercised this path before a custom backend (ours) did.

title: Decide: drop signingTime from CMS SignedAttributes (cloister's wasm32-portability fix)
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-10 from cloister-bd8c41 audit. cloister's `cms.rs` REMOVES `signingTime` from CMS signed attributes; ll-open 0.2.0's still includes it.

## Context

RFC 5652 §5.3 lists `signingTime` as a useful-but-unauthenticated attribute. It's spec-legal to omit. cloister's rationale (per `cms.rs` doc comment):

> The wasm32 emit needs a per-host time source. `js_sys::Date` in V8, `wasi:clocks` in WASI, `SystemTime::now()` native — and a fixed-time placeholder shipping across hosts would silently collapse the temporal-binding property of any verifier that trusts signingTime.

So cloister's `sign_data` doesn't write a signingTime at all; temporal context comes from `cert.not_before` / `cert.not_after` (signed by the master at mint time) and the attestation row's server-timestamped `created_at`.

## The decision for ll-open

A. **Mirror cloister and drop signingTime upstream.** Any verifier that relied on it was relying on an unauthenticated attribute anyway; the spec doesn't promise it.

B. **Keep signingTime in ll-open** and let cloister diverge. ll-open's native builds have a real time source so the attribute is meaningful for them. cloister keeps its local fork for the wasm32-only behavior.

C. **Make signingTime conditional on a `#[cfg]` flag.** wasm32 builds omit it; native builds emit it. Compiles to the right behavior per-target without forking.

Recommend C — cleanest, no upstream/downstream divergence, no behavior surprises for native consumers.

## Acceptance

- Decision recorded in an llo doc / ADR / commit message
- If A or C: cloister's `cms.rs` doc comment + NOTICE updated to reflect no longer being a delta
- If B: cloister's NOTICE keeps the delta entry; bd8c41 closes as "won't merge upstream"

## Refs
- cloister cms.rs (current source of the delta + rationale)
- RFC 5652 §5.3 (signingTime is optional + unauthenticated)
- ll-open's existing leyline-sign cms.rs (the upstream baseline)
- cloister-bd8c41 — audit identifying the delta

comments.text:
## Update from cloister-side audit (2026-06-24) — recommend Cargo-feature gating

Per-file audit of cloister's vendored `cms.rs` re-confirms: signingTime omission is still wasm32-required for cloister, still inline-documented, still spec-legal per RFC 5652 §5.3.

**Recommendation: land the change behind a default-off Cargo feature** rather than unconditionally dropping signingTime. That way existing LLO consumers (signet, ley-line, others) see no behavior change; cloister enables it explicitly in its wasm32 build. Feature name suggestion: `no-signing-time` (short, says exactly what it does).

Patch shape (gated):

```rust
#[cfg(not(feature = "no-signing-time"))]
let signing_time_attr = build_attribute(&oid::ID_SIGNING_TIME, &encode_utc_time_now());

#[cfg(not(feature = "no-signing-time"))]
let mut attrs = vec![content_type_attr, message_digest_attr, signing_time_attr];
#[cfg(feature = "no-signing-time")]
let mut attrs = vec![content_type_attr, message_digest_attr];
```

`Cargo.toml`:
```toml
[features]
default = []
no-signing-time = []
```

Cloister already has a regression test pinning the omission (`signed_attributes_omits_signing_time`) that would carry over once cloister-side consumes upstream — happy to PR it along with the gating change.

Full coordinated-PR plan + cloister-side post-merge work at [`docs/problems/leyline-sign-wasm32-convergence.md`](../problems/leyline-sign-wasm32-convergence.md) (staged in this repo today).

Cloister ADR ratifying the convergence principle: [`cloister/docs/adr/0035-cloister-llo-boundary.md`](../../../../cloister/docs/adr/0035-cloister-llo-boundary.md) — "bridge crates in cloister; leyline-* names in LLO."

P3 still feels right (P2 for the FFI exports because those unblock cloister build path; P3 here because signingTime is a behavioral change that wants the feature gate). With the Cargo-feature approach, this becomes a low-risk additive change.

title: Auto-start leyline daemon on login (LaunchAgent / systemd user unit)
description:
Filed 2026-05-11. P2 chore. Real friction surfaced today.

## Problem

After `task install`, the leyline binary is on PATH but the daemon isn't running. Every workflow that needs the daemon (mache mounts, cloister MCP routing, anything via UDS) requires the user to manually:

```
leyline daemon --mcp-port 8384 --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0 &
```

Forget it = silent failures downstream. mache hangs on UDS connect. cloister returns empty tool results.

User observation today: "Why do I have to start it" — fair.

## Work

### macOS — LaunchAgent

Create `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.agentic.leyline.daemon.plist` with:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>sh.agentic.leyline.daemon</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  <array>
    <string>/Users/USER/.local/bin/leyline</string>
    <string>daemon</string>
    <string>--mcp-port</string><string>8384</string>
    <string>--mcp-bind</string><string>0.0.0.0</string>
    <string>--mcp-allow-public</string>  <!-- gated by future b7dd03; until then bare 0.0.0.0 -->
  </array>
  <key>RunAtLoad</key><true/>
  <key>KeepAlive</key><true/>
  <key>StandardOutPath</key><string>/tmp/leyline-daemon.log</string>
  <key>StandardErrorPath</key><string>/tmp/leyline-daemon.log</string>
</dict>
</plist>
```

Then: `launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.agentic.leyline.daemon.plist`

Wire as a Taskfile target:

```yaml
install:agent:
  desc: "Install macOS LaunchAgent that auto-starts the daemon on login (idempotent)"
  cmds:
    - cp dist/launchagent/sh.agentic.leyline.daemon.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
    - sed -i '' "s|USER|$(whoami)|g" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.agentic.leyline.daemon.plist

```

Ship the plist template in `dist/launchagent/` (gitignored allowlist).

### Linux — systemd user unit

Parallel artifact at `dist/systemd/leyline-daemon.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Leyline daemon

[Service]
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/leyline daemon --mcp-port 8384 --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

Taskfile target similar shape.

### task install hook

`task install` triggers `task install:agent` as a `deps:` step. Could be opt-in via `task install:full` if some users prefer manual control.

## Acceptance

- After `task install` on macOS, daemon auto-starts immediately and on every login
- `lsof -nP -iTCP:8384` shows the daemon listening
- `nc -U ~/.mache/default.sock <<< '{"op":"status"}'` returns a response without manual daemon launch
- `task uninstall:agent` (or similar) cleanly tears it down

## Why P2 not P1

P2 because the daily friction is real but the workaround (manual start) is trivial. Worth doing soon, not blocking anything.

title: P1: Sheaf stalks store raw counts, not rates — degenerates every downstream threshold
description:
Math-friend audit (agent `a9d5e5a2`) 2026-07-10 found the root cause of ~4 downstream constants failing: `complex_build_pass.rs:443` stores stalks as raw activity counts, while the spec comment at `:230-233` says "scalar token-activity **rate**." With integer counts + identity restrictions, every downstream absolute threshold (EPS=1e-4, LOW_DELTA0_THRESHOLD=0.1, DELTA0_EPS_SQUARED=1e-8) degenerates to zero/nonzero tests — the input's units set the regime, not the math.

## Fix

Either (a) implement the spec: normalize stalks to rates (`activity / observations.len()`) at `complex_build_pass.rs:443`, making magnitudes ∈ [0,1] so the fixed thresholds have a defined regime. Or (b) make thresholds relative in `cache.rs` / `complex.rs`: violation iff `|δ⁰ᵢ| > ε·(‖f_u x_u‖ + ‖f_v x_v‖ + ε)`. 

**Option (a) preferred** — one-line fix, matches the written spec.

## Downstream impact

- Ablation study (bead `2775a3`, PR #169) shows 91×; the 91× validates LABELING, not the sheaf constants — this fix won't affect that number.
- P4 (bead `<TBD>`) also degrades under counts; P1 unblocks P4's re-derivation.
- `detect_violations` currently saturates (every edge with unequal counts is a violation) — this fix restores discrimination.

## Falsification test provided by Fable (F1)

Fixture A: observation corpus where every adjacent token pair has counts differing by exactly 1. Expected today: router returns `HighDelta0*`, `detect_violations` flags every edge.
Fixture B: identical topology, stalks divided by total observation count. Expected today: every edge routes `LowDelta0FewCells`, zero violations.

Both assertions pass today = same code, opposite regime = thresholds encode units, not structure. That IS the falsification.

## Files

- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/complex_build_pass.rs:443` (fix)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/complex_build_pass.rs:230-233` (spec comment for reference)
- New adversarial test capturing F1 above

## Rules for fix

- After fix, RE-RUN the sheaf ablation study (bead `2775a3`) and update `docs/research/sheaf-ablation-study.md` with new numbers (may go UP since labels+math now align)
- Include F1 as regression test

title: P2: h0_dimension sign bug + returns 0 as resource-cap fallback (semantic wrong-answer)
description:
Math-friend audit (agent `a9d5e5a2`) 2026-07-10 found `h0_dimension` (`rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/complex.rs:1275`) uses `bounds[i] <= EPS` to select "active" (satisfied) rows for the H⁰ SVD. This is a SIGNED comparison — a row with δ⁰ = −5 (severe violation) passes as "satisfied." H⁰ dimension is not orientation-invariant: swapping an edge's endpoint order flips the sign of its δ⁰ rows and changes which rows enter the SVD → different reported dim H⁰ for the same complex.

Also `:1283-1285` — when active_rows × ncols exceeds MAX_DENSE_ELEMENTS (1e7), returns 0. Semantic: "no globally consistent section exists." This is a WRONG ANSWER, not an error. Downstream consumers get corrupt topology summaries.

## Context

`detect_violations` was already fixed to symmetric `val.abs() > EPS` (see `complex.rs:1157-1161` doc). `h0_dimension` was missed.

## Fix

- **`complex.rs:1275`**: change `bounds[i] <= EPS` → `bounds[i].abs() <= EPS`. Mirror the detect_violations fix.
- **`complex.rs:1283-1285`**: change return-type to `Option<usize>` or `Result<usize, HOError>`; return `None`/`Err` on the resource cap; document the semantic. Do NOT silently return a valid-looking answer.

## Falsification test provided by Fable (F2)

Two-node complex, dim 1, identity restrictions, stalks `[0.0]` and `[5.0]`. Build twice: once with `add_edge(id, 0, 1, …)`, once with `add_edge(id, 1, 0, …)`. Assert `h0_dimension()` equal across the two orientations — expected to FAIL today. Companion: complex with active_rows × ncols just above 1e7, all-equal stalks, assert `h0_dimension` is NOT 0 (trivially consistent section exists) — expected to fail (returns 0).

## Files

- `rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/complex.rs` (the two fixes above)
- Existing consumers of `h0_dimension` if any (grep, may need Option/Result unwrap adjustments)
- New adversarial test capturing F2

## Rules

- The return-type change is intentionally load-bearing — silent wrong answers are worse than errors
- If any consumer swallows the Option/Result silently, flag it — do not paper over

Post-fix: `bounds[i].abs() <= EPS` active-row filter + `Option<usize>` return (`None` on cap). No in-tree callers needed migration — grep found doc references only. CHANGELOG Breaking entry added. task ci green.

title: Generalize notme's schema-bridge into a public substrate crate: one generator/evaluator core, bindings for Rust/Go/TS
description:
Three languages plus custom middleware across ten repos currently means hand-mirrored implementations. The pieces to fix this already exist but are scattered; this bead is about assembling them in the one repo that can host them publicly.

## The reference implementation already works, in notme

notme runs the full pipeline in production for auth:
- schema/identity.capnp + schema/codegen (IDL source of truth)
- packages/schema-bridge — a RUST crate living inside a TS monorepo, doing the bridging
- gen/go/identity.capnp.go and gen/go/verify/{grpc,identity,middleware}.go — note middleware.go is GENERATED, which is the hard part of the three-language problem already solved
- gen/ts/identity.ts

It cannot be the shared home: notme is PRIVATE, so rosary, mache, signet, cloister, canonical-hours, and go-cms cannot consume it. Same disqualifier rules out vigil (also private; Cargo.toml has exactly three deps and vigil-8888fd records "preserve vigil's small Rust single-binary model").

## Why ley-line-open is the home

- Public.
- Already ships wasm32 cdylibs consumed cross-language: leyline-sign and leyline-cas-ffi per ADR-0019, whose own README frames the pattern as "Rust substrate primitives compiled to wasm32 and consumed by cloister via workerd". That is also Python's only path into this ecosystem, via cloister.
- Already the capnp/codegen hub: rs/ll-core/{schema-capnp/schemas, public-schema/capnp} with clients/go/leyline-schema/regen.sh, gated by leyline-schema-go.yml (regen -> git diff --exit-code). ley-line-open-ae89aa (done) already established the "ship a capnp schema as a substrate primitive with Go/TS bindings" precedent for cache.capnp.
- Already upstream of rosary (leyline-vcs), cloister (cas wasm), and mache (staticlib), so lifting schema-bridge here creates no new dependency cycles.

## What the core does

Two jobs, one mechanism, because both are "compare a declaration against a realization":

1. GENERATE — emit per-target descriptors from one in-code/IDL truth so drift is unrepresentable rather than merely detectable. Targets: Go, TS, and Rust, including generated middleware.
2. EVALUATE — the release-contract evaluator from vigil's design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md section 4.1): given a contract and an observed public surface, return resolved / not-yet / error. Compiling one evaluator to wasm32 is what makes the producer's CI gate provably the same code as vigil's checker, which vigil-151b07 requires explicitly.

Rust and Go link natively; TS and Python import the wasm. One implementation, not three that drift.

## Design questions to settle

- Crate boundary and name; whether generation and evaluation are one crate or two sharing a core.
- Which existing hand-rolled drift gates it subsumes: leyline-schema-go.yml here, cloister's generated-drift.yml, rosary's registry:check-drift and taskfile-contract. Three implementations of regen -> git diff --exit-code today.
- Binding/packaging per target: wasm32 cdylib for TS/Python, native staticlib or Go module for Go, plain crate for Rust. Reuse the leyline-sign / leyline-cas-ffi packaging precedent rather than inventing one.
- Build-dependency constraint: cloister deliberately checks in generated files so its OCI build can skip capnp entirely (Wolfi ships none). The core must not reintroduce a build-time capnp requirement for consumers.
- Whether the shared .taskfiles/{generate,release}.yml layers ship from here, vendored per repo and drift-gated.

## Out of scope

- Schemas themselves stay with their producers (the boundary approved on vigil-302ad5). This crate ships the machinery, not the definitions.
- Picking OpenAPI tooling; that follows once there is a non-MCP HTTP surface worth describing.
- The declare-vs-generate rule itself, which is vigil-4b304d.

Related: vigil-4b304d (umbrella rule), vigil-143ef8 (release contract design), vigil-151b07 (single-evaluator requirement), rosary-1a4c0b (CLI/MCP parity, a consumer of the generate half).

Concrete cloister adoption case, 2026-07-27. This bead's acceptance criteria
already calls for "adoption beads in rosary, cloister, and vigil" — here is
cloister's, and it is further along than it looks.

## The pipeline already runs cloister-side

Cloister does not vendor a schema-bridge. Its `rs/crates/` holds exactly two
crates (`cas`, `host-runtime`). Everything matching `schema-bridge` under
cloister is a BUILD ARTIFACT of THIS repo's crate:

    cloister/rs/target/release/capnpc-schema-bridge-zod
    cloister/rs/target/release/capnpc-schema-bridge-go
    cloister/rs/target/debug/.fingerprint/leyline-schema-bridge-*

and cloister's Taskfile has a `cluster:zod` / `cluster:zod:verify` pair fed by
that zod plugin. So the generator→zod path from LLO into cloister is wired and
running today. Generalizing the core does not require cloister to adopt a new
mechanism; it widens what an existing one covers.

## The adoption target: credential-isolation/v1

The wire spec lives here (`rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/`)
together with a Python reference implementation (`ref-impl-py/credisolation/`).
Cloister consumes that contract by HAND-MIRRORING it: `InjectionStrategy`, a
discriminated union typed out by hand at `src/routes/vault-proxy.ts:21`, with a
comment citing the spec by a path that does not resolve (cloister-e83a33).

That is exactly the "hand-mirrored implementations" this bead opens with, and
it is the highest-value first target because the drift is already observable
rather than hypothetical.

## On moving the implementation here

The operator's read is right and the license mechanics support it. The spec is
already in the Apache-2.0 half per README.md:113. An AGPL implementation moving
into this repo lands in the AGPL half, which is what that half is for — no new
carveout, no change to what downstream consumers may do with the contract.

One ordering constraint: **ley-line-open-4392a2 should land first.** The
Apache/AGPL split is currently asserted only in README.md:113 with no `license`
field in any Cargo.toml and nothing enforcing the dependency direction. Moving
an AGPL implementation next to an Apache spec is precisely the situation where
an unenforced direction rule starts mattering — an Apache-declared crate
acquiring an AGPL dependency would silently void the contract's license claim
for every consumer.

## Relation to ley-line-open-e7f466

e7f466 (TS bindings) is the narrow version of this; if the generalized core
here emits TS, e7f466 is subsumed rather than parallel. Worth deciding
explicitly which of the two owns TS emission before either starts, so the
answer is not two TS generators.

comments.text:
Evidence toward "finish generalizing", measured 2026-07-27 at SHA abd5b86.

## The crate is here and is enforced nowhere

schema-bridge is in-tree at rs/ll-open/schema-bridge (leyline-schema-bridge v0.10.4)
and is wired into NOTHING:

    grep -c "schema-bridge" Taskfile.yml            -> 0
    grep -rc "schema-bridge" .github/workflows/     -> 0

Its own README concedes the posture: "Today the codegen is opt-in — cloister's Taskfile
carries entries per (schema, format) that regenerate + drift-check, but none are wired
into its `task lint` or `task verify` yet." In LLO it is not even opt-in; there is no
entry point at all.

That is the same unwired-capability shape as ley-line-open-918a75 (leyline-fs/splice:
declared, shipped, compiled out of every binary, so flush_node degraded to a silent
no-op). A generator nobody runs cannot prevent the drift it exists to prevent — it is a
declaration of intent, not a mechanism.

## Cross-repo state, measured

cloister — the generator has ALREADY been lifted out (ADR-0036 Phase 2). Only
           docs/adr/0022-schema-bridge-substrate-positioning.md and
           docs/adr/0036-schema-bridge-multi-output.md remain, plus GENERATED artifacts
           src/generated/cluster.zod.ts, src/generated/identity.zod.ts and
           .task/checksum drift-check entries. This is the CORRECT end state for a
           consumer: generator centralized, outputs local. Nothing to move.

signet   — docs/design/cross-language-schema.md names notme/schema/identity.capnp as
           "the single source of truth" and instructs contributors: "Do not redefine
           them in signet — import the generated bindings instead (Go from
           notme/gen/go/identity, TypeScript + Zod from notme/gen/ts/identity, Rust
           from notme/gen/rust/identity when wired)."

           notme is PRIVATE. So a public repo's canonical types live where its own
           consumers cannot read them. That is the concrete harm this bead exists to
           fix, stated in signet's own documentation.

LLO      — the public home. Crate present, generalization unfinished, enforcement absent.

## Why this is load-bearing beyond schema plumbing

Per vigil-4b304d's declare-vs-generate rule ("Regenerable deterministically -> GENERATE.
Drift becomes unrepresentable."), capnp schemas are squarely in the GENERATE arm. Two
open beads depend on that arm actually working:

- ley-line-open-e7f466 (TS bindings) is filed as "publish clients/ts", which would
  hand-mirror the very thing it exists to prevent. The Go client already IS generated
  (clients/go/leyline-schema/**/*.capnp.go carry the "Code generated" marker). It should
  be "wire schema-bridge's TS target + drift gate".
- ley-line-open-2037b4 (symbol identity) — whatever its ADR decides must be PUBLISHED
  through this surface, or consumers hand-mirror it again. That is exactly how mache
  ended up keying constructs on rendered names and losing 733 Rust constructs plus 16.9%
  of Go init() bodies. Fixing the instance without the publication path leaves the class.

## Suggested next concrete step

Wire ONE (schema, format) pair into `task ci` with a drift check, before adding more
targets. That proves the mechanism end-to-end and converts the bead from "a crate exists"
to "a gate exists" — which is the only form that prevents drift.

comments.text:
DECISION 2026-07-28 — the wasm framing in this bead's description is superseded. Read this before starting.

THE EVALUATOR IS ONE BINARY, INVOKED, NOT LINKED. JSON in, JSON out, three outcomes on the exit code. Rust, Go, TS, Python, CI, and a human invoke it identically. No cgo, no wasm runtime, no FFI, no build-time schema dependency.

Why the original framing was wrong: it reasoned about LINKING when this ecosystem's integration primitive is INVOKING. vigil has exactly three dependencies because it shells out to git/gh/rsry; rosary shells out; Taskfile is nothing but shelling out. The whole "how do three languages share one implementation" problem was self-inflicted by assuming the evaluator had to live inside the calling process.

CLOISTER ALREADY MADE THIS CALL, FOR THIS REASON. ADR-0009 (compute-substrate portability) fixes cluster tier-2 bundles as "OS process + container namespace per bundle. NOT v8 isolates — they can't be without WASM compile + losing native dependencies." Same trade-off, same conclusion, May 2026. Do not re-litigate it here; read ADR-0009 first.

The packaging that follows already exists and should be reused rather than invented: OCI images via apko/melange, and cluster.toml's `confinement.fs.allow` / `holdsCredential` as a declarative capability manifest. That matters for this specific binary — the observer needs network reach to github.com, ghcr.io, and proxy.golang.org and nothing else. The same artifact runs as a plain subprocess in CI, or as a confined cloister bundle where that scoping is ENFORCED rather than trusted. That is the enforce-vs-observe split of vigil-4b304d applied to the verifier itself.

ALSO READ FIRST: cloister ADR-0041, "OCI image-publish contract" (Proposed, 2026-07-06). It states the release-contract thesis directly — "A tool that declares ghcr.io/org/mache:0.13.0 but never pushes it produces a manifest that fails at compose up, not at resolve" and "Every producer already carries the image recipe, and none of them runs it in CI" — and audits the same three producers (mache, rosary, ley-line-open), three weeks before the vigil spec and independently of it. It is the image surface of the same contract. Whatever this bead builds should satisfy ADR-0041's Opens (publish pipeline, digest pinning) rather than duplicating them, and ADR-0041 is a candidate to be ratified alongside.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL DECIDES, now narrower:

1. Whether the JUDGMENT half is code at all. "Does this observation satisfy this contract" is a set of assertions over a record — asset present, checksum covers it, tag resolves, digest matches, version agrees. That is data. If the assertion set is CLOSED, make it declarative and the binary becomes an interpreter over a table, which is vigil-4b304d's declare-vs-generate rule one level up. If producers will want per-repo escape hatches, the binary matters more than the table. This is the open question the user was asked and it was explicitly deferred here.

2. The observation report as a schema'd artifact. Genuine cross-language wire data, so a capnp candidate alongside daemon.capnp — and the thing conformance fixtures bind against.

3. Whether the binary is vigil itself or a separate `release-contract` tool vigil invokes. Folding it in is fewer artifacts; splitting keeps vigil an observer rather than making it a dependency of every producer's CI.

4. Unchanged from the original description: what the shared generator half looks like, and which existing hand-rolled drift gates it subsumes (LLO's leyline-schema-go.yml, cloister's generated-drift.yml, rosary's registry:check-drift and taskfile-contract).

Spec reference: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md section 4.1 (in the vigil repo, commit 13b9da4). Sections 12.1, 12.2, and 12.8 are marked RESOLVED by this decision and retained as the record of how it was reached.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my evidence comment above, 2026-07-27. I overstated the gap.

I wrote "schema-bridge is wired into NOTHING" and "a generator nobody runs prevents no
drift". I measured LLO's Taskfile and workflows, found zero references, and generalised
to the ecosystem. Wrong — and the same over-generalisation that produced three other
corrections today.

## What is actually true

LLO hosts the generator and does not run it AS A GENERATOR:
  - rs/ll-open/schema-bridge/tests/integration.rs DOES run, in the workspace test sweep
  - zero `schema-bridge` references in Taskfile.yml, zero in .github/workflows/

cloister runs it, today, with a drift check. Per cloister-871aed: every schema-bridge
path under cloister is a build artifact of LLO's crate
(rs/target/release/capnpc-schema-bridge-{zod,go}), and cloister's Taskfile carries
`cluster:zod`, `cluster:zod:verify` and `cluster:zod:check-drift`. Verified by reading
that Taskfile.

So the generator IS exercised — just not by the repo that owns it.

## Why the corrected gap still matters, and is a smaller job

The risk is not "nothing verifies the output". It is that LLO can regress generation
semantics and only a DOWNSTREAM repo finds out. LLO's own schemas also have no generated
surface, which is why e7f466 has nothing to wire into yet.

That makes the first slice smaller than I implied: ONE (schema, format) pair of LLO's own
in `task ci` with a drift check. Not a from-scratch wiring effort.

Worth copying rather than reinventing: cloister's check-drift regenerates into a temp dir
and DIFFS the committed copy — content comparison, not mtime staleness — and it already
guards the failure mode we keep hitting elsewhere:

    # `capnp compile` exits 0 even when the plugin errors and writes nothing —
    # its stderr carries the real diagnostic. Check that the output file actually
    # landed before diffing, otherwise `diff` would fail on a missing file with a
    # misleading "DRIFT" framing.

That is a positive control, already written, for exactly the "tool exited 0 having done
nothing" class that cost several CI runs here today.

## The adoption beads this bead's acceptance criteria asked for already exist

4ec276 asks for "adoption beads in rosary, cloister, and vigil". Two are filed and not
linked here:

  cloister-871aed  Adopt LLO's generated schema surface — stop hand-mirroring
                   credential-isolation/v1 in TS. Names the concrete drift:
                   cloister/src/routes/vault-proxy.ts:21 hand-writes InjectionStrategy
                   as a mirror of LLO's wire/injection-strategies.md.
  cloister-86ce1f  Amend ADR-0057: parity should be GENERATED, not asserted. The
                   stronger form — generate both halves from one source and
                   disagreement is unrepresentable rather than caught.
  rosary-1a4c0b    Conformance/no-drift harness: exercise every tool path + assert
                   CLI<->MCP parity from one declarative registry (ADR-0006). This is
                   effectively the rosary-side adoption case, though not filed as one.

## An additional generation target, and a precedent LLO already runs

OpenAPI belongs on the list: schema-bridge already emits JSON Schema, and OpenAPI 3.1
uses JSON Schema for component types, so it is another emitter off the same IR rather
than a new axis. mache is the natural consumer — it serves MCP over Streamable HTTP.

And LLO already proves the one-source-plus-drift-gate pattern, just from Rust rather than
capnp: `gen:server-json` regenerates server.json from leyline-cli-lib::daemon::mcp
(tool_registry + cloister_groups), and `gen:server-json:check` fails the build on drift
from inside the ci chain. Pointing that pattern at capnp reflection instead is what would
let ONE source emit MCP tool defs, the CLI surface, Go/TS clients and OpenAPI — which is
what rosary-1a4c0b wants for its 40 tools and its known parity gaps.

## Scope honesty

This closes the declare-vs-generate class. It does NOT close two others, and vigil-4b304d
is explicit that GENERATE is one of three mechanisms:
  - where independence is the POINT (ref-impl-py), generating deletes the signal
  - generation makes consumers agree with the SCHEMA; it does not make the schema true
  - a gate that returns success while checking nothing is untouched by codegen
The positive-control discipline still has to carry those.

SCOPE ADDITION 2026-07-28: server.json generation is being generalized here, and it belongs in this bead rather than beside it.

Verified current state — LLO already has the STRONG half of the declare-vs-generate rule:

  rs/tools/server-json-gen/src/main.rs — reads `leyline_cli_lib::daemon::mcp` (the in-code
  MCP registration) and emits server.json. Version comes from a single workspace source
  (`leyline_cli_lib::daemon::version::BINARY_VERSION`), not a second declaration.

  Taskfile.yml:895  gen:server-json        — regenerate
  Taskfile.yml:906  gen:server-json:check  — fail if the committed file drifts
  Taskfile.yml:1020 wired into the CI gate

Currently LLO-specific only by its constants (SERVER_NAME, SERVER_DESCRIPTION, SCHEMA_URL); the SHAPE is fully generic — in-code registry -> descriptor -> drift gate.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND LLO. rosary's Taskfile describes its own server.json as a "hand-maintained MCP manifest" with server-json:check bolted on. Two repos, same file, opposite halves of the rule stated in vigil-4b304d: LLO GENERATES so drift is unrepresentable, rosary ASSERTS so drift is merely detected. rosary-1a4c0b exists to fix that across a 10-shared / 31-MCP-only / 38-CLI-only split, and vigil-cd74de needs the same emitter from zero (vigil's entire CLI surface today is one subcommand). Neither should reinvent what already works here.

So the generalization should parameterize the constants and the registry source, and ship the emitter plus its drift gate as something rosary and vigil consume rather than copy. That is the same "plurality of outputs, singularity of source" principle already in this bead's description, applied to the surface nearest to hand.

Note it also touches the release contract: LLO's `release:version-check` requires "binary, schema, generated metadata, and docs to agree", and server.json is one of that generated metadata. Generating it from the binary's own registry makes one clause of section 5's version-agreement requirement true by construction instead of by check.

Consumers to notify when the emitter lands: rosary-1a4c0b, vigil-cd74de.

comments.text:
CONVERGENCE NOTE 2026-07-28 — the evidence layer is migrating into this repo, which collapses a seam this bead was designing around.

Verified today:

- cloister ADR-0035 "cloister<->LLO boundary — bridge crates in cloister, leyline-* names in LLO" (Proposed 2026-06-24) states the migration rule, and explicitly relates_to 0007-interlace-substrate.md.
- ADR-0045 is the worked precedent and is ACCEPTED (2026-07-09): leyline-sign moved from a cloister fork to the shared LLO artifact and the cloister-side fork was deleted (bead cloister-8f4d3f).
- ADR-0051 records the current split directly: "interlace-spec/0.1.0/, reference encoders in LLO rs/ll-open/sign/".
- Confirmed in this repo: rs/ll-open/sign/src/cert_chain.rs (verify_cert_chain), kid.rs (canonical_kid), ffi.rs. The IDENTITY half of Interlace is already here, inside leyline-sign — the cdylib/wasm32 crate cloister consumes.

So the split today is: protocol SPEC vendor-neutral in cloister (interlace-spec/0.1.0/, with canonical test vectors, ref-impl-py, and a CI drift gate), cert/identity ENCODERS already in LLO, and chain/attestation/disclosure still cloister-side in the Durable Objects.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS BEAD. The release-contract design (vigil docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-27-release-contract-design.md section 6.0.1) now depends on Interlace for evidence: attestation chains with predecessor linkage, the COMPLETE/PENDING/GAP state model, and the disclosure endpoint. That looked like a cross-repo dependency — release machinery in LLO, evidence layer in cloister. It is not. Under ADR-0035 the leyline-* primitives land HERE, so the release-contract machinery this bead scopes and the evidence layer it would emit into are the same crate family in the same repo.

Practical consequences:
1. Do not design an evidence-emission seam between LLO and cloister. Design for both halves being local.
2. The generator/evaluator core this bead scopes should expect to sit alongside leyline-sign, not call across a boundary to it.
3. Encoding follows Interlace, NOT capnp: RFC 8949 deterministic CBOR, X.509 DER, UTF-8 byte concatenation with no separators for chain-hash input, canonical JSON for cert claims, JSONL for disclosure. The spec's threat model §7.7 (a-e) catalogues how each wrong encoding choice breaks the §13.2 "silence is evidence" property. capnp stays on the daemon protocol and generated bindings.

SEQUENCING, per the user: Interlace's remaining lift waits on the schema/IR work settling, because the chain encoding has to ride whatever schema machinery this repo lands. Lifting before that means lifting twice. So this bead should not block on the lift, but should not assume the current cloister-side location is permanent either.

Related: vigil-8870d4 is flagged for rescope from "define an Evidence Capsule schema" to "map release evidence onto Interlace and find what it does not cover."

comments.text:
FROM MACHE — two additions to scope, both small.

1. MACHE IS A CONSUMER AND IS NOT IN THE ADOPTION LIST.

The acceptance criteria names "adoption beads in rosary, cloister, and vigil". mache publishes a server.json (repo root, schema 2025-12-11) and is consumed through it — cloister's cluster.toml pins `github://agentic-research/mache/server.json@a585418`. If generation lands without a mache adoption bead, mache's file stays hand-authored while its consumers read a generated contract, which is the drift this bead exists to remove.

Mache-side tracking is mache-e28a9f, rescoped today from "hand-add a field" to "populate the generated one" on the news that generation is coming.

2. ONE SUBSTANTIVE INPUT MACHE OWES THE SCHEMA — SESSION SEMANTICS ARE PER-TRANSPORT, NOT PER-SERVER.

This is the thing worth getting right before the shape sets, because it is currently modelled wrongly downstream and generation would propagate the wrong model.

mache's http transport is session-stateful: each client gets a session ID mapped to its own projected graph (cmd/serve_repo.go, sanitizeSessionID). mache's stdio transport is a per-client subprocess and needs no session at all. Same server, two transports, opposite answers.

cloister models it as ONE boolean per input:

    cluster.toml    [inputs.rosary]  requiresSession = true
                    [inputs.mache]   absent -> false

    cluster.ts      { "name": "mache",  ..., "requiresSession": false }   <- wrong today
    (generated)     { "name": "rosary", ..., "requiresSession": true  }

So the cluster runs mache as sessionless against a session-stateful transport. Nobody wrote a bug — the fact is not published anywhere the consumer reads, and the default is the wrong answer.

If the generated schema models this as a server-level boolean, that defect gets re-encoded upstream where it is harder to fix and every consumer inherits it. If it is per-transport, mache can state the truth and cloister derives it.

Not asking for a decision here — flagging that mache has the evidence and would like to be asked before the field shape is fixed.

3. UNRELATED BUT WORTH RELAYING TO WHOEVER REGENERATES: cloister's mache pin reports version 0.17.0 against mache's current 0.19.0, two minor versions stale. A regeneration picks that up, which is an argument for doing it deliberately rather than deferring it further.

comments.text:
Answering your session-semantics question on 4ec276 — and the answer is worse than
the option you were guarding against.

## Neither. It models NO sessions, and ONE transport.

leyline-mcp-descriptor's ServerMeta carries:

    pub transport_type: &'a str,
    pub transport_url:  &'a str,

Two scalars. There is no session field at all, and because the transport is
singular rather than a list, per-transport session semantics is not merely
unmodelled — it is UNREPRESENTABLE in the current shape.

So your input landed before adoption, which is what you asked for, and it is
correct.

## It is already wrong for LLO, not just for mache

v0.11.2 added `--mcp-uds` (ley-line-open-6569de) so the daemon can serve MCP over
a Unix socket for the cloister attested path. LLO therefore serves TWO transports
now — streamable-http over TCP, and UDS — and its own server.json can describe
only one. The producer broke the shape within hours of the shape being written.

That is independent confirmation of your point from the other direction: it is
not a mache quirk, it is the shape being wrong.

## What I have NOT done, deliberately

I have not guessed at a fix. Two things need deciding and one needs verifying,
and you hold context I do not:

1. WIRE SHAPE. Does the pinned MCP registry schema
   (static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json) permit
   more than one transport per package, or a session/stateful attribute on a
   transport? If it does not, the honest emission may be one package PER
   TRANSPORT rather than one package with a transport list — and that changes
   what `identifier` + `version` mean per entry. I have not verified this against
   the schema and will not assert it.

2. WHERE SESSION SEMANTICS BELONG. Your framing says per-transport (http
   stateful, stdio not). LLO's UDS carries the same streamable-http protocol over
   AF_UNIX rather than TCP, so for us the session semantics track the PROTOCOL,
   not the socket family. If that generalises, the attribute may belong on the
   protocol rather than on the transport entry — which would be a third answer,
   not either of the two on the table.

3. CLOISTER'S BOOLEAN. You said cloister models one boolean per input and
   currently runs mache sessionless. If the descriptor grows per-transport
   semantics, something has to consume them — otherwise we have moved an
   unrepresentable defect into a representable-but-ignored one, which is not
   obviously better.

## Timing

Cheap to change now: only LLO uses the emitter, the crate shipped in v0.11.2
today, and there is no adopter to migrate. It gets expensive the moment
rosary-1a4c0b or vigil-cd74de wires it in — which is exactly the window you were
trying to catch.

Tell me the shape you want and I will build it. If the answer needs the schema
checked first, say so and I will check it rather than assume.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
## Transport/session shape: ANSWERED — no LLO change needed

I said I would check the schema rather than assume. Checked, plus cloister's
actual consumer code. mache's question ("per-transport or per-server?") has a
third answer: **neither — it is not in the descriptor at all.**

### 1. Session semantics are consumer-side, and the mechanism already exists

`cloister/cluster.toml` declares it per-input:

    [inputs.rosary]
    requiresSession = true

`manifest/cluster.capnp:483` — `requiresSession @10 :Bool`, documented as
*"Operator transport override for MCP servers that require the Streamable HTTP
initialize/session handshake (for example mcp-go). Threaded into every generated
backend derived from this input."*

So it is **per-server** (threaded into every backend from that input),
**operator-declared**, and tracks the **protocol handshake, not the socket
family** — which is exactly the distinction that matters for LLO, whose UDS
would carry the same protocol.

The registry schema has no session field because session semantics do not
belong to the producer.

### 2. LLO is genuinely session-less, and correctly declared

`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:823-833`: `initialize` returns ok but
issues no `Mcp-Session-Id` (zero occurrences in the file), and `tools/list` /
`tools/call` dispatch unconditionally with no session gate.

`[inputs.llo]` omits `requiresSession`. That is correct, not an oversight.

### 3. A UDS transport is NOT expressible in server.json

`StreamableHttpTransport.url` / `SseTransport.url` carry pattern
`^https?://[^\s]+$`. A `unix:` URL is schema-invalid. `transport` is also a
single object, not an array, so "two transports on one package" cannot be
expressed either — two transports would require two `packages[]` entries, each
needing its own required `identifier` + `version`.

cloister expresses UDS cluster-side instead, via `wires[].transport = "uds"`
and `bundles.external.ipcSocket`. Load-bearing for `ley-line-open-6569de`.

### 4. If LLO ever publishes a session DEFAULT, the pattern is `_meta`

Precedent is tenancy (`cluster.capnp:473-478`): server.json
`_meta.art.cloister/v1.tenancy` declares the DEFAULT, cluster.toml is the
OPERATOR OVERRIDE. `requiresSession` currently has no server.json counterpart —
operator-only. Adding one now would be inventing a contract with no consumer.

### Consequence

Nothing here blocks the release. Filed `ley-line-open-891dd5` for the real
defect this surfaced: no gate validates the emitted descriptor against the
schema it pins.
