title: 5f7100-1: mutex held across await — op_reparse + snapshot timer can deadlock
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: deadlock risk + tail-latency.

op_reparse (daemon/ops.rs ~line 235) holds ctx.live_db.lock().unwrap() across the synchronous parse_into_conn call. parse_into_conn can take >500 ms on a cold cache. Meanwhile cmd_daemon.rs ~line 287 has a periodic snapshot timer firing every 500 ms; each tick does `let guard = ctx.live_db.lock().unwrap()`. While reparse holds the lock, every snapshot tick queues. When reparse finishes, the queued ticks fire in a burst — and any concurrent `query` op (which only borrows the live db read-only) blocks behind them.

Worse: std::sync::Mutex (not tokio::sync::Mutex) — a panic in a critical section poisons it permanently. Some lazy-enrich paths hold the mutex across .await, which std::sync::Mutex permits but is the canonical Rust async anti-pattern.

Acceptance:
- swap to tokio::sync::Mutex OR document why std::sync is safe AND verify no .lock() spans an .await
- snapshot timer try_lock + skip-with-log if reparse is in flight (or replace timer with a debounce signal)
- stress test: 10 concurrent lsp_hover + simultaneous reparse, all bounded time

Related: 5f7100-4, 5f7100-7.

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Core deadlock-risk fix shipped at commit f5a0a45.

**Two-part fix:**

1. **`try_snapshot_or_log`** added — the 500ms periodic snapshot timer now uses `try_lock`:
   - WouldBlock → debug log + skip this tick (next tick retries)
   - Poisoned   → log::error + recover via `into_inner()` (avoid wedging timer permanently; same strategy as 294fd6b embed drainer)
   - Ok(guard)  → snapshot normally
   Wired into the periodic timer at cmd_daemon.rs. Snapshots no longer queue behind a long reparse.

2. **`std::sync::Mutex<Connection>` safety documented**: `rusqlite::Connection` is `!Send`, so `MutexGuard<Connection>` is `!Send`, so holding it across `.await` is a compile error. **Rust's type system enforces "no .await while holding the lock" for free.** No need for `tokio::sync::Mutex`. Documented inline at `DaemonContext.live_db`.

**Acceptance progress:**
- [x] swap to tokio::sync::Mutex OR document why std::sync is safe → DOCUMENTED
- [x] snapshot timer try_lock + skip-with-log if reparse is in flight → DONE
- [ ] stress test: 10 concurrent lsp_hover + simultaneous reparse → spawned as follow-up bead 5f7100-1b

Two unit-level pin tests landed:
- `try_snapshot_or_log_skips_when_lock_contended` — holds lock from test thread, asserts try_snapshot_or_log returns false without deadlocking
- `try_snapshot_or_log_recovers_from_poisoned_lock` — poisons via panicking thread, asserts recovery via into_inner()

The bug-fix portion is complete. The stress test (acceptance criterion #3) is named as follow-up bead. Closing this bead and tracking the stress test separately.

Note: there's also a future improvement to wrap op_reparse in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so the long sync work doesn't block the tokio worker (separate from deadlock — that's "blocking-the-runtime"). Tracked in the doc comment on `live_db`.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: 5f7100-2: PoisonError swallowed in embed drainer — silent zombie
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: silent failure.

daemon/embed.rs:194-217 (start_drain): both the queue lock and the live_db lock use `match ... .lock() { Err(_) => continue, ... }`. If either mutex is ever poisoned, the drainer becomes a permanently-spinning interval(1s) no-op — no log, no exit, no recovery. Same idiom at embed.rs:173.

Result: a panic anywhere in the embed path silently disables embedding for the rest of the daemon's life, while RSS slowly grows from un-drained queue entries.

Acceptance:
- log::error! (with the PoisonError details) before any continue
- consider lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover poisoned state explicitly
- a stress test that injects a panic into the embedder and verifies the daemon either recovers or exits with a meaningful error

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Fully addressed by commit 294fd6b (today's scale-hardening sweep).

Both poison sites in `start_drain` and the embed loop now log::error and recover via `poisoned.into_inner()`:

- daemon/embed.rs:259-264 — embed_queue lock: `Err(poisoned) => { log::error!("embed_queue mutex poisoned, recovering"); poisoned.into_inner() }`
- daemon/embed.rs:285-287 — live_db lock: same pattern with `live_db mutex poisoned in embed drain, recovering`

The drainer no longer becomes a silent spinning no-op on poison. Acceptance criteria met (log + recover); a stress-test bead can land later but the silent-zombie behavior is gone.

Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: 5f7100-3: unbounded mpsc channel for event router — heap can grow without bound
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: resource leak.

daemon/events.rs:181 uses mpsc::unbounded_channel for emission. The dispatch loop is single-consumer; if it ever blocks (e.g. waiting on subscribers.read().await while another emit holds the write lock), raw events accumulate in heap forever. Combined with git_watch_loop emitting on every tick (every 2 s) and EmbeddingPass emitting on every drain batch, this is an unbounded queue feeding a single dispatcher.

Acceptance:
- bounded channel with backpressure (mpsc::channel(N))
- on overflow: drop-oldest with metric, OR block emitter (with a timeout) so callers know the bus is congested
- test: pile up 100k events while keeping subscribers stalled, verify RSS stays bounded

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Fixed at commit e57dc09.

**Change**: `mpsc::unbounded_channel()` → `mpsc::channel(EVENT_EMIT_CHANNEL_BUFFER=4096)`. `EventEmitter::emit` uses `try_send`:
- Full → `log::warn` + drop the new event (drop-newest)
- Closed → `log::debug` (benign late-emit during teardown)

**Why drop-newest, not drop-oldest**: drop-oldest would require synchronous `recv` then `send` per emit, defeating the lock-free fast path. The EventLog (separate from this channel) is the authoritative replay source — missed in-flight events surface as `replay_gap: true` on subscriber reconnect, not as permanent loss. Production emitters are fire-and-forget; drop-newest matches their semantics.

**Acceptance**:
- [x] bounded channel with backpressure
- [x] drop-newest with log::warn metric on overflow
- [x] burst test (`router_under_burst_emit_does_not_panic`): emit 2× buffer-size events, subscriber sees ≥1 and ≤ EVENT_EMIT_CHANNEL_BUFFER — the heap-bound guarantee.

Five new tests: const pin, drop-when-full, drop-on-closed, burst, noop-survives. 145/145 lib pass. Clippy clean.

Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: 5f7100-4: maybe_enrich race — duplicate work + double-write to _lsp on concurrent hover
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: correctness + wasted work.

daemon/ops.rs:619-632 (maybe_enrich): calls with_live_db to check whether _lsp data exists, drops the lock, then try_enrich_file (line 589) re-acquires it and runs LSP enrichment under the lock. Two concurrent lsp_hover calls on the same file will both pass the no-data check, both spawn a language server, the second wastes work and may double-write _lsp rows.

No dedup, no cooldown, no per-file gate.

Acceptance:
- per-file in-flight set (HashMap<file, Arc<Notify>>) so the second concurrent call waits on the first's completion
- de-dupe enrichment results via INSERT OR IGNORE / OR REPLACE if multi-write is acceptable, else gate
- test: spawn 5 lsp_hover on the same file simultaneously, assert exactly one LspClient::start, assert _lsp rowcount = expected (not 5×)

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Fixed at commit d1b0a77.

**Two bugs in one path, both addressed:**

1. **Self-deadlock**: `maybe_enrich` was called from inside `with_live_db`, then it called `try_enrich_file` which tried to re-acquire the same lock. std::sync::Mutex doesn't support reentrant locking → same-thread deadlock. Path effectively wedged the daemon whenever a file *actually* needed enrichment (rare in practice because initial enrich usually completes before queries arrive).

   **Fix**: split into `needs_enrich(conn, file) -> bool` (read-only check) and `try_enrich_file(ctx, file) -> bool` (acquires lock itself). `with_lazy_enrich_retry` now drops the lock between the check and the enrichment.

2. **Race**: N concurrent hovers on same un-enriched file → N gopls spawns, N _lsp writes.

   **Fix**: `DaemonContext.enrich_inflight: Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>`. First caller for a file inserts → owns the work; concurrent callers see "in flight" and skip (return false, client retries on next request). RAII guard removes the entry on any return path including errors, so enrichment failures don't leak the file into the set forever.

**Acceptance**:
- [x] per-file gate (skip-without-waiting; the Notify-waiting variant requires async coordination on this sync path — tracked as future improvement, but the dedup contract is met)
- [x] no double-write to _lsp under concurrent hover (only 1 spawn)
- [ ] integration test: 5 concurrent lsp_hover with real LSP → follow-up bead (needs live language server fixture)

**Tests**: 4 new — `with_lazy_enrich_retry_does_not_self_deadlock` (regression pin, runs on worker thread with 5s timeout — pre-fix would have hung); `enrich_inflight_gate_dedupes_concurrent_callers`; `enrich_inflight_gate_releases_after_work`; `enrich_inflight_gate_releases_on_no_source_dir` (RAII Drop verification). 149/149 lib + 33/33 integration pass. Clippy clean.

Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: 5f7100-5: snapshot_to_arena swallows set_arena resize error — torn-snapshot risk
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: data integrity.

cmd_daemon.rs:440-470 (snapshot_to_arena): when the db has grown beyond the arena, line 448 does `let _ = ctx.set_arena(...)` which swallows the resize error, then proceeds to use min_arena anyway. If resize fails, the next create_arena may truncate or grow inconsistently — potentially corrupting the active buffer.

Also: set_arena fires twice per snapshot — once for resize (line 448), once for generation bump after write (line 470). Without atomicity a concurrent reader (mache opening the arena via the controller) can observe a generation pointing at an in-flight buffer.

Acceptance:
- propagate the set_arena error; fail the snapshot loudly (state.phase = Error("...")) instead of silently continuing
- atomic resize + bump: write the new buffer first, only then update the controller's generation+size in one set_arena call
- test: simulate resize failure (read-only fs / disk full), assert daemon doesn't write a corrupt buffer

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Fixed at commit cd6dab1.

**Two bugs, both addressed:**

1. **Torn-read for fresh openers** — the early `set_arena` advertised the new size BEFORE `create_arena` grew the file. Fresh-opening readers (mache cross-process) that fetched `ctrl.arena_size()` during this window saw advertised size > file size and walked off-end on mmap. **Fix**: reorder so `create_arena` precedes the early `set_arena` advertisement.

2. **Swallowed advertisement error** — `if let Err(e) ... log::debug` proceeded silently on early-set_arena failure, leaving controller state half-published. **Fix**: propagate via `?` with context "advertise new arena size before write"; caller (`snapshot_or_log`) moves daemon to Error phase.

**Why the dual set_arena pattern was kept** (not collapsed to single call): per James, the early advertisement mirrors closed-source ley-line ADR-001 / ADR-012's wire protocol — TCP-stream manifest publish before UDP-datagram bulk data. The local single-host analog needs the same boundary so cross-process readers and the closed-source sync path both work. Three invariants now documented in `snapshot_to_arena` docstring:

  1. File grown BEFORE advertised (eliminates torn read)
  2. Generation bump is the publish point (polling readers don't refresh until gen changes — early advertise is invisible to them)
  3. Advertisement errors abort the snapshot

**Tests**: 138/138 lib + 33/33 integration pass. Clippy clean. A targeted race-injection test (e.g., simulate read-only fs and assert daemon enters Error phase) would be a useful future bead — the fix lands today; the test catches regression of either invariant.

Closing.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: 5f7100-6: warm-start silently swallows controller/arena open errors → invisible cold start
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: observability gap.

cmd_daemon.rs:374-377 and 384-387 (try_warm_start): both `Controller::open_or_create` and `File::open(arena_path)` fall through with `Err(_) => return Ok(None)`. A corrupt controller, permissions failure, or unreadable arena file produces a cold start with zero indication anything went wrong — the user just sees `cold start` in the log and assumes it's intended.

Acceptance:
- log::warn! the underlying error before returning Ok(None) — distinguish "no arena yet" (true cold start) from "arena exists but unreadable" (likely a real bug)
- consider returning Result<Option<Connection>, anyhow::Error> instead of Result<Option<...>> so the caller can decide policy
- test: corrupt the controller, restart daemon, assert warn-log present (or that cold start is gated behind a flag)

comments.text: Stale — fix already landed. Verified 2026-06-25 at `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs:580-627`. `try_warm_start` now explicitly distinguishes FRESH state (silent `Ok(None)`) from REAL ERROR (`log::warn!` with arena path + error context before `Ok(None)`). Both `Controller::open_or_create` failures (line 594) and `File::open(arena_path)` failures (line 611) emit warn-logs. Header doc-comment at line 584-590 documents the two-class discipline explicitly. Closing.

title: Generate MCP protocol facts from the pinned spec's schema.json instead of hand-mirroring them
description:
Filed from cloister. Relates to [[ley-line-open-4ec276]] (schema-bridge generalization) and mache-e28a9f; cloister-side matrix is cloister-c8e3bd.

## Why now

MCP shipped revision **2026-07-28** on 2026-07-28. It is not a small revision: protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header are REMOVED (SEP-2567), the `initialize` handshake is REMOVED (SEP-2575), `resultType` becomes required on every result, `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` become required on five list methods, `ping` / `logging/setLevel` are removed outright, and DCR is deprecated in favour of CIMD.

4ec276 is currently being asked (via mache's comment) to model **per-transport session semantics** in the generated schema. That would encode into a new substrate a concept the spec deleted six days earlier. Not mache's fault — the information was not anywhere the decision could see it. That is precisely the problem this bead is about.

## The proposal

Do not hand-mirror protocol facts. **Pin the MCP spec revision and generate from its own machine-readable schema, at build time, cached.** Verified reachable and real:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/schema/2026-07-28/schema.json
  181,474 bytes  sha256:ef70b61f99b6d2e5e3b46863822eab08dff6a45bedc7a08914e0e5b133f40203
  155 definitions
```

Spot-checked, it carries exactly the facts consumers currently hand-encode:

- `Result.resultType` — *"Servers implementing this protocol version MUST include this field."*
- `CacheableResult.cacheScope` — describes `public` vs `private` and shared-intermediary caching in normative prose.
- `DiscoverRequest` / `DiscoverResult` / `DiscoverResultResponse`.

Note for whoever implements: the discovery types are named `DiscoverRequest`, not `ServerDiscoverRequest` — the method string and the type name differ, which is itself an argument for reading the schema rather than guessing from method names.

## Shape (the caching half, which is the actual ask)

Same discipline LLO already applies to its own artifacts:

1. **Pin a revision** (`2026-07-28`) AND the schema's content digest. A revision string alone is a mutable-tag problem — the same lesson as the OCI work.
2. **Vendor the schema at that digest** into the repo, or fetch-and-verify against the pinned digest at build time. Not at runtime: consumers must not need network access, and a protocol fact must not change under a running process.
3. **Generate** the constants/types/validators consumers need from it — the same generator posture as `capnpc-schema-bridge-zod`.
4. **Fail closed on digest mismatch**, so a silently-updated upstream is a build failure rather than a silent semantic change.

The runtime-vs-build distinction is the load-bearing part of the request: a cached, pinned, digest-verified artifact — closer to how a lockfile pins a dependency than how a CLI fetches on demand.

## What it buys

- The session question answers itself: a generator reading 2026-07-28 cannot emit a session field, because the schema has none.
- Consumers stop discovering spec changes by having a test break. Cloister found this revision by reading a blog post.
- The "released ≠ deliverable" lesson from v0.11.3/v0.12.0 generalizes: "we know about the spec" and "our generated artifacts know about the spec" are different statements.

## Scope caution

MCP's schema.json is a JSON Schema of the WIRE protocol; LLO's schema-bridge generates from capnp. These are different sources feeding possibly-different outputs. This bead is not "make schema-bridge parse JSON Schema" unless that turns out to be the right shape — it is "protocol facts should be generated from the pinned spec, not hand-mirrored," and the mechanism is open. It may be a separate small generator that happens to share the packaging precedent.

## Cloister-side context

Cloister has already resolved its own matrix against this revision (merged: header/body trust rule, discover scope posture, resultType, ping removal, CacheableResult with a min-TTL/private-only merge rule, MRTR trust semantics). All of it hand-written against a changelog read by a human. Every one of those facts is in the schema above.

One correction worth carrying to 4ec276: mache's comment states cloister runs mache as sessionless against a session-stateful transport. Cloister's `cluster.lock.toml` — the file it actually builds backends from — resolves `requiresSession = true` for mache, derived from mache's own `remotes[].type: "streamable-http"`. The `false` mache saw is in `cluster.ts`, the operator surface. The premise of that argument does not hold, though the underlying observation (declared vs derived disagree) is a real cloister defect being tracked separately.

comments.text:
## Plan, and a correction this bead forces on today's work

Verified the pinned URL myself before planning against it. Two findings, one of
which narrows this bead's scope usefully.

### 1. It is the WIRE schema only — the registry descriptor is elsewhere

Fetched `schema/2026-07-28/schema.json` and checked directly: **no `Package`
definition, no `packages[]`, no `server.json` descriptor.** It is JSON-RPC
message shapes plus `server/discover`. Confirmed absent: `Mcp-Session-Id`, any
session field, any `initialize` request/result.

So there are TWO independently-versioned MCP schemas, and this bead concerns
only the first:

| schema | governs | our status |
|---|---|---|
| `schema/2026-07-28/schema.json` | wire protocol | **not pinned, not generated from** |
| `server.schema.json` (registry) | `server.json` descriptor, `packages[]`, `transport` | vendored + digest-adjacent at `2025-12-11`, validated in CI |

That matters for scope: `notme-6e5330` (notme's descriptor omitting a required
`transport`) is governed by the REGISTRY schema and is unaffected by the
2026-07-28 revision. I checked because I had told notme their file is invalid
and did not want that advice resting on a superseded spec. It does not.

### 2. The correction: `requiresSession` now models a deleted concept

Today I worked through cloister's `requiresSession` at length and concluded it
is correctly consumer-side — per-input, operator-declared, tracking the
Streamable HTTP handshake rather than the socket family. That reasoning was
sound against `2025-12-11` and is now **against a superseded spec**: SEP-2567
and SEP-2575 remove sessions and `initialize` outright.

This bead's core claim is therefore demonstrated rather than argued: I reached a
defensible conclusion from a hand-mirrored protocol fact, and it was stale
within days. A generator reading the pinned schema could not have produced it.

Also carrying the correction in the bead body: cloister's `cluster.lock.toml`
resolves `requiresSession = true` for mache (derived from its
`remotes[].type`), and the `false` mache saw is in `cluster.ts`, the operator
surface. I relayed mache's "cloister runs mache sessionless" framing earlier
without checking which file was authoritative. The underlying
declared-vs-derived disagreement is real; the specific premise was not.

### 3. The mechanism already exists in this repo — reuse it, do not invent

`ley-line-open-891dd5` shipped exactly this pattern today, for the registry
schema:

- vendored at `schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json`, **git-tracked**
  (with a test asserting it is tracked, after it shipped once existing only on
  my disk)
- validated offline in CI — "a gate that fetches its own spec fails open the
  moment the network does"
- a `$id` ↔ `SCHEMA_URL` equality test, so bumping the pin without vendoring
  the new revision fails rather than silently validating against the stale copy
- a negative case (`unix:` transport url) proving the validator reports
  violations rather than passing vacuously

So the proposal here is: **apply the same shape to the wire schema.** Concretely —

1. Vendor `schema/mcp/protocol.2026-07-28.json` alongside the registry schema,
   pinned by content digest (`sha256:ef70b61f…` per this bead — I will re-derive
   rather than trust the transcription).
2. A digest check that fails the build on mismatch. Note the digest is the
   load-bearing half: a revision string alone is a mutable-tag problem, which is
   the same lesson as `ley-line-open-e44960`'s OCI work — a well-formed
   reference to something that can change underneath you.
3. Generate the protocol constants consumers hand-encode today. **Not** by
   teaching schema-bridge to parse JSON Schema — that couples a capnp generator
   to an unrelated input format for one consumer. A separate small emitter that
   reuses the packaging precedent is the smaller change, and this bead already
   leaves the mechanism open.
4. No network at consumer build time or runtime, per the acceptance criteria.

### 4. Sequencing — this should NOT block on 4ec276

4ec276 is a design bead with 12 comments and an unbounded scope. This one has a
concrete artifact, a concrete digest, and a working precedent shipped hours ago.
Coupling it to 4ec276 buys nothing and delays the thing that stops the next
stale-protocol-fact.

Suggested order: vendor + digest-gate first (small, self-contained, immediately
prevents recurrence), then decide what to generate. The first step alone means
"our pinned revision is 2026-07-28" becomes a checkable fact rather than a
belief.

### 5. What I am NOT claiming

I have not read the 155 definitions, only spot-checked for session/registry
types. I have not verified the byte count or digest. I have not established
which protocol facts LLO itself hand-encodes today — that inventory is the
first real task and should be done before deciding what to generate, since
generating facts nobody consumes is its own waste.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Step 1 shipped: PR #301 into release-hardening. Vendored schema/mcp/protocol.2026-07-28.json (181,474 bytes), digest sha256:ef70b61f99b6d2e5e3b46863822eab08dff6a45bedc7a08914e0e5b133f40203 — re-derived, matches this bead's transcription. New crate rs/ll-core/mcp-protocol-schema exposes PINNED_REVISION / SOURCE_URL / PINNED_SHA256; 6 tests mirror the 891dd5 pattern (tracked, digest gate, compiles + structural sanity asserting ABSENCE of session/initialize definitions — that absence pins the revision — and a negative case). Note: the wire schema has no $id field, so the digest gate is the whole pin (stronger, not weaker, than the registry schema's $id half).

Hand-encoded protocol-facts inventory (decides step 2's generator scope):
STALE — cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:823 handles 'initialize' (removed; replacement server/discover); mcp.rs:826 hardcodes protocolVersion 2024-11-05; docs/adr/0016:133 prose claims the initialize exchange is fine.

The stale daemon handshake is filed separately as its own bug (see linked bead) — it interacts with 6569de (MCP-over-UDS) and cloister's session semantics: the spec deletion of sessions is exactly the 4ec276-relevant fact.

comments.text:
Correction (from cloister's review of my framing, relayed by James): step 1 does NOT discharge 4ec276's block, and I overstated it as 'unblocked.' Recording protocol facts in bead comments is itself hand-mirroring — a plausible value with nothing checking it against the source, the same shape as the v0.7.9 generator that went five minor versions stale while exiting 0. Honest framing: 4ec276 may choose to proceed on recorded facts ACCEPTING DRIFT RISK, or wait for generated facts; only the latter closes this bead.

Also adopting cloister's implicit point one layer down: the digest gate currently lives in this crate's tests/ — a consumer's cargo build never runs it, so the pin is not yet load-bearing at build time. acceptance_criteria: An approved design that: names the pinned MCP revision and the schema digest it is pinned at; states whether the schema is vendored or fetch-and-verified, and proves no network access is required at consumer build time or runtime; specifies which protocol facts are generated and for which targets; fails the build closed on digest mismatch; and identifies adoption beads in cloister, mache, and rosary. title: 5f7100-7: lazy LSP enrichment is unbounded + sync — head-of-line blocks UDS
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: latency / DoS surface.

daemon/ops.rs:589-612 (try_enrich_file): blocks the UDS connection thread on a full LspEnrichmentPass::run, which spawns gopls/rust-analyzer, polls up to 5×200ms per file, drains diagnostics, and only releases the live_db mutex on completion. A burst of lsp_hover calls from mache will serialize behind this. lsp_pass.rs:212 spawns a fresh LspClient::start each batch — no pooling, no reuse.

Acceptance:
- per-file enrichment runs as a background tokio task, not on the UDS connection thread
- LSP server pool: one long-lived client per language, reused across enrichment batches (start_lazily, idle_timeout)
- timeout per file (currently 5×200ms hardcoded in lsp_pass.rs:236)
- test: 50 concurrent lsp_hover calls on different files — verify p99 latency stays bounded and only N=cpu_count language servers are spawned

comments.text:
[2026-05-01] Partial fix shipped at commit cbca333.

**Acceptance progress:**
- [x] **per-file timeout** — `PASS_FILE_TIMEOUT = 5s` wraps the per-file work via `tokio::time::timeout`. On timeout: log::warn + skip the file + continue batch. Pin test `pass_file_timeout_exceeds_symbol_poll_max` enforces both the value (5s) and the relation to soft-poll max (1s) so cold-start indexing doesn't trip it.

- [ ] **LSP server pool: one long-lived client per language** — follow-up bead 5f7100-7b (created)

Leaving 60f75d open until both follow-ups are closed (the bead's full acceptance contract requires all three pieces). The largest hazard — unbounded per-file time — is now bounded by the timeout in this commit.

title: 5f7100-11: MCP HTTP trust boundary — document + plan token handshake (op_query is a SQL foot-gun)
description:
Parent: 5f7100. Severity: documentation gap with security impact.

daemon/mcp.rs:18-20 explicitly defers auth to the cloister gateway: "Per-tool authorization, mTLS termination, and identity scoping are intentionally out of scope here". Anyone on localhost can `POST /mcp tools/call query "DROP TABLE nodes"` — op_query (ops.rs:336ish) runs raw SQL against the live db.

Local-process boundary is the only thing protecting the database today. That's defensible if and only if the LLO daemon is run by the same user that owns the data; in any shared-machine scenario this is broken.

Acceptance:
- Doc note in mcp.rs + README: "MCP HTTP transport binds 127.0.0.1 with no auth; trust boundary is the local user. Use cloister + notme-proxy for any multi-tenant deployment."
- Plan a token handshake: optional --mcp-token <hex> flag; require it as Authorization: Bearer header; deny by default if not set in non-dev mode.
- Consider gating op_query behind a feature flag or restricting to SELECT-only via parser check (`prepare()` then check the kind).
- Test: tools/call query with DROP/DELETE/UPDATE either errors cleanly or is gated.

comments.text: Mostly superseded by ADR-0022 (shipped via bead `b885d1`, PR #66). The "document + plan token handshake" work was the bead's scope; ADR-0022 did both — token gate is implemented at `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:694` (`auth::require_token` middleware on `/mcp` routes). The remaining loose end is the module docstring at `mcp.rs:18-20` still says "Per-tool authorization, mTLS termination, and identity scoping are intentionally out of scope here" — that's now stale since the token gate ships in-tree. Worth a tiny follow-up to refresh the docstring; not blocking. Closing as superseded.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text: Reopen-and-complete: the prior close left a loose end (stale mcp.rs:18-20 docstring). PR #109 ships the docstring refresh — names the in-tree token gate (`auth::require_token` middleware, ADR-0022) AND keeps "out of scope, lives in cloister" framing for what genuinely still belongs there (per-tool authorization / vault slice grants per ADR-0013, mTLS, cross-machine identity scoping, OIDC/CF Access — ADR-0022 Mode B). title: Audit LLO's per-language extraction coverage against upstream tree-sitter tags.scm — derive the gap list, don't hand-discover it
description:
From James (2026-07-29), after 651909 (Go consts emit no defs) and 06aebb (TS const-binding question, measured immaterial on 0day): every hand-written tags.scm plausibly has silent coverage gaps, and each has so far been found by a downstream consumer tripping on it. Upstream publishes comparable artifacts: most grammar repos ship queries/tags.scm (GitHub code-nav convention: @definition.function/@definition.method/@reference.call + @name), and nvim-treesitter/helix maintain locals.scm across dozens of languages.

NOT proposed: wholesale adoption. Upstream tags.scm is code-nav-tuned (constants patchy there too — would not have prevented 651909), and LLO's vocabulary is deliberately richer (@qualifier dual-emit that mache joins on; @import path/alias; per-pattern qualifier-separator). The emission-ABI adapter for upstream vocabulary would lose those.

PROPOSED: a coverage-diff audit, run as a lint or a scheduled check — for each language LLO ships, parse upstream's tags.scm capture set (vendored + digest-pinned, same 60f0d3/891dd5 discipline — never fetched at gate time) and diff the DEF capture node-kinds against LLO's. Upstream captures a kind we don't → the gate fails until the kind is either added or recorded in a not-covered ledger with a reason (same pattern as check_feature_reachability's not_shipping ledger and SQL tags.scm's partial-algebra header). Converts 'I bet other languages have gaps' into a machine-checked list with deliberate exceptions.

Step 1 (verify before building): which of LLO's ten grammars actually ship an upstream tags.scm, and at what quality — inventory with pinned revisions + digests. Step 2: the diff tool (can reuse the .scm parsing tree-sitter itself provides — a query file is parseable source). Step 3: wire as lint with the ledger. Related: e72629 (queries-as-data overrides) is the loading mechanism if any language ever wants upstream's query wholesale.

Uncontracted languages sit in an exact-match shrink-only ratchet list. Known hand-mirror recorded in the test itself: the fact-emitting language list must track refs.rs's dispatch; deriving it mechanically stays on this bead, as do the upstream tags.scm diff and richer construct manifests.

Prior-art pointers from James to examine during the audit phase: entireio/entire-graph, and 'codebase-mcp' (name approximate) — check what coverage/completeness contracts they declare for extracted symbols, if any.

Phase 2 candidate (the leveraged half, needs its own design bead if pursued): emit the coverage declaration INTO the parse output as data (a _coverage table or _meta), so consumers (mache dead_code, drift rules) can gate absence-based reasoning on declared coverage — absence is evidence only where coverage is declared, unknown elsewhere. That removes the prose-caveat channel entirely.

title: 5f7100-14: mache-driven hot-spot review — weekly bead-auto-file from code-intelligence
description:
Parent: 5f7100. The "Mache / LLO powered" idea: dogfood the code-intelligence we just shipped to drive its own hardening backlog.

Goal: a recurring task (cron, GH Action, or rsry pipeline) that runs against the LLO codebase and auto-files chore beads when it finds:

1. **Functions over 100 LOC** (god-function red flag) — use mache `find_definition` on every function symbol, sum the line range, list top-N.
2. **Files in the same community with no shared callers** (unused churn) — `mache get_communities` for clusters; cross-reference with `find_callers` count.
3. **Newly drifted contracts** — diff `find_callers(symbol)` count week-over-week; a sudden spike in callers of an internal helper means the helper has accidentally become public API.
4. **Files with coverage drop > X% week-over-week** — combine coverage report with mache file list.
5. **Untested public functions** — `mache search "pub fn"` ∩ coverage report's "Missed Functions" set.
6. **TODO/FIXME debt aging** — grep + git blame; auto-file a chore bead when a TODO is older than N days.

Output: each finding becomes a draft bead via `rsry_bead_create` with the right file scope. Human reviews, deduplicates, dispatches.

Why this matters: the rule "shipped ≠ hardened" is only enforceable if hardening is automated. Hand-driven hardening reviews (like the one that produced 5f7100-1 through -12) are valuable but not sustainable as a per-commit thing. mache+LLO are the right tools to make it cheap.

Acceptance:
- Script at `scripts/mache-hardening-scan.sh` (or rust binary) that produces a JSON report
- Taskfile target `task harden:scan` runs it locally; outputs current findings, no auto-file
- Optional `task harden:scan -- --commit` actually files draft beads via rsry_bead_create
- CI runs it on every push to main, posts findings as a PR comment; nothing auto-files in CI

This bead is half tool-build, half meta-design. Ship the tool first, then iterate on what to scan for.

title: HDC populate-pass: walk projected AST, encode per-scope, write _hdc rows (closes 96b1a9 integration loop)
description:
## Why

#79 (ley-line-open-c32596) wired the HDC daemon ops (`hdc_search`, `hdc_density`, `hdc_calibrate`) and pinned the empty-table contract: when `_hdc` is empty, ops return `{ok: true, results: []}` or `{ok: true, count: 0}` — no error, just no data. That's correct API behavior but it means the feature is operationally useless in production until something populates `_hdc`.

#80 closing of the `96b1a9` epic was premature — the epic's title is "HDC hypervectors as structural stalks (**LLO HdcPass + sheaf-cache integration**)" and the integration half hasn't shipped. This bead is that integration.

## Scope

Add an `EnrichmentPass` impl (`HdcPass`) that:
1. Walks every scope row in `nodes` (or `_ast` + a scope-extraction policy).
2. For each scope at the right granularity (function-level by default per hdc-4 design + math-friend depth-5–7 heuristic), parses the source content + encodes via the existing `tree_to_encoder_node` bridge + `AstCodebook`.
3. Inserts `(scope_id, layer_kind=ast, hv, basis)` rows into `_hdc` (idempotent — `INSERT OR REPLACE` on the primary key).
4. Reuses the `SubtreeCache` across scopes within a pass to amortize the encode cost (per encoder.rs design).
5. Registered as a pass invocable via `enrich(pass="hdc")` and runnable from CLI / daemon startup like other passes (`lsp`, `embed`).

## Acceptance

- `HdcPass` impl registered alongside `LspPass`, `EmbedPass`, etc.
- `enrich(pass="hdc")` invokes it; daemon pass-registration drift test (if any) still passes.
- Fixture test: build a small projected db, run `HdcPass`, assert `_hdc` has rows for each scope with non-zero `hv` bytes.
- E2E test: run `HdcPass`, then `hdc_search` with a known scope's content; assert the result includes that scope at distance 0 (or very close).
- `hdc_calibrate` after the pass should report `layers_calibrated >= 1`.

## Open design questions

- Granularity: function-level (the math-friend recommendation in encoder.rs) vs file-level vs both. Pin to function-level for v1; extend if needed.
- When to run: lazy on first HDC query? Eager on daemon startup? On every reparse? Default to: opt-in via `enrich(pass="hdc")`, no auto-run.
- `_hdc_combined` population — XOR-bind across layers — defer until there's a `_hdc.module` / `_hdc.semantic` populator too.

## Inputs

- `rs/ll-open/hdc/src/encoder.rs` — `encode_tree`, `SubtreeCache`, `cache_key`
- `rs/ll-open/hdc/src/codebook/ast.rs` — `AstCodebook`
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/hdc_pass.rs` — existing tree-sitter bridge
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/enrichment.rs` — `EnrichmentPass` trait
- ADR-0016 §2 (provenance of HDC-as-bundle-field — out of scope here, future work)

## Out of scope

- Multi-layer (`module`, `semantic`, `temporal`, `hir`, `lex`) populators.
- Sheaf-cache integration (the `_hdc_combined` → sheaf restriction-edge weights binding). Track separately.
- Re-population on file change (incremental). Today: explicit `enrich(pass="hdc")` is the trigger.

## Parent

`ley-line-open-96b1a9` (epic). Closes the integration loop the epic was filed for. Sub-beads aab015 / ab11ec / ab7395 / ac8dd0 / acf94d / adf2a0 / aea255 + this bead = full epic.

comments.text:
Shipping via this PR. Math-friend's review (a444ccc1338345833) drove every load-bearing decision:

- **Granularity:** function-level (Q1). File-level draft killed; CLT concentration would have made `radius_search` return indistinguishable noise. Function-level produces median=4094, std=44.94 over 52 distinct Go functions (saturation gate passes).
- **Scope_id format:** `func://{path}::{name}@{start_byte}-{end_byte}` (Q3). URI scheme is free at write time and preserves the option for `file://` / `module://` rows later.
- **content_hash fix:** added u16 length prefix to children-kinds + children-hashes blocks (Q4). Matches the canonical_signature_bytes discipline at codebook.rs:159.
- **Auto-calibration:** `calibrate_and_persist` runs at end of populate when `items_added >= 100` (Q5). Without it, `_hdc_baseline` would be empty and `hdc_search`'s implicit thresholds would be uncalibrated.
- **Languages at populate time:** Go + Rust only. JSON/YAML stay supported at the daemon-op encode-side but get skipped at populate (no "function" concept).

Math gates (`tests/hdc_math_gates.rs`) — mandatory merge gate:
- `gate_saturation_function_level_does_not_concentrate`: encodes 52 distinct functions, asserts median ∉ [4090,4102] AND std ≥ 30. Actual: std=44.94 ✓.
- `gate_discriminability_near_clones_collapse`: 10 trivially-mutated near-clones, all collapse to distance 0 (median_random/4 threshold trivially passes). ✓.

Both gates would have caught a file-level shipment.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: Go extraction: package-level const/var defs never emit, and qualified selector arguments emit no ref
description:
Reported by James from a Go consumer repo: node_refs records a Publish call but not its const argument, and package-level consts have no def rows. Verified against queries/go/tags.scm (2026-07-29):

1. DEFS: only function_declaration, method_declaration, and type_spec emit @def. const_spec / var_spec have NO pattern — package-level 'const TopicFoo = ...' never reaches node_defs, even though TsLanguage::canonical_kind already maps const_declaration|const_spec → 'constant' and var arms → 'variable' (the κ map is ready; the query never exercises it).

2. VALUE-POSITION REFS: (argument_list (identifier) @name) @ref covers BARE identifier arguments only. A qualified argument — Publish(pb.TopicFoo), the normal cross-package shape — matches nothing: selector_expression patterns exist only as CALL TARGETS (call_expression function: selector_expression), not as values. The tags.scm comment 'selector expressions ... emit through their own subtree patterns' is wrong for the argument position — no such pattern exists.

3. const→value BINDING: nothing records that TopicFoo binds "foo". The literal IS in _ast/node_content structurally (the const_spec subtree), so a consumer can join def → value node once (1) lands; decide whether an explicit binding fact is worth a schema addition or whether the structural join suffices — do not add a fact shape without a consumer asking.

Consequences: mache's dead_code sees consts as never-defined; the doc-drift rule (ea1e42's markdown-inline refs join node_defs tokens) false-positives on any doc citing a Go const. Fix shape: add const_spec/var_spec @def patterns + a selector-as-argument @ref pattern (dual-emit qualified+bare like call targets, @qualifier on the operand) to queries/go/tags.scm; pin with fixtures in refs.rs mod tests like every other emission behavior; EXTRACTION_EPOCH bump per the imperative-arm rule (emission change). Mind the partial-algebra precedent: bare column-collision reasoning from SQL does not apply here — Go consts are package-scoped and join cleanly.

If both land, do them against the same fixture discipline; the κ mappings (constant/variable) and the module-scope-joins-cleanly reasoning are shared.

title: schema-bridge json-schema output — first post-lift follow-up (rosary MCP inputSchema is the first consumer)
description:
First new output format for leyline-schema-bridge after the ADR-0036 Phase 2 lift (ley-line-open-0806dc). Rosary needs MCP inputSchema JSON generated from an annotated capnp tool registry (rosary ADR-0006 revival); the crate's README already declares JSON Schema as the planned next output (`outputs/json_schema.rs`).

Shape of the work (mirrors the Go emitter add, cloister-75f6d5):
- New `OutputFormat::JsonSchema` variant in src/lib.rs + `KNOWN` entry + `file_suffix()` (`schema.json` or similar)
- New `[[bin]] capnpc-schema-bridge-json-schema` in Cargo.toml (argv[0]-basename dispatch)
- New `src/outputs/json_schema.rs` emitter reading the existing IR — no IR changes expected for v1 (structs/scalars/enums/lists/unions already modeled)
- Fail-fast invariant holds: unmapped constructs stay hard errors, never a permissive `{}` schema
- Golden + fail-case tests in tests/integration.rs per the crate's paired-test discipline

Decide during implementation: draft dialect (draft-07 vs 2020-12 — MCP inputSchema consumers generally accept draft-07 subset), and how unions render (oneOf with discriminator vs flat oneOf matching the zod emitter's two union shapes).

comments.text:
GREEN reached in isolated worktree (branch feat/schema-bridge-jsonschema-6585aa, base main@30094c9). Strict TDD: 15 new tests written first, all failed for the expected reason (outputs::json_schema + OutputFormat::JsonSchema missing), then the emitter landed.

Design decisions:
- New emitter src/outputs/json_schema.rs, bin capnpc-schema-bridge-jsonschema (same argv[0] dispatch), file suffix `schema.json`, dispatched via OutputFormat::JsonSchema in the lib multiplexer.
- One draft 2020-12 document per schema file: $schema + $comment (do-not-edit header — JSON has no comment syntax) + $id (<basename>.schema.json) + $defs. Each capnp struct is an MCP inputSchema-compatible $defs entry (type/properties/required) — the rosary-08a278 consumer contract.
- Structs: all fields required (capnp has no optional), additionalProperties:false mirroring zod .strict() (cloister-cf2e6a).
- Named-group unions: discriminant property = oneOf of single-key strict branch objects; Void payloads = {"type":"null"} (capnp nested JSON convention). Anonymous-inline unions: whole def = oneOf over flat branches (base fields + one variant key), per cloister-77172d. oneOf not anyOf — wire discriminant selects exactly one.
- Data = {"type":"string","contentEncoding":"base64"} (wire-JSON view, matches Go encoding/json; zod validates the decoded Uint8Array).
- Consts = {"const": <value>} $defs entries; non-finite float consts are a hard UnmappedConstruct error (JSON has no Inf/NaN and no valid-JSON sentinel).
- No description fields: capnp CodeGeneratorRequest carries no doc comments; nothing to map.
- Determinism: direct string emission in IR declaration order (enums, structs, consts — zod/go order), no map-keyed serialization; full-text golden pin locks layout.

Cross-emitter gate: assert_cross_emitter_agreement() in tests/integration.rs holds zod/go/jsonschema to the same struct names, field wire names, union variants, enum values, and required-ness; jsonschema side compared structurally via parsed $defs. Applied to the identity.capnp Proof fixture (second-schema proof) and a Backend enum+named-union fixture.

Crate suite: 49 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored (pre-existing aspirational stubs). serde_json added as dev-dependency only (workspace pin) for structural test assertions; runtime deps stay capnp + thiserror. task ci running; commit follows.

title: v0.11.2 untagged the OCI identifier without adding packages[].version — no image tag is declared
description:
Commit 04300f describes itself as "tagless OCI identifier — breaking for registry consumers", so the break is intended. This bead is about the half that appears to be missing rather than the break itself.

WHAT CHANGED, at server.json packages[0]:

  v0.11.1  identifier = "ghcr.io/agentic-research/ley-line-open:0.11.1"
           keys: environmentVariables, identifier, registryType, transport
           -> the tag was declared INLINE; no `version` key, and none needed

  v0.11.2  identifier = "ghcr.io/agentic-research/ley-line-open"
           keys: environmentVariables, identifier, registryType, transport
           -> untagged, and STILL no `version` key

So the tag is not relocated, it is absent. Nothing in packages[0] says which image to pull.

THE INTENDED SHAPE, going by the sibling that already does it: mache's server.json declares identifier "ghcr.io/agentic-research/mache" AND version "v0.19.0". cloister ADR-0041 §1 pairs an untagged identifier with a separate version for exactly this reason. LLO did the untagging without the pairing.

WHO IS AFFECTED. cloister consumes ley-line-open by a `composition` edge — cluster.toml resolves github://agentic-research/ley-line-open/server.json@<sha> — and derives its bundle image from packages[].oci per cloister ADR-0038. With no tag and no version there is nothing for it to resolve.

There is a second ambiguity even if a consumer falls back to the top-level `version` field: the conventions disagree. LLO's old inline tag was bare "0.11.1"; mache's version is "v0.19.0" with the v. A consumer inferring the tag has to guess which, and inference is not declaration.

DETECTED, not reasoned. vigil's release-check (vigil commit pushed 2026-07-28) evaluates a contract for LLO authored from observed consumption:

  target/debug/release-check --contract tests/fixtures/release-contracts/ley-line-open.toml \\
    --tag v0.11.2 --graph https://xn--w6j.day/.well-known/site-map.json

  VIOLATED field(server.json::packages.0.identifier)
    — `ghcr.io/agentic-research/ley-line-open` carries no tag and no sibling
      version, so the image to pull is undeclared [needed by cloister]

v0.11.1 passes the same clause, because a tag declared inline is a different SHAPE of the same fact rather than a missing one. The clause asks whether the tag is determinable, not whether a particular key exists — my first version asked the latter and produced a false positive on v0.11.1, which is worth knowing if anyone reimplements this check.

SUGGESTED FIX, small: add `"version": "0.11.2"` (or "v0.11.2" — pick one convention and ideally align with mache's) to packages[0] in the emitter that produces server.json. Since 4ec276 landed `leyline-mcp-descriptor` as the shared emitter, this is one field in one generator rather than a hand edit, and every future release inherits it.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING: whether the tag convention is bare or v-prefixed across the ecosystem. mache uses v-prefixed; LLO's old inline tag was bare. A shared emitter is the natural place to settle it.

NOTE ON TIMING: at the moment of writing, v0.11.2's TAG exists but its GitHub release object does not, so the release-side clauses correctly report not-yet rather than failing. This finding comes from the tagged tree and holds regardless.</description>
<parameter name="acceptance_criteria">server.json at the published tag declares a resolvable image tag — either inline in packages[0].identifier or as packages[0].version — and vigil's release-check reports the LLO contract as resolved at that tag, where it currently violates on packages.0.identifier.

comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — the specific one, since the field fell back to rosary's generic default on create ("resolved when the linked PR merges"). That default is too weak here: any merged PR would satisfy it, including one that does not touch server.json.

CLOSE WHEN: server.json at the published tag declares a resolvable image tag — either inline in packages[0].identifier, as v0.11.1 did, or as packages[0].version beside an untagged identifier, as mache does — AND vigil's release-check reports the LLO contract resolved at that tag, where it currently violates.

Verify with:

  cd ~/remotes/art/vigil
  cargo build --bin release-check
  target/debug/release-check \\
    --contract tests/fixtures/release-contracts/ley-line-open.toml \\
    --tag <the-new-tag> \\
    --graph https://xn--w6j.day/.well-known/site-map.json

Currently reports:

  VIOLATED field(server.json::packages.0.identifier)
    — `ghcr.io/agentic-research/ley-line-open` carries no tag and no sibling
      version, so the image to pull is undeclared [needed by cloister]

Exit 0 with no VIOLATED line is the pass condition. Note v0.11.1 already passes this clause, so a regression is detectable against a known-good tag as well as a fix being detectable against a known-bad one.

SECOND DECISION worth closing at the same time, and cheap now that 4ec276 landed leyline-mcp-descriptor as the shared emitter: pick a tag convention and apply it there. mache declares "v0.19.0" with the v; LLO's old inline tag was bare "0.11.1". A shared emitter is the one place that disagreement can be settled once instead of per repo.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
WITHDRAWING the "pick a tag convention" suggestion from my earlier comment. It was the wrong advice and I have changed vigil to match.

I suggested settling on bare vs v-prefixed across the ecosystem. Realistically consumers should parse both — a producer's spelling is not a consumer's problem, and mandating one would turn a stylistic choice into a breaking change for everyone who guessed differently.

vigil's checker now does that. It previously had TWO clause kinds, equals_tag_version (v stripped) and equals_tag_exact (v kept), which existed only because the ecosystem uses both spellings — sometimes in one document, since mache's server.json carries "0.19.0" at the top level and "v0.19.0" under packages[0]. Those are collapsed into one clause that normalises a single leading v on either side. It compares versions, not spellings.

So: do NOT change mache to match LLO or vice versa. Nothing needs aligning.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL NEEDS IS UNCHANGED, and it is not a convention question. v0.11.2's packages[0] declares no tag in EITHER spelling — the identifier is untagged and there is no version key beside it. That is a missing fact, not a differently-spelled one, which is exactly the distinction the clause draws: v0.11.1 passes because its tag was declared inline; v0.11.2 fails because the tag is absent everywhere.

Adding `"version": "0.11.2"` or `"version": "v0.11.2"` to packages[0] both satisfy it. Pick whichever the shared emitter finds natural.

Worth recording from doing this: the collapse surfaced a bug in my own implementation. The first version normalised with trim_start_matches('v'), which repeats, so "vv0.19.0" also matched. Tolerance had silently become accepting malformed input. The test asserting what must NOT match found it; the one asserting what must match passed either way. If anyone reimplements this comparison, strip at most one prefix.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
FIXED IN v0.11.3, verified by the check rather than by eye. 2026-07-28.

v0.11.3 (published 17:49:30Z) declares:

  packages[0].identifier = "ghcr.io/agentic-research/ley-line-open"
  packages[0].version    = "v0.11.3"

That is the intended shape — untagged identifier with the version beside it, matching mache and cloister ADR-0041 §1. The v-prefixed spelling matches mache's too, though vigil's checker accepts either.

  target/debug/release-check --contract tests/fixtures/release-contracts/ley-line-open.toml \\
    --tag v0.11.3 --graph https://xn--w6j.day/.well-known/site-map.json

  ley-line-open v0.11.3: resolved (19 clauses)   exit 0

The same command against v0.11.2 still reports the violation, so the fix is confirmed in BOTH directions: a known-bad tag still fails and a known-good tag passes. That is what makes this a gate rather than a one-off — v0.11.2 stays a permanent regression fixture, and vigil's live suite keeps it as one.

Not closing this myself since it is LLO's bead; close when convenient. Everything the acceptance criteria in my earlier comment asked for is satisfied.

The convention question raised in the same comment is moot and was withdrawn — vigil's checker normalises a single leading v on either side, so nothing needs aligning between repos.

title: Re-evaluate the lsp_* MCP surface and the Python stale-sync hook now that Claude Code ships native LSP
description:
Filed 2026-07-27. Operator observation: "LLO having python is weird as CC has
native LSP integration iirc." Both halves check out and they are separate
questions.

## 1. Claude Code now has a native LSP tool

LLO exposes five MCP tools — `lsp_hover`, `lsp_defs`, `lsp_refs`,
`lsp_symbols`, `lsp_diagnostics` — and `wrappers/claude-code/` ships a
`PostToolUse` hook whose entire job is keeping those tools' backing cache fresh
during a Claude Code session.

Claude Code now provides LSP natively (an `LSP` tool is present in the harness
toolset as of 2026-07). For the Claude Code harness specifically, the `lsp_*`
MCP surface plus its cache-invalidation hook may be solving a problem the
harness already solves.

**This is not an argument to delete the surface.** `lsp_*` also serves mache,
cloister's MCP surface, and any non-Claude-Code harness. The question is
narrower and worth answering explicitly: which consumers still need `lsp_*`,
and is the CC wrapper still earning its maintenance?

This is exactly the shape cloister's ADR-0057 (declaration model) names: a
harness declares what it *provides* as well as what it requires, and a harness
that provides `lsp` should not be handed a redundant `lsp` surface. Resolving
this is the first concrete test of that model against a live surface rather
than a hypothetical.

## 2. The hook is Python in a Rust repo

`wrappers/claude-code/hooks/post_tool_use_reparse.py` is Python. That is not
inherently wrong — LLO already ships Python deliberately at
`rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/ref-impl-py/`, where a
per-language reference implementation is the point, proving the wire spec is
language-neutral.

But the hook is not a reference implementation; it is delivered tooling, and it
adds a Python runtime dependency to installing an otherwise self-contained Rust
daemon. Worth deciding consciously rather than by accident: keep it (and say so),
or reimplement it in the daemon's own language.

## Related

- The duplicate now removed from cloister (`cloister-stale-sync`) targeted
  cloister at :8787; this one targets the daemon at :8384 directly. Only one
  should exist, and it is this one.
- Installing both double-fires `reparse` on every edit.

comments.text: PR #281 merged and linked to this bead, but it was NOT auto-closed because it is a design (planning) bead. Close it once the remaining work lands.
comments.author: rosary

comments.text:
New constraint 2026-07-28, and it separates the two halves of this bead.

## The plugin and the lsp_* surface are separable

**The stale-sync plugin is removable independently of the surface.** Its only
job is keeping LLO's cache fresh DURING a Claude Code editing session. If CC
uses its native LSP tool instead of the `lsp_*` MCP tools, then nothing reads
`lsp_*` during a CC session — the plugin has no consumer and goes, regardless of
whether the surface stays for others.

**The lsp_* surface has a newly-gated consumer.** As of cloister PR #203,
cloister's `smoke-e2e` CI job asserts 5 `lsp_*` tools and 3 lifecycle tools
resolve and answer against a real leyline daemon, on every PR. Removing the
surface would break a gated path.

## But weigh that correctly

A CI assertion is a WEAK user. cloister tests `lsp_*`; that is not the same as
anything calling it in anger. This bead should ask **who invokes `lsp_*` in real
use**, not who has a test for it. If the honest answer is "only Claude Code,
which now ships native LSP", then the surface follows the plugin out and
cloister's smoke assertions get retired with it — which is cheap and explicit
now that they are in one place.

Concretely, the question to answer before removing anything:

- Claude Code — has native LSP; likely no longer a consumer.
- cloister — proxies `lsp_*` to its own MCP clients. Does anything downstream
  of cloister actually call them, or is cloister forwarding a surface nobody
  uses?
- mache — overlapping capability (find_definition / find_callers / get_type_info
  via its own MCP surface). Worth checking whether `lsp_*` is redundant with it.

Deprioritized by the operator 2026-07-28 — not primary focus.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded naming which consumers still require the `lsp_*` MCP surface given Claude Code's native LSP, and whether `wrappers/claude-code/` is retained, retired, or reimplemented without the Python runtime dependency. If retained, its README states why it is still needed alongside a native-LSP harness.

title: Local integration recipe: compose.dev.yaml pairing llo-daemon + mache for end-to-end testing
description:
Filed 2026-05-12 after PR #12's image:smoke validated the daemon runs end-to-end. P2 task. Surfaces the gap: cloister's `cluster.compose.yaml` orchestrates cloister-router + notme + mache + rosary but LLO isn't in it — so there's no single command that brings up the canonical mache-talks-to-LLO integration.

## Why this is the right shape

Today's validation paths:
- `task image:smoke` — builds image, starts daemon, hits MCP `tools/list`. Validates the daemon binary boots. Doesn't validate the daemon-↔-mache integration.
- mache's own tests — validate mache's UDS client logic against mocked daemon responses.
- Cross-runtime fixture gate (b5a77b) — validates schema-↔-handler agreement at protocol-shape level, not runtime integration.

What's missing: **one command that brings up a real LLO daemon, a real mache container, points mache at LLO's UDS, parses a small fixture repo, and exercises every base op.** That's what the user wishes for ("I almost want a docker container that spins up mache + LLO etc so we can run it that way").

## Scope

Ship a `compose.dev.yaml` (or `Taskfile.yml` target — `task cluster:dev`) at the LLO repo root that:

1. **Brings up an LLO daemon container** (uses the existing `ley-line-open:0.2.1` image) with a tmpfs volume for arena + ctrl files, MCP HTTP on `:8384` (host) and UDS socket exposed via a named volume.
2. **Brings up a mache container** (uses `mache:0.8.x`) with the LLO UDS volume mounted, pointed at LLO via env (`LLO_UDS_PATH=/run/llo/default.sock` or similar).
3. **Parses a fixture repo** — small enough to be embedded in the repo (say `tests/fixtures/sample-repo/` with a few Go/Rust files) — via a one-shot `leyline parse` invocation inside the LLO container or via the `reparse` op against MCP.
4. **Smoke-tests the integration**: a `task cluster:smoke` target that brings up the cluster, runs a query through mache (which goes mache → UDS → LLO), and asserts the response is well-formed.

## What this is NOT

- Not a replacement for `task image:smoke` (that tests LLO standalone).
- Not the same as cloister's `cluster.compose.yaml` (which is cloister-shaped — workerd tenants + cloister-router). This is LLO-shaped — two services, no cloister required.
- Not production deployment scaffolding. Dev/test only. Production users would compose differently.

## Coordination

- mache version: pin to whichever mache release consumes the current LLO daemon protocol. After PR #12 (capnp-json wire), mache needs the `clients/go/leyline-schema/v0.3.0` decoder updates (Int64-as-string). So `compose.dev.yaml` pins `mache:0.8.x+` once that lands.
- Could optionally add cloister-router as a third service (LLO ↔ mache via cloister) — but that's gold-plating; two-service is enough for the integration story.

## Files

- `compose.dev.yaml` (new — root of LLO repo)
- `Taskfile.yml` (new `cluster:dev` and `cluster:smoke` targets)
- `tests/fixtures/sample-repo/` (new — small embedded repo for the parse target)
- `README.md` (Getting Started section — single-command integration)

## Acceptance

- `task cluster:dev` brings up llo-daemon + mache, both healthy
- `task cluster:smoke` parses sample-repo, queries via mache, asserts shape
- Documented in README's Getting Started section as the canonical "see it work" command

title: Expose restriction-addressed derived-view cache over daemon wire
description: Productionize ADR-0031 for external consumers such as Mache. Mache PR #622 measured 79-156 seconds and ~8 GB allocations per call for three handlers that independently derive the same CommunityResult from one already-built graph. Add a generic durable derived-view cache surface keyed by an explicit versioned scheme tag plus an exact BLAKE3 restriction address computed by the consumer over the rows it actually observes. Store result bytes content-addressed, return/verify the value address on read, and expose typed UDS operations usable by the generated Go client. This is not a source-byte CDC key: daemon --cdc / leyline cdc currently chunks nodes.record or source_blobs and content_manifest has no root. CDC may optimize underlying blob storage, but enabled/disabled must not alter the derived view's logical address or hit/miss semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A daemon black-box test proves: put(scheme, restriction_hash, value) then get returns byte-identical content and its verified BLAKE3 value address; a second request and daemon restart hit the durable entry; same restriction with a different scheme misses; corrupted stored bytes fail closed; CDC enabled and disabled produce identical logical key/hit behavior. Generated Go wire bindings expose the typed operations. Existing sheaf, CDC, wire, and release gates pass.

title: T8.7: add qualifier field to BindingRecord — LLO emits selector LHS
description:
Bead 8.7 of T8 under decade ley-line-open-9d30ac. Channel: final.

**Why.** The whole T8 reframe is "schema-as-data-plane = producer emits the structural fact, consumer projects." `BindingRecord` carries `targetNodeId`, `refToken`, `constructNodeId`, `refSiteNodeId`, `refUri`, `refRange`, `parseGen` — but **not the qualifier** (the LHS of a `selector_expression` like `pkg.Method` → `pkg`). So mache's `fan_out_skew` find-smells rule has to **rewalk the AST** in `internal/ingest/ast_walker.go::ExtractQualifiedCalls` to recover that one structural fact. That's a duplicate AST walker across runtimes — exactly what T8 promised to dissolve.

mache-42118e (open, P3) is mache trying to plumb its rewalker into derived tables. T8.7 changes the proposition: LLO emits `qualifier`, mache reads it as a column on `_capnp_binding_refs`, no rewalk needed.

**Schema change** (additive, ordinal `@7`):

```capnp
struct BindingRecord {
  ...existing @0..@6...
  qualifier @7 :Text;
  # The LHS of a `selector_expression` containing the ref site, e.g.
  # `pkg` in `pkg.Method`, `obj` in `obj.method`, empty when the call
  # is a bare identifier with no qualifier. Distinguishes structurally
  # equivalent shapes (`Method` qualified vs unqualified) without
  # consumer-side AST re-walks.
}
```

**Producer change** (`rs/ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs::project_references`):
- New helper `lookup_qualifier(conn, uri, range)` — query `_ast` for selector_expression containing the ref site; if found, return the leftmost identifier text from the same `_ast` row range.
- Pass through `write_binding_record` as the new field.

**Or via leyline-ts ref extraction** (`rs/ll-open/ts/src/refs.rs`):
- The call extractor already walks selector_expression nodes (it just doesn't record qualifier on `node_refs`). Add qualifier to `ExtractedRef::Ref` and pipe through `cmd_parse.rs` writers — symmetric write to both `node_refs` SQL and `BindingRecord` capnp.

Pick the simpler path; latter is cleaner if `node_refs` will also gain the column (likely yes for mache-42118e to fully use it).

**Test pins:**
- `binding.capnp` schema test: a record with qualifier set round-trips via canonical encoding (deterministic bytes; pin via `segment_hash_is_canonical_byte_stable`-style).
- `lookup_qualifier_extracts_selector_lhs` — fixture `pkg.Method()` Go file; verify capnp record has `qualifier == "pkg"`.
- `lookup_qualifier_returns_empty_for_bare_call` — fixture `Foo()`; verify `qualifier == ""`.

**Cross-repo coordination:** mache-paired bead (separate; tracks regeneration of mache's vendored schemas + the `fan_out_skew` rewrite).

**Schema-evolution rule applied:** appended at next ordinal `@7` with default empty Text. Per ADR-0014 §1, canonical encoding means existing instances (no qualifier set) hash identically — Σ root not advanced for unchanged data. This is the test of T8's promise; verify via `segment_hash_is_canonical_byte_stable` after the change.

title: ADR-0037: falsify content-addressed multi-vector retrieval (kernel-delegated caching) vs witchcraft's bespoke WAL-SQLite index
description:
Design note + falsification ladder drafted 2026-08-07, growing out of the crates.io publish-batch discussion for `leyline-text-search`. See `docs/adr/0037-multi-vector-retrieval-over-cas.md` for the full thesis and ladder.

## Thesis
LLO delegates caching to the kernel everywhere else it ships (mmap'd arena, `leyline-fs`'s NFS mount explicitly relying on "the kernel's native NFS client handles page cache and readahead"). `witchcraft`'s `DB` (WAL-mode SQLite, SHA-256-hashed, its own SCHEMA_VERSION) is the one place in the dependency closure that reinvents that job — which is why `leyline-text-search`'s README already has to wall it off from the Σ substrate. The proposal: token-level embeddings as content-addressed blobs (via `leyline-cdc`/`leyline-core`) exposed as ordinary files through the existing mount, letting the kernel manage residency the same way it already does for everything else.

## Why this is 3 independently-falsifiable claims, not 1
1. Performance — per-file FUSE/NFS overhead for scattered per-token reads vs. a locality-tuned SQLite B-tree.
2. Compression — high-entropy float embeddings don't dedup the way CDC's boundary-stability wins on repeated byte sequences; content-addressed ≠ small.
3. Indexing — XTR-WARP's real contribution is a compressed index that prunes candidates; kernel caching doesn't fix an architecture still doing a near-linear scan.

## The ladder (full detail in the ADR)
Rung 0 (precedent check, free) → Rung 1 (toy-scale kill switch, ~1 day) → Rung 2 (real A/B vs `WitchcraftEngine` on a real corpus, latency + on-disk footprint both measured) → Rung 3 (correctness invariant — no partial-write blob resolves to a valid address) → Rung 4 (indexing sufficiency — the rung most likely to actually kill it).

## Explicitly NOT gated on this bead
- Whether unstructured-text search beyond `leyline-chat-embed`'s existing fastembed/MiniLM path is even a validated need (precondition, not part of the ladder).
- Encoder backend choice (candle vs MLX/Apple Silicon) — recorded as an addendum in the ADR, downstream of whether an own-encoder is ever built.

## Status
Nothing implemented. Nothing blocked on this today — `leyline-text-search` stays correctly deferred from crates.io publishing and keeps `NullEngine` as production default regardless of this ADR's outcome. This bead exists so the design work already done isn't lost, per this session's own "bank findings where they persist" discipline.

File is docs/adr/0039-multi-vector-retrieval-over-cas.md on branch docs/cross-runtime-pins (commit ad73452), and it is now listed in ARCHITECTURE.md's ADR index — which had itself stopped at 0032, so 0033-0037 were added in the same commit.

The capnp ecosystem doesn't ship cross-runtime fixtures (the RTFM dossier flagged this — capnp's own runtimes test internally). We'd be ahead of community practice; appropriate for a substrate.

**Concrete deliverables:**

`rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/tests/fixtures/` — new dir with one `.bin` per schema, each accompanied by a `.expected.json`:

```
tests/fixtures/
├── binding-record-minimal.bin       (canonical-encoded BindingRecord, all defaults)
├── binding-record-minimal.expected.json
├── binding-record-realistic.bin     (BindingRecord with all fields populated, including qualifier post-T8.7)
├── binding-record-realistic.expected.json
├── ast-node-minimal.bin
├── ast-node-minimal.expected.json
├── source-file-minimal.bin
├── source-file-minimal.expected.json
└── head-minimal.bin
└── head-minimal.expected.json
```

`.bin` files: bit-exact canonical-encoded capnp messages. Generated once, committed as gold.
`.expected.json`: human-readable decoded form for assertions.

**LLO Rust test** (`rs/ll-core/schema-capnp/tests/cross_runtime_fixtures.rs`):
- Read each `.bin`, decode via Rust capnp runtime, assert fields match `.expected.json`.
- Builder-side: build typed message → `set_root_canonical` → write → assert byte-equal to `.bin`. Fails if Rust's canonical encoder ever drifts.

**Mache Go test** (paired bead in mache repo, gated on this one):
- Read each `.bin`, decode via Go capnp runtime, assert fields match `.expected.json`.
- Same builder-side check.

**Falsifiability:** any drift between Rust and Go canonical encoding fails CI on at least one side. Catches:
- A capnpc/capnp version bump that changes encoding mechanics
- A capnpc-go bug that decodes a field at wrong ordinal
- Any future producer regression that breaks canonical-bytes invariant

- `tests/fixtures/*.bin` committed
- `tests/cross_runtime_fixtures.rs` passes via `cargo test -p leyline-schema-capnp`
- Mache CI (paired bead) consumes same fixtures and passes
- Drift in either runtime fails CI loudly

**ADR-0014 notes:** this is the first place we ship something the capnp community itself doesn't have. Document the fixture-gen procedure as part of the test (a `regen` cargo feature so devs don't accidentally re-generate on every build).

title: Publish the generated execution/v1 tooldefs as a release asset — cloister's contract lock cannot be advanced without an LLO checkout
description:
Filed 2026-08-05 from vigil, measuring the cloister <-> LLO release coupling.
Upstream half of `cloister-464216`; sibling of `ley-line-open-a03156` (crates)
and `ley-line-open-c3e8c6` (git-dep pinning).

## The gap

cloister pins the generated execution/v1 tooldefs by content:
`llo-execution-contract.lock.json` names `sourceCommit`, `sourceTag`, and the
`sha256` of `src/generated/llo-execution-tools.json`. Its own header states the
regeneration procedure, and states the cost:

    REGENERATING (needs an LLO checkout; cloister CI deliberately has none):
      1. node scripts/fetch-schema-bridge.mjs capnpc-schema-bridge-tooldefs
      2. from <llo>/rs/ll-core/schema-spec at the tag named by sourceCommit:
         capnp compile -o<path-from-step-1>:<outdir> --src-prefix=. execution/v1/execution.capnp
      3. copy <outdir>/execution.tools.json over `artifact`, update sha256.

So the artifact LLO produces can only be obtained by rebuilding it from LLO's
source tree with a capnp toolchain. cloister CI can verify the digest it already
has; it cannot produce the next one. That makes this the single channel of eight
that `task llo:bump` (cloister-464216) cannot write, and it turns every LLO
release into a manual step on the consumer side.

The header also records that the manual step has already gone wrong: "The v0.15.0
re-vendor was first done with a hand-downloaded binary, which is the same
unverified-input shape the schema-bridge lock exists to prevent."

## Why LLO is the right side to fix it

The producer already has the toolchain, the source, and the tag. It also already
has the mechanism: `release.yml` attaches 20 assets asserted by
`tools/release-assets.txt` (leyline-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64},
libleyline_fs-*.a, leyline_sign.wasm, leyline_cas_ffi.wasm,
leyline_envelope.wasm, SHA256SUMS). Adding `execution.tools.json` is one more
entry in an existing, parity-checked list — not a new pipeline.

Doing it in cloister instead means either shipping capnp + an LLO checkout into
cloister CI (the dependency it deliberately dropped) or keeping the step manual.

## What it buys

  - `task llo:bump -- <tag>` in cloister can write all eight channels unattended.
  - The provenance constraint relaxes. The lock currently requires `sourceCommit`
    be "reachable from a published tag, not a branch tip" — a rule written after
    a pin named commit 2835bdce on `integration`, which PR #317 squash-merged and
    which was therefore unreachable from any released history. An asset is
    attached to the release object, so provenance comes from the release rather
    than from a commit whose branch may be deleted. The rule stops needing to be
    remembered.
  - It becomes observable. vigil's `latest_release_assets` condition (shipped
    2026-08-04) watches named assets on the latest release without pinning a tag
    nobody has cut yet, so cloister's bump can be triggered by the asset
    appearing rather than by someone noticing.

## Scope note

This does not depend on `ley-line-open-a03156` (crates.io publishing) and does not
substitute for it. They cover different channels: a03156 fixes the six Cargo pins,
this fixes the generated-artifact pin. Both are needed for cloister to stop
hand-sweeping 24 occurrences across 8 files.

## Close condition

The release dry-run lists execution.tools.json among the staged assets and
tools/release-assets.txt asserts it.

comments.text:
## Ordering: land `ley-line-open-a28476` first, and this asset is signed for free

Found a28476 ("Sign published Rust release assets with the Signet artifact Action",
P1, open, filed 2026-08-04) after filing this. It signs the publication set named by
`tools/release-assets.txt` — so if it lands first, adding `execution.tools.json` to
that list gets a Signet signature and its verification sidecars with no extra work
here.

That matters more for this asset than for the binaries. cloister's other pinned LLO
artifacts are checked against **out-of-band hand-captured digests** because
`schema-bridge.lock.json` explicitly refuses to treat SHA256SUMS as a trust root
("it comes from the same place as the binary, so a compromised release supplies
both"). If this asset ships unsigned it inherits that: cloister would have to
transcribe one more digest by hand, which is the manual step
`cloister-464216` exists to eliminate. Signed, the contract lock can verify
provenance against the release workflow's OIDC identity and `task llo:bump` can
advance it unattended — which is the entire point of this bead.

So the acceptance criterion above is amended: the asset must be in the SIGNED
publication set, not merely uploaded and covered by SHA256SUMS.

Dependency: a28476.

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED in PR #336 (feat/publish-execution-tooldefs), 2026-08-05.

execution.tools.json now ships as a release asset. Single-uploader on the linux-amd64 leg, same rule as the C header and the wasm set.

NOT generated in the release path, deliberately: the artifact is already committed at rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/execution-tools.json, produced by `task gen:execution-tools`, and held to the IDL by schema-bridge's execution_v1 conformance test ('registry artifact drifted'). Generating it here would add a second producer of a file that already has one. This uploads what is already correct. Staged under the emitter's output name (execution.tools.json, dot) rather than the vendored copy's (execution-tools.json, hyphen) — cloister's lock names the artifact, not our checkout's path.

FOR CLOISTER: once released, advancing llo-execution-contract.lock.json is fetch + digest-verify against the release object. No LLO checkout, no capnp toolchain. That is their eighth pin channel, so `task llo:bump` can write all eight instead of stopping at seven (cloister-464216) — and it dissolves the tag-reachability rule, since provenance moves onto the release asset rather than needing a commit reachable from a published tag.

THREE THINGS THE FIXTURES CAUGHT, all invisible by reading, worth recording because the next person adding an asset hits the same three:
  1. The task var never reached the script's environment — INCLUDE_HEADER lives in the stage task's env: block, so adding the flag to cmds alone left the export unreachable and the asset simply absent.
  2. Putting TOOLDEFS_SOURCE in env: fixes that and breaks it the other way — the path is then set on every leg, the stage script's -n test fires everywhere, and three colliding copies reach the basename inventory. Only the FLAG belongs in env, which is why HEADER_SOURCE is not there either: a constraint the existing code encodes without stating.
  3. test_release_publication.sh simulates all four legs independently and needed its own source; without it the aggregate was 31 against an expected 32 and the fixture refused the incomplete publication.

The release fixtures are good. They assert the exact asset set and the fail-closed mutations, so an incomplete addition cannot pass as probably-fine.
