comments.text:
PRIOR ART. Checked what established code indexers actually store, because this is
a solved problem and the chunked-pipeline work was tuning the wrong layer.

## Finding: none of them store the AST

SCIP (Sourcegraph; replaced LSIF) -- scip.proto:

    Document    = { language, relative_path, occurrences[], symbols[],
                    text?, position_encoding }
    Occurrence  = { range, symbol (STRING), symbol_roles (bitset),
                    syntax_kind, diagnostics?, enclosing_range }
    SymbolInfo  = { symbol, kind, display_name, documentation,
                    relationships[], enclosing_symbol }

No tree structure. No child pointers. No ancestry beyond one enclosing_range /
enclosing_symbol. Symbols are human-readable strings, deliberately NOT opaque
ids -- that is what makes indexes independently mergeable and incremental.

The LSIF problems SCIP was built to fix are our symptoms verbatim:
"performance issues requiring large in-memory data structures" and "complexity
of implementing incremental indexing" caused by globally-incrementing ids. SCIP
is ~8x smaller and indexed ~10x faster (Meta's measurement, per the Sourcegraph
announcement).

codebase-memory-mcp (the tool this repo was benchmarked against): "extracts
definitions, calls, imports ... creating nodes and edges rather than raw syntax
trees". Claims Linux kernel, 75K files, 3 minutes.

rust-analyzer: no eager index at all. Salsa memoised demand-driven queries;
"eagerly indexing an entire codebase can waste resources on indices that are
never used".

## The specific mapping to our schema

daemon/ops.rs query_definitions joins _ast for exactly seven columns:

    SELECT d.node_id, d.source_id, a.node_kind,
           a.start_row, a.start_col, a.end_row, a.end_col,
           a.start_byte, a.end_byte
    FROM node_defs d
    LEFT JOIN _ast a ON a.node_id = d.node_id AND a.source_id = d.source_id
    WHERE d.token = ?1

and node_defs is:

    CREATE TABLE node_defs (
        token, node_id, source_id, container_node_id, canonical_kind
    );

node_defs IS a SCIP Occurrence with the range left out. token ~ symbol,
container_node_id ~ enclosing_symbol, canonical_kind ~ syntax_kind. The ONLY
missing field is position -- which is why the query has to reach into _ast, and
therefore why _ast has to be materialised eagerly.

Consequence, on the 8000-file kibana slice: 3 150 849 _ast rows are written so
that 337 688 def+ref rows (20 911 + 316 777) can find their spans. Denormalising
the seven columns onto node_defs/node_refs -- where SCIP puts them -- removes
_ast from the primary query path at roughly 9:1.

## The other half: content addressing

node_content + node_child = 4.57M rows on that slice, ~33% of write volume, and
zero production SELECTs (they exist for ADR-0027 and as the FK target of
node_defs.node_hash / node_refs.node_hash).

Glean gets the same incremental-invalidation property for ~7% of database size:
every fact is labelled with a UNIT (typically a filename); ownership sets are
stored as interval maps with Elias-Fano coding; invalidation hides units, and
ownership propagation prevents dangling references. Stacked immutable databases
make a layer's hides/adds transparent to the querier. Reported overhead: 2-3%
indexing for Python, <10% on typical queries, O(changes) rather than
O(repository).

So the Merkle-DAG-per-subtree buys us something Glean achieves with ownership
sets at a fraction of the write cost. That is worth an explicit decision rather
than an assumption.

## Recommended re-frame

The ingest cost is a SCHEMA problem, not a pipeline-tuning problem. Ordered by
value:

1. Denormalise {node_kind, start_byte, end_byte, start_row, start_col, end_row,
   end_col} onto node_defs/node_refs. Makes _ast non-load-bearing for
   find_definition/find_callers -- the thing that blocked lazy AST in
   ley-line-open-b4509b.
2. With _ast off the query path, the whole AST layer becomes a rebuildable
   cache (it already is: source_blobs holds exact bytes, the fold is pure over
   them -- ley-line-open-20988a).
3. Evaluate Glean-style unit ownership as the invalidation mechanism against
   the current Merkle layer, on cost as well as elegance.
4. ADR-0026 pointer dual-write stays a separate roadmap call (its own kill
   process in ADR-0026 sections 7 / 9.2.5).

Sources:
  https://sourcegraph.com/blog/announcing-scip
  https://github.com/sourcegraph/scip/blob/main/scip.proto
  https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/19/developer-tools/glean-open-source-code-indexing/
  https://glean.software/blog/incremental/
  https://rust-analyzer.github.io/blog/2020/07/20/three-architectures-for-responsive-ide.html
  https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp

title: mutants_diff.sh reads stale missed.txt from a previous run
description:
tools/mutants_diff.sh:202 checks [ -s mutants.out/missed.txt ] after each slice, but nothing removes mutants.out before a slice runs. A slice with zero candidates ('INFO No mutants to filter') leaves the PREVIOUS run's mutants.out in place and the gate reads its missed.txt — reporting survivors from a diff that is no longer under test, and failing with exit 201.

Observed concretely while landing PR #329: an earlier local run legitimately reported 1 survivor (the :186 cfg-gate macOS artifact). After the fix commit, the re-run's first slice had nothing to test, read the stale missed.txt, printed 'MISSED: 1 surviving mutant(s) in this slice' BEFORE the runtime slice even started, and exited 201 — while the runtime slice itself was 16 tested / 14 caught / 2 unviable / 0 missed. rm -rf rs/mutants.out and identical re-run: exit 0.

CI is unaffected (fresh runners have no stale mutants.out), which makes this worse rather than better: it is a local-only false RED, and the local gate exists precisely so people trust it before pushing. A gate that cries wolf locally trains the 'just push and let CI decide' habit.

Fix shape: rm -rf mutants.out at the top of run_slice (or before each cargo-mutants invocation), so missed.txt can only ever describe the slice that just ran. One line, plus a fixture test in the same spirit as the existing false-green fixtures — the script already has regression coverage for 'diff paths match nothing => must fail rather than pass', this is the mirror case.

comments.text:
Reproduced concretely 2026-08-05 on `feat/daemon-cdc-target` (#338).

Round 2 of a local `mutants_diff.sh` run against a diff with real, freshly-fixed mutants (both cli-lib and fs slices) exited 2 — "MISSED: 3 surviving mutant(s) in this slice" — with **zero** `MISSED   <file>:<line>` per-mutant lines anywhere in the actual cargo-mutants output, and both slice summaries reading "6 caught, 1 unviable" / "6 caught, 2 unviable" (0 missed each). `rs/mutants.out/missed.txt` on disk was 0 bytes at the time.

Root cause: `mutants.out/` was not cleared between the prior (real-failure) run and this one. `run_slice`'s `[ -s mutants.out/missed.txt ]` check (`tools/mutants_diff.sh:202`) reads whatever the file contains AFTER `cargo mutants` runs, but cargo-mutants apparently does not reliably truncate `missed.txt` to empty on a slice where nothing survived — so a stale non-empty file from an earlier invocation in the same directory persists and fails a run that actually caught everything.

Fix that worked: `rm -rf rs/mutants.out rs/mutants.out.old` before re-running — round 3 was clean (`MUTANTS_EXIT=0`, zero per-mutant MISSED lines, same 7+8 mutant counts).

Not fixed here — this comment is the reproduction, not the patch. The real fix is in `mutants_diff.sh`: either `rm -rf mutants.out` at the top of the script (before the first `run_slice` call) or pass `cargo mutants` an explicit `--output` per invocation so stale state from a prior script run can't leak into the next one's pass/fail check.

title: A-1: Cross-runtime fixture gate for daemon protocol responses
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.1 of decade `daemon-typed-wire`, thread `daemon-json-type-lockdown`. Supersedes prior single-bead Bead A (`a373ba`, now closed).

## Context

`TABLE_CONTRACT.md` (LLO, 2026-05-08 stamp) distinguishes two cross-runtime contracts in LLO:

1. **Substrate contract** — canonical capnp segment files at `${db}.{bindings,ast,source,head}.capnp`. Gated by T8.10's cross-runtime fixture suite (bead `6b7d43`): Rust emits `tests/fixtures/binding-record-{minimal,realistic}.bin`; Go decodes the same fixtures via `clients/go/leyline-schema/binding/binding_test.go`; byte-equality asserted from both ends.

2. **Daemon protocol contract** — typed JSON-on-wire per `daemon.capnp`. NO gate today. This is the surface where mache-98aa97's drift accumulated (`op_status` returning 5+ fields not in `StatusResponse`, etc.).

The structural answer to *"how do we make sure things don't keep happening"* (the user's question) is **extending T8.10's pattern from the substrate surface to the daemon protocol surface.** Same shape, new fixtures.

This bead INSTALLS THE GATE FIRST, before any handler swap or schema reconciliation. The gate immediately starts failing on every existing drift — which is the point. Then A-2 (schema reconciliation) makes the gate green by reconciling the schema to reality. Then A-3 (wire.rs lockdown) keeps it green going forward via typed serialization.

Gate-first is non-negotiable: if we did A-3 first, the swap would be schema-blind. The gate is what makes A-3 mechanical instead of guess-and-test.

## Work

### A-1.1: Fixture infrastructure
- Create `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/fixtures/daemon-protocol/` directory.
- Write a fixture-emit harness: a `#[test]` that spawns the daemon (via `spawn_test_socket` from integration.rs), sends each op in `base_op_names`, captures the response, writes to `tests/fixtures/daemon-protocol/<op>.json` (gitignored during dev; committed once the schema reconciliation in A-2 stabilizes them).
- Alternative: hand-write the fixtures for each op based on the audit's documented current shapes. Slightly more work to maintain but avoids the chicken-and-egg of "fixtures change every time a handler does."
- Decide at implementation time which path; defaults to harness-based.

### A-1.2: Go side decode test
- Create `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon/daemon_protocol_test.go` (or similar)
- For each fixture, load → `json.Unmarshal` into the corresponding Go binding type from `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon`
- Assert no `json.UnmarshalTypeError`, no unexpected `null` on required fields
- If the Go bindings don't yet have JSON tags (T8.10 emits binary capnp Go types, not JSON-tagged structs), this bead's prerequisite is A-2 generating JSON-tagged Go bindings via `regen.sh` extension. The cross-runtime fixture mechanism itself is the gate; the binding generation is part of A-2.

### A-1.3: CI workflow extension
- Extend `.github/workflows/leyline-schema-go.yml` with a "daemon-protocol-decode" step that runs the Go test
- Wire the trigger so it runs on changes to `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/**`, `rs/ll-core/public-schema/capnp/daemon.capnp`, and `clients/go/leyline-schema/daemon/**`

### A-1.4: Documentation
- Update `TABLE_CONTRACT.md` to mention the daemon protocol fixture gate alongside the substrate fixture gate. Two cross-runtime gates now, same pattern.

## Acceptance

- Each op in `base_op_names` has a fixture file checked in
- Go test loads each fixture and decodes via the matching typed binding
- CI workflow runs the test on relevant path changes
- The gate is INTENTIONALLY FAILING for some ops at the time this bead merges — that's the diagnostic that A-2 needs to do schema reconciliation work
- TABLE_CONTRACT.md reflects the new gate

## Why this lands first

- Tiny PR. Pure additive. No handler changes, no schema changes.
- Makes the drift visible structurally. After this lands, you can SEE which ops have schema/reality mismatch by reading the CI red.
- A-2 and A-3 both depend on the gate being in place to validate their work.

## Falsifiable claim

*If A-1's gate is structurally sufficient, then any future PR that changes a handler's JSON output without updating the matching `daemon.capnp` field will fail CI before merge. If the gate has a hole, a future contributor will demonstrate it by landing drift the gate didn't catch. That's the audit point — first occurrence after this bead lands triggers a refinement to the gate.*

title: CDC GC cannot reclaim orphaned manifests — unbounded arena growth
description:
Found by adversarial review of the merged CDC work (main @ 353dd07).

`collect_unreachable_chunks` (gc.rs:59-76) only ever runs DELETE FROM content_chunks (gc.rs:73). It reads content_manifest purely as a reachability predicate (gc.rs:62-63) and never deletes manifest or content_manifest_meta rows.

Consequence: any writer that deletes or renames nodes without invalidating leaves manifest rows the freshness witness correctly REFUSES forever — and those rows keep their chunks permanently GC-reachable. Repeated leyline-ts reprojects outside flush_node/batch_splice accumulate one dead manifest generation each; `leyline cdc gc` deletes nothing; the single-portable-.db grows without bound.

This is the hygiene half of ley-line-open-0330c7. Correctness is structurally closed (the read-side freshness gate is compiler-enforced and mutation-tested at chunked.rs:1915-1961), but explicit invalidation is now documented as defense-in-depth/orphan-prevention (chunked.rs:794-796, 1996-2004) — and THAT convention has no backstop.

Fix shape: invert the witness query from chunked.rs:818-828 to select non-fresh manifests, reap them, THEN collect unreachable chunks. Small, composes with existing logic, gives hygiene the same backstop-not-discipline shape correctness already has.

Proposed as F7c in the retroactive CDC ADR.

comments.text:
WHY MUTATION TESTING DID NOT CATCH THIS (measured 2026-07-27)

`task mutants:fs-gc` on the current tree: "8 mutants tested in 55s: 7 caught, 1 unviable". Zero survived. The gate is green and the bug is real, so the gate is not the safety net it appears to be here.

Two independent blind spots, both active:

1. MISSING CODE HAS NO MUTANTS. Every mutant of `collect_unreachable_chunks` is caught because the function does exactly what it claims — skip the DELETE, invert the NOT EXISTS, corrupt a GcReport count, all caught. The defect is the absent manifest-reaping statement, and you cannot mutate a line that was never written. Mutation testing audits tests against the implementation; it cannot audit the implementation against a requirement nobody articulated.

2. LOGIC IN SQL STRINGS IS OPAQUE TO A RUST MUTATION ENGINE. Only 8 mutants exist for the whole file because gc.rs's decision logic lives inside a SQL string literal (the NOT EXISTS reachability predicate at gc.rs:59-76). cargo-mutants mutates Rust expressions; it can blank a string but cannot alter the semantics of a query. The 8 mutants cover the scaffolding around the decision, not the decision.

Blind spot 2 generalizes beyond this bead. The materialize-on-read design deliberately pushes logic INTO SQL (chunked.rs: "a range read becomes a SQL WHERE clause rather than a full scan"), and `mutants:fs` targets chunked.rs on the same assumption of coverage. The more logic lives in query text, the less a green mutants gate means. Worth its own bead — the mutation gates may be measuring substantially less of the CDC path than their green status implies.

WHAT WOULD CATCH IT: an invariant test, not an example test. F7c as filed is universally quantified — "after reaping, zero manifest rows without a fresh witness AND zero unreachable chunks remain" — a shape example-based tests cannot express and mutation cannot generate. A metamorphic complement: N reproject cycles, then GC, then storage returns to baseline; that is a relation across time, which no single-example assertion captures.

Implementation note for whoever takes this: write the invariant test FIRST. It should fail against today's GC by construction, which makes it a clean RED rather than a test written to match whatever the fix happens to do.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `collect_unreachable_chunks` reaps non-fresh manifests before computing chunk reachability, in the same IMMEDIATE transaction. Test: write a chunked node, mutate `nodes.record` out-of-band without invalidating, run `leyline cdc gc`, assert the dead manifest rows AND their chunks are deleted. Today this asserts zero deletions.

title: Measure CDC storage overhead and dedup ratio — the missing F4c/F5c gates
description:
CDC shipped with no storage measurement anywhere in-repo. The ~2x figure is arithmetic from the schema (chunked.rs:84-100), not a measurement: `nodes.record` is never nulled for chunk-backed nodes and `conn.serialize` carries record + chunk tables in one buffer (graph.rs:2510-2531), so content is stored twice minus dedup.

Every comparable substrate ADR pinned dedup as a falsification gate — ADR-0026 F4, ADR-0028 F4s. CDC skipped its equivalent, so nobody can currently evaluate whether the trade is net positive.

The instrumentation already ships: `ActivationReport.unique_chunk_bytes` (activation.rs:44-46) and `GcReport` (gc.rs:16-40) make this close to a one-command exercise. What is missing is the gate, not the machinery.

This is load-bearing for the substrate direction: if CDC becomes the incremental publication path (see the partition-algebra thread), this ratio stops being a nice-to-have and becomes the gating number.

title: sheaf crate hashes with SHA-256 in production src — violates the BLAKE3 substrate lock
description:
`substrate.rs:28-42` declares BLAKE3 LOCKED and warns explicitly that mixing hash functions inside a single substrate breaks (DET) and (CR) *at the composition boundary*. The sheaf crate does exactly that, in production source, not tests:

- rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/merkle.rs — an entire Merkle implementation on SHA-256 (lines 18, 31, 47, 68, 127, 154)
- rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/restriction_cache.rs:57, 249, 439, 514
- rs/ll-open/sheaf/src/restriction_review.rs:9, 378

ADR-0031 specifies SHA-256 for the restriction key, so this is an ADR defect, not just a code slip. Amend the ADR rather than grandfathering the divergence — per the remove-don't-deprecate policy for a pre-1.0 project with a real versioning story.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: it bars restriction keys from participating in the address algebra at all, and the moment anything signs, a foreign-hash address is a cross-protocol confusion hazard. `RootSigner::sign` takes a bare 32-byte Hash whatever its provenance — see the domain-separation rationale at head_digest.rs:50-65.

Cheap now, expensive after signing generalizes.
acceptance_criteria: No `sha2`/`Sha256` in rs/ll-open/sheaf/src; restriction and merkle hashing route through `leyline_core::ContentAddressed`. ADR-0031 amended to specify BLAKE3. A lint or test fails if `sha2` reappears as a non-dev dependency of any substrate crate.

title: Delete apko.yaml + melange.yaml — abandoned image-build path

title: A-2: Schema↔reality reconciliation (additive ordinals per ADR-0014)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.2 of decade `daemon-typed-wire`, thread `daemon-json-type-lockdown`. Depends on `b5a77b` (the gate must be in place to validate this work).

## Context

The audit of `ops.rs` against `daemon.capnp` revealed substantial drift. Examples:

| Op | `daemon.capnp` says | `op_*` returns | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `ok, generation, arenaPath, arenaSize` | `ok, phase, current_root, arena_path, arena_size, enrichment, head_sha?, last_reparse_at_ms?, error?` | Add `phase`, `currentRoot`, `enrichment: List(EnrichmentStatus)`, optional `headSha`, `lastReparseAtMs`, `error` at ordinals 4+ |
| `load` | `ok, generation` | `ok, current_root` | Replace `generation` semantic (was misleading anyway; the wire field is `current_root`). Append `currentRoot` at @2; deprecate `generation` doc-only. |
| `reparse` | `ok, generation, stats:ParseStats` | `ok, current_root, parsed, unchanged, deleted, errors, changed_files` | Flat shape; either ratify the flat shape (append fields, leave `stats` deprecated) or refactor handler to nest under `stats`. Decide at implementation time. |
| `snapshot` | `ok, generation` | `ok, current_root` | Same as `load`. |
| `enrich` | `ok, generation, passes:[EnrichmentStats]` | `ok, current_root, passes` | Append `currentRoot`. |
| `list_children` | `List(Node)` (full Node) | `[{id, name, kind, size}]` (no parentId, no record) | Either bring handler up to full Node (more work; mache wants this anyway per the N+1 discussion) OR introduce a `NodeStat` struct and reference it from `ListChildrenResponse.children`. Decide at implementation time; recommend full Node + drop the N+1 in mache (`mache-a55625`). |
| `query` | `List(QueryRow)` with `values: List(Text)` | `[{col1: val, col2: val}]` (column-keyed objects + outer `columns:[col1, col2]`) | Either match schema (refactor handler to emit positional values), OR keep current shape and update schema. Current shape is more JSON-idiomatic and easier for mache; recommend updating schema. |
| `read_content` | `ok, content, error` | `{ok, content}` or `{ok:false, error}` | Schema is fine; reality matches if you treat unset `content` and `error` as the optional shape. Document the branching. |
| LSP ops (5) + `vec_search` | **not in schema** | various typed responses | Add 6 net-new request/response struct pairs to `daemon.capnp`. Use `_lsp` family ordinals reserved for this. |

## Constraints (ADR-0014 §2 schema evolution)

- **Ordinals are stable for life of file.** Existing `@N` declarations don't move.
- **Adding fields is safe.** Append at `@N+1` with appropriate defaults / optionality.
- **Removing fields is never.** Leave a hole if a field is unused.
- **Renaming is never.** Same identity = same name forever.

This bead is PURELY ADDITIVE. No handler changes; no field removals; no renames.

## Work

### A-2.1: daemon.capnp updates
Per the audit table above, append new fields/messages at next ordinals. Bump nothing; just extend. Document each addition with a `# add for $op` comment.

### A-2.2: Regen Go bindings
- Run `clients/go/leyline-schema/regen.sh` — emits updated `daemon.capnp.go`
- Verify the new fields are present in the typed Go struct
- If `regen.sh` doesn't already emit JSON tags on the Go structs (likely capnp-only binary today), extend it to also emit JSON-tagged structs for daemon-protocol types. This is what A-1's fixture gate needs to actually decode.

### A-2.3: Make A-1's gate green
- Run the daemon-protocol-decode test (from A-1)
- For each op whose fixture fails: the schema now declares the field, and the Go binding has the JSON tag — decode should succeed
- Iterate until all ops in `base_op_names` pass

### A-2.4: Cross-runtime fixture suite update
- Regenerate or hand-update the fixtures from A-1 to reflect the reconciled schema (if the schema shape change moved any field names)
- Commit fixtures
- The T8.10 test pattern continues to pass for substrate; the new daemon-protocol test pattern now also passes

## Acceptance

- `daemon.capnp` declares every field that `ops.rs` handlers actually emit
- Go bindings regenerate cleanly; CI gate `leyline-schema-go` regen-diff passes
- A-1's daemon-protocol-decode test passes for every op in `base_op_names`
- No handler code changed
- Mache PRs that consume Go bindings still build (additive changes are backwards-compatible)

## What this enables

- A-3 (wire.rs lockdown) becomes mechanical: serde structs mirror the now-correct `daemon.capnp`; the gate enforces correctness during the swap.
- mache's typed-binding adoption (`mache-a5ad09`) can pick up the expanded types when convenient.

## Risk

- The decision points in the audit table ("ratify flat shape vs nest under `stats`", "full Node vs NodeStat", etc.) are real design calls. Each should be made at implementation time with the trade-off captured in a bead comment. Default: ratify current handler shape (least disruptive), but document any case where the schema-intended shape is meaningfully better.

title: daemon ops: collapse 4 op-name lists to 1 source of truth
description:
Per coupling audit F1 (`docs/audits/2026-06-17-coupling-audit.md`).

## Problem

`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs` declares the canonical set of base ops in **four** places:

1. `base_op_names()` (`ops.rs:47-87`) — `#[cfg(test)]` `Vec<&str>`, 30 names + feature `.push`es
2. `is_known_base_op()` (`ops.rs:151-188`) — production `matches!` pattern, 29 string literals + feature `||` arms
3. `dispatch_typed()` (`ops.rs:190-251`) — typed match on 32 `BaseRequest` variants (compiler-enforced)
4. `tool_registry()` (`daemon/mcp.rs:61-326`) — MCP tool definitions; drift test `mcp.rs:882`

A fifth tiny list (`STATE_CHANGING_OPS`, 5 names) is acceptable as-is (disjoint).

The load-bearing comment on `ops.rs:95-99` says "Adding a new op is a 3-step process the compiler enforces." Actual reality: **4-5 places** (wire variant + dispatch arm + `is_known_base_op` + `base_op_names` + optionally `tool_registry`). The comment is wrong.

## Drift tests that exist

- `handle_base_op_dispatches_every_canonical_name` (`ops.rs:2587`) — checks `base_op_names() ⟶ dispatch + is_known_base_op recognize` (asymmetric — undetected if `is_known_base_op` has an extra)
- `STATE_CHANGING_OPS ⊆ base_op_names()` (`ops.rs:3018`)
- `tool_registry() ⊆ base_op_names()` (`mcp.rs:882`)

## Two candidate shapes

### Cheapest — runtime probe (smaller delta, less type safety)

- `is_known_base_op(op)` switches to `serde_json::from_value::<BaseRequest>(json!({"op": op})).is_ok()` — only the `op` tag is needed for the parse to choose a variant; missing args is fine, the probe is throwaway.
- `base_op_names()` reads `serde::Deserialize::introspect`-style or simply enumerates a derived const.
- Cost: ~150 LOC delta. Removes 2 of the 4 lists.

### Cleanest — name on the enum (larger delta, type-safe)

- Add a `BaseOp` enum (`Status`, `Flush`, ...) tagged with `pub const ALL: &[BaseOp]` + `pub fn name(&self) -> &'static str`.
- `is_known_base_op(op) = BaseOp::from_name(op).is_some()`
- `base_op_names() = BaseOp::ALL.iter().map(|b| b.name()).collect()`
- `dispatch_typed` still takes `BaseRequest` (typed args); the tag-only `BaseOp` is a parallel enum for name introspection.
- `tool_registry` indexes by `BaseOp`, not by string literal — drift test becomes structural.
- Cost: ~250 LOC delta. Removes 3 of the 4 lists. Adds compile-time guarantees.

**Recommendation:** Cleanest approach. The maintenance debt scales linearly with op count; we now have 32 ops; the trend is upward. One-time refactor pays per-op-added forever.

## Implementation plan (cleanest variant)

1. Define `BaseOp` enum with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]` + `name()` + `from_name(&str)` + `ALL: &[BaseOp]` const slice — all in one block.
2. Replace `is_known_base_op` body with `BaseOp::from_name(op).is_some()`.
3. Replace `base_op_names()` body with `BaseOp::ALL.iter().map(|b| b.name()).collect()` (still `#[cfg(test)]`).
4. Update `mcp::tool_registry` to construct `McpTool::name` from `BaseOp::name()` references.
5. Audit the three existing drift tests — adjust to new shape (they should get *simpler*).
6. Update `ops.rs:95-99` comment to reflect the new actual step count (should drop to 2-3 places).

## Acceptance gates

- All existing tests pass unchanged (drift tests + dispatch tests).
- Adding a new op requires touching `BaseRequest` variant + `BaseOp` variant + `dispatch_typed` arm + `tool_registry` (if MCP-exposed). Down from 5 → 3 (or 4 with MCP).
- `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings` clean.

## Scope

- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs` (the four-list collapse)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs` (tool_registry consumer)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/wire.rs` (possibly — `BaseRequest` enum lives there)

No public-API changes; the wire shape is unchanged. Pure internal refactor.

title: Head.rootHash hashes a concatenation, so it does not commit to segment boundaries
description:
head.capnp:26-30 defines rootHash as BLAKE3 over `source.capnp || ast.capnp || bindings.capnp`. A hash of a concatenation does not commit to where the parts divide, so two different segment triples whose bytes concatenate identically share a root.

The only guard is `segmentBytes` (head.capnp:40-43), which records TOTAL bytes only — it detects a torn write, not a re-division.

Fix: make the root a tagged fold over the three segment addresses with framing, i.e. A(seg-spec, [sigma(source), sigma(ast), sigma(bindings)] + lengths). This is the same shape `head_digest` (head_digest.rs:38-44) already uses correctly for (generation, root, parent) — the pattern exists in-repo, it just was not applied here.

Pre-1.0 clean break plus CHANGELOG, not a deprecation cycle.

Found during the partition-algebra analysis; it is the concrete instance of the general rule that an address must commit to its decomposition, not merely to its bytes.
acceptance_criteria: `rootHash` is a tagged fold over the three segment addresses plus their lengths, not a hash of the concatenation. Falsifying test: two distinct (source, ast, bindings) triples with identical concatenated bytes produce DIFFERENT roots. CHANGELOG records the clean break.

title: ADR-0033: retroactive decision record for CDC chunk-backed content
description:
CDC shipped with no ADR. docs/adr/ runs 0014-0031; CDC appears only as a mention inside 0026 and 0028. Every comparable substrate decision — pointer store, source blobs, CAS-backed workspace, sheaf-over-embeddings, restriction-addressed caching — got its own ADR with explicit falsification gates. CDC's rationale lives in module docstrings, which are unusually honest (chunked.rs has a real 'what this does NOT do' section) but carry no gates and were never reviewed as a decision.

Three decisions are true in code and written nowhere:

D1. Dual-store is the PERMANENT end state. `nodes.record` is the cross-runtime SQL ABI — mache reads it directly with no cgo — so dropping it is a wire break for every schema-pinning consumer. ADR-0028's dual-store governs _source/source_blobs where LLO owns both sides and Phase 3 can drop the duplicate. Different ownership, different commitment. A future engineer applying 0028's Phase-3 pattern to nodes.record would break mache. This paragraph is the whole point of the ADR.

D2. The real invariant is 'every record writer moves (size, mtime-nanos)', not 'every writer invalidates'. All 13 production writers are safe; correctness rests on a compiler-enforced read-side choke point, mutation-tested at chunked.rs:1915-1961. Residual envelope: a caller of leyline_schema::insert_node supplies its own mtime and can defeat the witness by replaying a stale (size, mtime) pair onto changed bytes.

D3. Chunk identity is private and subordinate, committed by containment under current_root rather than by proof. A manifest root becomes mandatory the moment chunks are shared ACROSS arenas (xet-style shard, cross-repo dedup) — hand off to the root-domain ADR (ley-line-open-ef5c1d).

Existing gates to cite: F1c read equivalence (chunked.rs:1803, 1583), F2c read amplification (chunked.rs:1379, EXPLAIN pin 1682), F3c edit locality (graph.rs:2306-2319), F6c stale-witness refusal (chunked.rs:1927, 1966). Missing: F4c/F5c (own bead) and F7c GC completeness (own bead).

comments.text:
CORRECTED GATE SET for ADR-0033, from the b5faa9 measurement. Do NOT write F4c/F5c into the ADR as passing gates — they measured the wrong table.

## Why the original gates don't decide anything

F4c (storage bound) and F5c (dedup) were both measured against `nodes.record`. Three findings make those numbers characterization rather than a verdict:

1. `records_over_min_chunk` = 0 on all three corpora. Largest record is 5,633 bytes against MIN_CHUNK 8,192, and `next_boundary` returns immediately for sub-MIN_CHUNK input. The GearHash NEVER FIRES. What ships is a BLAKE3-keyed intern table, not content-defined chunking. Zero dedup on sub-minimum inputs is arithmetic, not a measurement.
2. F4c passes at 1.200x/1.217x/1.216x, but only because the AST projection is already 200-269x its own source, so 403 MB of manifest hides in a 2 GB denominator. `dbstat` attributes mache's growth exactly: manifest 86.1 MB, witness 77.3 MB, indexes 161.8 MB, and `content_chunks` — the actual payload — 3.8 MB. Chunk bytes are 0.31-0.56% of what CDC costs.
3. `nodes.record` is very likely the wrong target entirely. Its contract is undeclared (see edec5b): mache reads it as a JSON `{data, properties}` envelope in graph/sqlite.go:162-175 AND as a raw AST token in ast_walker_calls.go:341, while LLO writes raw content bytes. Three interpretations, one column, and the JSON reader fails SILENTLY on the mismatch.

## The measurement that does decide it (commit 10113ee, examples/cdc_churn.rs)

Cross-generation churn, mache 5a990e3 -> 520ee6c, a real 4-file/+102-line commit:

| target | spans | chunks | new chunks | churn |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nodes.record | 386,893 | 40,469 | 37 | 0.1% |
| source_blobs | 1,203 | 1,203 | 4 | 0.3% |

The prediction that manifest-targeting would show near-total chunk invalidation was WRONG. Both targets keep their payload nearly stable, because AST tokens are massively repetitive and the intern table dedups them well across generations.

The differentiator is the MANIFEST. A reparse invalidates every freshness witness — (size, mtime), and mtime always moves — so every manifest row is rewritten whether or not its content changed. 386,893 rows to absorb a 4-file commit, versus 1,203. **322x more bookkeeping per commit.**

Honest counterweight: record's 37 new chunks are ~10 bytes each; blobs' 4 are 8-16 KB. Blob-targeting rewrites ~130x more BYTES while rewriting 322x fewer ROWS. Rows dominate SQLite insert cost and footprint, so blobs win, but it is a trade and the ADR should say so rather than claiming a free 340x.

## Proposed gates for ADR-0033

- **F1c-F3c, F6c** — keep as-is, they already exist and pass (read equivalence, read amplification, edit locality, stale-witness refusal).
- **F4c storage bound** — RETAIN but restate: measured against the target CDC actually chunks, not against whatever `nodes.record` happens to hold. Record the 1.20-1.22x figure as characterization of the current mis-target, with the dbstat breakdown showing 99.5% is bookkeeping.
- **F5c dedup** — RESTATE as cross-generation, not within-generation. Within-generation whole-file dedup is 0.0% by construction and ADR-0028 predicted it; the number that matters is churn per commit.
- **F8c NEW — manifest churn per commit.** Rows rewritten to absorb a typical commit. Currently 386,893 vs 1,203. This is the gate that decides the target.
- **F9c NEW — ingest wall-clock.** The user-visible number, absent from the original gate set which measured arena size only. Activation ran at ~10 KiB/s because it committed once per node; fixed in 0d0f7f5 (65 commits -> 2 for 64 nodes, ~256x at default batch_size). Any target decision should carry a rebuild-time figure.
- **F10c NEW — the rolling hash must actually fire.** Assert a nonzero fraction of inputs reach MIN_CHUNK. At `nodes.record` that fraction is 0, which makes every dedup number on that target meaningless. This gate would have caught the mis-target immediately.

## Blocked on

edec5b — until `nodes.record`'s contract is declared, "the right target" is not answerable, and neither is what `read_content` is supposed to return. That bead is currently p2 and scoped as clarifying `nodes.kind`; it is actually the root of this and should be p1.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text: baa57f's measurement (mache's real projection: 100% of nodes sub-floor, +21% db for 1.9 MB of dedup) forces the two decisions ADR-0033 must record beyond the retroactive chunk-store design: (1) WHICH authoritative tables the derived content_* index may be built over — nodes (mutable, witness-gated) and source_blobs (content-addressed, witness-free; ADR-0028 §2.2's anticipated CDC refinement) — and (2) the floor policy: activation over source_blobs skips rows with byte_len < MIN_CHUNK by design, because manifesting sub-floor rows is measured pure overhead. Design detail in baa57f's comments; ADR-0033 will be written with the source_blobs activation PR.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: ADR-0033 is WRITTEN and in review as part of PR #308 (docs/adr/0033-cdc-chunk-backed-content.md): retroactive chunk-store/manifest/witness record plus D2 (explicit activation targets: nodes witness-gated, source_blobs witness-free) and D3 (sub-floor rows skipped by design, baa57f's measurement cited). Close this bead when #308 merges.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text: CLOSING: ADR-0033 (docs/adr/0033-cdc-chunk-backed-content.md) merged to main in PR #308 (tip 2ee9dab4), filling the reserved number slot. Records the retroactive chunk-store/manifest/witness design plus the decisions baa57f forced: D2 explicit activation targets (nodes witness-gated; source_blobs witness-free by immutability, per ADR-0028 §2.2's anticipated refinement) and D3 the sub-floor skip policy with the mache measurement cited.
comments.author: rsry-cli

comments.text:
Independent re-measurement, 2026-08-05, from mache (v0.15.1, different corpus and later version than ADR-0033's own numbers): `--target source-blobs` on mache's own 2.24 GB projection (826 files) came in at **+0.35% db size, zero measured dedup** — reproduces the ADR's central §D3 claim ("sub-floor rows are skipped... zero dedup beyond what source_blobs' own INSERT OR IGNORE already provides") on a corpus the ADR's author didn't run this on. `--target nodes` regression also reproduced unchanged (+21%, matching the original baa57f measurement almost exactly despite mache's corpus growing 777→826 files since).

Also falsified the boundary-stability claim directly (single-line edit to a real file, not synthetic data): 2-chunk file, edit-containing chunk's hash changed, the other chunk's hash was byte-identical across the edit despite its absolute offset shifting +83 bytes. Full writeup: mache-abf404 (closed) and mache-c436a6 (forward bead, blocked on ley-line-open-c3d746).

Filed separately: ley-line-open-c3d746 — `leyline daemon --cdc` never got the `--target` selector `baa57f` shipped on the standalone `cdc enable` CLI; still hardcodes the `nodes` target. Consumers spawning a managed daemon (mache) can't reach the cost-neutral path yet.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: ADR-0032 merged, recording D1 (dual-store is permanent because nodes.record is cross-runtime ABI, explicitly NOT ADR-0028's transitional pattern), D2 (freshness invariant is 'every record writer moves (size, mtime-nanos)'; correctness does not depend on call-site invalidation; stated envelope = stale pair replay), D3 (chunk identity is private, committed by containment; a manifest root is required before any cross-arena chunk sharing). F-gates F1c-F7c enumerated with F4c/F5c marked as gaps to close.

title: ADR-0014 §3: update capnp pin language (=0.20.0 → =0.25.0) + Go alpha-pin section
description:
Per coupling audit F4 (`docs/audits/2026-06-17-coupling-audit.md`).

## Problem

ADR-0014 §3 ("Per-language generators / Per-language runtimes") declares an exact pin:

> Rust: `capnpc = "=0.20.0"` exact (currently `"0.20"` semver-range — TIGHTEN). Go (mache side): `capnp.org/go/capnp/v3/capnpc-go@v3.0.X` exact tag, NOT `@latest`. Per-language runtimes. Rust: `capnp = "=0.20.0"` exact. Go: `require capnproto.org/go/capnp/v3 v3.0.X` exact.

Actual workspace pin (2026-06-17):

| Crate | `capnp` | `capnpc` | `capnp-json` |
|---|---|---|---|

title: PartitionSpec: one tagged-fold descriptor for every declared decomposition
description:
The substrate Sigma = (V, C, rho, sigma, R, S) defines naming but not PARTITIONING. sigma is total on whole values; there is no partition operator and no law composing part-addresses into whole-addresses. So five layers each invented their own cut of the same bytes — current_root (none), Head.rootHash (per-segment concat), CDC chunks (content-defined), ADR-0031 restriction keys (logical row-sets, SHA-256), ADR-014 sheaf-blocks (structural) — producing five incommensurable roots.

Formal result (partition-algebra analysis, 2026-07-27): there IS one composition operator — a tagged Merkle fold over a declared decomposition — but there is NO single lattice containing all five roots, and provably cannot be. Roots are never mutually derivable (pigeonhole: a 256-bit root cannot determine an n*256-bit leaf vector). Only WITNESSES are, and only under an alignment law: root_B is computable from A's leaf vector in O(#leaves) iff B's parts are unions of A's parts.

The prototype already exists in-repo at exactly one site: `head_digest` (head_digest.rs:38-44) uses blake3 new_derive_key with a context tag binding (generation, root, parent), and its test at lines 50-65 states the security rationale — without a context tag a head signature is bit-identical to a bare-root signature, 'the same key, two meanings'. ADR-015's HierarchySpec + canonical_serialize + hierarchy_id is the same operator, scoped to transport.

This bead generalizes that pattern into one descriptor family. The 'domain' field is load-bearing: an interval fold and a set fold over identical children MUST differ or the CDC manifest and a sheaf-block alias. The absent hash-algorithm field is equally load-bearing — multihash-style agility is an ANTI-feature under the BLAKE3 lock (substrate.rs:30-42).

Scope honesty: the DESCRIPTOR is zero-copy. Traversal of the value stays native to the value's format — SQLite pages are not capnp. Promise zero-copy manifests, not IPLD-style universal value traversal; the latter smuggles back the translation layer the semantic-file thesis exists to abolish.

comments.text:
Rust fold landed in eca1b99 — `rs/ll-core/core/src/partition.rs`. TDD: 9 tests written and verified RED before any implementation, then GREEN; 83 pass in leyline-core.

Pinned properties: domain separation (keyed fold, generalizing head_digest's new_derive_key), injectivity via length-prefixing (('ab','c') vs ('a','bc') must not alias — the b64505 defect class stated as a test here), domain field distinguishing interval vs set folds over identical children, entry order and framing both committed, empty partition not colliding with Hash::ZERO.

SCOPE CALL — the capnp schema is deliberately NOT included, so this bead is not fully closed by that commit.

Reasoning: ADR-0014 fixes ordinals permanently (append only, never rename or remove). Nothing produces or consumes a PartitionSpec across a runtime boundary today. Freezing a wire shape before it has a producer is how you end up maintaining a hole — and it is the same argument the ADR itself makes for why logicalRoot needed a shipping family rather than a reserved field.

Additionally: `clients/go/leyline-schema/` has per-schema Go bindings generated by a manual regen.sh with no drift gate, so landing a Rust-side schema now would create exactly the producer/consumer divergence bead e76959 exists to prevent.

The wire form should land with its first consumer — b68fa6 (Head' co-attestation) — together with the Go bindings in the same change.

REMAINING for this bead: the capnp PartitionSpec family + Go bindings, to be done as part of b68fa6 or as a follow-up once a producer exists. Not closing until then.

1. A remaining-scope note on an otherwise-done bead is work nobody actions. It reads as done in every list and rollup.
2. My original deferral named the WRONG consumer. It said the schema lands with b68fa6 (Head co-attestation) — but b68fa6 depends on this bead, which made the graph circular. Head' carries roots (32-byte hashes), not specs, so it never needed the wire schema. The first genuine consumer is a receiver that must RE-DERIVE a partition: cloister's skip attestation resolving spec_digest, and the disclosure-stream bundling. That is the d274a4 thread.

Deliberately NO hash-algorithm field. title: Head co-attestation: bind the incommensurable roots in one signed claim
description:
Resolves the linkage question in ley-line-open-ef5c1d. The roots CANNOT be made mutually derivable — see the PartitionSpec bead for the impossibility results — so 'link them cryptographically' cannot mean a hash equation. It means CO-ATTESTATION: the Head names all the roots in one signed claim, and consistency between them is RE-DERIVABLE rather than assumed.

Head' = {rootHash, manifestRoot, logicalRoot?, hierarchyId?, generation, parentHash, signature}.

The precedent is already established: `signature @5 :Data` was added as an additive field precisely so an unset field does not change canonical bytes for existing instances (head.capnp:63-66, ADR-0014 section 1). These fields follow the same rule.

Consistency check is one linear pass: stream the manifest's chunks through BLAKE3, assert it reproduces rootHash, and fill the bao outboard tree in the same pass. That makes it third-party re-executable — the semantic-file 'answer = f(root, query)' property applied to the roots themselves.

This is also what makes signing safe to generalize (cloister). Today RootSigner::sign accepts a bare 32-byte Hash whatever its provenance, so every untagged root is a cross-protocol confusion hazard the moment anything signs.

OPEN QUESTION for the ADR: whether logicalRoot belongs in v1 at all, or whether the row structure stays unbound until a restriction family actually ships.

Depends on: PartitionSpec descriptor. Blocks: cloister signing generalization.

comments.text:
DECISION (operator, 2026-07-27): logicalRoot is REQUIRED in Head v1, not optional.

The open question in this bead's description is closed — we design for the restriction family shipping. Acceptance is amended accordingly: Head' = {rootHash, manifestRoot, logicalRoot, hierarchyId?, generation, parentHash, signature}, with logicalRoot populated by the v1 restriction family rather than reserved.

Rationale: binding a structure with no consumer produces a sixth root nobody can derive. Shipping a family alongside it makes logicalRoot load-bearing from day one and forces the row-addressing design to be validated by a real workload.

The additive-field discipline is unchanged — an unset field must not change canonical bytes for existing instances (ADR-0014 section 1, precedent set by signature @5).

Shipping vehicle: see the restriction-family-v1 bead.
comments.author: rsry-cli

acceptance_criteria: Head carries manifestRoot (+ optional hierarchyId, logicalRoot) as additive fields; head_digest binds them alongside generation/rootHash/parentHash; one linear pass re-derives consistency (stream manifest chunks through BLAKE3, reproduce rootHash, fill the bao tree in the same pass) and is exposed as a verify entry point. Falsifying test: a Head co-attesting a manifestRoot inconsistent with rootHash fails verification.

title: A-3: wire.rs typed-struct lockdown + 20-op handler swap
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.3 of decade `daemon-typed-wire`, thread `daemon-json-type-lockdown`. Depends on `b631c8` (schema reconciliation must land first so wire.rs has a stable target).

## Context

After A-1 (drift gate) and A-2 (schema reconciled), the daemon protocol contract is finally accurate. This bead makes the wire generation MECHANICAL via typed Rust structs, so future drift can only happen through deliberate schema bumps + corresponding wire.rs updates — all gated by the cross-runtime fixture test.

## Work

### A-3.1: wire.rs scaffolding
- Create `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/wire.rs`
- For each message in `daemon.capnp` (the reconciled version from A-2), define a Rust struct with `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]`
- Use `#[serde(rename = "...")]` to control JSON shape where Rust naming conventions differ from the JSON wire (e.g. capnp `currentRoot` → Rust struct field `current_root` → JSON field `current_root`)
- Tagged request enum: `enum Request { Status(StatusRequest), ListChildren(ListChildrenRequest), ... }` with `#[serde(tag = "op", rename_all = "snake_case")]` (or whichever serde shape matches the existing `{"op": "..."}` dispatch shape)

### A-3.2: ops.rs handler swap
For each op in `base_op_names`:
- Replace `json!({...})` builder with `let resp = ResponseStruct { ok: true, ... }; serde_json::to_string(&resp)?`
- Replace `req.get("foo").and_then(|v| v.as_str())` extraction with a typed request struct destructure (or use the tagged enum from A-3.1 if `socket.rs` does the parse)
- Same wire bytes; no behavior change
- Iterate per-op; the A-1 gate validates each conversion

### A-3.3: socket.rs typed dispatch
- Replace the `req.get("op").as_str()` extraction in `socket.rs` with `serde_json::from_str::<Request>(&line)` to deserialize the tagged enum
- The dispatch chain (event ops → base ops → extension async/sync → unknown) stays — just routes typed values instead of `&serde_json::Value`
- Error responses go through `ErrorResponse` typed struct

### A-3.4: Cross-runtime parity tests
- Each op gets a unit test in `tests/integration.rs`: build the typed `<Op>Response` struct → serialize via `serde_json::to_string` → compare byte-for-byte against the equivalent fixture from A-1
- If the comparison fails, the wire shape drifted — fix the struct, NOT the test
- The Go side (A-1's fixture decode test) continues to validate cross-runtime

### A-3.5: Drift-prevention enforcement
- The A-1 gate now catches three classes of drift:
  - Rust handler emits a field not in `daemon.capnp` → Go decode succeeds (extra fields tolerated) but the typed Rust struct refuses to serialize an unknown field — caught at compile time
  - `daemon.capnp` declares a field not emitted by a handler → Go decode may fail on the missing field if required (depending on JSON tag) — caught at test time
  - Schema and handler disagree on field SHAPE → Go decode raises `UnmarshalTypeError` — caught at test time
- Document the gate's coverage in `TABLE_CONTRACT.md`

## Acceptance

- No `json!({...})` calls remain in `ops.rs` for any op in `base_op_names` (audit via `cargo clippy -W ...` or a grep test)
- Every op handler emits its response via a typed `<Op>Response` struct
- All A-1 fixtures decode cleanly on the Go side
- `task ci` green
- `task image:smoke` green
- `nc -U` debuggability preserved (manual probe still returns parseable JSON)

## What's NOT in scope

- Migrating the wire encoding off JSON — explicitly deferred (bead `a4e860`)
- Adding new ops — Bead B (`a47d7d`) handles `find_callees` independently
- mache-side typed binding adoption — `mache-a5ad09`, separate timeline
- LSP/vec ops — included if they have schema entries from A-2; otherwise scope to base_op_names that DO have schema entries and file follow-up for any that don't

## Risk / rollback

- Wire encoding does NOT change. Byte-for-byte the existing JSON output is preserved (the typed structs serialize identically to current `json!({...})`).
- Rollback: revert the PR; existing tests cover the JSON wire shape.
- mache: no required change. Existing untyped consumers keep working.

title: bao outboard tree: incremental root maintenance + per-page verify-on-fault
description:
Closes the 'verification is latent, not free' gap named in the semantic-file essay, WITHOUT breaking the BLAKE3 lock.

BLAKE3 is internally a Merkle tree over fixed 1024-byte chunks. That intrinsic tree — not CDC — is the partition algebra for the integrity axis. Retaining it as an outboard (bao / fs-verity shape) buys incremental root maintenance O(edit * log n) and per-page verify-on-fault, while current_root remains exactly blake3::hash(buffer).

Why this is NOT the CDC tree: BLAKE3's chunk counter is position-BINDING (it exists to kill splice/reorder attacks); CDC boundaries are position-INDEPENDENT, which is exactly what makes dedup work. The two share no interior nodes and cannot be unified. Verify and dedup are irreducibly two structures — forcing one means abandoning either sigma(v)=BLAKE3(v) or dedup. Keep both.

Cost, against measured numbers on this machine (aarch64): today the snapshot loop pays flat O(arena) BLAKE3 EVERY flip — 64 MB live arena, 1.0 GB legacy. One-time entry is full CDC at 1547 MiB/s (~41 ms at 64 MB, ~0.68 s at 1 GB) with the outboard fill riding the same linear pass. Steady state is a <=512 KiB rescan per edit plus a microsecond-scale fold. Net: replaces per-snapshot O(arena) with amortized O(edit) — strictly less work than today. Storage ~6% (about 4 MB per 64 MB arena).

Prior art to steal wholesale: bao, and fs-verity as kernel precedent.

comments.text: Related work landed 2026-07-29 (f8ebe7 + b86699, riding the v0.13.0 train): the CDC refresh path now hashes only the rechunk rescan window — carried manifest rows are existence-probed, never re-derived — and edit coordinates arrive as a parsed leyline_cdc::Edit whose truthfulness contract is documented and enforced at the fs call site. Relation to this bead: that fix makes the CHUNK layer's cost O(edit + window), but the RECORD-level σ (and anything that wants a whole-content root after an edit) still pays a full hash — which is precisely what bao's incremental root maintenance removes: O(log n) root update along the affected subtree path. The Edit/rehashed-window plumbing from f8ebe7 is the exact input shape bao's incremental maintenance consumes (which spans changed), and per-page verify-on-fault is the read-side sibling of the contains() existence probe (verify a faulted page against the outboard tree without whole-file hashing). Sequencing note: LL's wire CDC and mache's dataflow analysis are premised on sub-file granularity end to end — chunk layer is done; this bead is the content-address layer's half.

The acceptance criterion holds and is pinned as the headline test: root() bit-identical to blake3::hash across every tree boundary shape. update() returns the rehash count and the test asserts work == dirty chunk span exactly. In-place edits (the arena page case) are O(dirty) in bytes hashed; parent re-merges are O(chunks/1024) 64-byte compressions per root() call — interior-node caching left as a same-API optimization. comments.text: Design note from James for the interior-node caching phase: ADR-0031 (restriction-addressed derived-view caching) is the governing discipline — and the outboard tree is its FIXED POINT. ADR-0031 keys a derived view on the exact hash of its input closure; a Merkle parent node IS definitionally the hash of its input closure (its two child CVs), so the cache key and cached value coincide and no separate key scheme is needed. The restriction map is the dirty ancestor path: update() invalidates exactly the O(log n) parents above the dirtied leaves. Unlike ADR-0031's review cache, false-skips here are structurally unrepresentable rather than empirically zero — a stale parent disagrees with its recomputed children by construction, and the root==blake3::hash pinned test falsifies end to end. Implementation shape when taken: store interior CVs alongside leaf_cvs (heap layout or per-level vecs), update() marks the dirty path, root() re-merges only marked nodes. Same API, ADR-0031 cited in the module docs.

title: Prolly-tree index for restriction closures — verifiability of row membership against logicalRoot
description:
ADR-0031 restriction closures are LOGICAL row sets spanning multiple objects (ADR-0031:45-49, 99-103). They are not byte-representable stably: a row's byte extent depends on physical layout, so inserting an UNRELATED row splits B-tree pages and relocates rows the closure never touched — destroying exactly the locality restriction-addressing exists for. They are also not even a PARTITION: different review families' closures overlap, so they form a cover.

The bridge is snapshot-indexed and unstable in the byte direction, but exact and stable in the VALUE direction: make rows first-class values (canonical serialization -> BLAKE3 per row) and fold over row addresses exactly as over chunk addresses. The restriction key becomes A(family-spec, sorted row addresses) — same operator, different leaf universe. ADR-0031's ~6-row indexed gather already computes this shape, with the wrong hash and ad-hoc serialization.

Prolly trees (Noms design docs; Dolt storage) are CDC applied to a sorted key space: history-independent canonical shape, root as a pure function of logical content, O(log n) node churn per row edit, inclusion proofs. That gives restriction keys what they lack — verifiability of a key's rows against a snapshot root. Caveat to evaluate: prolly proofs are range-efficient while ADR-0031 closures are scattered sets, so cost is O(k log n) point inclusions.

Note the lineage is already in the stack: the bead store itself is Dolt-backed.

Also cite (do not build): Merkle Search Trees, Auvolat & Taiani, SRDS 2019.

Recommended F-gate for the instability claim: insert one unrelated row, count how many CDC chunks change.

comments.text:
SCOPE CHANGE (operator, 2026-07-27): this is no longer speculative research.

Because logicalRoot ships in Head v1 and a restriction family ships with it, the row structure needs a real index rather than a recommendation. Treat this bead as the INDEXING STRATEGY for the shipping family: evaluate prolly trees against the concrete requirement of verifying a family key's rows against logicalRoot, at the scale that family actually uses (ADR-0031's measured closure is ~6 rows).

The mismatch to resolve rather than note: prolly proofs are range-efficient while restriction closures are scattered sets, so cost is O(k log n) point inclusions. At k~6 that is fine; the deliverable should say at what k it stops being fine.

Lineage is already in the stack — the bead store itself is Dolt-backed.

acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation on whether to adopt a prolly-tree index over canonically-serialized rows: what it buys for restriction-key verifiability, what the scattered-set vs range-proof mismatch costs at k~6 rows, and whether logicalRoot is worth binding into Head. Cites Noms/Dolt primary sources.

title: hdc-3e: HIR codebook — per-compiler HIR walker fingerprinting
Document krust pinning policy or fallback recipe
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Risk-mitigation follow-up to ley-line-open-2b255c.

`task image` depends on [`krust`](https://github.com/imjasonh/krust) v0.0.1 (alpha). During the v0.2.1 image migration we hit two real bugs in krust 0.0.1 in a single session:
1. **Path doubling** — when `project_dir` is a relative path, krust passes `--target-dir <relative>` to cargo *after* `cd`'ing, so cargo resolves it against the new cwd → nested `rs/ll-open/cli/rs/ll-open/cli/target/krust/...` (workaround: pass an absolute path).
2. **Crate-name ≠ bin-name** — krust assumes `cargo metadata`'s package name is the binary name, ignoring `[[bin]] name = ...` (workaround: `-- --bin <bin-name>`).

Both have working workarounds in `Taskfile.yml`'s `image` task. But:
- We're coupled to a barely-released tool with active alpha churn
- A regression in krust could silently break our `task image` flow
- New contributors hitting `krust install --force` could get a different version than what we tested against

## Two paths (pick one)

### Option A: Pin to known-good
- Add a comment + `cargo install krust --git https://github.com/imjasonh/krust --rev <sha>` to README install instructions
- Or vendor krust as a workspace member (heavier)
- Pro: deterministic, survives upstream regressions
- Con: misses upstream fixes for the two bugs above; manual bumps

### Option B: Document fallback
- Add a `task image:no-krust` Taskfile target that does:
  - `cd rs && cargo zigbuild --release -p leyline-cli --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl --target-dir target/krust`
  - `docker build -f image.Dockerfile -t ley-line-open:0.2.1 .`
- README mentions both: "active path uses krust; if krust regresses, `task image:no-krust` is the documented escape hatch"
- Pro: zero coupling to upstream stability; we own the recipe
- Con: two paths to maintain; each release cycle re-verifies both

Recommend **Option B** — krust is a thin wrapper over `cargo zigbuild` + image assembly; replicating it ourselves is ~10 lines and removes a dependency from our hot path. Option A makes us a permanent downstream adopter for tooling we don't need long-term.

## Acceptance
- README `## Building the image` section names the policy
- `task image:no-krust` exists and produces an identical-shape image (same tag, same CMD, smoke passes against it)

title: Gate --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0 behind --mcp-allow-public flag
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.1 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `mcp-auth-hardening`.

## Problem

`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mcp.rs:19` says: *"this module assumes localhost-only or already-attested"*. That trust assumption was true when MCP only spoke over UDS (filesystem-permission-gated). With v0.2.1 we added `--mcp-bind <IpAddr>` (loopback default; container deployments pass `0.0.0.0`). The flag works, but the user's intent is ambiguous:

- "I'm running this in a container, 0.0.0.0 is just netns plumbing" — fine
- "I want this exposed on my LAN to non-cloister consumers" — VIOLATES the no-auth assumption silently

Today we mitigate via documentation (README, Dockerfile comments, clap help text), but the wire allows it either way. A future deployment script that defaults to `--mcp-bind 0.0.0.0` "to make it work in docker" can leak MCP onto a public host IP without anyone noticing.

## Work

Make the deliberate-intent flag a hard requirement at the binary level:

1. Rename internal: `--mcp-bind <IpAddr>` stays, but for non-loopback addresses *also* require `--mcp-allow-public` (or it fails fast with an error pointing at the security model)
2. `--mcp-allow-public` requires either:
   - You're a cloister-attested deployment (env var? parent process check?), OR
   - You explicitly accepted the risk (the flag alone)
3. Update `image.Dockerfile` CMD: bake `--mcp-allow-public` alongside `--mcp-bind 0.0.0.0` since container deployments are the legitimate case
4. Update clap help text + README + mcp.rs module doc to reflect new contract

## Acceptance

- `leyline daemon --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0` (no --mcp-allow-public) fails immediately with an error message pointing at the bead / docs
- `leyline daemon --mcp-bind 0.0.0.0 --mcp-allow-public` works (current behavior)
- `leyline daemon --mcp-bind 127.0.0.1` (or omitted) works without --mcp-allow-public (loopback is the safe default)
- Container image's CMD updated to include the flag — `task image:smoke` still passes
- Existing tests (integration.rs) still pass; new test added for the gate

## Why this is T1 of the thread

Stops the bleed before more deployments adopt bare `--mcp-bind 0.0.0.0` as their idiom. Subsequent beads (T1.2 ADR + T1.3 implement-real-auth) take longer; this one is mechanical and high-leverage.

comments.text:
Merged via PR #30 at commit ac0864f. 4-flag opt-in gate live: `--mcp-bind` to a non-loopback address now requires `--mcp-allow-public` and fails fast with a clear error otherwise.

Image deployment unchanged in behaviour — image.Dockerfile CMD passes both flags, host-side publish pinned to 127.0.0.1 in `task image:smoke` and the recommended docker run. 4 new gate tests in `cmd_daemon::tests`. 4 Copilot review threads addressed (test rename + 3 docker syntax fixes), all resolved.

This is the "stop the bleeding" piece; the durable auth model is `ley-line-open-b8395d` (ADR) → `ley-line-open-b885d1` (implement). Closing.

title: CDC freshness witness is (size, mtime) — a change heuristic, not a mutation identity; same-shape replacement serves prior bytes
description:
External review (relayed by James 2026-07-29), verified: content_manifest_meta(node_id, source_len, source_mtime) at fs/src/chunked.rs:126-129; the gc + read gates compare m.source_len = n.size AND m.source_mtime IS n.mtime (gc.rs:147-148). One wording correction to the review: the code never claims 'provably fresh' — its term is 'freshness witness', which is honest. The exposure stands anyway:

- A writer that replaces nodes.record with SAME-LENGTH bytes within mtime granularity leaves the witness valid → reads serve the OLD manifest's bytes. Two in-model paths: rapid successive legit writes inside one mtime tick, and any direct-SQL writer (the 'third write path' class this ecosystem already treats as real — cf. never-touch-beads-sqlite). Worst case is the path-reuse disclosure scenario the CDC design itself flags: prior occupant's bytes served after replacement.
- The legit write path captures the witness in the same transaction (chunked.rs:303), so the witness earns its keep exactly where writes DON'T go through it — which is why it must be a mutation identity, not a stat pair.

Fix (reviewer's, endorsed): nodes.content_generation INTEGER NOT NULL, incremented in the SAME transaction as every record write; manifest stores the generation; freshness = exact equality, no byte re-reads (a stored content hash also works but costs a full-record hash per write; generation models mutation, which is what freshness IS here). Migration: existing rows get generation 0 + witness invalidation (falls back to slow-but-correct, the design's own stated degradation). Until fixed, docs/comments should say 'fresh per the (size,mtime) witness; external writers must invalidate' — no stronger claim. Tests: same-length same-mtime replacement must MISS the fast path (this is the case the current suite cannot express).

comments.text:
Companion findings from the type-driven-correctness agent (blind; report in _agent_log/2026-07-29-types-friend-cdc-report.md) — fold into this bead's fix since the generation-counter rewrite touches the same predicate:

F3: the freshness predicate is implemented THREE times and two copies disagree with the tested one. manifest_witness_is_fresh (chunked.rs:724-731) carries source_len >= 0; the read gate SQL (chunked.rs:830) and gc's dead_manifest_predicate (gc.rs:146-148) do NOT. The tested truth table includes the (-1,-1) row the shipped gates get wrong: read gate says fresh -> usize::try_from(-1) hard-errors on a node whose record is readable (violates 'degrade to slow-but-correct'); gc never reaps it (the exact b5e56f failure). Fix shape: one WITNESS_FRESH_PREDICATE const consumed by both SQL sites (the OVERLAP_PREDICATE pattern the same file already models), plus an agreement test driving Rust and SQL arms over the same truth table. When this bead replaces the witness with a generation, define the NEW predicate once, with that agreement test, from day one.

F4: nodes.size / nodes.record are NULLABLE in the canonical DDL; all three witness readers decode them as non-null — NULL becomes an ERROR out of the read path instead of 'not fresh' (rusqlite InvalidColumnType; .optional() only converts NoRows). Under SQL three-valued logic a NULL size makes the gate expression NULL -> decode error, on a node servable from record. Fix: Option decode folded into existing not-fresh/no-manifest branches + COALESCE(...,0) on the SQL arm. Also: chunked_and_record_paths_agree tests only ASCII — the record arm decodes TEXT and is only byte-identical for UTF-8-surviving content, guaranteed by graph.rs's from_utf8_lossy and stated nowhere in chunked.rs; add the one-line doc.

Also noting for this bead's design: the agent CREDITED the witness mechanism itself ('correctness genuinely no longer depends on remembering anything', the strip-every-invalidate falsification test) — the generation fix should preserve that test shape, swapping the witness column, not the discipline.

comments.text: CLOSING: shipped in PR #306 (merged, tip 0ddaa3bf). The (size, mtime) heuristic witness is replaced by a generation counter maintained by SQLite TRIGGERS on nodes (UPDATE OF record WHEN new IS NOT old, plus AFTER INSERT for the reused-node-id disclosure case) — every SQL writer advances it, including foreign writers that never heard of the CDC module. WITNESS_FRESH_PREDICATE is defined once and consumed by the read gate, the GC reaper, and the Rust arm; witness_predicate_arms_agree drives both arms over one truth table, and same_shape_replacement_by_a_foreign_writer_is_not_served_stale pins the exact attack this bead documented. Migration via source_generation DEFAULT -1 (pre-upgrade manifests refuse and rebuild). Runner CI green including the feature-routed mutants gate: manifest_witness_is_fresh and has_chunked_content mutants all caught under the correct feature set.

title: ADR: MCP wire auth model — token / mTLS / cloister-only?
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.2 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `mcp-auth-hardening`. Depends on `b7dd03` (the deliberate-intent flag bead — that's the stopgap; this is the durable answer).

## Decision needed

`mcp.rs` says *"assumes localhost-only or already-attested"*. What does "attested" mean operationally? The ADR needs to nail down:

1. **Trust model.** Is MCP HTTP a closed contract between LLO and cloister, or do we want third-party MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) to connect directly?
   - If LLO↔cloister only: cloister-attested means *the wire never leaves the host* + cloister identifies itself
   - If third-party allowed: needs a real wire-level auth (tokens or mTLS)

2. **Auth mechanism options:**
   - (a) Bearer token from env (`LEYLINE_MCP_TOKEN`), checked against `Authorization: Bearer <tok>` header
   - (b) mTLS (cloister presents a cert; LLO verifies against pinned issuer)
   - (c) Unix peer credentials when over UDS only (already free); HTTP transport requires (a) or (b)
   - (d) Capabilities-style — JWT with scope claims (which tools the caller may invoke)

3. **Defaults.** What does a fresh `leyline daemon --mcp-port 8384` do without auth config?
   - Reject all requests until token configured (safe default, slightly hostile to local dev)
   - Generate an ephemeral token printed to stderr (dev-friendly, matches `jupyter` pattern)
   - Accept only loopback (current behavior, which is what the `b7dd03` stopgap codifies)

4. **Compatibility.** How does this interact with cloister's `LLO_MCP_URL` consumer? Cloister currently makes unauthenticated POSTs.

## Deliverable

`docs/adr/00XX-mcp-wire-auth.md` written + reviewed. Pattern from existing ADRs (`docs/adr/0014-capnp-as-protocol.md` is the closest precedent — explicit options weighed, decision recorded, falsifiable claim, success criteria).

## Acceptance

- ADR file written with: context (the trust assumption + how it's currently violated), options weighed (at least the four above), decision + rationale, falsifiable claim ("if our auth model is wrong, X will happen by Y"), implementation pointer (the next bead, T1.3)
- ADR linked from `mcp.rs` module doc + README MCP section
- `b7dd03` (deliberate-intent flag) referenced as the stopgap that this ADR supersedes

## Why this is T1.2 (not T1.1)

The flag-gate (`b7dd03`) buys time. The ADR is the durable answer. We don't want to ship real auth without first writing down what we're solving for — premature mechanism is how you end up with three half-baked auth schemes.

title: rechunk is pub and promises chunk(new_data) equality for inputs it never validates — consume a validated manifest type
description:
External review (relayed by James 2026-07-29), verified: cdc/src/lib.rs:127 pub fn rechunk / :160 pub fn rechunk_with_stats accept (&[Chunk], new_data, edit_offset, old_edit_end, old_len) and check none of: edit_offset <= old_edit_end <= old_len; old tiles [0,old_len) sorted/contiguous/nonempty; lens <= MAX_CHUNK; shifted offsets nonnegative ((c.offset as isize + delta) as usize can wrap). The doc contract promises result == chunk(new_data) — false for arbitrary type-valid inputs. The intended call path (capture_chunked_content) validates coverage indirectly, so this is API robustness, not a live bug.

Fix options (reviewer's, endorsed, pick one): (a) crate-private + a ValidatedManifest { chunks, source_len } newtype whose constructor checks tiling — fits the declared-decomposition direction; (b) Result-returning precondition validation. Per this repo's remove-don't-deprecate posture, (a) with a clean API break + CHANGELOG note is the better shape. Property test regardless: proptest random (old_data, edit) pairs asserting rechunk == chunk(new) — the existing fixed-case tests are exactly the mutants-vs-property-testing gap James raised.

What the review confirmed is NOT broken (recorded so nobody re-litigates): per-boundary GearHash state reset is coherent with the bounded decision-window argument; the resynchronization tail-reuse logic is sound; range-read validation (ordered contiguous coverage, no partial writes) is the strongest part.

comments.text:
Sharper remedy from the type-driven-correctness agent (F5+F6, report in _agent_log/2026-07-29-types-friend-cdc-report.md): TWO parse types, not one.

F6 (this bead, upgraded): replace the three positional usizes with Edit::parse(offset, old_end, old_len) — mis-ordering becomes unrepresentable at the call site; the semantic half (bytes outside the interval unchanged) STAYS at the TX rung and must be SAID: name store_content_manifest's ensure!(stored == c.hash) as the enforcement, because f8ebe7's fix removes that rehash — land these together or corruption path opens. NEW in-repo evidence the triple is already dishonest today: graph.rs computes coordinates against raw bytes but passes String::from_utf8_lossy output — a write landing mid-UTF-8-sequence rewrites bytes BEFORE edit_offset; today the ensure! catches it and a legitimate binary write turns into an error via an undocumented path. Fix alongside: compute coordinates post-conversion, or fall back to Full refresh when new_str.len() != content.len().

F5 (add to this bead's scope): ValidatedRangeManifest is decorative — select_range_manifest validates then passes the raw &[Chunk] to read_range_into, which re-validates identically; four discharged-but-call-distance slice ⊥s hang off it. Remedy: SelectedRange::parse in leyline-cdc as the ONLY constructor; read_range_into takes it, drops validation AND the offset param (already inside the parsed value). Sibling: read_range silently requires complete tiling (via manifest_len) — undocumented; give it Manifest::parse carrying that postcondition. Existing rejection tests port as parse rejection tests.

Also from the same review, smaller CDC promotions to ride the same PR: F8 chunked_content_len uses 'as usize' where three neighbors use try_from (one line); F9 chunk_into's debug_assert_eq vs fs's ensure! for the same invariant — promote (the crate's own test suite ships three non-conforming BlobStores as the threat model); F10 GC byte-accounting balance asserted only in an example — add the in-transaction ensure (operands already in scope); F11 ContentSource::Record fabricated for empty reads — add ContentSource::Empty variant; F7 NonZeroUsize for Chunk.len — decide-and-document (agent's own cost analysis says declining is defensible if said aloud).

comments.text: Edit parse type implemented and shipped with f8ebe7 on the v0.13.0 train (ordering unrepresentable; semantic half documented as caller obligation with the enforcement chain named; graph.rs lossy case fixed via full-refresh fallback; rejection tests in cdc). REMAINING in this bead's scope, post-release: F5's SelectedRange/Manifest parse types for read_range_into/read_range, F7 NonZeroUsize decision, F8 as-usize->try_from, F10 GC byte-balance ensure, F11 ContentSource::Empty.
