title: Implement MCP wire auth per ADR (decided in b8395d)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.3 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `mcp-auth-hardening`. Depends on `b8395d` (the auth ADR — this bead implements whatever it decides).

## Work

Implement the auth mechanism the ADR (`b8395d`) selected. Concrete shape will depend on the ADR outcome; this bead exists as a placeholder + dependency anchor so the ADR work knows there's an implementation slot waiting for it.

Likely shape (assuming token-bearer is the ADR outcome — the simplest viable answer):

1. New `LEYLINE_MCP_TOKEN` env var read at daemon startup. If unset and `--mcp-bind` is non-loopback, daemon either generates an ephemeral token + prints to stderr OR fails (per ADR decision)
2. `daemon/mcp.rs::handle_post` + `handle_get` check `Authorization: Bearer <tok>` against the configured token; reject 401 on mismatch
3. Cloister side (separate repo): set `LEYLINE_MCP_TOKEN` in cloister's daemon spawn args, pass through `Authorization` header on each MCP HTTP call. Cloister-side change is a follow-up bead in cloister's repo, NOT in scope for this LLO bead.
4. `--mcp-allow-public` (from `b7dd03`) becomes redundant once auth is enforced; deprecate per the T1.4 bead

## Acceptance

- Auth check in `handle_post` / `handle_get`
- New integration test: 401 on missing/wrong token; 200 on correct token
- README + clap help describe how to set the token
- Cloister-side wiring filed as a follow-up bead in cloister's repo (cross-repo dep noted in this bead's comments at handoff time)

## Why this lives behind the ADR

Implementation without the ADR is just guessing — and we've already shown (in v0.2.1's --mcp-bind story) that "ship the obvious thing first, document later" creates trust drift. ADR first.

title: Deprecate --mcp-allow-public after wire auth lands
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.4 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `mcp-auth-hardening`. Depends on `b885d1` (the implement-auth bead — once real auth is enforced, the deliberate-intent flag is redundant).

## Work

Once `b885d1` ships real wire auth, `--mcp-allow-public` (from `b7dd03`) becomes belt-and-suspenders. Two paths:

### Option A: Remove the flag entirely
- Delete `--mcp-allow-public` from clap, cmd_daemon, mcp.rs
- Bump LLO MAJOR (or document as a breaking CLI change in CHANGELOG)
- Pro: clean
- Con: anyone scripting `leyline daemon --mcp-allow-public` breaks

### Option B: Keep as a no-op + deprecation warning
- Flag still parses but just emits "DEPRECATED: --mcp-allow-public has no effect; auth is now enforced via LEYLINE_MCP_TOKEN. Remove this flag."
- Schedule removal for a later release (3 versions out)
- Pro: gentle
- Con: maintenance burden; deprecated surface lives forever in practice

Recommend **Option B** for one minor release cycle, then **Option A** in the next major. Standard deprecation cadence.

## Acceptance

- `--mcp-allow-public` either removed or made a deprecation no-op (per chosen option)
- CHANGELOG entry noting the change
- Test that the deprecation warning fires (if Option B)
- `image.Dockerfile` CMD no longer passes `--mcp-allow-public` (since it's redundant); test with `task image:smoke`

## Why this is T1.4

Closes the loop: T1.1 added the flag, T1.2 wrote the auth ADR, T1.3 implemented the auth, T1.4 retires the flag. Thread is done when this bead closes.

title: Audit: UDS socket vs MCP HTTP dispatch — confirm or list divergences
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T2.1 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `daemon-transport-convergence`.

## Context

`cmd_daemon.rs`'s docstring claims UDS socket and MCP HTTP "share the same dispatch table" — different transports, identical ops surface. This bead tests that claim.

`daemon/socket.rs` (UDS) and `daemon/mcp.rs` (HTTP) both call into the same op registry, AFAICT. But:
- The MCP transport speaks JSON-RPC (`tools/list`, `tools/call`)
- The UDS transport speaks... a length-prefixed binary protocol? raw JSON? capnp? (haven't read it carefully)
- If they truly share dispatch, they should expose the same set of operations with the same arg/result types

If they're not identical, that's either:
- A latent bug (an op that works on UDS but not MCP, or vice versa)
- An intentional divergence (e.g. UDS exposes admin ops MCP doesn't)
- An unintentional divergence (MCP added without porting all UDS ops, or vice versa)

We can't make a transport-convergence decision (T2.2) without knowing the current truth.

## Work

Read-only audit. Output: a markdown table or doc with rows for each operation, columns for "exposed via UDS / exposed via MCP / arg type identical / result type identical / notes." Posted as a comment on this bead, OR added to `docs/` as `daemon-transport-audit-2026-05-10.md`.

Specifically:
1. Enumerate ops in `daemon/socket.rs`'s dispatch
2. Enumerate ops in `daemon/mcp.rs`'s tools/list
3. Diff
4. For any divergence: classify as (a) intentional, (b) bug, (c) future work / undecided
5. Note any ops that have different SHAPES across transports (e.g. UDS takes raw bytes, MCP takes JSON — but they're nominally the same op)

## Acceptance

- A bead comment (or `docs/` file) lists the audit table
- Any (b) bug-class divergences are filed as separate beads (high priority — silent transport drift is a correctness issue)
- A handoff note for T2.2 (the convergence decision bead) summarizing the inventory

## Why this is T2.1

You can't pick a convergence strategy without the inventory. This is the data-gathering pass.

title: ADR: pick daemon transport convergence strategy
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T2.2 of decade `daemon-trust-and-transport`, thread `daemon-transport-convergence`. Depends on `b93871` (the audit — its output is the input to this decision).

## Decision needed

Given the audit results from `b93871`, pick one:

### Option A: Fold UDS into MCP — single transport
- MCP HTTP becomes the canonical surface; UDS becomes thin shim that does HTTP-over-UDS (or removed entirely if UDS-specific consumers have all migrated)
- Pro: one dispatch table, one place to add ops, one place to add auth
- Con: HTTP overhead on every UDS call (small, but present); breaks any consumer hardcoded to the binary UDS protocol
- Compatible with: cloister, any MCP-compatible client. Hostile to: legacy local tools.

### Option B: Keep both as peers, share op registry
- Define op contracts in one place (a trait, a registry, or capnp schema)
- Both transports call into the registry; transports are pure I/O
- Pro: keeps UDS's wire efficiency; consumers of either transport see identical ops
- Con: transport-specific quirks (auth, framing, error reporting) live in two places

### Option C: Specialize each — UDS for admin, MCP for tool-call
- Explicitly diverge: UDS exposes ops cloister/operators need (status, snapshot, restart-pass); MCP exposes only the tool-call surface AI clients want (parse, query, enrich)
- Pro: each surface is justified by its consumer; no pretense of "same thing"
- Con: doubles the contract maintenance; auth model has to handle both

## Inputs to weigh
- Audit table from `b93871`
- Cloister's actual consumption pattern (does it use UDS at all today, or only MCP HTTP?)
- Any other consumers of the UDS transport (mache? leyline-private? ad-hoc scripts?)
- Auth model from `b8395d` — does the chosen auth scheme apply to both transports cleanly?

## Acceptance

- `docs/adr/00XX-daemon-transport-convergence.md` written
- Decision recorded with rationale
- Falsifiable claim ("if we picked wrong, X will happen by Y")
- Implementation pointer to T2.3 bead

## Why this is T2.2

The audit makes the inventory legible; this turns it into a decision. Implementation (T2.3) follows.

title: Emit referrer_node_id (+ qualifier) on node_refs — enclosing-def linkage for ref-based consumer rules
description:
From mache's smell-gate parity investigation (mache-608a3c). node_refs currently emits (token, node_id, source_id, node_hash) where node_id = the FULL AST path of the call_expression SITE (leaf), e.g. `api/schema.go/method_declaration/block/.../call_expression`. Consumer rules that aggregate refs BY CALLER cannot work: mache's fan_out_skew (COUNT DISTINCT callee GROUP BY caller) and untested_function (was this def called from within a Test* function?) both need the ENCLOSING DEFINITION of each ref, but today every ref has a unique call-site node_id so GROUP BY yields n=1 -> 0 findings on the LLO projection (vs 33 and 9 on tree-sitter). Confirmed still absent in v0.7.3.

Ask: add a referrer_node_id column to node_refs = node_id of the nearest enclosing definition (function_declaration / method_declaration / function_item / etc.) of the ref site. Derivable from the AST already built (the enclosing def IS a real node_defs.node_id -- verified `api/schema.go/method_declaration` exists in node_defs). Makes ref-based rules backend-agnostic (matches the mache-schema projection semantics) instead of forcing consumers into brittle call-site-path string surgery. Optionally also surface qualifier (LHS of the selector expr; BindingRecord.qualifier / T8.7 already exists) as a column for fan_out's distinct-origin metric.

Wire impact: additive column, backward-compatible; no existing consumer breaks.

comments.text:

1. KIND normalization (LLO agent's canonical_kind proposal): NOT NEEDED to unblock mache. node_content already has a `kind` column that IS mostly-canonical (function_declaration/function_item/function_definition/function -> 'function'; method_declaration/method_definition -> 'method'), node_hash-joinable from node_defs/node_refs/_ast. mache can filter kind via JOIN today. Ship canonical_kind as a proper closed κ vocabulary if wanted for the decade (T3 taint, self-analysis; completes the tail: generic_function/function_signature_item/method_elem don't collapse) — clean but optional for smells.

CALLER/ENCLOSING-DEF linkage (THIS bead — the real blocker): node_refs.node_id = the call-SITE path (unique leaf). fan_out_skew needs to GROUP BY the enclosing caller def; untested_function's test-caller arm needs to know a ref fired from inside a Test* function. mache CANNOT derive this cleanly (only brittle call-site-path prefix surgery). This appears to be your existing `container_node_id` shape — if a `container_node_id` (= nearest enclosing def node_id, matching a node_defs.node_id) lands on node_refs, that fully satisfies this bead. Please align to that column name; PRIORITIZE over canonical_kind for smell parity.

title: Daemon protocol: add a `version` op so consumers can handshake wire-compat on connect
description:
Requested by downstream (mache, session 2026-07-01). The leyline daemon socket has no `version` op today (verified against 0.5.x). Consumers can't verify at runtime that the daemon binary they're talking to is wire-compatible with their compiled schema-client — they rely on a human keeping two pins in lockstep.

Concrete case: mache pins `leyline-schema` (Go client) in go.mod AND `leylineBinaryVersion` as a const, and documents (internal/leyline/socket.go:735-766) that major.minor must match for wire compat while patch floats. mache wants to query the daemon's version on connect and refuse on major.minor mismatch (mache-8kif) but cannot, because no version op exists.

ASK: add a `version` (or `hello`/handshake) op returning at least the daemon's semver + wire/schema version, so any consumer can fail loud on skew instead of silently decoding a mismatched wire. Cheap, unauthenticated (localhost socket metadata).

Unblocks: mache-8kif (runtime handshake). Interim downstream guard already exists (mache-b8af69, build-time parity gate) but that can't catch a daemon swapped at runtime.

NOTE: file scope needs an LLO-side scoping pass (daemon op dispatch + socket protocol definition) — filed as design pending that.

title: Refactor: replace 11-arg run_daemon with DaemonConfig struct
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.1 of decade `daemon-shape-debt`, thread `daemon-config-refactor`.

## Problem

`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs::run_daemon` takes 11 parameters:

```rust
pub async fn run_daemon(
    arena: &Path,
    arena_size_mib: u64,
    control: Option<&Path>,
    mount: Option<&Path>,
    backend: &str,
    nfs_port: u16,
    language: Option<&str>,
    timeout: Option<&str>,
    ext: Arc<dyn DaemonExt>,
    source: Option<&Path>,
    mcp_port: Option<u16>,
    mcp_bind: Option<std::net::IpAddr>,  // I just added this in v0.2.1, now 12
) -> Result<()>
```

It carries `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]`. Every new feature adds another parameter. The v0.2.1 `--mcp-bind` work bumped it from 11 to 12 and required threading through 4 sites. This is a code smell that compounds.

`cmd_daemon` (the open-edition wrapper) takes the same shape. `main.rs` constructs the call. Tests construct it differently. Each addition is a 4-file change.

## Work

1. Define `DaemonConfig` struct in `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs`:
   ```rust
   pub struct DaemonConfig<'a> {
       pub arena: &'a Path,
       pub arena_size_mib: u64,
       pub control: Option<&'a Path>,
       pub mount: Option<&'a Path>,
       pub backend: &'a str,
       pub nfs_port: u16,
       pub language: Option<&'a str>,
       pub timeout: Option<&'a str>,
       pub source: Option<&'a Path>,
       pub mcp_port: Option<u16>,
       pub mcp_bind: Option<std::net::IpAddr>,
       pub ext: Arc<dyn DaemonExt>,
   }
   ```
2. Or — given the lifetime juggling — use owned types (`PathBuf`, `String`) with `Default` impl + builder
3. Refactor `run_daemon(config: DaemonConfig)` and `cmd_daemon` (the open-edition wrapper)
4. Update `main.rs` Cmd::Daemon arm to construct DaemonConfig from clap args
5. Update tests in integration.rs that call run_daemon
6. Update `ley-line` (private edition) — heads-up to the user, since this is a breaking API for ll-private's daemon entry point. May need a coordinating PR over there.

This is a mechanical refactor — NO behavior change. PR description should explicitly say "no functional change; pure shape refactor."

## Acceptance

- `run_daemon(config: DaemonConfig)` and `cmd_daemon(config: DaemonConfig)` — single arg
- `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` removed
- `main.rs` and integration.rs updated
- `task ci` green; `task image:smoke` green (behavior unchanged)
- Cross-repo: `ley-line` (private) updated in a coordinating PR (filed as a follow-up bead in ll-private if the user wants me to)

## Why this is T1.1

Lowest-risk, highest-leverage. Subsequent refactors (T1.2 feature-gate registry, T1.3 lifecycle module decomposition) become easier once the function signature isn't a wall of args.

description:

comments.text:
Shipped at bfbab59.

**API:** new `set_arena_with_root(path, size, generation, root)` in leyline-core. Writes path/size/root as plain stores, then `std::sync::atomic::fence(Release)`, then atomic-Release-store of generation. Existing `set_arena(path, size, gen)` preserves current_root unchanged — 20+ existing callers needed zero changes.

**Wired:** `snapshot_to_arena` step-4 now computes `BLAKE3(db_bytes)` and publishes via `set_arena_with_root`. Σ §3.4's "BLAKE3 locked" claim has its concrete enforcement site.

**Tests (5):**
- `set_arena_with_root_writes_all_four_fields` — basic API
- `set_arena_preserves_current_root` — legacy preservation regression-proof
- `set_arena_with_root_visible_across_controllers` — cross-Controller visibility
- `set_arena_with_root_root_never_stale_under_writer_race` — concurrent writer-monotone invariant
- `snapshot_populates_current_root_with_blake3_of_db_bytes` (integration) — end-to-end pin
- `snapshot_idempotent_root_for_same_db_state` — pure-function-of-bytes
- `snapshot_root_advances_when_db_changes` — negative pin

**Bug found and resolved during testing:** the original concurrent-ordering test asserted `gen=N ⟹ root[0]==N`, which is wrong. Writer can race ahead and write root for N+1 *before* publishing gen=N+1; reader observing gen=N can legally see future root. The actual invariant is *writer-monotone advancement* (root never reverts to a previous gen). The seqlock-strict version of the test caught this; replaced with the correct invariant pin.

**Unblocks:** T2.3 (`bad8f1` reader-side verify), T2.4 (`baee26` deprecate generation). Also T8.5's daemon-side root advance lights up once 5f7100-15 (file-backed live db) ships — until then `:memory:` connections still don't get capnp segments to hash.

Closing.

title: Refactor: extract per-feature daemon initialization into a registry/trait pattern
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.2 of decade `daemon-shape-debt`, thread `daemon-config-refactor`. Depends on `ba8294` (DaemonConfig struct — easier to plumb a registry once the args are a struct).

## Problem

`cmd_daemon.rs::run_daemon` body is full of `#[cfg(feature = "vec")]` and `#[cfg(feature = "mount")]` blocks, each doing its own initialization (resolve embedder → register vec → build queue; or backend → mount setup → spawn fs handlers). Adding a new feature means inserting another `#[cfg]` block at the right point in the lifecycle.

Lines from rust-analyzer's diagnostics on the file:
- `13:1` `mount` cfg block
- `31:1` `vec` cfg block
- `178:5`, `184:5`, `192:5`, `210:13`, `228:9`, `230:9`, `232:9`, `238:5` — more `vec` blocks scattered through
- `263:5` `mount` block
- `1326:9`, `1331:9`, `1344:13`, `1346:13`, `1348:13` — more in the lower half

That's a lot of feature-conditional code interleaved with core lifecycle. Two readability problems compound: which of these are core lifecycle vs feature-gated additions, and which features depend on which other lifecycle phases.

## Work

Pattern: each feature contributes a `DaemonModule` (or similar trait) that hooks into named lifecycle phases. Core lifecycle becomes `for module in registered_modules { module.on_phase(...) }`.

Concrete shape (subject to revision when the work starts):

```rust
trait DaemonModule {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn on_init(&self, ctx: &mut InitContext);  // called before context built
    fn on_post_mount(&self, ctx: &PostMountContext);  // after mount stage
    // etc.
}
```

`#[cfg(feature = "vec")]` then registers a `VecModule`. `#[cfg(feature = "mount")]` registers a `MountModule`. Core `run_daemon` body is feature-gate-free; module registration block is the only `#[cfg]` zone.

This is a bigger refactor than T1.1 (config struct). Take it after the config struct lands, when the context plumbing is cleaner.

## Acceptance

- `run_daemon` body has zero `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` blocks (registration block at the top is the exception)
- New feature is added by writing a `DaemonModule` impl + adding it to the registry — no edits to `run_daemon` itself
- `task ci` green with all feature combinations: default, `--no-default-features`, `--features vec`, `--features mount`, `--features lsp`, `--all-features`
- Existing tests still pass

## Why this is T1.2

The config struct (T1.1) was a shape change. This is a structure change. They compound — config-as-struct makes module-context plumbing pleasant; doing this before T1.1 would mean threading a giant context through a giant function.

comments.text:
## 2026-05-22 — Implementation pass on feat/cache-schema-ae89aa (executed in same branch as ae89aa per thoroughness directive)

### What landed

- **`rs/ll-core/core/src/blob_store.rs`** (~580 lines including tests) — FsBlobStore + MemBlobStore impls of the existing BlobStore trait
- **`rs/ll-core/core/src/lib.rs`** — module declaration + re-exports

### Beyond the bead's stated minimum

The bead specified put/get/contains + git-shaped layout + basic tests. Shipped additionally per the user thoroughness directive:

1. **Atomic write** — temp file in same dir + fsync + rename. POSIX rename atomicity guarantees no torn reads; failure modes documented in module rustdoc.
2. **Verify-on-read enforcement** — `get()` recomputes σ over retrieved bytes; mismatch = hard error naming the path. Honors the BlobStore trait doc's promise + ley-line-open-bad8f1 pattern. Tested with disk-corruption simulation.
3. **MemBlobStore** — companion in-memory impl with same axiom honoring (idempotent put, verify-on-read). Future tests across crates don't need TempDir-shaped fs setup; substrate consumer crates can ship trait-tests using MemBlobStore as the canonical fixture.
4. **`FsBlobStore::open` vs `FsBlobStore::new`** — open() auto-creates the root recursively; new() refuses missing root (for callers asserting external init). Both documented.
5. **`path_for()` public** — diagnostic accessor; useful for "where would this blob land?" tooling without breaking the abstraction.

### Test coverage (17 unit tests)

- **Round-trip:** fs + mem
- **Idempotency (IM axiom):** fs + mem, including a hardened "preserves original bytes under double-put" variant
- **Absence:** fs + mem (get of missing → None; contains → false)
- **Verify-on-read corruption:** fs (filesystem tamper) + mem (inner-map tamper) — both must refuse to vouch for mismatched bytes, error names path/key
- **Layout pin:** asserts the exact git-shape (2-char prefix dir, 62-char remainder file, both hex-only)
- **Prefix collision coexistence:** brute-forces two contents sharing byte[0]; both readable, neither overwritten
- **Edge cases:** empty blob (canonical BLAKE3-of-empty), 1 MiB large blob
- **Persistence:** close store, reopen at same root, contents readable
- **Constructor discipline:** new() refuses missing, open() creates parents recursively
- **`contains()` reflects state** — pre/post put

### Verification

- `cargo test -p leyline-core blob_store` → 17 / 17 pass
- `cargo test -p leyline-core` → 51 / 51 pass (full crate, including the 34 existing tests; nothing regressed)

### Open follow-ups (NOT in this bead's scope)

- GC of unreachable blobs — explicit `gc()` API per substrate.rs:152's (IM) axiom note (`get` may return None after explicit GC). Separate bead when prioritized.
- Concurrent-writer fuzz testing — two processes putting same content simultaneously. The atomic-rename design SHOULD handle it; would want a stress test before claiming so.
- Network-backed BlobStore impl (R2/S3) — needed for me-bundle remote distribution. Different bead, consumes the trait.

Status: ready to close once committed.

title: Decompose cmd_daemon.rs (1300+ LOC) into lifecycle-phase modules
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. T1.3 of decade `daemon-shape-debt`, thread `daemon-config-refactor`. Depends on `badb31` (the module-registry refactor — easier to split a file once features are registry-driven).

## Problem

`rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs` is 1300+ lines. Its module docstring already enumerates the lifecycle in 10 phases:

> 1. Arena setup (create/open arena + controller)
> 2. If `--source`: parse source dir → load .db into arena
> 3. Event router created
> 4. `ext.on_init(emitter)` — extension initializes state
> 5. UDS socket spawned (base ops + extension ops)
> 6. If `--mount`: mount via NFS/FUSE (omit for headless mode)
> 7. `ext.on_post_mount(ctrl_path, router)` — extension spawns background tasks
> 8. If mache on PATH: spawn `mache serve --control <ctrl>` as child
> 9. Wait for shutdown (Ctrl+C or timeout)
> 10. Cleanup (kill mache child, remove socket file)

The docstring already does the decomposition mentally. The code doesn't.

## Work

Split into a `daemon/lifecycle/` module with one file per phase:

```
daemon/lifecycle/
  mod.rs              -- pub fn run(config: DaemonConfig) -> Result<()>
                          orchestrates the phases
  arena_setup.rs      -- phase 1
  source_parse.rs     -- phase 2
  router.rs           -- phase 3
  extension_init.rs   -- phase 4
  socket_spawn.rs     -- phase 5
  mount.rs            -- phase 6 (cfg-feature mount)
  post_mount.rs       -- phase 7
  mache_child.rs      -- phase 8
  shutdown.rs         -- phase 9 + 10
```

Each phase is a free function or small struct with `fn run(state: &mut LifecycleState) -> Result<()>`. `cmd_daemon.rs` becomes the thin orchestrator (~100 LOC).

This is the BIGGEST of the three thread beads. Land after T1.1 + T1.2 reduce the surface area of what each phase needs from the surrounding state.

## Acceptance

- `cmd_daemon.rs` is < 200 LOC
- Each lifecycle phase has its own file with a focused docstring
- `daemon/lifecycle/mod.rs::run` reads top-to-bottom as the lifecycle docstring describes
- `task ci` green; `task image:smoke` green
- All feature combos (default / +vec / +mount / +lsp / --all-features) build clean

## Why this is T1.3 (not T1.1)

Decomposing 1300 LOC ahead of the struct refactor (T1.1) and registry refactor (T1.2) means re-doing it twice. Stack the cheap shape changes first, then split.

title: Research: leyline-hdc — production-path or research-shelf?
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Standalone research bead — no thread, no commit pressure.

## Question

`leyline-hdc` (in `rs/ll-open/hdc/`) is described in README as "Hyperdimensional computing — `HvCell` sheaf-stalks-over-hypervectors (Heyting algebra; bit-level Hamming agreement)." That's a strong, distinctive claim. But it's listed alongside ordinary projection-engine crates with no obvious caller in the daemon hot path.

Need to know: **is HDC pulling weight in production code paths today, or is it research-shelf code that's a workspace member because it's convenient?**

## Audit work

1. `rg "leyline_hdc::" --type rust` — find all call sites
2. Categorize:
   - Daemon hot path (called per-request)
   - Build-time / startup (called once at init)
   - Test-only
   - Demo / example
   - Dead code (no callers — workspace member only because Cargo workspace)
3. Read each call site briefly — what does it do with the HDC types?
4. Read `leyline-hdc/src/` overview — how big is the surface? Is there a "production API" vs "exploratory API" distinction?
5. Compare the README claim ("sheaf-stalks-over-hypervectors with Heyting algebra") to what's actually wired — is the math claim load-bearing or aspirational?

## Possible outcomes

- **Pulling weight**: leave alone, document caller patterns better in `leyline-hdc/README.md`
- **Sometimes used / opt-in**: feature-gate it (`--features hdc`), document as opt-in, set off-by-default
- **Research-shelf**: move to a separate `experiments/` crate or out of the workspace entirely; README "Tier 2" table should reflect status accurately
- **Mixed**: split into a thin "always-on" core + an "experimental" extended module

## Acceptance

- A bead comment summarizing the audit findings
- A recommendation (one of the four above) with one-paragraph rationale
- If recommendation is "feature-gate" or "split", a follow-up bead filed for the actual work

## Why no thread

Standalone — answer informs whether more work is needed, but the audit itself is self-contained. If it produces follow-up beads, those can form a thread later.

title: Shell exit-status dataflow analysis: shellcheck misses 3 of our 4 real defects, and the substrate already exists
description:
Filed 2026-07-27 after a day in which FOUR shell defects shipped into gates whose
entire purpose is catching silent failure. Three of the four are invisible to
shellcheck (measured, not assumed).

## The measured gap

Reproduced each defect faithfully and ran shellcheck at default and `-o all`:

  backticks inside a double-quoted argument -> command substitution      CAUGHT
    (mangled a cross-repo bead comment: four identifiers silently vanished)
  `cmd | tail` then `$?` -> tail's status, not cmd's                     MISSED
    (produced a false "CI green" on a run that had failed)
  `set -e` + `grep` returning 1 inside a captured while-subshell         MISSED
    (killed the loop on the first non-matching task; result silently empty,
     every downstream check passed vacuously)
  `awk -v` with a multi-line value -> split() matches nothing            MISSED
    (vacuous pass; the gate reported success having compared nothing)

One of four. Our own tools/*.sh are already shellcheck-clean at warning level
(1 finding, a false positive on `CDPATH= cd`), so the marginal value of adding
shellcheck alone is small — worth doing, not sufficient.

## Why the misses are tractable, not fundamental

The two most costly misses are EXIT-STATUS DATAFLOW, not syntax:

- a pipeline's status is its last command's, so `$?` after `cmd | tail` cannot
  observe `cmd`
- under `set -e`, any command whose status is not consumed by a condition can
  terminate the enclosing shell — including a subshell whose stdout is being
  captured, which silently yields an empty string rather than an error

Both are decidable on the CFG. shellcheck does not model status propagation, so
it shrugs. This is a solved shape in other domains — it is ordinary dataflow
analysis over a lattice (status ∈ {0, nonzero, unknown}) with `set -e`,
pipelines, `||`/`&&`, and `if` as the transfer functions. The grammar is
decidable and the analysis is a fixed computation, not a learned one: expressible
as a fixed-weight network / composition of finite automata if that framing is
useful, but nothing here needs training.

## Why this belongs in LLO specifically

The substrate already exists:

- `leyline-ts` ships tree-sitter-bash in its DEFAULT features, and LLO already
  projects shell structurally today — measured: a 4-line script yields
  node_defs `build`/`deploy` with canonical_kind='function' and node_refs
  `build cargo deploy scp`. Consumers (mache) can read shell now, with no schema
  change.
- `cfg.rs` already builds a CFG over the kappa vocabulary (T1.b3,
  docs/decades/analysis-substrate.md).
- `rs/ll-open/lsp/src/languages.rs:113` already maps `shellscript` -> sh, bash.

So the missing piece is a status lattice over the existing shell CFG — not a new
language, parser, or projection.

## The fourth defect is a different problem, deliberately out of scope

`awk -v` with a multi-line value requires reasoning about awk's split() semantics
— i.e. analysing a FOREIGN language embedded in a string literal. LLO has
`injections.rs` for that class, which makes it adjacent rather than impossible,
but it should not be bundled: it is a second analysis with a second grammar.

## What NOT to conclude

This does not replace positive controls. Two of the three misses were caught
today by asserting the mechanism fired (`the resolve must name --features cdc`,
`the resolve must contain ll-open/ts/rust`) — three lines each, no analysis
required. Static analysis raises the floor; it does not remove the obligation to
assert that a check checked something. Ship the cheap controls regardless of
whether this bead is ever taken.

## Suggested first slice, if taken

Status lattice over the existing bash CFG, targeting exactly two rules:
  1. `$?` / `set -e` observation of a pipeline's non-final command
  2. a `set -e`-abortable command inside a command-substitution subshell
Validate against the four fixtures above: rules 1 and 2 must fire on defects 2
and 3, and must NOT fire on tools/*.sh (which are clean today).
acceptance_criteria: A status-lattice analysis over the existing bash CFG fires on the two exit-status fixtures (pipeline status masked by $?; set -e abort inside a captured subshell) and does NOT fire on the current tools/*.sh, which are shellcheck-clean today. Scope excludes embedded-language (awk/sed) analysis.

title: Research: vec sidecar trajectory — first-class projection or opt-in feature?
description:
Filed 2026-05-10. Standalone research bead.

## Question

The `vec` cargo feature gates a sidecar vector index, embedder, and an enrichment pass (`crate::daemon::embed::EmbeddingPass`). Today it's:
- Off by default in `leyline-cli` (the leyline-cli crate's `[features]` declares `default = ["lsp"]`, no `vec`)
- Plumbed extensively in `cmd_daemon.rs` (per the diagnostics output: lines 31, 178, 184, 192, 210, 228, 230, 232, 238 — at least 9 cfg-gate sites)
- Not exposed in the production image (the v0.2.1 distroless build is `--features lsp` default, no vec)

That suggests vec is *experimental* — wired but not relied on. Need a clear answer for the next design phase:

- Stays opt-in feature gate forever (current shape)?
- Becomes first-class — embedding is a projection alongside SQL tables, always-on (or default-on)?
- Gets retired — code lives in a branch / experiments folder, removed from mainline?

## Inputs to gather

1. Which crates / call sites depend on `vec` being available? Is it self-contained or does it leak into supposedly-feature-free code?
2. What's the embedder model? (`ZeroEmbedder` default in `cmd_daemon.rs:177-180` suggests no real model is wired today — placeholder.) What was the original intent?
3. Does the substrate (capnp schemas) reserve room for embedding bytes? (Look at `binding.capnp`, `common.capnp` — do any structs have an embedding field, even feature-gated?)
4. What would "first-class embedding" mean for Σ root advance? Are embeddings part of the canonical bytes that get BLAKE3'd, or sidecar?
5. Performance: is the embedding pass cheap enough to be always-on? Or does it gate on having a GPU / model loaded?

## Possible outcomes

- **Keep opt-in**: document trajectory clearly in `cmd_daemon.rs` module doc + `vec` feature description in Cargo.toml. No production change.
- **Promote to default**: write ADR for "embedding as projection," wire ZeroEmbedder as the production default, leave real embedder behind a runtime config (so production deploys ship empty embeddings until a model is loaded).
- **Retire**: delete the feature gate, move code to a `crumb-experiments/` branch or out-of-tree crate, leave behind a one-line comment pointing at the moved code.
- **Split**: separate "embedding storage" (substrate-level) from "embedding computation" (engine-level). Storage stays in substrate; computation stays opt-in.

## Acceptance

- A bead comment with the audit + recommendation
- If a clear direction emerges, a follow-up bead (or thread) filed for the work

## Why no thread / no commit pressure

This is a strategy question, not a defect. Filing it captures the question so it doesn't drift; doesn't demand resolution this cycle.

title: [ADR-0013/Step 1 followup] _lsp_refs.referrer_node_id is always NULL — schema shipped, resolution didn't
description:
Sister/followup to ley-line-453f7e (ADR-0013 Step 1). The schema migration shipped at 12330fc added `referrer_node_id` and `ref_token` columns to `_lsp_refs`, plus `def_token` to `_lsp_defs`. Verified via `.schema _lsp_refs`. But `referrer_node_id` is **NULL on every row** — the column exists, the data flow does not.

## Reproduction

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/lsp-fixture/pkg
cat > /tmp/lsp-fixture/go.mod <<EOF
module fixture
go 1.21
EOF
cat > /tmp/lsp-fixture/pkg/auth.go <<EOF
package pkg

type Authenticator interface {
	Validate(token string) bool
}
type TokenAuth struct{}
func (t *TokenAuth) Validate(token string) bool { return token != "" }
func UseAuth(a Authenticator, token string) bool { return a.Validate(token) }
EOF

leyline parse /tmp/lsp-fixture -o /tmp/lsp-fixture.db --lang go
leyline lsp --server gopls --input /tmp/lsp-fixture/pkg/auth.go \
            --output /tmp/lsp-out.db --merge-db /tmp/lsp-fixture.db

sqlite3 /tmp/lsp-out.db "
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
         SUM(CASE WHEN referrer_node_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_ref,
         SUM(CASE WHEN referrer_node_id = '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS empty_ref,
         SUM(CASE WHEN referrer_node_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_node_id != '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS populated
  FROM _lsp_refs;"
# 9|9|0|0   ← 100% NULL
```

`ref_token` IS populated (`Validate`, `Authenticator`, `TokenAuth`, etc.). `def_token` IS populated. Only `referrer_node_id` is empty.

## Why it matters (consumer side)

ADR-0013's binding-fidelity design relies on the consumer query

```sql
WHERE r.target_node_id = d.node_id
   OR (r.target_node_id IS NULL AND r.token = d.token)
```

…where `target_node_id` comes from `_lsp_refs.node_id` (the def the ref points at) and the **alive-check edge in `dead_code` is keyed on `(referrer_node_id, target_node_id)`**. Mache's canonical view explicitly filters `WHERE referrer_node_id IS NOT NULL AND ref_token != ''` (cmd/serve_find_smells.go:ensureCanonicalViews) so empty-referrer rows don't pollute mention-fidelity joins.

Result today: on a `leyline lsp`-enriched .db, `v_refs` surfaces **zero binding rows** because every `_lsp_refs` row is filtered out. The dead_code rule's binding arm never fires; the textual mention path runs alone; the skip-list compensation is still load-bearing. ADR-0013's headline experiment (Falsifiability A skip-list ablation, mache-3509aa) cannot deliver its empirical result until referrer_node_id is populated.

## What "populated" should mean

For each `_lsp_refs` row, the producer needs to map the source location `(ref_uri, ref_start_line, ref_start_col)` back to a mache node_id of the **enclosing construct** (the function/method body that contains the reference site). The producer already has the AST tree loaded (it called `descendant_for_byte_range` to extract `ref_token`); the same descendant walk + ancestor traversal up to the nearest `function_declaration` / `method_declaration` / `var`-with-initializer would yield the referrer node_id.

In our reproduction:

title: schema-bridge: $doc/$optional/$default annotation vocabulary + $op-driven MCP tool-definitions output mode (unblocks rosary-08a278)
description:
The capnpc-schema-bridge-jsonschema emitter (ley-line-open-6585aa, PR #228) named rosary's MCP tool registry (rosary-08a278) as its first consumer, but as shipped it CANNOT reproduce rosary's live MCP surface (src/serve/tools.rs, 41 tools, 840 lines) without regression. Four load-bearing gaps, measured against tools.rs:

1. DESCRIPTIONS DROPPED — 206 property-level + 41 tool-level descriptions, all load-bearing MCP UX (e.g. bead_create.files: "CRITICAL: these scope parallel dispatch — has_file_overlap() blocks concurrent beads…"). The emitter's own header documents it emits none: "capnp's CodeGeneratorRequest carries no doc comments (capnp discards comments at parse) … descriptions arrive later via an annotation vocabulary, not invented here." WORSE: enum values are encoded IN descriptions (0 JSON `enum` arrays in tools.rs — issue_type/work_mode list valid values as prose), so descriptions are doubly load-bearing.

2. OPTIONALITY INVERTED — emitter marks ALL fields required + additionalProperties:false (capnp has no optional fields). rosary curates required SUBSETS: bead_create has 14 properties, only `title` required; many tools are `"required":[]` (all optional). Generating makes every argument mandatory — a breaking change to every tool contract.

3. DEFAULTS DROPPED — 21 `"default"` values in tools.rs; emitter emits no JSON `default`.

4. WRONG OUTPUT SHAPE — emitter produces a `$defs` bag of TYPE schemas (one entry per struct). rosary's tool_definitions() returns the MCP tools/list ARRAY of {name, description, inputSchema} objects. The `$op`/OpInfo annotation in _traits.capnp exists to declare "this struct is an operation (input/output/errors)" but the jsonschema emitter consumes NO annotations yet — it is a pure type→schema shape mapper.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD:
- Add to rs/ll-core/schema-spec/_traits.capnp: a `$doc(text)` field+struct annotation (→ JSON Schema `description`; struct-level → the tool description), an `$optional` field annotation (→ curated `required` subset instead of all-required), and optionally `$default(text)` + explicit enum support. Follow the file's naming + append-only ordinal rules (range @0xd3b652fd6a4debe7..ff).
- Teach outputs/json_schema.rs to lower these annotations, and add an `$op`-driven output mode that emits the MCP tools/list array ({name, description, inputSchema} per `$op` struct) rather than only the `$defs` bag.
- Keep the existing $defs/type-schema mode (other consumers) working; the tool-definitions mode is additive.

CONSUMER CONTRACT (the acceptance bar): a schema-bridge tool-definitions run over rosary's registry capnp must be byte-reproducible into rosary's committed tool_definitions() JSON — i.e. rosary-08a278's drift gate (generated == committed live tools.rs surface) must be able to pass. Descriptions, curated required-sets, defaults, and the tools/list shape must all round-trip. Coordinate the exact JSON shape with rosary-08a278.

title: Decade dataflow-substrate: staging-layer for reflow-accurate offsets (raised by T1.b3 F1 authoring)
description:
Decade-level open question surfaced while writing the F1_cfg_reflow_stable gate in T1.b3 (`ley-line-open-46f7d1`).

## The gap

`_cfg.node_hash` IS reflow-invariant (ADR-0027 merkle-AST content address; whitespace-invariant by construction). But `_cfg.entry_offset` / `_cfg.exit_offset` are body-*source*-relative — they measure position in the raw text of the body, which includes interior whitespace. Reflow shifts them.

The F1 gate had to be narrowed from "byte-identical row content" to "byte-identical row COUNT + node_hash + block_kinds", with offsets deliberately excluded from the invariant. That works for T3's differential-dataflow `arrange` (which keys on node_hash + block_id) but it means consumers reading offsets after dedup get **first-writer's source-relative positions**, which are only valid for that specific parse of that specific file.

## The right fix: staging layer

Offsets should be positions INTO A CANONICAL STAGED FORM of the body, not into raw source. Two candidates, both already in the substrate:

1. **Pre-serialized capnp `AstNodeList` blob** (ADR-0026 Phase 1 today, per-file). Phase 2 (`ley-line-open-ddfc1c`) explicitly names per-semantic-unit refinement — that's this staging layer. `_ast_pointer.offset_in_blob` is already exactly this shape for AST nodes.
2. **The linearized fold buffer** the merkle hash consumes (κ kind + tokens + child hashes) — content-addressed by construction, portable.

If `_cfg.entry_offset` / `_cfg.exit_offset` were offsets into a per-body staged blob (option 1) instead of body-source-relative, reflow would be fully byte-identical — offsets included — AND sub-file parsing fits by direct extension (staging IS the sub-file unit).

## Impact on already-shipped work

- T1.b2's schema doesn't need to change *shape* — `entry_offset INTEGER, exit_offset INTEGER` still works. Only the *semantics* flip. No migration needed; rows already merged in v0.7.x carry source-relative offsets and can be respected as "legacy source-relative" while new rows carry blob-relative.
- T1.b3's cfg.rs and F1 gate DON'T change — they're offset-agnostic under the narrowed invariant.
- T1.b4 (cyclomatic complexity, `ley-line-open-471195`) is offset-agnostic — safe to land unchanged.
- T2 (dfg-ssa) is offset-agnostic — safe to land unchanged.

## When to decide

**Before T3.b3 (Bootstrap-mode taint, `ley-line-open-485113`).** T3's differential-dataflow arrangement compounds on content-addressed keys; if downstream consumers start depending on the offset semantics before we lock them, migration cost climbs.

## Scope

1. Add a decade-doc section naming the staging layer explicitly (docs/decades/analysis-substrate.md §2 or §5).
2. Decide: canonical staged form = ADR-0026 pointer blob (per-body variant) OR fold buffer OR something else. Coordinate with `ley-line-open-ddfc1c` (ADR-0026 Phase 2) so we don't fork the pointer-store discipline.
3. Migrate cfg.rs to emit blob-relative offsets. Rewrite F1 to assert byte-identical row CONTENT (including offsets) under reflow.
4. Companion change in T2's `_dfg` and T3's `_taint` when they land.

## Close condition

`cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib --test f1_cfg_reflow_stable` passes with STRENGTHENED invariant (row bytes byte-identical, offsets included) under reflow. Task ci green.

## Priority

P2. Non-blocking for T1.b4 / T2 / T3.b1-b2, but blocking for T3.b3 shape decision.

title: release.yml: publish libleyline_fs-<os>-<arch>.a FFI staticlibs as release assets (unblocks mache release off public LLO)
description:
## Why

mache's `release.yml` links its binaries against the ley-line FFI staticlib (`libleyline_fs-<os>-<arch>.a`). Today it fetches that from the **private** `agentic-research/ley-line` repo via an octo-sts OIDC exchange (`identity: mache-release`). That exchange is failing (see mache bead `mache-55d3e1`) and is blocking the mache v0.9.0 binary publish.

LLO already *builds* the staticlib — `rs/ll-open/fs/Cargo.toml` is `crate-type = ["cdylib","staticlib","rlib"]` (crate `leyline-fs` -> `libleyline_fs.a`), and `cargo build --release` (already run in the release job) produces it. LLO just never uploads it. Publishing it from **public** LLO lets mache fetch with a plain `GITHUB_TOKEN` and drop octo-sts + the private-repo dependency entirely. (mache release.yml's own header says the private dep exists only "until ley-line-open ships the FFI" artifacts.)

## What

In LLO's `.github/workflows/release.yml`, in the per-asset build matrix job (which already does `cargo build --release` and `gh release upload "$TAG" "$ASSET_NAME" --clobber` for the `leyline` daemon binary), add a stage+upload for the staticlib:

    - name: Stage FFI staticlib
      run: cp "rs/target/$BUILD_TARGET/release/libleyline_fs.a" "libleyline_fs-${OS}-${ARCH}.a"
    - name: Upload FFI staticlib
      run: gh release upload "$TAG" "libleyline_fs-${OS}-${ARCH}.a" --clobber

Map the existing matrix os/arch to the names mache expects:
- libleyline_fs-darwin-arm64.a
- libleyline_fs-linux-amd64.a
- libleyline_fs-linux-arm64.a

(mache's release matrix has no darwin-amd64, so that one is optional.)

Then cut an LLO release (e.g. v0.4.6) so the assets exist for mache to fetch.

## Consumer change (separate mache PR, blocked on this)
mache `release.yml`: replace the octo-sts step + `gh release download --repo agentic-research/ley-line` with `gh release download --repo agentic-research/ley-line-open ...`. Tracked under mache-55d3e1.

## Acceptance
- An LLO release (tag) carries libleyline_fs-{darwin-arm64,linux-amd64,linux-arm64}.a assets alongside the existing leyline-<os>-<arch> daemon binaries.
- mache's release.yml, repointed at public LLO, builds + publishes v0.9.0 binaries with no octo-sts and no private-repo access.

title: L7 — add provenance + certainty fields to bundle responses (extends ADR-0016 §2)
description:
From `docs/problems/agent-first-semantic-surface.md` (L7). User-named missing piece from ADR-0016 — it's the field that makes the surface genuinely "agent-first" beyond what ADR-0016 currently commits to.

⚠️ **Depends on L1** (`inspect_symbol`) — depends_on edge to be linked once L1's bead ID is known.

## Problem

ADR-0016 §2's bundle shape does not include provenance (which analyzer answered) or certainty (full / partial / heuristic / tree-sitter-only). Agents can't distinguish "ra_ap_ide returned this at full fidelity" from "tree-sitter token match, low confidence." Extend the response schema with two new fields applied uniformly across `inspect_symbol`, `inspect_neighborhood`, `lsp_hover`, `lsp_defs`, `lsp_refs`. Backend annotates each sub-result with its provenance; certainty is the analyzer's self-reported confidence.

## Acceptance

- `Provenance` enum: `{ RustAnalyzer, Gopls, Pyright, Tsserver, Clangd, JDTLS, ZLS, TreeSitter, HDC, Combined }`
- `Certainty` enum: `{ Full, Partial, Heuristic, Cached }`
- Every bundle response carries `provenance` + `certainty` at the top level AND inside each sub-array (e.g. `callers[].provenance`)
- Schema-validation test gates the field's presence in CI; missing field on any path = test fail
- Round-trip fixture: gopls-backed LSP path → `provenance == Gopls`, `certainty == Full`
- Tree-sitter-only fallback path: `provenance == TreeSitter`, `certainty == Heuristic`

## Inputs

- `docs/adr/0016-ai-native-query-surface.md` §2 (current bundle shape)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs` (all bundle-producing paths)
- `rs/ll-open/lsp/src/languages.rs` (server-id → Provenance mapping)
- L1's bead (bundle shape baseline)
- `docs/problems/agent-first-semantic-surface.md` L7

## Output shape

PR; ~300 LOC (enum + threading + schema-validation test).

## Scope

Field additions only. Per-language ranking model (which provenance "wins" when two analyzers answer) is a future bead.

## Failure mode

Schema-validation test fails (field missing on any path).

Shipping in this PR. `inspect_symbol` bundle now carries `provenance` + `certainty` at the top level AND inside every sub-array row.

## Fields

- Top-level `provenance: "composed"` (bundle mixes tree-sitter rows + optional LSP hover); `certainty: "full" | "partial"` where "partial" signals hover_typed is null (LSP enrichment hasn't reached this symbol).
- `definitions[]` rows: `provenance: "tree-sitter"`, `certainty: "full"` (structural truth from node_defs ⋈ _ast).
- `references[]`, `callers[]`, `callees[]` rows: same — tree-sitter / full.
- `hover_typed` object (when non-null): injected `provenance: "lsp"`, `certainty: "full"`.

## Why v1 is inspect_symbol only

L7's original scope listed lsp_hover / lsp_defs / lsp_refs too. Those handlers go through capnp + capnp_json (typed response shape), so adding new fields requires schema bumps in the public capnp definitions. That's a separate scoping decision; inspect_symbol is JSON-only end-to-end and lets the v1 contract ship without touching the capnp surface.

## Schema gate (catches the silent-degradation regression)

`inspect_symbol_carries_provenance_and_certainty_everywhere` walks every sub-array of a fully-populated response and asserts both fields are present. Catches the regression case where a new sub-field is added without provenance/certainty — exactly the case L7 exists to prevent.

## Tests

- 4 inspect_symbol tests pass (including the new schema gate)
- 3 at_position tests still pass (L7 doesn't affect L2)
- All drift tests pass
- `task ci` clean

title: Partition invariants are tested per-domain by hand, so a universal-sounding test covered 1 domain of 3 and let the b67a73 regression through
description:
Found 2026-07-28 answering vigil's question on `ley-line-open-afa8be`:
"how did this regress undetected?"

## The answer is worse than "no upstream test existed"

A test DID exist, and predates the regression:

    $ git show ad272d3^:rs/ll-core/core/src/partition.rs | grep -n "fn framing_is_committed"
    247:    fn framing_is_committed_to_the_address() {

and its body is:

    fn framing_is_committed_to_the_address() {
        let s = spec(Domain::ByteStream);     // <-- one domain, of three
        ...
    }

The NAME asserts a universal property. The BODY covers `ByteStream` only. So
`ad272d3` could erase framing for `ChunkSet`/`RowSet` and every upstream test
stayed green; the only detector was a test in cloister's tree, which fired only
because they happened to bump their pin.

## The general defect

This is the second instance today of a check that reads broad and is narrow.
The first: schema-bridge's goldens assert
`emitted.contains("subject: z.string()")`, which passes for
`z.string().default("")` and any other appended suffix — which is why they could
not catch `ley-line-open-8c00c6`.

Same shape, different mechanism: the assertion is true but far weaker than its
name implies, so a reader (and a future author) trusts coverage that is not
there.

## Fix

Not "add a set-domain framing test" — `ley-line-open-b67a73` already did that.
The structural fix is that nothing FORCES an invariant to be checked across all
domains.

Add a domain-parametrized harness iterating `[ByteStream, ChunkSet, RowSet]`
and asserting the invariants that must hold for every domain:

- framing is committed
- scheme is committed
- params are committed
- canon_version is committed
- domain separation from plain BLAKE3
- determinism

Domain-SPECIFIC invariants stay as individual tests and must say so in the name
(`byte_stream_...`, `set_domains_...`), so an unqualified name means "all
domains" and is enforced to mean it.

Then adding a `Domain` variant fails the harness until its behaviour is
declared, and adding an invariant covers every domain by construction.

## Acceptance criteria

Adding a fourth `Domain` variant, or reverting `ad272d3`'s framing erasure for
EITHER set domain, fails the parametrized harness. Proven by doing both, not by
reading the code. And the existing per-domain tests still pass unchanged, so
the harness is additive rather than a rewrite.

Reference `ley-line-open-2607d2` — a check must assert the mechanism fired; a
test named for a universal property must exercise it universally.

title: daemon --cdc hardcodes the nodes target; no way to select source-blobs (unlike the standalone `cdc enable --target` CLI)
description:
Found 2026-08-05 while re-validating ley-line-open-baa57f against v0.15.1 for mache (mache-abf404).

## The gap

`leyline cdc enable --target nodes|source-blobs` (standalone CLI, `cmd_cdc.rs`) correctly exposes both targets — `baa57f` shipped this and it works: re-measured on mache's own 2.24 GB projection, `--target source-blobs` costs +0.35% vs `--target nodes`'s +21% regression.

But `leyline daemon --cdc` (the flag consumers like mache actually use for live-managed daemons) does NOT expose target selection at all:

```
rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs:1343-1360
pub fn activate_cdc_and_snapshot(conn, ctrl_path, enabled: bool) -> ... {
    let report = if enabled {
        Some(leyline_fs::activation::activate_chunked_content(
            conn,
            leyline_fs::activation::ActivationOptions::default(),
        )...)
    } ...
}
```

`activate_chunked_content` is the `nodes`-only activation function (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/activation.rs:76`) — it has no target parameter. The `source_blobs` path lives in a separate function, `activate_chunked_source_blobs` (`rs/ll-open/fs/src/activation.rs:435`), which `cmd_daemon.rs` never calls.

`leyline daemon --help` confirms: `--cdc` is a bare boolean, no `--target` flag exists at the daemon subcommand level.

## Impact

Any consumer (mache, or anyone else spawning `leyline daemon --cdc`) gets the measured-regressive `nodes` target with no way to opt into the cost-neutral `source_blobs` target that `baa57f` was built to provide. The daemon path and the standalone-activation path have drifted: one target selector exists, but only reachable from the CLI surface nobody uses for a live-managed daemon.

## Ask

Either:
(a) Add `--cdc-target <nodes|source-blobs>` (or reuse the same `Target` enum) to `leyline daemon`, threading it into `activate_cdc_and_snapshot` → `ActivationOptions` (which will need a target field — it currently only has `batch_size`), or
(b) Change the daemon's default CDC activation to call `activate_chunked_source_blobs` instead of `activate_chunked_content`, if source_blobs is meant to be the generally-recommended target now that it exists.

## Test plan

A daemon started with `--cdc --cdc-target source-blobs` (or whatever flag lands) populates `source_blobs`/`blob_manifest`, not `nodes`/`content_manifest`. `cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib` covers the new flag parsing + activation dispatch.

title: Publish LLO libraries to crates.io via Trusted Publishing — git-dep pinning makes multi-version resolution of leyline-core structurally unavoidable
description:
Filed 2026-07-28. Raised by vigil reviewing the generator-publishing plan:
publishing BINARIES fixes the build-tool path and does nothing for libraries.
Correct, and under-weighted — they are different problems.

## The problem is structural, not hygiene

cloister SHA-pins five LLO crates, which had drifted to five distinct revs:

    leyline-sign          a6eba83a   0.7.6
    leyline-cas-ffi       593ee610   0.4.5
    leyline-fs            f62a5430   0.8.0
    leyline-schema-bridge e8a501ba   0.7.9

with **`leyline-core` resolving three times simultaneously** (0.4.5 / 0.8.0 /
0.10.4) — `cas` pinned it directly while `cas-ffi` and `fs` each dragged their
own. `cargo update -p leyline-core` refuses as ambiguous, which is that
condition made visible.

**Cargo cannot unify git dependencies at different revs.** Each pin drags its
own copy of the shared type substrate. So this is not carelessness downstream —
it is the only thing git-dep pinning can do. Publishing to crates.io makes the
resolver unify compatible semver automatically, which makes the multi-version
state **unrepresentable** rather than merely discouraged. Same move as
"generate the guarantee rather than assert it".

## Mechanism: Trusted Publishing, no tokens in CI

crates.io Trusted Publishing (RFC 3691) grants a short-lived (~15 min) token
over OIDC, scoped to org/repo/workflow. **Nothing is stored in CI.** Since
2026-01 a crate can additionally ENFORCE trusted publishing, disabling
token-based publish entirely — worth turning on.

Scope to the five crates consumers actually pin, `leyline-core` first since the
others depend on it.

## Two things that need a human, and cannot be automated

1. **A crates.io account** (GitHub OAuth) to own the names and configure the
   trusted publisher per crate.
2. **Bootstrap.** Trusted Publishing attaches to an EXISTING crate, so the
   first publish of each name needs a local `cargo publish` or a short-lived
   token. Five crates, one time; OIDC covers everything after.

## The decision worth making deliberately

crates.io publishes are **permanent** — yank hides a version from resolution
but never deletes it. That cuts against this repo's stated "remove, don't
deprecate" policy, which assumes a bad artifact can be withdrawn. A bad
`0.11.5` would be public forever.

Consequence: binaries can publish on every tag freely; libraries should
probably publish on a deliberate subset. That asymmetry should be decided and
written down, not discovered.

## Acceptance criteria

A `v*` tag publishes the five crates via OIDC with no stored secret; a gate
asserts the published versions match the set `verify_release_version.sh`
already enforces (otherwise "released but not deliverable" reappears in a new
place); and cloister can replace all five git pins with semver ranges and get
ONE `leyline-core`. Proven by cloister resolving a single core version, not by
the publish job exiting 0.

Related: `ley-line-open-e44960` (binaries — the tools half of the same gap),
`cloister-9170d0` (stale-generator hazard, deletable at the root once the
binaries publish).

title: Mutation gates generate zero mutants for SQL logic — the gated files' decisions are invisible to the engine
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-27, not inferred.

cargo-mutants mutates Rust expressions. It cannot alter the semantics of a SQL string literal — it can blank the string, but it cannot generate "what if this predicate also considered X", because that is a different program rather than a mutation. Where this codebase pushes decisions into query text, the gate goes blind.

## The numbers

`chunked.rs` (the only SQL-heavy production file under a mutation gate):
- production region lines 1..1009
- 41 mutants generated
- 49 production lines bear SQL
- **0 mutants land on any SQL line**

Mutants cluster on the Rust scaffolding around the queries (row closures, offset arithmetic, error mapping). The load-bearing predicates — the freshness-witness join at chunked.rs:818-828, the span-overlap range select, the reachability NOT EXISTS — have no mutants at all.

Confirmed empirically on gc.rs: it had 8 mutants while containing an unbounded-growth bug (ley-line-open-b5e56f), and 17 after the fix moved a decision out of a SQL string into Rust. The +9 is exactly the logic that became visible to the engine. A green gate said nothing about the bug before or after; the RED-first invariant tests are what caught it.

## Scope: 14 files with >= 15 SQL lines, 1 gated

Production files with substantial SQL and NO mutation gate:
- ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/ops.rs (32) — contains the symbol-resolution join (`JOIN node_defs d ON r.token = d.token`), the single most semantically load-bearing query in the system
- ll-open/fs/src/graph.rs (28) — the write path whose invalidation discipline 0330c7 was about
- ll-open/lsp/src/project.rs (25)
- ll-open/fs/src/staging.rs (21)
- ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_parse.rs (15)
- ll-open/ts/src/schema.rs (75) — mostly DDL constants, lower risk

This is not an argument against the design. ADR-0026 and chunked.rs deliberately push work into SQL ("a range read becomes a SQL WHERE clause rather than a full scan") and that is correct for the read path. The consequence is that mutation coverage measures progressively less as more logic moves into the engine.

## The fix is NOT SQL mutation tooling

SQL mutation testing is a real research line (Tuya et al., mutation operators for queries), but: (a) there is no wired-up Rust tooling, and (b) it would not have caught b5e56f anyway. Its operators mutate an EXISTING query — flip NOT EXISTS, alter a join, change a comparison — and every one of those would be caught by the tests already present. The b5e56f bug was a missing second statement, which is not a mutation of anything.

## The fix that works, and is already proven here

Differential and invariant tests, which the repo already does in exactly the right shape in two places:
- `fuzz_chunked_reads_match_naive_slicing` (chunked.rs:1583) — tests the SQL's BEHAVIOR against an independently computed oracle rather than mutating the SQL
- the EXPLAIN plan pin (chunked.rs:1682) — pins the query plan so a silent index regression fails loudly

Adopt that as the standard for SQL-bearing decisions, and state in the gate docs what mutants do and do not cover. The concrete work: identify each load-bearing predicate in the files above, and give it either a differential oracle or a universally-quantified invariant test.

## Close condition

cargo test -p leyline-fs --no-default-features --features cdc,splice,validate, plus the hand-corruption check in acceptance_criteria.

title: Remove wall-clock sleeps from tests — 25 remaining across 10 files; one already flaked CI
description:
A `thread::sleep`-based stop condition in a test is a race against the scheduler. Under load the machine loses, and the test fails with nothing actually broken — which then blocks unrelated PRs and trains people to ignore or bypass the gate.

## The one already fixed (the pattern to copy)

`rs/ll-core/core/src/blob_store.rs::fs_concurrent_put_get_interleaved` flaked CI on the Apache-2.0 licensing PR, which touched ZERO code. Writer/reader threads looped `while !stop.load(..)` while the main thread slept 50ms then set `stop`. On a loaded machine a thread may not be scheduled inside that window at all: it observes `stop` already true, does zero iterations, and fails `"reader loops produced 0 reads"`.

Fixed by deleting the sleep and the AtomicBool entirely — fixed iteration counts instead, so the test does identical work on an idle laptop and a saturated runner. The assertions got STRONGER as a side effect: `total_reads > 0` became `assert_eq!(total_reads, THREADS * READS_PER_THREAD)`, which also catches a thread bailing early. Tuned to 40 writes / 200 reads per thread after measuring — the naive 200/500 was deterministic but cost 3.2s of fsync-bound work for no extra signal; current runtime is ~0.7s.

The general principle: a timing-based stop condition CANNOT express "the loops weren't no-ops". A count can, and that is what these tests actually mean.

## What is left

25 occurrences across 10 files:

- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/version_handshake_blackbox_test.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/event_push_blackbox_test.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/integration.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/substrate/f1_crash_mid_write.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/benches/wal_concurrent_readers.rs
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/benches/wal_snapshot_experiment.rs
- rs/ll-open/sign/tests/host_adversarial.rs
- rs/ll-open/sign/tests/host_integration.rs
- rs/ll-open/sign/src/host/keystore.rs
- rs/ll-core/core/src/control.rs

These are NOT all the same fix. At least two distinct shapes:

1. **Bounded-loop sleeps** (like the one fixed) — replace with fixed iteration counts. Mechanical.
2. **Waiting for a process/daemon to become ready** (the blackbox and daemon tests) — these need a real readiness predicate, i.e. poll-until-condition with a generous ceiling that only fails on genuine hang, not a fixed sleep. Deleting the sleep without adding the predicate makes them worse, not better. Do NOT bulk-replace.

Benches are lower priority than tests — they do not gate CI.

## Related

The `f2_concurrent_writers_throughput` fix (already landed) is the sibling case: a wall-clock THROUGHPUT ratio rather than a sleep. It was gated behind `LLO_PERF_GATES` and moved to `task test:perf`, following `cold_parse_perf_regression`'s existing convention. Same root cause — a wall-clock assertion inside the every-push gate.

A `sleep_in_tests` smell rule is being added alongside this bead to hold the line at the current count so no NEW sleeps land while these are burnt down.

comments.text:
Shipping in this PR. `inspect_neighborhood(symbol_id, depth, max_neighbors_per_hop)` returns focal symbol + BFS neighborhood in one round-trip.

## Shape

```
inspect_neighborhood(symbol_id, depth=1, max_neighbors_per_hop=20) -> {
  ok, symbol_id, depth,
  focal: { symbol_id, kind, definitions: [...], provenance, certainty },
  neighbors: [
    { symbol_id, kind, hop, definitions: [...], provenance, certainty },
    ...
  ],
  provenance, certainty
}
```

Neighbors are reachable via callers + callees relation. BFS frontier visits each symbol at the FIRST hop reached (deduped via `visited` HashSet).

## v1 simplifications (documented inline)

- **No `max_bytes` byte-cap.** ADR-0016 §5 spec'd one; v1 bounds via per-hop count + depth ceiling instead. Byte-cap is a follow-up if response-size budgeting becomes load-bearing.
- **No `edge_kinds` filter.** Always traverses both callers AND callees. Filtering one direction or specific edge types is a follow-up bead.
- **Single round-trip** (ADR-0016 §5 falsifiability gate `writes_for_neighborhood_query == 1`): the entire neighborhood is built inside one `with_live_db` closure and serialized once. Pinned implicitly by the handler architecture (no nested daemon calls).
- **Depth ceiling 4** per ADR-0016 §5; clamped at handler entry.
- **L7 provenance/certainty** carried through on every neighbor row.

## Tests (3 new)

- `inspect_neighborhood_empty_db_returns_empty_neighbors`
- `inspect_neighborhood_depth_1_returns_callers_and_callees` — A calls B, C calls A → neighbors = {B, C}
- `inspect_neighborhood_depth_is_capped_at_max` — depth=999 → response says depth=4

All drift tests pass; `task ci` clean.

title: leyline-sign cert_chain: add the confinementDigest Interlace extension (lane-2 identity commit for confinement/v1 §7)
description:
## Why
cloister/confinement/v1 §7 commits the `confinementDigest` (BLAKE3-256 of the §6-canonical ConfinementManifest) to the bundle's **lane-2 workload identity** so a runner enforcing a different manifest than the identity-committed one fails at the trust boundary. `_capability-mapping.md` §4: "the bundle-side commit lives in lane-2 (workload identity)." That commit is a **cert extension**, and the Interlace cert extensions are canonically here — `rs/ll-open/sign/src/cert_chain.rs`, OID arc `1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1.*`:
- `.4` epoch (DER INTEGER), `.5` peer_fp (UTF8String), `.6` scope (UTF8String).

There is **no confinementDigest extension yet**. cloister's a34edc (#129, merged) shipped the digest computation + conformance but can't complete §7 until this exists.

## Scope
1. Add OID `1.3.6.1.4.1.99999.1.7` = **interlace-confinement-digest**, encoded as a DER **OctetString** of the 32-byte BLAKE3-256 digest.
2. Parse it in `verify_cert_chain` → add `confinement_digest: Option<[u8; 32]>` to `CertClaims` (Optional — pre-existing certs without it stay valid; the field is None).
3. Emit it in `tests_helpers::mint_test_cert` (add an optional `confinement_digest` param) so dev/test minters + cloister's mint-dev-cert can commit it.
4. Document the extension in the cert_chain.rs header comment (alongside .4/.5/.6) + interlace-spec / _capability-mapping.

## Consumers (cross-repo)
- cloister `src/wire/signet-verify.ts` + `src/routes/lease-middleware.ts` — extract + compare to the bundle's declared confinement facet digest (cloister-side bead, depends on this).
- notme — mints the extension on bundle workload certs (production).

## Non-goals
- No enforcement runner (that's the compute-substrate, ADR-0044).
- Keep the wasm verify artifact byte-stable except the new optional extension parse.

title: Daemon arena admission has gaps — pre-0cba88 daemon coexistence + warm-start cross-source pollution; consumers see non-deterministic parse state
description:
## Symptom

Mache (2026-07-13) observed three stale `leyline daemon` processes coexisting on `~/.mache/default.arena` (PIDs 14121, 9420, 60375, oldest from Tuesday) with a 361 MB `default.db` from 2026-04-27. Consumers hitting the shared daemon see non-deterministic counts on smell rules (dead_code/dup-def changing between identical builds on untouched files). Mache's own subprocess parse path is fully deterministic (byte-identical `_ast` between runs); the pollution only hits the daemon path.

## Root causes (two, same class)

### RC1: pre-0cba88 daemon coexistence

Bead `ley-line-open-0cba88` (PR #130) added `flock(2)` admission control in `daemon/arena_lock.rs`. It works correctly for two post-fix daemons — the second refuses to start with a clear PID-holder error.

But it only protects against **post-0cba88 daemons.** A daemon started before that fix landed (long-running, or a stale user session) holds no lockfile. A new daemon starts, calls `try_acquire(arena)`, sees the lockfile is unlocked (because the old daemon never took the lock), and succeeds. Both now write to `<arena>.snapshot` — the classic race the fix was supposed to prevent.

Same failure mode if `leyline daemon` was ever invoked with a binary that predates the flock code (external users, container versions, dev machines with stale `~/.local/bin/leyline`).

### RC2: warm-start restores arena state without verifying `--source` match

`cmd_daemon::try_warm_start` reads the controller's `current_root`, reopens the WAL live-db, and serves whatever the previous daemon snapshotted. `_meta.source_root` (bead `ley-line-open-cbbedf`) records the source path but is not currently VERIFIED against the new `--source` argument at warm-start.

Consequence: daemon A parsed repo R1 (source_root = `/repos/R1`); daemon A crashes/is killed; daemon B started with `--source /repos/R2` warm-starts on the SAME arena; `_meta.source_root` still reads R1, but B doesn't check, silently serves R1's cached `_ast`/`node_defs`/`node_refs` alongside any R2 parses it does layer on. Consumer queries hit both.

This is exactly the mache-observed pattern: the shared `~/.mache/default.arena` accumulates cross-repo pollution because different mache invocations use different `--source` but reach the same warm-started arena.

## Deliverable

1. **Arena-owner sentinel with heartbeat**, replacing/augmenting flock. On daemon start:
   - Write `{"pid": N, "started_at": T, "leyline_version": "0.7.x", "source_root": "..."}` to `<arena>.owner` (JSON, atomic-write via temp+rename).
   - Update the sentinel's `heartbeat_at` every N seconds (10s default) while alive.
   - New daemon reading the sentinel:
     - PID not alive OR heartbeat stale by > 3 × heartbeat interval → treat as stale, take over.
     - PID alive + heartbeat fresh + source_root matches → refuse (same as flock semantics today).
     - PID alive + source_root MISMATCHES → refuse with error naming both source_roots (this is the new gate — closes RC2 for daemon-vs-daemon).
   - Sentinel survives crashes (no cleanup) — new daemon parses it, decides.
   - Complements flock (belt+suspenders); flock stays as the fast path.

2. **Warm-start source-root check**. `try_warm_start` reads `_meta.source_root` and refuses to warm-start when it disagrees with the current `--source`:
   - Error message: "arena source_root=A conflicts with --source=B; refusing warm-start. Pass `--reset-arena` to invalidate and cold-start, or use `--arena` to specify a different arena path."
   - `--reset-arena` flag drops all arena state (unlink live.db, zero controller) and proceeds with cold parse.

3. **Cross-repo isolation guidance in docs** — README + GETTING-STARTED note that `--arena` should be per-project (not the default `~/.mache/default.arena`) if consumers are going to share a daemon across repos.

## Falsifiable checks (four F-gates)

### F1_multi_daemon_admission_survives_pre_0cba88_holdovers

Simulate a pre-0cba88 daemon: `open(arena)` + `mmap` without flock, keep the fd alive. Then start a real `leyline daemon --arena SAME` — new daemon should detect the arena is being mmap'd by another PID (via `<arena>.owner` sentinel OR fcntl `F_GETLK` probe) and refuse. Currently: succeeds and coexists.

Test: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f1_pre_0cba88_coexistence.rs`. Requires the sentinel implementation.

### F2_warm_start_refuses_source_mismatch

Start daemon A with `--source /tmp/repoA`; wait for parse; snapshot to arena; kill daemon A cleanly. Start daemon B with `--source /tmp/repoB` on the SAME arena. Assert daemon B refuses with a clear error naming both source_roots.

Test: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f2_warm_start_source_mismatch.rs`.

### F3_stale_lock_recovery

Start daemon A on arena X, get its PID. `SIGKILL` daemon A (leaves stale sentinel but flock auto-releases). Wait for heartbeat-stale timeout. Start daemon B on same arena — B must succeed (sentinel detects PID not alive OR heartbeat stale).

Test: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f3_stale_lock_recovery.rs`.

### F4_deterministic_parse_across_daemon_restart

Cold-parse repo R with a known corpus. Snapshot to arena. Kill daemon A. Cold-parse R again (no arena warm-start). Assert `_ast`, `node_defs`, `node_refs`, `node_content` row counts + hashes are byte-identical across runs. This is the regression gate mache's find-smells baseline depends on.

Test: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f4_deterministic_parse_across_restart.rs`.

## Non-goals

- **Network-scoped admission** (two machines mounting the same NFS-served arena). NFS flock is advisory; scoping fixes beyond local per-machine is out of scope for v1.
- **Windows** (arena_lock.rs already stubs it out).
- **Auto-recovery from cross-source pollution** — v1 refuses with a clear error + `--reset-arena` opt-in; auto-invalidation could be v2.

## Files

- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/arena_owner.rs` (new; sentinel + heartbeat)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/arena_lock.rs` (existing; keep as fast path)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs` (wire sentinel + warm-start guard)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f1_pre_0cba88_coexistence.rs` (new)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f2_warm_start_source_mismatch.rs` (new)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f3_stale_lock_recovery.rs` (new)
- `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/f4_deterministic_parse_across_restart.rs` (new)
- `README.md` / `GETTING-STARTED.md` — per-project arena guidance

## Close condition

All four F-gates pass under `cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib`. `task ci` green. Mache's `dead_code`/`fan_out_skew` baseline is deterministic across two runs (external validation).

## Priority

P1 — silent cross-repo cache pollution is a correctness bug that undermines every LLO-consuming smell/audit gate. Blocks mache's consolidation baseline (they can't trust counts they can't reproduce). Also blocks any future analysis-substrate consumer (T3 taint reachability, dataflow, etc.) that depends on deterministic parse state.

title: Injections: injections.scm embedded-language extraction with own-CA-root injected subtrees
description:
Phase after engine+epoch in the queries-as-data design (bead e5addb analysis + _agent_log/theoretical-foundations-analyst_2026-07-15_agent_log.md). Falsification-shaped MVP (EXP2): go host → sql injected, driven by rs/ll-open/ts/queries/go/injections.scm using upstream tree-sitter conventions (@injection.content + #set! injection.language).

Hard requirements:
(a) Injected subtrees get their OWN content-addressed root — host file structural hash must NOT depend on injected grammar version (bumping tree-sitter-sql must not re-hash Go files containing SQL).
(b) Extraction epoch becomes COMPOSITE — injected facts depend on host injections.scm + injected-language tags.scm + both grammar versions. Composite = hash over {EXTRACTION_EPOCH, injections.scm content, injected tags.scm content}.
