comments.text:
ASSESSMENT — Tier 3 partial algebra for sql/bash (pre-implementation, per the 2026-07-15 restructure item 5: "sql/bash get whatever algebra is well-posed"). Grammar shapes verified empirically against tree-sitter-sequel 0.3 and tree-sitter-bash 0.25 via scratch AST dumps in the worktree. Verdict: BOTH languages carry a well-posed PARTIAL algebra. No COMPLETE algebra exists (upstream ships no tags.scm for either — structural, per the theoretical-foundations log), but the honest subset below produces stable, join-usable tokens for mache's dead_code (def↔ref token join) and god_file (κ kinds).

── SQL (tree-sitter-sequel 0.3) — IN ──
Defs (all anchor kinds get κ arms):
- create_table (incl. TEMPORARY; object_reference has optional schema field → engine dual-emit `analytics.events` + `events`, sep ".") → κ type
- create_view, create_materialized_view → κ type
- create_function (incl. OR REPLACE) → κ function
- create_schema (bare identifier child, no object_reference) → κ module
Refs (use-sites that join to those def tokens; schema-qualifier dual-emit throughout):
- (relation (object_reference)) — FROM / JOIN / UPDATE targets
- (insert (object_reference)) — INSERT INTO target
- (from (object_reference)) — DELETE FROM shape (delete's from holds object_reference directly; select's from wraps it in relation, so no overlap)
- (invocation (object_reference)) — function call sites (`SELECT add_one(2)`); builtins (count, lower) emit as unresolved refs — same class as C's printf call_expression refs, harmless to dead_code's direction
- create_trigger body edges: ON-table ref + EXECUTE FUNCTION ref (adjacency-anchored patterns) — a function used only by a trigger is NOT dead
Imports: NONE — SQL has no in-language import construct (\i / \include are psql metacommands outside the grammar).

── SQL — REJECTED, with reasons ──
- create_index def: an index name has no use-site in the language (only DROP INDEX) → a def token that can never join → permanent dead_code false positive. Junk.
- create_trigger def: same never-referenced shape. Its body REFS are emitted (above); the trigger NAME is not.
- column defs/refs: bare column tokens collide across tables (`users.name` vs `orders.name` both emit `name`) — join requires schema resolution the token algebra cannot express. Junk joins, rejected.
- DROP/ALTER object_references: lifecycle statements, not use. Counting DROP as a ref would mask "created, altered, never queried" dead tables.
- CTE defs: query-scoped transient names. CTE use-sites ride the same relation shape as table refs and are indistinguishable without scope resolution; a CTE shadowing a table name errs toward false-NEGATIVE (table marked used) — acceptable direction, documented in the .scm, no def emitted.
- create_procedure: tree-sitter-sequel 0.3 does not parse CREATE PROCEDURE at all (ERROR nodes, verified both AS-first and LANGUAGE-first spellings) — grammar limitation, not a choice.

── BASH (tree-sitter-bash 0.25) — IN (smaller) ──
Defs:
- function_definition (covers both `f() {}` and `function f {}` spellings; name: (word)) → κ function
Refs:
- (command name: (command_name (word))) — statically-named command invocations. Joins to shell-function defs. External binaries (grep, echo) emit unresolved refs — same class as builtins in every other language. `source`/`.` excluded via #not-any-of? — those nodes emit as Imports; one node, one fact.
Imports:
- `source x.sh` / `. x.sh` with a static word path — first-argument anchored (source's path IS argument 1)
- same with a static double-quoted string path — sole-named-child anchor `(string . (string_content) @path .)` structurally excludes any expansion-carrying string
- VERIFIED: the Rust binding's QueryCursor::matches evaluates #eq?/#any-of?/#not-any-of? text predicates natively (scratch test passed) — no engine change needed; predicates are per-pattern query data.

── BASH — REJECTED, with reasons ──
- variable_assignment defs + $VAR expansion refs: dynamic scoping + export/env crossing process and file boundaries makes def↔ref joins unsound; expansion refs are the noisiest emission shell has. Rejected outright.
- expansion-carrying source paths (`source "$HOME/x.sh"`): path is dynamic — not join-usable, no Import.
- command names through expansions (`$CMD ...`): no stable token (command_name holds no word).
- alias definitions: `alias ll='ls -l'` is a plain command node; the defined name lives inside a string argument — text parsing, not structure. Rejected.

── κ mappings (languages.rs) ──
sql: create_table/create_view/create_materialized_view → type (closed κ set has no "table"; a named relation shape is nearest to type — same collapse rationale as proto messages), create_function → function, create_schema → module, program → module. bash: function_definition → function, program → module. bash `command` (the Import anchor kind) stays UNMAPPED — mapping command→import would collapse every command node in the symbols path.
container_node_id works free of charge: the fold's container walk keys on κ function/method, so refs inside a create_function body / bash function body get the right container.

EXTRACTION_EPOCH 2→3: both languages previously emitted nothing; the bump forces existing arenas to re-derive so the new facts appear on binary upgrade.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

title: schema-bridge IR has 4 outputs but 1 input — add a GraphQL input lowering
description:
The IR's own header states 'Inputs (capnp, JSON extensions, future formats) lower into this type-set', but src/inputs/ contains only capnp.rs while src/outputs/ has four (zod, go, json_schema, tool_defs). The generalization ADR-0036 proposed went one way: outputs multiplied, inputs did not.

MOTIVATING INSTANCE (found 2026-07-27 while working canonical-hours-edb256):
canonical-hours/agent/lib/sources/github.ts has two GraphQL response shapes.
- The static SEARCH_QUERY is codegen-validated (SearchPrsQuerySchema from ./generated/github).
- buildRequiredCheckQuery is runtime-templated (aliases pr0..prN built per call), so codegen cannot target it. Its response is a hand-written TypeScript interface, GqlRequiredCheckResponse.

That hand-written interface DRIFTED: it modeled data.prN.commits... while the query actually returns data.prN.pullRequest.commits.... It broke the live task tick and was fixed by hand. This is precisely the failure mode ADR-0036 names as the reason to generalize — 'Each repo hand-writes types from the same conceptual schemas... the recurring failure mode' — but with a twist ADR-0036 did not anticipate: the schema is not capnp, it is GraphQL, and part of it is generated at runtime.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT LAYER
canonical-hours could hand-write a zod schema next to the builder (the bead's own fallback suggestion) and that would fix the instance. It would not fix the class: every repo consuming a GraphQL API keeps hand-modeling response shapes, and a runtime-templated query has no codegen story at all. A GraphQL input lowering into the existing IR gives all four outputs for free, including the go one signet/mache would want.

SCOPE NOTE
The runtime-templated case may need more than a plain SDL lowering — the alias set is a function of call-site data (N PRs), so the useful artifact is a schema FACTORY parameterized by alias count, not a fixed schema. Worth deciding whether that belongs in the IR (a repeated-alias construct) or in the zod output as a generated builder. IR V1 scope is explicitly narrow (structs of named fields, scalar or struct-ref) with enums/unions/lists as UnmappedConstruct, so GraphQL's unions (CheckRun | StatusContext, exactly what the reference case needs) require IR work first.

Prior art in-repo: docs/adr/0022-schema-bridge-substrate-positioning.md and docs/adr/0036-schema-bridge-multi-output.md (both in cloister; 0036 still Proposed).
acceptance_criteria: A GraphQL document (SDL or operation + schema) lowers into the existing IR and emits zod via the current output, verified by generating a schema that a consuming repo currently hand-writes — canonical-hours' required-check response is the reference case.

title: Adversarial audit of CDC layering and overloaded substrate terminology
description: Review docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the CDC/storage/graph implementation boundaries. Enumerate every materially different meaning of `substrate`, trace ownership and dependency direction, detect abstraction inversions or duplicate sources of truth, and turn confirmed findings into scoped follow-up beads.

comments.text:
Adversarial review result (2026-07-24).

Observed architecture domains:
1. Formal Σ primitive API: leyline-core Hash/ContentAddressed/BlobStore/RootPointer/RootSigner.
2. File-backed segment identity: Head.rootHash = BLAKE3(canonical source.capnp || ast.capnp || bindings.capnp), chained by parentHash.
3. Daemon publication identity: Controller.current_root = BLAKE3(sqlite3_serialize(living db)); readers use it for arena hot-swap/integrity.
4. SQL query ABI: nodes/_ast/_source/etc. are consumed across runtimes by mache even while docs call them local projections.
5. Derived analysis/cache products: _cfg/_dfg/_taint, HDC, CDC content_* tables.

Severity-ranked findings:
P0 — Two unrelated root byte domains are both presented as “the Σ root.” README:56/102 describes segment root; cmd_daemon.rs:1201-1265 computes current_root over serialized DB; ARCHITECTURE:92-106 calls the latter the Σ runtime model. No equality/derivation gate links them. Bead ef5c1d.
P1 — Authority claims contradict each other. README:56 says substrate is Cap'n Proto bytes, not SQL. ARCHITECTURE:75 calls nodes/_ast/_source/node_content canonical substrate. TABLE_CONTRACT:3-9 and 136-140 deny SQL is cross-process contract, while its diagram sends SQL to mache and Rule 5 at 184 says '.db file is the contract'. Bead ef5c5a, dependent on ef5c1d.
P1 — CDC has two retrieval abstractions. leyline-cdc::chunk_into/read_range use formal BlobStore and verify σ on get; production leyline-fs content_chunks directly reads SQLite and explicitly skips verify-on-read. It is safe under the whole-arena-root threat model but does not satisfy BlobStore/ρ while docs call it a Σ storage primitive. Bead ef5c84.
P2 — “Three layers” mixes compile-time package layers with a runtime transport surface: UDS/MCP are implemented inside leyline-cli-lib, which the same doc places in Layer 2. This is a documentation model problem, included in ef5c5a.
P2 — “substrate” is further reused for analysis-substrate and HDC similarity identity, which are derived facts/modalities rather than storage/identity primitives. Included in ef5c5a.

CDC placement verdict: correct only if scoped as a private, derived range-read/dedup cache inside the SQL projection, with nodes.record authoritative for that ABI and arena-root integrity as its boundary. Wrong if promoted as the canonical Σ blob store, cross-runtime contract, or distributed Git/CAS layer. Existing freshness/GC/consumer tests strongly support the narrow interpretation; docs and formal-interface composition do not yet enforce it.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: The review bead contains an evidence-backed layer map, terminology collision inventory, severity-ranked findings, and a bead ID for each actionable defect.

title: Compare CDC/graph architecture against ForgeMark and GraphMark evaluation surfaces
description: Research Entire's public ForgeMark benchmark and the GraphMark references exposed by published entire-graph artifacts. Identify which claims are comparable to ley-line-open CDC/graph behavior, which are orthogonal, and propose falsifiable benchmark coverage without conflating Git transport throughput with semantic graph quality.

comments.text:
Comparison result (sources inspected 2026-07-24: public ForgeMark main, public entire-graph main and v0.2.0 module).

ForgeMark: real smart-HTTP Git load generator. Strategies branch/repo/clone/session; reports ops/s, p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max, CAS failures/errors across concurrency sweeps. It measures forge receive-pack/upload-pack/ref-update behavior. It does NOT evaluate code graph accuracy, agent task completion, CDC boundary stability, local index build, or semantic queries.

entire-graph graph-bench: public provider micro/macro benchmark over pinned public repos. Reports wall time, files/LOC per sec, allocation/peak RSS, output bytes, symbol/relation counts, resolution/confidence distributions, parse failures. Those “quality” fields are proxy/coverage telemetry, not ground-truth precision/recall.

Private GraphMark: entire-graph AGENTS.md says it holds methodology/prompts/caveats for two separate claims: (a) a frozen 283-task/21-repo fixed-answer semantic accuracy board behind the public 265/283 (94%) claim, and (b) an official SWE-bench Multilingual agent experiment (300 instances/9 languages/Haiku) reporting 54.9% weighted token savings vs no-tool, 27.4% for codebase-memory-mcp, 8/9 language wins, 216/293 instance wins, identical completion; Sonnet/open-model replications are claimed. The private corpus/harness prevents exact independent reproduction. Public entire-graph only exposes the claims and exact recommended prompt, not task rows/results.

Valid comparison stack for us:
- Git/CDC transport/storage: adopt ForgeMark workload SHAPES only when benchmarking a Git-compatible network endpoint. LLO CDC alone is not a forge and cannot honestly report pushes/s or clones/s.
- Provider scale: existing mache-543943 already tracks adopting entire-graph's pinned throughput/memory repos.
- Fixed-answer semantic correctness: mache-2acd4f; must use a clean-room/public board and never imply it is GraphMark's private 283 tasks.
- Query token compression: mache-544659; report distributions, not only a hero symbol.
- Agent outcome/token efficiency: new mache-ee4216 clean-room GraphMark-style SWE-bench Multilingual harness.
- Cross-tool MCP comparison: mache-7937c5.

Recommendation: do not build a single “GraphMark clone.” Maintain four named scorecards—storage/transport, provider scale, semantic correctness, and agent outcome—sharing pinned corpus metadata but never sharing denominators.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: A bead comment records a sourced comparison matrix, non-comparable claims, and concrete benchmark recommendations for ley-line-open.

title: Arena-resident query blobs: hash-allowlisted overrides for compiled-in .scm defaults
description:
Final phase of queries-as-data (analysis on ley-line-open-e5addb + _agent_log/theoretical-foundations-analyst_2026-07-15_agent_log.md §§1-2). .scm query files become content-addressed arena data: compiled-in defaults seed, arena-resident blobs override behind an operator-controlled BLAKE3 allowlist.

Requirements:
1. Bootstrap: query_set(lang) = arena blob (present AND trusted) else compiled default; version skew surfaces via extraction/injection epoch (query bytes already epoch inputs).
2. Trust: untrusted blob IGNORED with one loud stderr line; extraction falls back to compiled default, never silently to nothing.
3. Emission-ABI gate: blob declaring capture names unknown to the engine is a HARD ERROR at load; vocabulary versioned via emission_abi_version declaration, documented in query_engine.rs.
4. Resource bounds: QueryCursor match limits/timeouts so a pathological blob degrades to "no facts for this file" + stderr, not a hung daemon.
5. Provenance: active query-set source (compiled vs arena hash) observable via introspection; no per-row provenance columns.

Verification: cargo test -p ll-open-ts && task ci

comments.text:
STEP 2 — storage decision (pre-implementation).

DECISION: in-arena tables, following the content-addressed blob-table + pointer-table pattern the arena already uses twice:
- `query_blobs (blob_hash BLOB PRIMARY KEY, blob_bytes BLOB NOT NULL)` — same shape as ADR-0028 `source_blobs` and ADR-0026 `capnp_blobs`, keyed on BLAKE3(blob_bytes), verified at load (a row whose bytes do not hash to its key is treated as untrusted: one stderr line, compiled fallback).
- `_queries (lang TEXT, kind TEXT DEFAULT 'tags', blob_hash BLOB REFERENCES query_blobs, PRIMARY KEY (lang, kind))` — the pointer, same FK-shaped-pointer discipline as `_source.content_hash → source_blobs.blob_hash` and `_ast_pointer.blob_hash → capnp_blobs.blob_hash`.

PRECEDENT REJECTED: sidecar file next to the arena. The only sidecar today is the transient flock `<arena>.lock` (arena_lock.rs) — admission control, not data. Everything durable lives inside the one SQLite file: blobs (source_blobs/capnp_blobs), provenance (_meta.extraction_epoch/_meta.injection_epoch — the f6/f7 gates), facts. An arena is moved/backed up as a single .db; a sidecar would silently detach from it.

TRUST BOUNDARY: the allowlist does NOT live in the arena — whoever writes the arena must not be able to self-trust a blob. Operator control via env `LLO_TRUSTED_QUERY_HASHES` (comma-separated hex BLAKE3-32), matching the established env-knob surface (LLO_EMBEDDER; seams LLO_EXTRACTION_EPOCH, LLO_INJECTIONS_SCM).

WIRING PLAN:
- Resolution once per parse pass in `parse_into_conn` (leyline_ts::query_engine::QuerySet::resolve(conn)): override present + hash-verified + allowlisted → engine built from blob via ABI-gated constructor; otherwise compiled default + one stderr line. Unknown capture name or bad emission-abi declaration in a TRUSTED blob → hard Err out of parse_into_conn.
- Engines threaded per-file (ExtractCtx { queries: &QuerySet, budget }) through fold_children/fold_injected into extract_refs — no process-global override state, so per-arena resolution stays correct under the daemon.
- Epoch: `_meta.query_set_epoch` = σ composite over (lang, source-tag compiled|arena:<hex>, active scm bytes) per Tier-3 language, ANDed into the existing f6/f7 unchanged-skip gate in parse_into_conn. Compiled .scm edits now self-invalidate (the refs.rs EXTRACTION_EPOCH doc anticipated exactly this). Provenance: `_meta.query_source:<lang>` = `arena:<hex>` rows written only for active overrides (absence = compiled) — the smallest honest introspection surface.
- Resource bounds (tree-sitter 0.26.8): `QueryCursor::set_match_limit` + `did_exceed_match_limit` on every engine run; `matches_with_options` progress-callback deadline (per-file budget) on arena-blob engines, whose patterns are the untrusted input. Trip → facts for that file dropped, one stderr line, parse completes.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
STEP 2 (impl agent) — confirming scoping plan (comment 221) + two load-bearing refinements decided BEFORE implementing.

FOLLOWING the plan verbatim on storage: in-arena `query_blobs (blob_hash BLOB PK, blob_bytes BLOB NOT NULL)` + `_queries (lang TEXT, kind TEXT DEFAULT 'tags', blob_hash BLOB, PK(lang,kind))`. Precedent = source_blobs (ADR-0028) + capnp_blobs (ADR-0026): content-addressed blob table + FK-shaped pointer, all durable state inside the one .db. Trust allowlist OUTSIDE the arena via env `LLO_TRUSTED_QUERY_HASHES` (comma-sep hex blake3-32) so the arena writer can't self-trust. Provenance via `_meta.query_source:<lang> = arena:<hex>` (present only for active overrides; absence = compiled). Epoch via `_meta.query_set_epoch` ANDed into the existing f6/f7 unchanged-skip gate.

REFINEMENT 1 (blast-radius): `extract_refs(node,source,node_id,source_id,language,container)` stays UNCHANGED (7 call sites incl. 5 refs.rs test callers) — the compiled path is byte-identical. Overrides ride a NEW `extract_refs_resolved(..., queries: &QuerySet, bounds: &Cell<bool>)` called only from cmd_parse's fold. `parse_into_conn(conn,source,lang,scope)` signature UNCHANGED (60+ callers) — the QuerySet is resolved INSIDE it from conn + env allowlist. Resolution returns `(QuerySet, Vec<String> warnings)`; parse_into_conn prints one eprintln per warning (this is how "exactly one stderr line" is unit-testable — resolve is called directly in test b).

REFINEMENT 2 (override semantics): an arena override REPLACES the compiled QueryEngine's `.scm`-driven emission for that language. The query-inexpressible imperative arms (Rust use-list flattening, Python from-import joins, qualified Class.method defs, JS/TS κ fixups) are NOT re-run under an override — an operator shipping an override owns the complete emission for that language via the `.scm`. For the pure-delegate languages (Go/C/SQL/Bash) this is a lossless swap; documented in query_engine.rs. Demo/tests use Go (pure delegate).

ABI GATE (req 3): override blob MUST declare a leading `; emission-abi-version: N` comment. Missing, or N != EMISSION_ABI_VERSION(=1) → hard load error. After Query::new, every capture name not in {def,ref,import,name,qualifier,path,alias} and not `_`-prefixed (predicate helpers, e.g. bash `@_cmd`) → hard load error. Applies to TRUSTED blobs only (untrusted are ignored before the gate).

RESOURCE BOUNDS (req 4, tree-sitter 0.26.8): override engines run `QueryCursor::set_match_limit` + `matches_with_options` with a progress-callback tick budget; on `did_exceed_match_limit` or budget break, that file's extracted facts are dropped, one stderr line, parse completes. Compiled engines stay unbounded (trusted, fixture-pinned). Limits env-tunable (`LLO_QUERY_MATCH_LIMIT`).

Verification: `cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib` + `task ci` (run from rs/).
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
GREEN — implemented, committed, task ci exit 0. Bead stays OPEN.

TDD RED (captured by stubbing extract_refs_resolved to ignore overrides, then restoring):
- a_allowlisted_override_replaces_compiled_default — FAILED: "allowlisted override must emit the distinguishable package-name def; got [Alpha, Beta, Gadget]"
- d_pathological_override_is_bounded_and_file_skipped — FAILED: "a bounded override run must drop this file's extracted facts; got [Alpha, Beta, Gadget]"
- e_swapping_active_blob_bumps_epoch_and_rederives — FAILED: "OVERRIDE_PKG must emit only the package-name def; left [Alpha, Beta, Gadget] right [widget]"
- b (untrusted-ignored+warning) and c (ABI hard error) test resolve_query_set directly, so they were green pre-wiring — the resolver builds/rejects override engines independent of the fold. Result under the stub: 2 passed, 3 failed.

GREEN (feature restored):
- arena_query_blobs_test.rs: 5 passed / 0 failed.

title: Producer/consumer contract test discipline — prevent the caf423 class of gap
description:
Meta-lesson from bead `ley-line-open-caf423` (PR #165): mache found Python/JS producing zero symbols + unqualified method tokens + empty `source_file` because LLO's OWN tests confirmed schema shape but not the semantic contract downstream consumers depend on.

## The gap pattern

Producer tests today verify:
- Parser succeeds
- AST rows written
- Schema DDL matches

Producer tests DON'T verify:
- Every "supported" language produces non-empty extractions
- Method-scope qualification actually holds
- Populated columns (like `source_file`) are non-null across the row set
- The semantic contract mache queries against actually holds

Classic producer/consumer gap. Zero-symbol Python parsed successfully AND the test passed — the test didn't check for symbols, only that the parse ran.

## What ships — four-layer defense

### Layer 1: Per-language non-empty gate

New test that iterates every `TsLanguage::supported()` variant and asserts non-empty extraction:

```rust
#[test]
fn every_supported_language_produces_symbols() {
    for lang in TsLanguage::supported() {
        let fixture = canonical_fixture(lang);  // per-language hand-authored fixture
        let db = parse_into_conn(fixture);
        assert!(node_defs_count(&db) > 0, "{lang:?} defs empty");
        assert!(node_refs_count(&db) > 0, "{lang:?} refs empty");
        assert!(all_nodes_source_file_populated(&db), "{lang:?} source_file gap");
    }
}
```

Table-driven: adding a new language to `TsLanguage::supported()` REQUIRES adding a `canonical_fixture(lang)` entry — compile error if you don't. Structurally impossible to ship a "supported" language that produces zero output.

### Layer 2: Downstream-consumer smoke test

New task target `task ci:consumer-smoke`:

- Parses a small mixed-language fixture (Rust + Go + Python + JS + TS + Elixir + HCL) through LLO
- Runs mache-shape queries against the output
- Asserts semantic contract (find definition of `foo` returns `foo`; find callers of `bar` returns the callers, etc.)

Depends on either shelling out to a real `mache` binary or embedding the minimal query shape mache uses. Cheap to do the latter (a few SQL queries in the shape mache does).

### Layer 3: Machine-executable contract tests

Extract the prose contracts from `docs/audits/sheaf-invalidation-trace.md` and other audit docs into machine-runnable tests. Every substrate contract gets a test:

- Per-language extraction: non-empty + qualified where applicable + source_file populated
- Sheaf loop: payload shape stable, `daemon.sheaf.invalidate` fires on watcher change
- Pointer store integrity: F1 round-trip (already in place)
- Source blob content-addressing: F-git compat (already in place)

The audit docs stay for humans; the tests become the enforceable contract.

### Layer 4: Extend gate `fd07d8` to producer layer

`ley-line-open-fd07d8` (adversarial testing sweep) was scoped to storage changes. Extend the gate:

**Any PR that touches `refs.rs`, `hdc_enrich.rs`, `cmd_parse.rs`, or the extraction pipeline generally must include ≥1 downstream-consumer assertion (not just a schema check).**

Same rigor discipline, wider scope. Update the bead's mission or file a companion.

## What this bead does NOT deliver

- **NO changes to the producer code itself** — this is discipline + infrastructure
- **NO mache-side changes** — LLO's own gates are what's failing
- **NO retroactive fixture-authoring for languages not currently supported**

## Rules

- Commit prefix `[ley-line-open-<this-bead-id>]`
- `task ci` green with new gate + smoke test
- New per-language fixtures MUST fail compile if `TsLanguage::supported()` extends without a fixture

## Related

- `ley-line-open-caf423` (PR #165) — the discovered gap; this bead prevents recurrence
- `ley-line-open-fd07d8` — adversarial testing sweep gate; extend to producer layer
- ADR-0026 Phase 2 dual-read discipline — same pattern applied to reads

## Provenance

- Filed 2026-07-09 after mache found caf423 that LLO's tests missed
- User directive: "our testing missing this is a concern. how do we ensure it doesn't happen again?"
acceptance_criteria: Per-language non-empty gate test added + compile-forced fixture for every TsLanguage::supported(); task ci:consumer-smoke target present; contract tests extract audit-doc invariants into runnable assertions; fd07d8 gate wording extended to producer layer

## Context

Six inline `blake3::hash(...)` call sites across `ll-open/` bypass the trait. Seam scan (2026-05-19) confirmed: no CDC anywhere; no cross-repo edge between LLO and private ley-line; private ley-line's extras are RaptorQ FEC + UDP transport, not relevant here.

## Scope (Phase 0+1 ONLY)

This bead is the **retrofit-first** preparation step. Implements NOTHING. Just:

1. Enumerate all 6 inline `blake3::hash` call sites in `ll-open/` with file:line + surrounding function context.
2. Write characterization tests pinning observable behavior at each site. Tests MUST pass on current code AND survive the future retrofit (zero-change contract).
3. Audit pass at each site per `self-audit` skill checklist — dead fields, rotting comments, duplicate logic, test-only exports, scope drift, stale TODOs, hardcoded constants. Findings classified `inline-fix` | `separate-bead` | `noted-only`.

## NOT in scope

- No new `BlobStore` / `RootSigner` impls (those are Phase 2)
- No migration of call sites (Phase 3)
- No lint gate (Phase 4)
- No CDC, no algorithm-generic refactor, no `ArenaHeader` v3, no chunk-tree manifest

No source-file changes in this PR. Tests + audit doc only.

## Tracks

Downstream beads blocked on this:

title: Publish clients/ts as TypeScript contract bindings for schema-spec (mirrors clients/go/leyline-schema)
description:
Filed 2026-07-27. Establishes LLO's TypeScript consumer surface so downstream
repos stop hand-mirroring wire contracts, exactly as ley-line-open-41867b did
for Go ("so downstream repos ... stop forking capnp schemas").

## Motivating drift

cloister hand-writes the `InjectionStrategy` discriminated union at
`src/routes/vault-proxy.ts:21` as a mirror of
`rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/wire/injection-strategies.md`.
Nothing keeps the mirror in sync with the spec — the contract is versioned
precisely so it can evolve, and a hand-copy silently diverges when it does.
Generated bindings turn a copy into an import.

## Scope

- `clients/ts/` alongside `clients/go/leyline-schema`, following the same
  multi-module-monorepo pattern.
- Published to npmjs under the `@agentic-research/` scope, matching
  `@agentic-research/dpop` (Apache-2.0) which cloister already consumes.
- First contract to bind: `credential-isolation/v1` (the drift above).
  `build-cache`, `confinement`, `leyline-net`, `mcp-tool` follow.

## Licensing

No new carveout needed. README.md:113 already states "The schema and
wire-contract crates are Apache-2.0" and `rs/ll-core/schema-spec/` is squarely
inside it. Package declares `"license": "Apache-2.0"`.

This is what lets private/permissive consumers use it: cloister is
AGPL-3.0-or-later and rig is private, and both can consume an Apache-2.0
package. The reverse — publishing the contract from cloister — would have made
an AGPL repo the owner of a contract it does not own, violating ADR-0035
(leyline-* lives in LLO; cloister bridges, never reimplements).

## Note on the existing carveout

The Apache-2.0/AGPL split is asserted only in README.md:113. No `Cargo.toml` in
the repo declares a `license =` field, so nothing machine-checks which crate is
which, and nothing prevents an "Apache" schema crate from depending on an AGPL
implementation crate — which would make the Apache claim false for every
downstream consumer. Worth a separate bead; the npm package should declare its
license in `package.json` from the start rather than inherit the prose-only
pattern.

comments.text:
Correction to this bead's proposed layout, 2026-07-27.

A per-language reference implementation for THIS EXACT SPEC already exists in
this repo and I missed it when filing:

    rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/ref-impl-py/credisolation/
      __init__.py  injection.py  validate.py  receipt.py  envelope.py

So the precedent for shipping language bindings for `credential-isolation/v1` is
not only `clients/go/leyline-schema` (generated capnp bindings, a different
thing) — it is a hand-written reference implementation living *inside the spec
directory*, beside the wire docs it implements.

That changes the proposed home. Two options, and the ref-impl-py precedent
favours the second:

1. `clients/ts/` — alongside the Go bindings. Right if the TS artifact is
   GENERATED from capnp, matching what clients/go is.
2. `rs/ll-core/schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/ref-impl-ts/` — alongside
   ref-impl-py. Right if the TS artifact is a hand-written reference
   implementation of the wire spec, which is what cloister actually needs to
   replace its hand-mirrored `InjectionStrategy` union.

The distinction is not cosmetic: co-locating with the spec is what keeps the
implementation and the contract in the same review, which is the drift this
bead exists to close. A binding two directories away from its spec is how the
cloister mirror drifted in the first place.

Recommend option 2 unless the TS is genuinely capnp-generated. Also worth
checking whether ref-impl-py is published anywhere or is checked against the
spec by a test — if it is neither, it has the same unenforced-declaration
problem as ley-line-open-4392a2 and the TS should not copy that pattern.

comments.text:
RESCOPE 2026-07-27.

Filed as "publish clients/ts as TypeScript contract bindings ... so downstream repos stop
hand-mirroring wire contracts". The goal is right; the deliverable as written risks doing
the exact thing it exists to prevent — hand-mirroring.

## Why

capnp schemas are deterministically regenerable, which puts this in the GENERATE arm of
vigil-4b304d's declare-vs-generate rule: "Regenerable deterministically -> GENERATE.
Drift becomes unrepresentable. Total guarantee."

The Go precedent this bead cites (ley-line-open-41867b) did NOT hand-write a client —
clients/go/leyline-schema/**/*.capnp.go carry the "Code generated" marker. Writing
clients/ts by hand would diverge from the precedent it names, and would need a human to
remember to update it, which is the failure mode.

## Revised deliverable

"Wire schema-bridge's TS target + a drift gate", not "write a TS client".

LLO already hosts the generator: rs/ll-open/schema-bridge (leyline-schema-bridge v0.10.4,
ADR-0036 Phase 2), which emits zod TS / Go / JSON Schema from capnp and hard-errors on any
unmapped construct rather than silently emitting z.unknown().

## Blocker to know about

That generator is wired into NOTHING in LLO — zero matches for "schema-bridge" in
Taskfile.yml and zero in .github/workflows/ (measured at abd5b86). See the evidence
comment on ley-line-open-4ec276. So this bead depends on 4ec276 getting at least one
(schema, format) pair into `task ci` with a drift check first; otherwise "wire the TS
target" produces output nothing verifies.

## Connection to symbol identity

Whatever ley-line-open-2037b4's ADR decides for construct identity must be published
through THIS surface. mache keyed on rendered names and lost 733 Rust constructs plus
16.9% of Go init() bodies precisely because neither durable half of the identity was
reachable from a generated consumer surface. Fixing the identity without the publication
path fixes the instance and leaves the class.

comments.text:
NARROWING my rescope comment above, 2026-07-27. It was too sweeping in one direction and
rested on a claim I have since corrected.

## Two artifacts, two different answers — not one rule

My comment said this belongs in the GENERATE arm, full stop. That is right for wire
TYPES and wrong for reference IMPLEMENTATIONS, and this bead's thread contains both.

  wire types        clients/go (generated capnp bindings), a future TS surface,
                    cloister's InjectionStrategy union
                    -> GENERATE. Regenerable deterministically; drift unrepresentable.

  reference impls   schema-spec/credential-isolation/v1/ref-impl-py/credisolation/
                    -> DECLARE INDEPENDENTLY. Its purpose is to be a SECOND statement of
                       the spec's semantics, so spec-vs-implementation disagreement stays
                       detectable. Generating it deletes the signal.

vigil-4b304d carves this out explicitly, and I quoted it before failing to apply it:
"Generate when you want agreement BY CONSTRUCTION. Declare independently when you want
two statements that are ALLOWED to disagree, because the disagreement is the signal."

So comment 386's option-2 instinct (co-locate with the spec, beside ref-impl-py) and my
GENERATE push are not in conflict. They are about different artifacts. Concretely:
cloister-871aed asks to stop hand-mirroring the InjectionStrategy TYPE — that is the
generate case, and it does not touch ref-impl-py's role.

Comment 386's closing question stands and is still unanswered: is ref-impl-py published
anywhere, or checked against the spec by a test? If neither, it has the same unenforced
shape as everything else we found today, and being hand-written does not excuse it —
an independent statement nobody compares is not a signal.

## Correcting the blocker I stated

I wrote that schema-bridge "is wired into NOTHING in LLO — zero matches ... So this bead
depends on 4ec276 getting at least one (schema, format) pair into task ci first;
otherwise wiring the TS target produces output nothing verifies."

The measurement was right about LLO and wrong as a conclusion. cloister runs the
generator today with a content-diff drift check (cluster:zod / :verify / :check-drift,
off LLO's plugin binaries). So the mechanism is proven in production — just not by the
repo that owns it.

The dependency on 4ec276 is therefore weaker than I said. What LLO still lacks is a
generated surface OF ITS OWN plus a drift gate; that is a small slice, and cloister's
check-drift is a working template to copy rather than a design to invent.

Full correction on ley-line-open-4ec276.

title: Cold ingest holds the whole corpus in RAM twice: par_iter().collect() barrier + batch buffers that only flush at the end
description:
Measured 2026-08-17 on kibana v9.5.1 TypeScript slices (release build, M-series). Baseline = origin/integration @ 0958f54.

| files  | wall   | parse | insert | insert% | peak RSS | rows   |
|--------|--------|-------|--------|---------|----------|--------|
| 2 000  |   7.3s | 0.27s |   7.0s |   96%   |  2.9 GB  |  1.40M |
| 8 000  |  46.9s | 0.99s |  45.9s |   98%   |  8.5 GB  |  6.30M |
| 32 000 | 566.3s | 8.62s | 557.6s |   98.5% | 14.2 GB  | 28.49M |

## Finding 1 — parse is not the bottleneck

32 000 TypeScript files parse in 8.6s (~3 700 files/s). Parse is 1.5% of wall at
monorepo scale. Any effort aimed at the parser is aimed at the wrong 1.5%.

## Finding 2 — per-row insert cost degrades ~4x with scale

5.03 -> 7.29 -> 19.6 us/row across the three slices. Batching is already correct
(BULK_BATCH_ROWS=3000, multi-row VALUES, prepare_cached), so this is B-tree
maintenance once the index outgrows cache, on a single thread.

## Finding 3 — memory is O(corpus), and it is doubled

Two independent amplifiers, both in parse_into_conn:

1. `let parsed_files: Vec<Result<ParsedFile>> = to_parse.par_iter().map(..).collect();`
   A hard phase barrier. Every ParsedFile for the whole corpus — source bytes
   included — is live before row one is written.

2. All 13 batch buffers (content/child/nodes/ast/source_blob/source/refs/defs/
   imports/file_idx/blob/pointer) accumulate the ENTIRE corpus and only flush
   after the loop ends. `flush_batched` chunks the STATEMENTS at 3000 rows, but
   the Vec holding all 28.5M rows is fully materialised first.

Result: 14.2 GB resident to ingest 193 MB of source (74x), which drove this
machine into swap (8.3 of 9.2 GB). The RSS curve flattening at 32k (2.9 -> 8.5 ->
14.2 GB against 4x file steps) is physical memory running out, not the algorithm
behaving — 14.2 GB understates true demand.

## Why the buffers flush late, and the constraint any fix must keep

The FK-ordering comment above the flush block is load-bearing: with
foreign_keys=ON the node_hash FKs are checked per row, so node_content must land
before every referencing table. Naive per-buffer incremental flushing breaks
this — ast_buf could fill and flush before content_buf wrote the rows it
references.

## Proposed shape

- Flush ALL buffers in the existing FK order every K files rather than once at
  the end. Bounds buffer memory to O(K) while preserving the ordering invariant
  within each epoch. Rows stay uncommitted until the single COMMIT, so
  atomicity is unchanged; they move from Rust Vecs into SQLite's bounded page
  cache / WAL.
- Replace the collect() barrier with a bounded channel so insert overlaps parse
  and ParsedFiles do not all live at once. Insert must stay single-threaded
  (write connection), so this is producer-fan-out / single-consumer.

Together these make peak memory O(channel_depth + K) instead of O(corpus), and
recover the parse/insert overlap that the barrier currently forfeits.

## Related

ley-line-open-cd052b (PR #355) removes two per-file memcpys on this path and is
worth ~2-10% wall, but does not change the O(corpus) shape — it lowers the slope,
not the order. Benchmark harness + corpora manifest:
scratchpad/bench/, scratchpad/corpora/MANIFEST.md.
acceptance_criteria: Peak RSS on the kibana 32k-file slice is bounded by a tunable working-set constant rather than corpus size, and does not drive the machine into swap. Measured with scratchpad/bench/run_ingest_bench.sh against the same cumulative slices (2k/8k/32k) used for the 2026-08-17 baseline below. Row counts must stay byte-identical to the baseline (1397557 @ 2k, 6301699 @ 8k, 28486915 @ 32k).

title: Markdown inline content is never parsed — LLO runs tree-sitter-md's block grammar but never INLINE_LANGUAGE, so code spans do not exist as nodes
description:
Found 2026-07-29 while answering whether mache's disabled
`drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference` (shipped `WHERE 1=0`, described as
"requires a backtick-token preprocessor") is an LLO problem. It is — but not
the problem anyone downstream thinks it is.

## The gap, located exactly

`tree-sitter-md` ships TWO grammars, and its own crate docs say so:

    pub const LANGUAGE          // block grammar
    pub const INLINE_LANGUAGE   // "to parse inline content"

LLO uses `LANGUAGE` in both call sites — `ts/src/languages.rs:162` and
`ts/src/project.rs:353` — and **nothing anywhere calls `INLINE_LANGUAGE`.**

So the block pass runs and the inline pass never does. Measured on a fixture
containing `` `PartitionSpec::address` `` and `` `render` `` in a paragraph:

    $ leyline parse . -o md.db
    $ sqlite3 md.db "SELECT node_kind, COUNT(*) FROM _ast GROUP BY node_kind"
    inline|2                        <-- the ENTIRE paragraph, one opaque node
    fenced_code_block|1
    code_fence_content|1
    language|1
    info_string|1
    atx_heading|1
    section|1  paragraph|1  document|1

No `code_span`. No `link`. No `emphasis`. Every paragraph is a single `inline`
leaf, so inline structure is not merely unextracted — it does not exist in the
substrate at all.

Note the asymmetry this creates: FENCED code blocks are fully structured
(`fenced_code_block`, `code_fence_content`, `language`, `info_string`), so a
consumer can already reason about them. Inline spans, which is what prose
actually cites symbols with, are invisible.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Two downstream repos each built half a feature around the gap:

- mache's `drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference` ships as `WHERE 1=0` — a query
  hardcoded to return nothing. Its description names the blocker: "requires a
  backtick-token preprocessor."
- assay has the detection but no precision filter.

Neither needs a preprocessor. A preprocessor is **re-implementing what the
grammar already does**, and hand-rolled backtick scanning is precisely where
the precision problem comes from: it cannot reliably distinguish a span in
prose from a fenced block, an escaped backtick, a double-backtick span
containing a backtick, or an indented code block. The grammar handles all of
those; a regex does not. LLO has this exact scar already — `smell-projector`
carries hand-rolled backtick-stripping (`main.rs:797-824`) to stop the word
"unsafe" in prose from tripping a lint.

This is also the data-plane boundary working as intended in reverse: two
consumers wrote workarounds because the substrate did not supply a fact it is
positioned to supply.

## Scope

1. Run the inline parser over the byte ranges of `inline` nodes and splice the
   resulting subtrees into `_ast` under their block parent. tree-sitter-md's
   own README documents this two-pass shape; the crate exposes
   `NODE_TYPES_INLINE` alongside `NODE_TYPES_BLOCK`.
2. Decide the κ (`canonical_kind`) mapping for the new kinds, or deliberately
   leave them raw. Today no markdown kind has a κ arm at all. Whatever is
   chosen, it is a `node_hash` preimage input for markdown nodes — see ADR-0034
   D4: a κ-map change is a generation-lineage event, so this must move
   `_meta.ir_schema_version` (`merkle-ast-v2` -> v3) if it changes any existing
   node's kind. Adding NEW nodes where none existed does not rewrite existing
   addresses; confirm that before assuming either way.
3. Only then is "which symbols does this doc cite?" a query rather than a
   preprocessor. Whether those spans should also land in `node_refs` is a
   separate decision and should not be smuggled in here.

## Acceptance criteria

Parsing a markdown file containing `` `Foo::bar` `` in a paragraph produces a
`code_span` (or equivalent inline kind) node in `_ast` whose byte range covers
exactly the span, with the backticks' treatment stated explicitly either way.
Fenced-block content must NOT be double-parsed as inline. Proven by parsing a
fixture with: a prose span, an escaped backtick, a double-backtick span
containing a backtick, and a fenced block — then asserting the node set, not by
reading the code.

Existing markdown `node_hash` values must be shown either unchanged or
deliberately re-lineaged; do not leave that unestablished.

## Related

mache's `drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference`, assay's detection pass,
`ley-line-open-2607d2` (a check that cannot fire is inadmissible — `WHERE 1=0`
is the strongest form of that), ADR-0034 D4 (κ-map changes are lineage events).

comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION BRIEF for ley-line-open-ea1e42 (2026-07-29, coordinating session). Unblocks mache's drift_doc_dead_symbol_reference (mache-eb2bf3) and assay's precision filter.

## The problem, measured (from mache-eb2bf3)
LLO parses markdown with tree-sitter-md's BLOCK grammar only (`ts/src/languages.rs:162` — `tree_sitter_md::LANGUAGE`; no call site for `INLINE_LANGUAGE` anywhere). A paragraph containing `` `PartitionSpec::address` `` lands in `_ast` as one opaque `inline` node: no `code_span`, no `link`, no `emphasis`. Inline structure does not exist in `_ast` at all.

## The design: ride the existing injection mechanism — do NOT invent a second parse path
LLO already has exactly the needed machinery (`ts/src/injections.rs` + cli-lib `cmd_parse.rs::fold_injected`): an `injections.scm` per host language captures `@injection.content` ranges with `(#set! injection.language "…")`; the range is reparsed under the target grammar via `Parser::set_included_ranges` (host offsets preserved); the injected subtree gets its OWN content-addressed root so its hashes never enter host preimages; and the composite injection epoch (`current_injection_epoch`) hashes host injections.scm + injected tags.scm + both grammars into `_meta.injection_epoch` for the unchanged-skip gate. The Go→SQL injection is the working precedent — study how `GO_INJECTIONS_SCM` is compiled in, how `InjectionEngine` is constructed per host language, and how cli-lib folds the injected tree, then mirror all of it.

Concretely:
1. New `TsLanguage::MarkdownInline` variant (cfg feature "markdown", same crate dependency), mapping to `tree_sitter_md::INLINE_LANGUAGE.into()`, name "markdown-inline" (pick the name `from_name` resolution needs and use it consistently in the .scm).
2. New `queries/markdown/injections.scm`: capture `(inline) @injection.content` with `(#set! injection.language "markdown-inline")`. Wire it into the compiled-in constants + composite epoch exactly like Go's (note the cfg gates: Go's is `#[cfg(all(feature = "go", feature = "sql"))]` — markdown's should be `#[cfg(feature = "markdown")]`).
3. `queries/markdown-inline/tags.scm` (or however the injected language's query dir is keyed — follow the SQL precedent): minimal captures so extraction runs over the injected tree. The load-bearing outcome is that inline nodes land in `_ast`; if the fold only emits _ast rows for captured/named nodes, capture at least `code_span`, `link`, `emphasis` (verify against how SQL's injected nodes reach `_ast` — mirror it).

## Two decisions, already made (coordinating session, posted to mache-eb2bf3; do not re-litigate)
- κ (`canonical_kind`): NO κ mapping for any inline kind. Today no markdown kind has one; adding one is a `node_hash` preimage input (ADR-0034 D4 lineage event forcing downstream re-parses). None of that is needed for mache's rule. The κ closed set stays untouched.
- `node_refs`: _ast-only for now. mache's floor requirement is "code spans exist as nodes"; node_refs emission is a follow-up if mache asks after seeing this land (their rule reads `nodes` + `node_defs` today).

## Acceptance — mache's own measurement, as a Rust test
Add a test (in ts or cli-lib, wherever the parse-to-db integration tests live — find the existing pattern, e.g. tests that assert `_ast` contents after `leyline parse`) with a fixture markdown file containing a paragraph citing two symbols in backtick spans (e.g. `PartitionSpec::address` and `render`), a fenced code block, and a link. Assert:
1. `_ast` contains ≥2 `code_span` nodes (the paragraph's), with byte ranges pointing INTO the host file at the right offsets, and the span text matching the symbol names.
2. `link` and `emphasis` kinds appear when present in the fixture.
3. The fenced block's structure is unchanged from before (fenced_code_block etc. still present — the block grammar's output must not regress).
4. Host-file structural identity is unchanged by the inline grammar's presence: assert whatever the injection docs promise — the injected subtree has its own root and host preimages exclude it (there is an existing gate test `f7_injection_epoch_invalidation` in cli-lib; read it and add the markdown case following its shape if that is the established pattern).
5. Escaped backticks and double-backtick spans parse correctly (the grammar handles them; pin one case so a future "optimization" to hand-rolled scanning fails loudly).

## Constraints
- Base: release-hardening (your worktree HEAD — verify it contains [ley-line-open-080643] and [ley-line-open-db0920] commits).
- Branch: `feat/ley-line-open-ea1e42-markdown-inline`.

Do NOT run the full `task ci` — the machine is memory-constrained and the full gate runs on the integration branch afterward. Do not run rsry; do not write .beads/.

title: decade: living daemon — watch, reparse, notify, query
description:
The daemon should be a living process, not a one-shot parse. It watches source files, reparses incrementally on change, flips the arena, and notifies connected clients (mache) over the bidirectional UDS connection.

## What exists today
- Incremental parse (mtime+size diff, delete+reparse changed files)
- Arena load + auto-size
- UDS socket with structured query ops (list_children, find_callers, etc.)
- Event emitter (can push notifications to subscribers)
- Connection cache (invalidated on generation change)

## What's missing
1. **File watcher** — detect source changes in real-time (fsnotify or git status polling)
2. **Auto-reparse loop** — on file change, reparse affected files, flip arena, emit event
3. **Git-aware diff** — use git SHA as cache key, only reparse files in `git diff`
4. **Branch switch detection** — `git checkout` triggers bulk reparse of the delta
5. **Readiness signal** — `status` op returns parse state (parsing/ready/error)
6. **jj integration point** — LL's private VCS layer hooks into the reparse lifecycle via DaemonExt

## Architecture
```
file change → debounce (500ms) → incremental reparse → arena flip → event emission
                                                                          ↓
                                                              mache: generation changed
                                                              mache: invalidate cached conn
                                                              mache: next query reads new data
```

Git/jj are atomic snapshots. Each arena generation corresponds to a source state. The _meta table records the git SHA for that generation. Time-travel (jj) is LL's extension — LLO provides the reparse lifecycle, LL adds the VCS layer.

## Related beads (subsumed)
- ley-line-open-9b279e (git-aware incremental reparse)
- ley-line-open-9adb03 (readiness signal)
- ley-line-open-9af2c3 (progressive/streaming parse)
- ley-line-open-9b08e1 (priority queue)

title: nodes has no declared contract: kind claims file/dir while holding AST leaves, and record means three different things across two repos
description: CDC consumer harness exposed that nodes.kind=0 is repeatedly described as a file node even though the parsed projection uses it for readable structural leaves; source-file roots may be kind=1 with empty record. Misleading terminology appears in Graph::all_file_contents, embedding queries, docs, and tests and can cause consumers to select the wrong identity boundary. Audit and name the contract consistently (content leaf vs source file), document source_file discrimination, and add a schema/SQL smell or contract test if a machine-checkable predicate exists. Linked discovery from ley-line-open-f16e53.

comments.text:
PROMOTED to p1 and re-scoped 2026-07-27. This is not a clarity nit — it is the root cause of a measurement that characterized the wrong table, and it spans two repos.

## What is actually undeclared

TWO columns, not one.

`nodes.kind` is documented `0=file, 1=dir` — filesystem semantics — at rs/ll-core/schema/src/lib.rs:17 and graph.rs:118. The AST projection stores every AST LEAF as kind=0, so a node named `AGENTS.md/section/section_2/list/list_item_0/list_marker_dot` is a "file" whose content is the token text.

`nodes.record` has THREE live interpretations:

1. JSON envelope `{data, properties}` — mache graph/sqlite.go:162-175, json.Unmarshal into a struct with base64 values
2. Raw AST leaf token used directly — mache internal/ingest/ast_walker_calls.go:341, `SELECT n_leaf.record AS call_token`
3. Raw file/content bytes — LLO graph.rs write_content, `String::from_utf8_lossy(&content)`

And reader 1 is TOLERANT: `if err := json.Unmarshal(...); err == nil`. When an AST leaf's raw token reaches it, the parse fails and the node silently gets no Data and no Properties. No error, no log. A third repo hitting the same silence-as-absence trap.

Meanwhile graph.rs:544-549 documents the read path as "the nodes.record path: load the whole file, return a slice of it" — a shape NO producer creates. Verified: every production INSERT INTO nodes / UPDATE nodes SET record in the workspace writes tokens, not files.

## Why it is p1

Until this is declared, three separate things are unanswerable:

- What `read_content` is supposed to return, so graph.rs:544-549 cannot be corrected.
- What type `record` should be. It is declared `JSON`, which is wrong three ways (see f7966d): NUMERIC affinity coerces '007' to 7, the content is not JSON, and from_utf8_lossy mangles non-UTF-8. But the right type cannot be chosen for a column with three contracts — BLOB would break mache's json.Unmarshal and its LENGTH/SUBSTR usage.
- What CDC should chunk. The b5faa9 measurement found records average ~10 bytes against MIN_CHUNK 8,192, so the GearHash never fires and every dedup number on that target is arithmetic rather than evidence (see b6653a).

## The shape

This is ADR-0032's finding applied to ROW CONTENT rather than to addresses: an undeclared decomposition, N consumers, no field saying which. Same disease, one layer down, and it crosses the LLO/mache boundary so it needs coordinating rather than deciding unilaterally.

## What done looks like

A declared contract stating, per node kind, what `record` holds and how a consumer must interpret it — plus either a discriminator column or a kind vocabulary that distinguishes AST leaf from file from JSON-envelope. Then f7966d's type fix, graph.rs's doc, and CDC's target all follow mechanically.

Cross-repo: mache reads this column two different ways today, so the contract needs agreeing with mache rather than declaring at it.

comments.text:
FOURTH interpretation of nodes.record found 2026-07-27, via the feature-reachability gate.

I argued this bead on THREE readings. There are four.

`rs/ll-open/ts/src/pyproject.rs` — a 349-line dependency-graph projection, unwired and compiled out of every build (ley-line-open-988b93) — calls `leyline_schema::insert_node` storing PEP 508 VERSION SPECIFIER STRINGS:

    /deps/accelerate    record = ">=1.10.0"
    /dev/pytest         record = ">=9.0.2"

So the full set:

1. JSON envelope {data, properties}  — mache graph/sqlite.go:162-175
2. raw AST leaf token                — mache internal/ingest/ast_walker_calls.go:341
3. raw file/content bytes            — LLO graph.rs write_content
4. PEP 508 version specifier         — LLO ts/src/pyproject.rs

Four meanings, two repos, no discriminator column, and reader 1 fails SILENTLY on any of the other three.

Why this matters beyond arithmetic: the fourth arrived from a module NOBODY WIRED UP. An undeclared contract does not accumulate meanings through carelessness — it accumulates them because each author reasonably picked a representation for their own use, and nothing existed to disagree with. That is the mechanism, and it will keep operating until the contract exists.

It also sharpens what the contract has to cover. It is not 'is record a token or a file' — it is 'record is the content of a node, and node kinds are open-ended', which means the discriminator has to be extensible rather than an enum of two. `nodes.kind` currently claims 0=file/1=dir, and pyproject stores kind=1 for directory-shaped entries and kind=0 for leaves, reusing filesystem semantics for a dependency graph. That is a third projection shape reusing the same two-value vocabulary.

Also relevant to ley-line-open-f7966d: whatever type `record` becomes has to hold all four, or the contract has to split them into different columns/tables. TEXT holds all four today; BLOB would break mache's json.Unmarshal; capnp would break all of them.

title: Separate Σ segment identity from arena snapshot identity and SQL query ABI
description: The repo currently uses one `substrate`/`root` vocabulary for distinct domains: formal Σ (`Hash`, `BlobStore`, `RootPointer`), file-backed canonical Cap'n Proto segment identity (`Head.rootHash` over source/ast/bindings segments), daemon publication identity (`Controller.current_root` over sqlite3_serialize bytes), and the cross-runtime SQL query ABI consumed by mache. comments.text:
RESOLUTION SHAPE (2026-07-27, partition-algebra analysis).

The ADR no longer has an open design question — it has a result to record.

FINDING: the roots are not 'unlinked', they are INCOMMENSURABLE — hashes over different, undeclared partitions of the same value. Sigma defines naming but not partitioning: sigma is total on whole values, there is no partition operator and no law composing part-addresses into whole-addresses. Five layers each invented their own cut.

There is ONE composition operator (a tagged Merkle fold over a declared decomposition) but NO single lattice containing all five roots, provably: a 256-bit root cannot determine an n*256-bit leaf vector, so no universal root-to-root map exists. Refinement order induces NO maps between roots. Only WITNESSES compose, under an alignment law (root_B computable from A's leaf vector in O(#leaves) iff B's parts are unions of A's parts).

THREE irreducible structures, not four parallel roots:
1. integrity — BLAKE3's own intrinsic tree over fixed 1024-B chunks (position-BINDING). Root = current_root, unchanged.
2. dedup/transport — CDC chunks (position-INDEPENDENT) + set coarsenings. manifestRoot, hierarchyId.
3. logical view-validity — restriction folds over canonically-serialized rows. Not even a partition (closures overlap = a cover).

Structures 1 and 2 cannot be unified: position-binding is what makes BLAKE3 secure, position-independence is what makes dedup work. Forcing one means abandoning either sigma(v)=BLAKE3(v) or dedup.

DECISION TO RECORD: cross-structure binding is CO-ATTESTATION, not derivation. Head names all roots in one signed claim; consistency is RE-DERIVABLE by one linear pass, not assumed. Additive fields per ADR-0014 section 1, following the precedent already set by signature @5.

The pattern already exists correctly in-repo at exactly one site: head_digest (head_digest.rs:38-44) with its domain-separation test at lines 50-65. The work is generalizing it, not inventing it.

Downstream beads filed: PartitionSpec descriptor (b67a73), Head co-attestation (b68fa6), bao outboard (b6a4dd), prolly-tree research (b6ba16), Head framing defect (b64505), sheaf SHA-256 lock violation (b61cd6).

OPEN for the author: whether logicalRoot belongs in Head v1 or stays unbound until a restriction family ships.

That crate is the one legitimate exception to ADR-0032 D5 — canonical_kid is an interop identifier owned by signet ADR-012, not a substrate address — so the exception is now documented AND enforced, and silently broadening it fails CI.

VERIFIED THE GATE IS NOT DECORATION: injected each defect class and confirmed it fails — dangling decade, false count, cdc-as-canonical, new crate taking a sha2 dep. Four for four, clean after restore.

FINDINGS THAT ADR-0032 DOES NOT SETTLE, carried forward rather than decided here:
- D4 has no authority row for the Cap'n Proto segment root, though it ships and is signed. Written as a reading and labelled as such.
- manifestRoot and logicalRoot appear nowhere in rs/ — zero hits, they exist only in ADR-0032, while D3 says logicalRoot is required in v1. The authority table currently describes two unimplemented domains (b68fa6, d25f6e).

title: WAL adoption 15b: Mutex<Connection> → connection pool (enables concurrent readers)
description:
Sub-bead 15b of `ley-line-open-98fb67`. Depends on 15a (file-backed WAL, in flight as agent dispatch 2026-07-08).

## What 15b delivers (from parent bead)

Migrate `DaemonContext::live_db: Mutex<rusqlite::Connection>` → `DaemonContext::live_db: LiveDbPool` (or similar shape) so:

- **Readers check out a shared connection** from a pool of N reader-configured connections (`r2d2_sqlite` is a candidate; parking_lot-based hand-rolled works too)
- **Writers keep an exclusive dedicated writer connection** — no read contention on writes
- The `~30` (grep says 40+) call sites in `daemon/ops.rs` already migrated to `ctx.with_read` / `ctx.with_write` via bead `ba8294` Phase 2 (PR #137, merged 2026-07-08). **Sub-bead 15b is now a one-function change**: swap the impl of `with_read` from mutex-lock to pool-checkout; `with_write` keeps its exclusive-writer semantics.

## Load-bearing measurement

Empirical-validation report (`docs/research/2026-05-08-workerd-wal-sqlite-experiment.md`) H1 measured **p99 reads at 290-375 µs on file-backed WAL@N=10 readers + 1 writer** vs **120-250 ms p99 on DELETE-journal** — ~600× improvement. WAL@N=10 absolute throughput beats DELETE-solo by 3×.

**15a (file-backed WAL)** unlocks the WAL half; **15b (pool)** unlocks the concurrent-readers half. Without 15b, all readers still serialize on `ctx.with_read`'s mutex — the 600× is unrealized.

## What 15b does NOT deliver

- **NO change to op semantics** — reads still read, writes still write
- **NO change to `with_read` / `with_write` call sites** in `daemon/ops.rs` — the intent-marking is already correct; only the impl swaps
- **NO write concurrency** — SQLite WAL still serializes writers; the writer connection is exclusive by design
- **NO backpressure or queue** for the writer — that's a future refinement if writer contention becomes a real bottleneck

## Design questions to resolve before implementation

1. **Pool size**: N=10 was the bench config. Should the daemon pick N dynamically based on `available_parallelism()` or use a fixed default? Fixed default seems fine; bench showed diminishing returns above 10.
2. **Pool crate choice**: `r2d2_sqlite` is production-battle-tested. Alternative: hand-rolled `parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<Connection>>` for zero new dep. Recommend r2d2 for maintenance sanity.
3. **Reader pragmas**: each pool connection needs `PRAGMA query_only=ON` (or equivalent) so writes fail-loud on a reader connection. Currently `with_read` and `with_write` are structurally identical; 15b makes them structurally different.
4. **Writer connection lifecycle**: single dedicated connection held by `DaemonContext` from startup to shutdown; separate from the pool.

## Close condition

- Pool implementation lands with the pragmas + size + writer-separate architecture above
- `with_read` calls now checkout from pool; `with_write` uses the dedicated writer
- Integration test spawns N readers + 1 writer concurrently and measures throughput — must reproduce the bench's 600× p99 read win (within some CI-variance tolerance, e.g. 10×)
- All existing tests pass unchanged (behavior on the ops.rs side is intent-preserving)
- `task ci` green

## Files

- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/daemon/mod.rs (DaemonContext + LiveDbPool + with_read/with_write impls)
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/src/cmd_daemon.rs (init_living_db creates pool + writer connection instead of single mutex)
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/Cargo.toml (add r2d2 + r2d2_sqlite if that's the chosen route)
- rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/wal_pool_concurrent_readers_daemon_test.rs (new integration test)

## Depends on

- `ley-line-open-98fb67` sub-bead 15a (file-backed WAL) must land first — see agent dispatch 2026-07-08
- `ley-line-open-ba8294` Phase 2 (with_read/with_write helpers) landed via PR #137 ✓

## Provenance

- Parent bead 98fb67 explicitly names 15a + 15b as the two-step migration
- ba8294 Phase 2 was widened partly to unblock 15b by making the read/write intent structural at the call site
- 15a agent dispatch 2026-07-08 does file-backed + pragmas only; 15b captured here so it's discoverable rather than buried in 98fb67's description
acceptance_criteria: Pool + separate writer implemented; with_read routes to pool checkout; with_write routes to dedicated writer; integration test with N concurrent readers + 1 writer reproduces bench's throughput win (within CI tolerance); existing tests pass unchanged; task ci green

title: Perf gates race on LLO_PERF_GATES: env-mutating sanity test arms a release-calibrated ceiling inside a debug build
description:
Root cause of the `task ci` failure on main at 3752ce6 (job cli-lib:test:vec, run 31848026749).

## Mechanism

`cli-lib:test:vec` runs `cargo test -p leyline-cli-lib --features vec` — a DEBUG build with LLO_PERF_GATES unset, so the cold-parse gate should skip. It did not. Its sibling test in the same binary did:

    unsafe { std::env::set_var("LLO_PERF_GATES", "1"); }

justified by the comment:

    // Safety: tests in this file run in serial wrt this env var because
    // only this test mutates it; the real gate test only reads it.

One writer plus a concurrent reader is not serialization. Cargo runs the tests in a binary on parallel threads and the environment is process-global, so the gate's `perf_gate_enabled()` read landed inside the write window, armed, and asserted a ceiling calibrated for --release against a debug measurement.

## Numbers

CI failure (debug):   wall=580ms  per_row=15us   (ceilings: wall<500ms, per_row<25us)
Measured release:     wall=131ms  per_row=3us

The profile-independent per_row assertion passed with 40% headroom in the very run that failed — only the absolute wall ceiling tripped. A 4.4x build-profile gap against a ceiling carrying 1.15x headroom.

PR #304's 635ms failure has the same signature and was attributed to runner noise; the min-of-three-runs mitigation in the gate was added for that misdiagnosis.

## Second site

topology_pass_test.rs carries the identical racy shape with TIGHTER budgets. Its comment claims the only risk would be 'a *different* test also touching LLO_PERF_GATES, which none of the gate1* tests do' — but gate1a/gate1b/gate1c all call perf_gate_enabled(). They are the concurrent readers.

## Fix

Both files split a pure `gate_enabled_from(Option<&str>) -> bool` out of `perf_gate_enabled()`; the sanity tests check that directly. No test mutates the environment, so the race is removed rather than arbitrated, and both unsafe blocks go with it. The cold-parse gate additionally hard-skips under debug_assertions since both ceilings are release numbers.

Sibling defect already fixed once in this repo via #[serial(...)]: ley-line-open-d71cf6 (daemon/sheaf_ablation.rs, PR #184). That route fit there because production code reads the env; here the predicate is separable.

comments.text:
Acceptance met by PR #356, merged to main in the #361 promotion.

Neither cold_parse_perf_regression.rs nor topology_pass_test.rs mutates the process environment any more — both split a pure gate_enabled_from(Option<&str>) out of perf_gate_enabled() and the sanity tests check that directly, so the race is removed rather than arbitrated. Both unsafe blocks went with it.

Verified in both directions: a debug build with LLO_PERF_GATES=1 now skips with an actionable message instead of asserting a release-calibrated ceiling, and task test:perf still arms and passes in release (wall=131ms, per_row=3us).

Confirmed fixed in production, not just locally: main's CI had been red since 2026-08-14 on exactly this failure. The #361 promotion run (32272393665) is green.

title: node_defs: add canonical_kind column — closes mache dead_code / god_file rule parity
description:

## Symptom

Mache observed `dead_code = 321` on the LLO projection vs tree-sitter's `5`. Root cause: LLO's `node_defs` emits defs for every module-level named binding in Rust (functions, methods, types, mods, consts, statics) — mache-schema only exports functions/methods/types. title: ADR-0024: emit _cfg/_dfg/_taint fact tables — incremental dataflow/taint via differential-dataflow driven by the sheaf
description:
Producer-side implementation of mache ADR-0024 (docs/adr/0024-incremental-dataflow-taint-as-substrate-queries.md in the mache repo). The ADR decides the incremental dataflow/taint ENGINE lives here in LLO (Rust), not in mache's pure-Go/no-CGO projector: LLO computes the fixpoint and MATERIALIZES fact tables that mache reads read-only via WITH RECURSIVE.

Scope (sequenced; each is a shippable sub-bead):
1. `_cfg` — intra-procedural control-flow graph emitted from `_ast`. The control-flow nodes are already identified (mache counts if/for/case for cyclomatic_complexity); build per-language CFG edges (entry/exit, branch, loop back-edge, switch).
2. `_dfg` — variable-level intra-procedural def-use edges (not the current declaration-granularity node_defs/node_refs). SSA-lite or use-def chains.
3. `_taint` — a small rule set (source / sink / barrier / additional-step, per CodeQL's isSource/isSink/isBarrier/isAdditionalFlowStep shape) run over `_dfg`, materialized as reachability/edge facts. Barriers pre-applied as filtered edges so mache's projector needs only POSITIVE recursion (avoids SQLite's mutual/non-linear recursion ceiling).
4. INCREMENTAL: run the fixpoint in differential-dataflow (Rust), driven by the EXISTING daemon sheaf (sheaf_ops.rs — regions + restriction edges + δ⁰ invalidation → structurally affected neighbors). Map node_hash-change → differential-dataflow collection delta. Follow Soufflé's ELASTIC lesson: choose Bootstrap (full recompute) vs Update (incremental) by change impact — do NOT ship an always-incremental engine (incremental is not universally faster for large-impact changes).

Contract with mache = the _cfg/_dfg/_taint table schema; version it like the ADR-0023/0026 fact IR.

Open questions (from the ADR's research): (a) can the current tree-sitter pipeline cheaply produce intra-procedural CFG + variable-level def-use? (b) concrete node_hash-change → differential-dataflow-delta mapping; (c) whether barriers can always be pre-applied as filtered edges (so mache needs no stratified negation / Mangle).

DEPENDS ON ley-line-open-caf423 (extraction fidelity: real def/ref across languages, qualified method tokens, populated source_file) — the dataflow facts are only as good as the base extraction.

Close condition: LLO emits _cfg + _dfg + _taint tables for a Go/Rust fixture with a known source→sink taint path (and a sanitized non-path), incrementally updated via the sheaf on an edit, and mache can answer a taint-reachability query over them. Verify with a producer test (parse → assert tables) + a mache WITH RECURSIVE query test.

comments.text: Cross-repo status correction (2026-07-30, prompted by mache's ADR-0024 proximity assessment): mache's gap 1 ('No CFG at all — neither mache nor LLO emits one') is stale. LLO's CFG layer exists: leyline_ts::cfg (cfg.rs), _cfg/_cfg_edge DDL shipped v0.7.2 (TABLE_CONTRACT §_cfg — basic blocks keyed (node_hash, block_id), reflow-invariant via merkle-AST, CFG_CANONICAL_KINDS, complexity column). The honest gap is POPULATION: schema empty on parse output until a0fadd wires emit_cfg_for_source into cmd_parse's rayon/batched-insert plumbing — consumers can call it directly today. So the mache-visible dataflow ladder is: (1) CFG = one wiring bead (a0fadd), not a build; (2) variable-level def-use/SSA = T2 series fully decomposed and unstarted (476afe dominance → 47891e local vars → 47a26a SSA rename+phi → 47c1f1 _dfg DDL); (3) extraction fidelity = the caf423 class concluded into the open thread 651909 (Go consts/selector args) + 63cb83 (tags.scm audit) + 23377a (namespace qualification). 'How close': one small bead from mache being able to QUERY a populated CFG; a real T2 ladder from actual dataflow facts.

title: Add license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later" to leyline-core + leyline-cas-ffi (cloister cargo-deny block)
description:
## Problem

Cloister's `task verify` runs `cargo deny check` over the full Rust closure including LLO crates pulled in via the wasm32 BLAKE3 FFI (cloister-713b4e). Two LLO crates lack `license` fields, so cargo-deny's `licenses` check fails:

```
error[unlicensed]: leyline-core = 0.4.5 is unlicensed
error[unlicensed]: leyline-cas-ffi = 0.4.5 is unlicensed
```

LLO is AGPL-3.0-or-later per the root LICENSE; `leyline-text-search/Cargo.toml` already declares this. Other LLO crates inherited the unlicensed default — fine for in-repo use, breaks downstream cargo-deny.

## Fix

Add `license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"` to:
- `rs/ll-core/core/Cargo.toml` (leyline-core)
- `rs/ll-open/cas-ffi/Cargo.toml` (leyline-cas-ffi)

Both crates `cargo check` clean after the addition.
