- Cloister consumer: `cloister-713b4e` (CAS FFI consumption — closed)
- `leyline-text-search/Cargo.toml` (already declares this license — pattern)

## Followup

After this lands + LLO ships a new commit, cloister bumps the git-rev pin in `rs/crates/cas/Cargo.toml:21` to point at the new SHA. Tracked under `cloister-eefd45`.

## Acceptance

- Both manifests declare `license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"`
- `cargo check` clean
- Downstream cargo-deny stops emitting `unlicensed` errors for these crates

title: leyline-fs default features invert the risk: cargo test silently skips CDC, compiles system deps
description:
Observed 2026-07-27 while working b5e56f/b61cd6.

## The inversion

rs/ll-open/fs/Cargo.toml: `default = [\"validate\", \"fuse\", \"nfs\"]`. `cdc` and `splice` are opt-in.

So the obvious command — `cargo test -p leyline-fs` — does two wrong things at once:

1. Compiles `fuse` + `nfs`, which pull `fuser`/`nfsserve` and require a system libfuse. On a machine without it the build fails before any test runs. This is why `cargo check --workspace` fails on this repo today.
2. Silently omits `cdc` and `splice`, so every chunked-content test is ABSENT rather than failing. The read path, the manifest tiling invariants, the freshness witness, and the whole invalidation discipline go untested and the run still reports green.

The pure-Rust logic carrying the correctness invariants is opt-in; the system-dependency-heavy mount backends are on by default. That is backwards.

## It has already caused a real miss

Taskfile.yml records it directly: \"`splice` is REQUIRED here, not incidental: the manifest-staleness tests ... are gated on it. Without `splice` the invalidation logic is never exercised — mutation testing caught exactly that, with two live mutants in `invalidate_chunked_content`.\"

So the default feature set produced surviving mutants in the invalidation path, and the fix was to teach every invocation a four-flag incantation rather than to change the default.

## Why the incantation is not a fix

`cargo test -p leyline-fs --no-default-features --features cdc,splice,validate` is required for a correct run and appears in mutants:fs, mutants:fs-gc, and the fs test target. It is discoverable only from a Taskfile comment. Any contributor, agent, or IDE test-runner invoking the crate the normal way gets a green run over a configuration nobody ships. The safe path is not the default path — the same class of defect as b5e56f (dead manifests) and the partition set-malleability: correct behavior available but not structural.

## Proposed shape

`default = [\"validate\", \"cdc\", \"splice\"]`; `fuse` and `nfs` become opt-in, selected by the mount binaries and by CI targets that actually exercise a mount. Then:

- the bare command tests the logic
- no system dependency is needed to build or test the crate
- `cargo check --workspace` works again
- the Taskfile targets lose their incantation, which is the taskfile-ci-parity principle: CI should invoke a target, not re-specify a configuration

Check whether any consumer depends on leyline-fs with default features expecting a mount backend; if so they name `fuse`/`nfs` explicitly, which is the correct dependency declaration anyway.

## Close condition

cargo test -p leyline-fs (no flags) on a machine without libfuse, chunked suites present and passing.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to this bead's framing, and a widening of scope.

The description implies the RELEASE BINARY carries leyline-fs's default features. It does not. `leyline-cli-lib`'s own default is ["lsp","validate","hdc","cdc"], where cdc -> leyline-fs/cdc and validate -> leyline-fs/validate. `mount` (fuse+nfs) is opt-in via release:mount / install:full. So the shipped binary gets leyline-fs {cdc, validate} and no mount backends.

What remains TRUE and is the real defect: `cargo test -p leyline-fs` with no flags uses leyline-fs's OWN defaults {validate, fuse, nfs}, which is a configuration NO consumer has. So the crate's declared defaults describe a usage that does not exist, a developer running the obvious command tests a fiction, and the CDC suites are silently absent from that run.

THE WIDER PROBLEM — four configurations, none of them both shipped and tested:

| config | shipped | tested |
|---|---|---|
| {validate, fuse, nfs} — leyline-fs defaults | no | yes, cargo test --workspace |
| {cdc, splice, validate} — the CI incantation | no (cli-lib never enables splice) | yes, dedicated fs target |
| {cdc, validate} — the release binary | YES | not as a unit |
| {fuse, nfs, validate} — mount | yes, via install:full | BUILT only, never run |

Two are tested but never shipped; two are shipped but never tested.

Sharpest exposure is mount. install:full hands users FUSE and NFS, and the Taskfile only ever runs `cargo build --features mount`. A build-only nfs-isolation check exists, added after ley-line-open-95cd90 — the Taskfile calls it "an nfs-only libc bug that the default build masked." That class already bit once and the response was a build check rather than a test.

Second signal worth acting on: `splice` is tested and never shipped. cli-lib has no splice reference at all. Either the manifest-invalidation path genuinely needs it — in which case the release binary is missing it and that is a correctness question, not a packaging one — or it does not, and it should be removed per the remove-don't-deprecate policy. A feature whose only role is making a test pass is not a feature.

REVISED FIX SHAPE — not "test every combination" (four flags is sixteen, which is untestable and would produce a CI run nobody waits for) but REDUCE the space, then test what survives:

1. Resolve splice: promote to default or delete. Decide by asking whether {cdc, validate} without splice still invalidates manifests correctly.
2. Make leyline-fs's defaults match a real consumer, so the bare command tests something that exists.
3. Add a test target for the release configuration as a unit.
4. Test mount, or stop shipping it in install:full.

Item 1 gates the rest, because it may be a shipped-correctness bug rather than a test-hygiene one.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: `cargo test -p leyline-fs` with no flags compiles and runs the chunked/CDC and splice test suites, and does not require libfuse or any system dependency. The Taskfile's fs targets stop carrying `--no-default-features --features cdc,splice,validate`. Verified by running the bare command on a machine without libfuse installed and confirming the chunked test count matches the current flagged invocation (116 lib tests at time of filing).

title: Restore 3 schema-spec enforcements lost in cloister→LLO move (version-bump gate + Python conformance + capability-mapping coverage)
description:
Post-merge audit of cloister PR #120 (bead `cloister-a77222`, merged 2026-07-09) surfaced that LLO's `verify_vectors_sha256` cargo test is only 1 of 3 enforcements that cloister-side removed. Two ecosystem-level gates + one lint disappeared with the deletion of cloister-spec/ but were NOT re-established upstream in LLO's `leyline-schema-spec` crate.

## The three coverage gaps

### Gap 1: Version-bump-on-vector-change

Cloister's deleted `.github/workflows/credential-isolation-spec-drift.yml` job #2 checked: when `credential-isolation/v1/vectors/*` files change, the spec's `README.md` MUST also be touched (semver discipline). LLO's `verify_vectors_sha256` (108 lines) only re-hashes vectors — no diff-vs-base, no README.md touch check.

**What to ship in LLO**: add a `version_bump_on_vector_change` test that runs in CI, detects when a vector file changed since the last version-tagged commit, and fails if the corresponding `README.md` didn't change.

### Gap 2: Python ref-impl conformance runner

The `credential-isolation/v1/ref-impl-py/conformance/run.py` (432 lines) is byte-identical to what cloister shipped, but nothing in `rs/ll-core/schema-spec/tests/` or LLO's `Taskfile.yml` invokes it. Cloister's deleted `.github/workflows/credential-isolation-spec-drift.yml` job #3 ran it as a spec-authorship guard.

**What to ship in LLO**: a task (e.g., `task schema-spec:conformance`) that runs each capability's ref-impl `conformance/run.py`. Wire into CI. Same for future ref-impls in other languages.

### Gap 3: `_capability-mapping.md` §4 coverage lint

Cloister's `lint:capability-mapping-coverage` verified every `<name>/v<n>/` directory has a lane-3 (`cloister/<name>/v<n>`) identifier row in the mapping doc. Prevents "capability spec ships without a canonical identifier."

**What to ship in LLO**: a Rust lint (or small script) that walks `rs/ll-core/schema-spec/*/v*/` and asserts each has a matching row in `_capability-mapping.md`. Small; probably a build-time test.

## Why now

Filed 2026-07-09 as part of "never partial close" discipline — cloister PR #120 merged but the coverage claim in CHANGELOG.md overstates what upstream actually enforces. This bead closes the loop.

## What this bead does NOT deliver

- **NO cloister-side changes** — cloister's follow-up (fix CHANGELOG wording, pin doc URLs to stable ref, clean up scripts/*.mjs rewrite artifacts) is a separate bead in cloister scope
- **NO spec content changes** — only enforcement infrastructure
- **NO retroactive vector re-authorship** — existing pins stay pinned

## Rules

- Commit prefix `[ley-line-open-<this-bead-id>]`
- `task ci` green with all three new enforcements
- Prefer Rust tests over shell scripts (LLO discipline: cargo test is the enforcement surface)

## Related

- `cloister-a77222` (merged) — the move
- Cloister-side follow-up bead (to be filed) — fix CHANGELOG + doc URL pins + rewrite artifacts

## Provenance

- pr-reviewer verdict on cloister PR #120 2026-07-09 (agent `a4cd0b177023e3154`)
- User directive: "our testing missing this is a concern" — this bead is the LLO-side of that discipline

## Related

- `ley-line-open-729a7e` — schema-spec move to LLO (LLO-side tracker)
- `cloister-a77222` — cloister-side deletion (merged)
- `ley-line-open-e76959` — producer/consumer contract test discipline (related meta-lesson)
acceptance_criteria: 3 enforcements land in LLO: version-bump-on-vector-change test, Python ref-impl conformance runner task + CI wire, capability-mapping coverage lint; all pass in task ci; cloister's CHANGELOG can then be updated with accurate coverage claim

title: nodes.record is declared JSON, which gives SQLite NUMERIC affinity — the authoritative table silently corrupts numeric-looking tokens
description:
Found 2026-07-27 by the b5faa9 measurement harness, which could not activate CDC on ANY real corpus until the damage was repaired in a scratch copy.

## The defect

`rs/ll-core/schema/src/lib.rs:39` declares `record JSON`. SQLite assigns affinity by substring match: a declared type containing none of INT, CHAR, CLOB, TEXT, BLOB, REAL, FLOA, DOUB gets NUMERIC affinity. \"JSON\" contains none of them. So `nodes.record` has NUMERIC affinity and silently coerces any value that looks like a number.

Verified directly:

    CREATE TABLE t (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, record JSON);
    '007'   -> stored 7      typeof=integer  length 3 -> 1
    '1. '   -> stored 1      typeof=integer  length 3 -> 1
    '3.14'  -> stored 3.14   typeof=real     length 4 -> 4
    'hello' -> stored 'hello' typeof=text    length 5 -> 5

This is NOT a CDC bug. `nodes.record` is the authoritative cross-runtime contract — leyline-schema's own words, \"mache writes it, leyline-fs reads it\" — so the corruption is in the substrate's most load-bearing table and applies to every consumer, whether or not CDC is enabled.

## Measured blast radius (b5faa9 harness, three real corpora)

| corpus | eligible leaves | typeof=integer | typeof=real | byte-length changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mache | 391,556 | 9,332 | 113 | 1,143 |
| rosary | 208,195 | 4,572 | 164 | 807 |
| LLO | 254,472 | 9,669 | 166 | 801 |

~9,400 leaves per corpus read back with the wrong SQLite type; ~800-1,100 read back with the wrong LENGTH, i.e. actual byte loss. A markdown list marker \"1. \" becomes the integer 1.

## It also blocks a shipped command

`leyline cdc enable` aborts on the first length change:

    node AGENTS.md/section/.../list_marker_dot size 3 does not match 1 record bytes

Activation's `size == record.len()` guard is doing its job — failing closed on inconsistent state — but the inconsistency is upstream in the DDL. So the shipped CDC activation path cannot complete on any real corpus.

## Why it was never caught

Every existing activation test constructs `record TEXT` by hand rather than using `NODES_TABLE_DDL`. The fixtures drifted from the contract they are supposed to exercise, so the tests were green against a schema nobody ships. Same class as ley-line-open-f327e1 (default features skip the CDC suites) and ley-line-open-c45244 (mutation gates blind to SQL): the tested configuration is not the shipped one.

## Fix

`record JSON` -> `record TEXT` in NODES_TABLE_DDL and every mirror (rs/ll-open/ts/src/schema.rs has its own copies), plus a producer that binds bytes rather than relying on affinity. TEXT affinity stores the value as given.

Cross-repo: mache writes this column, so the DDL change wants coordinating — but note that mache is currently READING corrupted values too, so the fix strictly improves both sides. Existing databases carry the damage and need a reparse; the numeric-looking leaves cannot be recovered from the projection because the original bytes are gone.

Add a regression test that inserts a numeric-looking token through NODES_TABLE_DDL and asserts typeof()='text' — it fails today.

## Close condition

cargo test -p leyline-fs --no-default-features --features cdc,splice,validate, plus the round-trip assertions in acceptance_criteria, plus `leyline cdc enable` completing on a real corpus without repair.

comments.text: Auto-closed by rsry close-merged --local: PR #281 merged
comments.author: rosary

acceptance_criteria: Inserting the leaf tokens '007', '1. ', and '3.14' into nodes.record reads back byte-identical with typeof()='text' and unchanged length. `leyline cdc enable` completes on the mache, rosary, and ley-line-open corpora without size-witness repair. A regression test asserts typeof(record)='text' for a numeric-looking token, and fails against the current DDL.

title: publish-crates.yml runs `task` before installing it — fails at every tag, exit 127
description:
`publish-crates.yml` failed on the v0.19.0 tag, ~1 second in, before touching
crates.io:

    Install system deps
      task deps:ci
      /home/runner/work/_temp/....sh: line 1: task: command not found
      ##[error]Process completed with exit code 127

The "Install system deps" step invokes `task deps:ci`, but nothing has installed
Task on the runner at that point. Every other workflow that uses `task` installs
it first; this one does not.

Worth being precise about what this is NOT: it is not a credentials or Trusted
Publishing problem. The job never got far enough to authenticate — the earlier
expectation that publishing would need four manual `cargo publish` runs under
the maintainer's credentials was not tested by this run, and remains unverified
either way.

Not urgent — crates are not being published right now (maintainer, 2026-08-21).
But it fails identically on every future tag, and a release-time failure is the
worst moment to discover an install step is missing, so it should be fixed
before the next tag rather than during it.

Fix: add the same Task install step the other workflows use, ahead of
`task deps:ci`. Then re-run the workflow against the existing v0.19.0 tag to
confirm it gets far enough to exercise Trusted Publishing — which is also the
cheapest way to settle whether the credentials question is real.

v0.19.0 itself is fine: the tag is pushed, `Release` succeeded with 33 assets,
and `Sync integration` succeeded. Only crate publishing is affected.
acceptance_criteria: publish-crates.yml installs Task before invoking `task deps:ci`; re-running the workflow against the v0.19.0 tag gets past Install system deps and reaches the cargo publish step, confirming whether Trusted Publishing authenticates.

title: Expose ll-open validate as a daemon op (mache writeback CGO-removal dependency)
description: mache's writeback path (internal/writeback/validate.go) syntax-checks edits via CGO tree-sitter before commit. This is item 5 of mache-36d961 (eliminate CGO tree-sitter). The Rust validator already exists at ll-open/fs/src/validate.rs; expose it as a UDS daemon op + capnp payload (validate(lang, bytes) -> {ok, diagnostics[]}) so mache calls it over the socket/arena instead of linking tree-sitter. Without this, writeback keeps CGO and mache cannot become pure-Go. Pairs with mache-36d961 (consumer side). Thread: llo-arena-feed / decade: mache-pure-go-arena (proposed).

title: WAL adversarial: subprocess-isolated ENOSPC/RLIMIT_FSIZE test
description:
Deferred half of bead `ley-line-open-0cdf2d`. Filed 2026-07-08 during that bead's implementation.

## Why this couldn't ship inline

`RLIMIT_FSIZE` is process-scoped. `cargo test` runs integration tests as threads in one process. `tokio::test` with `flavor = "multi_thread"` spawns concurrent runtimes. Any in-process cap on `RLIMIT_FSIZE` leaks to sibling tests that spawn daemons concurrently, causing them to fail against the artificially low quota.

Attempted RAII Drop guard restores original limit at test end, but siblings running IN PARALLEL still see the cap during their execution.

## What this bead delivers

A subprocess-isolated ENOSPC test. Approaches, from cheapest to most robust:

**A. Fork + exec self via `std::process::Command::new(env::current_exe())`** with an env var flag to select just the ENOSPC test. Standard Rust integration-test pattern. Zero new deps. Only downside: re-invokes cargo's test binary, so the child re-runs the runtime init.

**B. Ship a dedicated helper binary** in `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/bin/wal_enospc_helper.rs` (with `[[bin]]` entry in Cargo.toml). Parent uses `Command::spawn`. Child does the cap + boot, exits with a status code. Parent asserts. Cleanest isolation; small `Cargo.toml` change.

**C. `libc::fork` + minimal child that boots the daemon.** Matches F1 crash-test pattern. Complicated by tokio needing to init in the child.

Recommend **A** (subprocess re-invocation with an env flag).

## What the test proves

**Claim**: under an aggressive `RLIMIT_FSIZE` cap (e.g., 4 KiB), a fresh daemon boot in a fresh dir returns Err rather than panicking or silently succeeding. After lifting the cap, boots recover cleanly.

**Assertions**:
- Constrained boot returns Err (or exits with non-zero if the harness is subprocess-based)
- Post-cap boot in fresh dir succeeds

## Provenance

- Parent bead `0cdf2d` — WAL adversarial (ENOSPC + bloat)
- Parent's WAL bloat test shipped inline; the ENOSPC half punted here
- Gate bead `fd07d8` — adversarial testing sweep (closed 2026-07-08 with this as documented deferral)
acceptance_criteria: Subprocess-isolated ENOSPC test lands; test suite doesn't leak RLIMIT to sibling tests; assertion proves daemon returns Err under quota + recovers cleanly post-cap

title: LSP readiness depends on upstream servers' human-readable progress titles
description:
`LspClient::await_ready` decides a language server is ready by substring-matching
its `$/progress` title against `"indexing"`, `"loading"`, `"ready"`
(case-insensitive). Those are human-readable UI strings owned by upstream
servers, not part of any contract we can hold them to.

Today it works because the strings happen to line up — rust-analyzer emits
`"rust-analyzer/Indexing"`, gopls `"setting up workspace"`. Upstream can rename
either in a patch release without it being a breaking change for them, and
nothing here would fail loudly. Readiness would silently never flip, the
deadline would expire, `await_ready` would return `false`, and queries would
come back empty or partial. That reads as "the index is cold", not "our matcher
stopped matching" — which is the expensive kind of wrong.

## Why this is worth a bead rather than a shrug

The failure is degradation, not deadlock, so it is genuinely lower severity than
`ley-line-open-cdd5d0`. But it is the same CLASS: depending on a signal that is
not part of any contract. And this exact shape has already bitten once — the
comment in `await_ready` records that gopls will not emit progress at all until
its `window/workDoneProgress/create` request is acked, so the client has to
answer server->client requests WHILE polling or the readiness signal never
arrives (mache-6584a0).

## What is already sound, and should not be changed chasing this

- Framing is Content-Length, so the LSP path has no EOF dependence and cannot
  hit the `cdd5d0` bug.
- The spawn uses no `pre_exec`, so it takes `posix_spawn`.
- `await_ready` is deadline-bounded and returns `false` rather than hanging.
- `shutdown` is request -> notify -> timeout -> `kill()`, and does not rely on
  stdin EOF either.

## Suggested direction

Prefer `experimental/serverStatus` where a server supports it — it is a status
signal rather than a UI string. Keep the title heuristic as a fallback, and add
a test that pins the known-good titles per server so a rename fails HERE, at a
named assertion, instead of silently downgrading every query that follows.
acceptance_criteria: Readiness prefers a structured signal (experimental/serverStatus) where available, with the title heuristic as documented fallback; a test pins the known-good progress titles per server so an upstream rename fails at a named assertion rather than silently degrading queries to empty.

title: Adversarial testing sweep for in-flight storage-layer changes (WAL 15a, pointer store, region diff)
description:
2026-07-08: four agents in flight touching storage-layer invariants (WAL migration, pointer store dual-write, region diff, mache subscription). Each was given happy-path test requirements. This bead enforces adversarial test coverage at PR review — the "how SQLite is tested" mindset (https://www.sqlite.org/testing.html) scaled to what our budget can support: **at least one adversarial edge-case test per load-bearing invariant.**

## Load-bearing invariants + required tests

### WAL 15a (`ley-line-open-98fb67`)

Invariant: existing snapshot + `sqlite3_serialize` still works under WAL.

- **[F1 reuse]** — the existing F1 falsification test (`f1_crash_mid_write.rs` from bead 9e7a9d) MUST cover the new file-backed WAL path. If it currently tests only `:memory:` behavior, extend or duplicate. Crash-during-WAL-write must leave a recoverable state.
- **[Disk-full during snapshot]** — inject an ENOSPC on the snapshot write path; assert daemon fails loud, doesn't corrupt existing arena.
- **[WAL bloat / checkpoint failure]** — force `wal_autocheckpoint=0`, run enough writes to grow the WAL, assert startup can still recover.
- **[Restart across corrupted WAL]** — write valid data, truncate the `.live.db-wal` file to a byte, restart, assert either clean recovery or clean failure — never silent corruption.

### Pointer store 3e87ad (`ley-line-open-3e87ad`)

Invariant: dual-write is transactional — both schemas advance together or not at all.

- **[Transaction atomicity]** — inject a failure between the `_ast` INSERT and the `_ast_pointer` INSERT. Assert both rollback (neither table has the file's rows) — no split-brain schemas.
- **[Same-file re-parse dedup]** — parse a file twice; assert `capnp_blobs` has ONE row for that file's blob, not two.
- **[Cross-file blob dedup]** — set up two source files with byte-identical ASTs (e.g., two empty files, or two files with an identical function). Assert `capnp_blobs` has ONE blob shared by both files' pointer rows.
- **[Large-blob handling]** — parse a source file whose canonical `List(AstNode)` blob exceeds the 8 KiB first-segment default that panicked v0.5.7 (bead 661727). Reuse the `write_canonical_message` helper. Assert no panic.
- **[F1 round-trip on 100+ files]** — extend the F1 test from 3-5 files to ≥100 to catch batching bugs.

### Fine-grained region diff e40566 (`ley-line-open-e40566`)

Invariant: `region_ids` is precisely the regions touched by `changed_files`.

- **[Multi-region file]** — a file that provides observations to 3+ regions. Payload's `region_ids` must contain all 3, not just the first.
- **[Zero-region file]** — a file that provides no observations to any region (e.g., a config file matched by CDC but with no code). Payload behavior must be documented + tested — probably skip the emit or emit with empty `region_ids` + `scope: "no-touched-regions"`.
- **[Stale file→region map]** — modify a file such that some regions it USED to touch are gone (function deleted) and some regions it now touches are new. Payload should include BOTH sets (or explicit design decision documented).
- **[Fallback to coarse]** — force the file→region map into an "unknown" state (e.g., pre-first-topology-set). Payload must fall back to `scope: "all-known"` cleanly.

### Mache SheafSubscriber e4c4ea (`mache-e4c4ea`)

Invariant: eviction actually fires end-to-end.

- **[Eviction actually fires]** — not just "subscriber received event." Assert the sheaf-scoped cache entry is GONE after the event fires. If mache's cache has no visible-from-test state, add a test-only accessor.
- **[Unknown scope safe]** — as spec'd; verify unknown value logs warning + defaults to coarse (over-invalidate).
- **[Concurrent query race]** — a query mid-flight during an invalidate. The query must either see the pre-invalidate state OR the post-invalidate state, never a torn view.
- **[Malformed payload]** — missing required field, wrong type. Subscriber must log + skip, never crash.

## Enforcement mechanism

- Every in-flight agent PR is subject to this bead at review time
- If a PR is missing one or more of the above tests, it does NOT merge until the tests are added
- The reviewing agent (me) requests changes with a link to this bead
- Post-merge, the bead closes only when all four agents' PRs have added their required adversarial tests OR the invariant has been reclassified as covered by a different test (e.g., an existing F-gate)

## Non-goals

- Do NOT rebuild sqlite's TCL harness. We're not sqlite. Aim for one adversarial case per load-bearing invariant, not exhaustive.
- Do NOT block on infrastructure that doesn't exist (e.g., ENOSPC injection may need a filesystem-mock helper — if so, ship the helper as part of the WAL 15a PR).

## Provenance

- 2026-07-08: user flagged "we gotta be v thorough in our testing with this shit" while 4 agents were mid-work on storage-layer changes
- SQLite testing philosophy reference: https://www.sqlite.org/testing.html
- Applies to LLO PRs #143+ (the four in-flight agent branches)

It set a discipline that every in-flight PR added ≥1 adversarial case per load-bearing invariant. Not sqlite-level (~590:1 test/code), but a step up from happy-path-only.

title: Measure F1w/F2w with a jj-workspace arm — decides whether ADR-0029 Phase 1 is superseded or unproven
description:
Raised from a mache-side review of the ADR-0029 status assessment (2026-07-23). Blocks a sound decision on `ley-line-open-de3f81` (ADR-0029 Phase 1).

## The error this corrects

`VcsIntegration::add_workspace` (rs/ll-open/vcs/src/lib.rs, PR #253) shipped a doc comment claiming jj multi-workspace gives "worktree semantics ... without the N× disk cost of `git worktree add`". That was ASSERTED, NEVER MEASURED — and it is very likely wrong on the axis that matters: the impl uses `LocalWorkingCopyFactory`, so each workspace materializes a real local working copy. Backend-store dedup is real, but `git worktree` already shares object storage via `.git/objects`. On *checked-out bytes per agent* — precisely what F2w measures — both flows plausibly pay ~1x the checkout.

That unmeasured claim then propagated into an architecture recommendation ("#253 may supersede ADR-0029 Phase 1"), which decomposition shows is backwards:

- #253 plausibly supersedes F1w (startup — jj-lib in-process, no subprocess) and moots F5w (jj does manifest->git natively).
- #253 does NOT address F2w (disk), F3w (structural read isolation — branch isolation is not read isolation), or F4w (sub-file granularity — whole-file checkout).

F3w and F4w are ADR-0029's actual novelty, and they are exactly the two F-tests that exist only as a baseline arm with "future mount-side measurement will assert..." comments. So the distinctive claims are not superseded; they are unproven.

The doc comment has been corrected in the CDC materialize-on-read branch to state the hypothesis rather than the claim.

## The experiment

The harness already exists: `rs/ll-open/cli-lib/tests/adr_0029_baseline_test.rs` measures the `git worktree` arm (F1w startup p50/p99, F2w disk per agent). Add a jj-workspace arm using `VcsIntegration::add_workspace` and compare on the SAME fixture.

## Why it is decisive

- If F2w(jj) ~= 100MB/agent (~1x checkout): supersession collapses on disk. ADR-0029's motivation stands as written; Phase 1 proceeds as specified.
- If F2w(jj) lands near the manifest target: re-scope ADR-0029 to lead with isolation (F3w) + sub-file granularity (F4w), demote F1w/F2w to no-regression guards, and Phase 1 shrinks considerably — possibly to scope enforcement layered on a jj workspace rather than a full mount driver.

Either way this is one measurement against an existing harness, and it is strictly cheaper than dispatching de3f81 on an unverified premise.

## Also fix while here

ADR-0029 section 2.2 (docs/adr/0029-cas-backed-workspace.md line 76) says "Mache's existing FUSE/NFS mount gains a manifest-mode." Mache removed FUSE in its v0.7.0 (ADR-0006) and is NFS-only; FUSE lives in leyline-fs. The ADR assigns the mount-driver work to a component shaped differently than it assumes. (Mache-side claim, relayed — verify against mache before editing.)

So ADR-0029 section 2.2's 'Mache's existing FUSE/NFS mount gains a manifest-mode' does assign work to a component that does not exist as described. Mache can supply an NFS manifest-mode; it cannot supply a FUSE one. FUSE is leyline-fs / 'leyline serve' in LLO.

title: Land merkle-branch bulk-load perf fix from mache-LLM handoff
description:
Mache LLM (2026-07-07 session) diagnosed the merkle-branch cold-parse slowdown as the classic SQLite bulk-load anti-pattern: `INSERT OR IGNORE` on a growing BLOB primary-key B-tree (`node_content`) + FK-guarded per-row probes (`node_child`, `_ast.node_hash`) under `foreign_keys=ON` produces ~2M probe operations to land ~150k unique rows.

They authored a 2-change surgical fix and left it in a worktree for LLO to review + land.

## Worktree location

`/private/tmp/llo-merkle-perf` — branch `perf/merkle-bulk-load` off `ir-producer-7ed023`.

## The 2-change fix

1. **Cross-file dedup in memory at the flush loop** — `HashSet<[u8;32]>` for `node_content` hashes and `HashSet<([u8;32], i64)>` for `node_child` (parent, ordinal) pairs. Buffers only push unique rows, so SQL sees ~150k rows instead of ~2M. Kills the probe storm at the source. The `INSERT OR IGNORE` prefix stays as a byte-identical-file backstop but the storm is gone.

2. **`PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON` after BEGIN** — FKs validated once at COMMIT instead of per-row probes into `node_content`'s BLOB PK. Still fail-loud (a dangling edge aborts the COMMIT).

Both are textbook "don't maintain a unique index + FKs during a bulk load" — the fix is old + well-understood.

## Measured impact (from mache LLM's session)

Merkle-branch cold parse was 1.4-2.8× slower than main (2× on full repo, 371 files). After fix: expected to close most of that gap on the merkle-specific work; the remaining baseline is what bead `ley-line-open-5ff6aa` addresses (pointer store reframe).

## Deeper design note (worth capturing but NOT this bead's scope)

Mache LLM noted: `node_content` on the merkle branch is literally a content-addressed BLOB store — git-object model, hash → object, dedup intrinsic to write. And LLO already has this primitive: `substrate.rs`'s `BlobStore` (the CA/IM/CR axioms). The merkle branch reinvented a worse CAS as a SQLite table with fake unique-index-dedup, next to the real one.

That framing belongs in bead `ley-line-open-5ff6aa` (pointer-store reframe) — the merkle branch's `node_content` should arguably BE the `BlobStore`, not a hand-rolled BLOB-PK table. Filing this note here for provenance; the reframe is 5ff6aa's design deliverable.

## Close condition

- Diff reviewed for correctness (in-memory dedup semantics match `INSERT OR IGNORE` semantics; deferred FK still catches dangling edges)
- `task ci` green on `perf/merkle-bulk-load` branch
- PR opened against `ir-producer-7ed023`, reviewed, merged
- Post-merge validation: instrumented cold-parse timing on merkle branch closes ≥80% of the gap to main baseline

## Provenance

- Mache LLM session 2026-07-07 diagnosed + patched. Handoff left in `/private/tmp/llo-merkle-perf`. This bead is the LLO tracking item.
- Base branch: `ir-producer-7ed023` (merkle IR work, ADR-0026 on that branch — note collision with LLO ADR-0026 filed on main this session for pointer store; resolve at merkle merge time by renumbering one).
- Related to `ley-line-open-5ff6aa` (pointer-store design bet — the deeper reframe of `node_content`).

## Validation

1. Cross-file dedup via `HashSet<[u8;32]>` + `HashSet<([u8;32], i64)>` — buffers push only unique rows so SQL sees ~150k rows instead of ~2M. `INSERT OR IGNORE` stays as cross-generation backstop.
2. `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys=ON` after BEGIN — FK checks batched to COMMIT instead of per-row probes into `node_content`'s BLOB PK.

title: Narrow ExecutionService state locks around backend calls
description: Workspace parking_lot audit found intentional direct uses across CAS, SQLite, signing caches, daemon coordination, FS graph, VCS, HDC, and runtime. The actionable runtime issue is ExecutionService::start holding its parking_lot::RwLock write guard while Backend::start performs potentially slow worker provisioning/readiness (up to the configured timeout), serializing unrelated starts and blocking inspect/status/cancel. Cleanup/cancel similarly performs backend work before state publication. Refactor state transitions into short lock scopes with an explicit in-flight reservation, preserving replay/idempotency and fail-closed lifecycle semantics. Add concurrent start/cancel/status tests; do not replace parking_lot mechanically.
